- [ ] **Step 5: Implement the decisions.** Append to the end of `ccd/history/lib.mjs`:

```js

// ===========================================================================
// W1-B2 recall, Task 1: identity, scope and ids (spec §8.2, §6.1, §6.9,
// §6.10, §8.4 describe, §8.6, §9.7). The CLI measures (the bounded tmux read,
// the registry files) and these functions decide; none reads a file, a
// process or the environment. Every registry fact arrives as a Presence, the
// three states the store-open table already takes, so a file that exists but
// cannot be read is never answered as absent (rev 3.2 review, IV5).
// ===========================================================================

/** The scope a read verb answers in (§8.2, the §8.3 header). Plan-chosen
 *  spelling of the three kinds the spec's header names. */
export const SCOPE_KINDS = Object.freeze(['family', 'project', 'workspace']);

/** The fewest hex digits a displayed node id keeps after its `L` or `N`,
 *  chosen (§6.1). Counted in hex digits so every display prefix passes the
 *  card's grammar gate, `L[0-9a-f]{6,20}` (§8.6). Prefixes are unique within
 *  the scope, never across it; `--json` always prints the full id. */
export const NODE_ID_DISPLAY_MIN = 6;

/** A full node id: `L` (leaf) or `N` (parent) plus 20 hex (§6.1). */
export const HISTORY_NODE_ID_RE = /^[LN][0-9a-f]{20}$/;

/** The directory under the history root that holds the eval control arm's
 *  per-id files (§9.7). Spelled once; the W2 verb writes it, B2 only reads. */
export const RECALL_OFF_DIR = 'recall-off';

/** `tmux display-message` prints `#S`; ccd names every session `cc-<id>`, and
 *  the hook requires the same prefix (spec §8.2). decideOpGate's pane test
 *  spells the prefix too, for a different decision (an irreversible form). */
const TMUX_SESSION_PREFIX = 'cc-';
const PANE_RE = /^%[0-9]+$/;

function refuseScope(reason) {
  return { ok: false, rc: EXIT.REFUSED, reason };
}

/** The session's id from tmux (§8.2, D-4675 (history-identity-from-tmux)). The
 *  caller ran `tmux display-message -p -t "$TMUX_PANE" '#S'` bounded at
 *  TMUX_DEADLINE_MS, ALWAYS with `-t`, and passes what came back; `tmux` is
 *  null when it never ran (no valid pane). A pane that is not `%<n>`, a run
 *  that did not settle or failed, or a name that is not `cc-<something>`
 *  answers `no-identity`; never "the most recent session". The stripped id
 *  then passes idOk before any path is formed from it, else `bad-id`
 *  (D-4170). */
export function decideIdentity({ pane, tmux }) {
  if (typeof pane !== 'string' || !PANE_RE.test(pane)) return refuseScope('no-identity');
  if (tmux === null || tmux.settled !== true || tmux.status !== 0 || typeof tmux.stdout !== 'string') {
    return refuseScope('no-identity');
  }
  const name = tmux.stdout.replace(/\r?\n$/, '');
  if (!name.startsWith(TMUX_SESSION_PREFIX) || name.length === TMUX_SESSION_PREFIX.length) return refuseScope('no-identity');
  const id = name.slice(TMUX_SESSION_PREFIX.length);
  return idOk(id) ? { ok: true, id } : refuseScope('bad-id');
}

/** The family's generation (§8.2, D-4192): the
 *  session's `CCRC_SESSION_GENERATION` when it has the uuid grammar, else
 *  `$REG/<id>.generation` read-only when IT has the grammar, else the id's
 *  newest family (§8.8: an unreadable or malformed file falls back too,
 *  because the generation only narrows a scope the id already bounds). */
export function resolveGeneration({ envGen, regGen }) {
  if (typeof envGen === 'string' && UUID_RE.test(envGen)) return { value: envGen, via: 'env' };
  if (regGen.state === 'value' && UUID_RE.test(regGen.value.trim())) return { value: regGen.value.trim(), via: 'registry' };
  return { value: null, via: 'newest' };
}

/** The harness check every read verb runs after the identity (§6.10 item 4,
 *  D-4679 (history-harness-unsupported-refused)). `$REG/<id>.harness` absent is
 *  Claude Code, today's only harness, which is HARNESSES' first row; a value
 *  with no HARNESS_TABLE row is `harness-unsupported`, never "not indexed
 *  yet"; a file that exists but cannot be read is `harness-unreadable`, never
 *  read as the default. */
export function decideHarness(p) {
  if (p.state === 'absent') return { ok: true, harness: HARNESSES[0] };
  if (p.state !== 'value') return refuseScope('harness-unreadable');
  const v = p.value.trim();
  return Object.hasOwn(HARNESS_TABLE, v) ? { ok: true, harness: v } : refuseScope('harness-unsupported');
}

/** A registry file's trimmed text, or null when it holds none: absent, empty,
 *  or unreadable. A decision that treats unreadable apart asks B1's
 *  module-private `presenceUnreadable` (beside `decideStoreOpen`) first
 *  (IV5), so this null never stands for two things it must tell apart. */
const presenceText = (p) => (p !== null && p.state === 'value' && p.value.trim() !== '' ? p.value.trim() : null);

/** Every scope decision a read verb takes (§8.2), in one place:
 *  - the scope source is DATA (`SCOPE_SOURCES`, D-4167):
 *    a source outside it is refused `no-identity`, never defaulted to tmux.
 *    W1 holds `tmux` only; W2 adds `env` with the headless seam;
 *  - `--project` with `--workspace`, or either with `--session`, is
 *    `bad-args`: each names a different scope;
 *  - `--session <id>` passes idOk (`bad-id`) and must share this session's
 *    project: a `.project` on either side that exists but cannot be read is
 *    `project-unreadable`; otherwise both must be present and equal, so an
 *    absent or empty one, which can never be shown equal, is
 *    `cross-project` like a different one (§8.2). Its generation is left to
 *    the caller (null);
 *  - `--project` needs this session's project (`project-unreadable`, absent
 *    or empty folded in on purpose: REASONS has no absent word, and an
 *    absent project widens nothing; D-4677 (history-recall-all-lanes));
 *  - `--workspace` needs this session's workdir AND project; either
 *    unreadable, absent or empty is `workspace-unreadable`, never a wider or
 *    narrower scope (D-4676 (history-workspace-scope));
 *  - otherwise the family (id, generation), the generation null when the
 *    caller must take the id's newest family. */
export function decideScope(i) {
  if (!SCOPE_SOURCES.includes(i.source)) return refuseScope('no-identity');
  if (!idOk(i.id)) return refuseScope('bad-id');
  const { project, workspace, session } = i.flags;
  if ((project ? 1 : 0) + (workspace ? 1 : 0) + (session !== null ? 1 : 0) > 1) return refuseScope('bad-args');
  const ownProject = presenceText(i.reg.project);
  const verdict = (kind, o) => ({
    ok: true, kind, source: i.source, id: i.id, generation: i.generation.value, project: ownProject, workdir: null, ...o,
  });
  if (session !== null) {
    if (!idOk(session)) return refuseScope('bad-id');
    const theirsFile = i.reg.sessionProject ?? { state: 'absent' };
    if (presenceUnreadable(i.reg.project) || presenceUnreadable(theirsFile)) return refuseScope('project-unreadable');
    const theirs = presenceText(theirsFile);
    if (ownProject === null || theirs !== ownProject) return refuseScope('cross-project');
    return verdict('family', { id: session, generation: session === i.id ? i.generation.value : null });
  }
  if (project) {
    if (ownProject === null) return refuseScope('project-unreadable');
    return verdict('project', {});
  }
  if (workspace) {
    const workdir = presenceText(i.reg.workdir);
    if (workdir === null || ownProject === null) return refuseScope('workspace-unreadable');
    return verdict('workspace', { workdir });
  }
  return verdict('family', {});
}

/** The shortest prefix of each id, its letter plus at least
 *  NODE_ID_DISPLAY_MIN hex digits, that no other id in THE SAME SET shares (§6.1: unique within the scope). The
 *  sorted neighbours bound it: an id needs one char past its longest common
 *  prefix with either neighbour. */
export function displayPrefixes(ids) {
  const sorted = [...new Set(ids)].sort();
  const lcp = (a, b) => {
    let n = 0;
    while (n < a.length && n < b.length && a[n] === b[n]) n += 1;
    return n;
  };
  const out = new Map();
  sorted.forEach((id, k) => {
    const shared = Math.max(k > 0 ? lcp(id, sorted[k - 1]) : 0, k + 1 < sorted.length ? lcp(id, sorted[k + 1]) : 0);
    out.set(id, id.slice(0, Math.min(id.length, Math.max(1 + NODE_ID_DISPLAY_MIN, shared + 1))));
  });
  return out;
}

/** An id or display prefix the session typed, resolved INSIDE its scope
 *  (§8.2, RV19; D-4678 (history-scope-on-every-verb)): exactly one in-scope match
 *  wins even when ids outside the scope share the prefix; none inside but
 *  some outside is `out-of-scope` (exit 2), never `not-found` (exit 3);
 *  several inside is `ambiguous`, which the CLI answers exit 2 `bad-args`
 *  with the candidates as a hint. */
export function resolveScopedId({ wanted, inScope, outOfScope }) {
  if (typeof wanted !== 'string' || !/^[LN][0-9a-f]{6,20}$/.test(wanted)) return { kind: 'bad' };
  const hits = [...new Set(inScope.filter((id) => id.startsWith(wanted)))];
  if (hits.length === 1) return { kind: 'ok', id: hits[0] };
  if (hits.length > 1) return { kind: 'ambiguous', candidates: hits.sort() };
  return outOfScope.some((id) => id.startsWith(wanted)) ? { kind: 'out-of-scope' } : { kind: 'not-found' };
}

// derived from lossless-claw src/tools/lcm-describe-id.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
const NODE_BARE_RE = /^[LN][0-9a-f]{6,20}…?$/;
const NODE_TOKEN_RE = /(?<![A-Za-z0-9])[LN][0-9a-f]{6,20}(?![A-Za-z0-9])/g;
const NODE_LOOSE_RE = /(?<![A-Za-z0-9])[LN][0-9A-Fa-f]{6,}(?![A-Za-z0-9])/i;
const escapeRe = (s) => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
const NODE_CARD_RE = new RegExp(`^${escapeRe(CARD_PREFIX)}node (L[0-9a-f]{6,20})…?(?=\\s|$)`);

/** `describe <id | pasted line>` (§8.4, §11 P28): a bare id or display
 *  prefix (the card's trailing ellipsis tolerated), or a pasted card line,
 *  whose structural id is the one right after `History: node ` (§8.6: the
 *  same node is named again as the describe argument, and a parent beside
 *  it, so counting mentions would refuse every card line). Free text is
 *  refused rather than guessed: several distinct ids, an uppercase or
 *  malformed one, or one id in prose each answer an error the CLI prints as
 *  exit 2 `bad-args`. An all-zero body is never an id. The error text echoes
 *  the input, so the CLI redacts it like any recalled field. */
export function extractNodeId(raw) {
  const trimmed = String(raw).trim();
  if (NODE_BARE_RE.test(trimmed)) return validNodeId(trimmed.replace(/…$/, ''));
  const card = NODE_CARD_RE.exec(trimmed);
  if (card !== null) return validNodeId(card[1]);
  const tokens = [...new Set(trimmed.match(NODE_TOKEN_RE) ?? [])];
  if (tokens.length > 1) {
    return { ok: false, error: `input names several node ids (${tokens.join(', ')}); give one bare id or one pasted ${CARD_PREFIX.trim()} line` };
  }
  const loose = NODE_LOOSE_RE.exec(trimmed)?.[0];
  if (loose === undefined) return { ok: false, error: `not a node id: ${raw}` };
  const checked = validNodeId(loose);
  if (!checked.ok) return checked;
  if (!/^[LN][0-9a-f]{6,20}$/.test(loose)) {
    return { ok: false, error: `malformed node id: ${loose}; an id is L or N plus 6 to 20 lowercase hex` };
  }
  return {
    ok: false, error: `not a node id or a card line: ${raw}`,
    hint: `give the bare id (${loose}) or paste the whole ${CARD_PREFIX.trim()} line`,
  };
}

function validNodeId(id) {
  return /^[LN]0+$/.test(id) ? { ok: false, error: `a node id cannot be all zeros: ${id}` } : { ok: true, id };
}

/** `~/.ccrc/history/recall-off/<id>` (§9.7). The id passes idOk BEFORE the
 *  path exists, so `../x` can never name a file outside the store
 *  (D-4170, C66). */
export function recallOffPath(home, id) {
  if (!idOk(id)) throw new TypeError(`recallOffPath: not a session id: ${JSON.stringify(id)}`);
  return `${historyPaths(home).root}/${RECALL_OFF_DIR}/${id}`;
}

/** Whether `recall-off/<id>` holds this family (§9.7,
 *  D-4680 (history-recall-off-generation)). Its content is the generation it was
 *  assigned to (`''` for a legacy family): equal to the resolved generation
 *  is `off` (exit 8, counted); another generation is `stale` (the id was
 *  purged and reused: recall proceeds and the drain counts
 *  `recall_off_stale`); absent is `none`. A file that exists but cannot be
 *  read is `off`: the id WAS assigned an arm, so answering it as the
 *  treatment arm would mix the eval's arms, while exit 8 only withholds
 *  recall. `generation` is the RESOLVED family's: when resolveGeneration
 *  answers `via: 'newest'`, the caller finds the id's newest family first
 *  and passes ITS generation: `''` only when that family is legacy or the
 *  store holds no family of the id, never resolveGeneration's unresolved
 *  `value ?? ''` before the family is known (§8.2, §8.8, §9.7). */
export function decideRecallOff({ file, generation }) {
  if (file.state === 'absent') return 'none';
  if (file.state !== 'value') return 'off';
  return file.value.trim() === generation ? 'off' : 'stale';
}
```

The ellipsis inside `NODE_BARE_RE`, `NODE_CARD_RE` and the `replace` in `extractNodeId` is the single character U+2026 (`…`), written as itself, not as an escape. Check it after writing with `grep -c '…' ccd/history/lib.mjs` (at least 3 more than before) and `od -c` on one of those lines if in doubt.

**Spec:** §8.4 grep (each token quoted, a trailing `*` outside the quotes; regex syntax refused without querying; `--regex` refused as a discriminated result or run under a 5 s kill; hybrid over integer `ts_ms`; the top 2,000 in-scope matches), §11 V2, P1, P8, P9, P10 and refuted candidates 1 and 2, §12 (the sanitiser's 17 test cases re-derived, not copied). It owns pin **C6**, and ships C7's and C8a's pure halves. Departures: B1's D-4243 (`history-fts-indexes-redacted-text`) (the snippet and the regex run over redacted text; the caller hands it); D-4681 (`history-grep-pages-end-at-rank-pool`) (named in `RANK_POOL`'s doc comment; Task 13 carries the paging).

Choices this task makes where the spec is silent (each is in the plan's open issues):
- `regexPrefilter` names only a WHOLE-WORD literal, as an exact-token query. A prefix query can drop a true hit, because porter stems prefix queries (measured: `"runn"*` does not find `running`), and `\b` can sit beside a non-ASCII letter that FTS5 keeps in the token. Most patterns therefore get no prefilter and are scanned in full under Task 14's 5 s kill.
- `guardRegex` adds a structural rule (a group repeated more than once whose body can match in more than one way), which refuses some harmless patterns such as `(a|b){2}`; patterns compile with no flags.
- `--since`/`--before` read `<n>d`, `<n>h`, `<n>min`, an ISO date (UTC midnight) or a date-time with `Z` or an offset. `m` is refused because `prune --older-than` reads it as months (upstream's `parseDuration`).
- `GREP_LIMIT_DEFAULT` is 20.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the mutation runner.** It is a gitignored scratch tool (`.superpowers/` is in `.gitignore`), never committed. It is the ONE runner of the B2 tasks that measure guards with a mutants file: Tasks 1–7, 7A, 7B and 8 write this same file, byte for byte (Task 5 writes it at its Step 8), so each task stands alone and rewriting it changes nothing. It runs vitest with `maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024` (Tasks 7A and 7B carry cases over large strings, coordinator ruling R-runner). A mutant is `{name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}`, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. For each mutant the runner copies the pristine file to `.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/`, applies the edits and runs the named tests, which must fail; it then restores the file from the copy, removes the copy, and runs the same tests again, which must pass. Every exit the runner sees restores. Only a kill no handler sees (SIGKILL, a tool timeout that escalates) leaves a copy in `scratch/keep/`; the next run then refuses, and the runner's header gives the one-line restore. From the repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <<'EOF'
// .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs: measures each guard RED with it mutated, then GREEN with
// it restored (the B2 plan's mutation-pin rule). Run from server/, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least
// 600000 ms:
//   node ../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <mutants.json>
// A mutant is {name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}. `file` is repo-relative, `test` is
// server/-relative, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. The
// pristine file is copied to scratch/keep/<file with '/' as '__'>.orig BEFORE it is touched, and the copy is
// removed only after the file is restored from it. A kill no handler sees therefore leaves the original findable,
// and the next run REFUSES while any copy is left. To restore by hand, from the repository root:
//   for f in .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/*.orig; do t="$(basename "$f" .orig)"; cp "$f" "${t//__//}" && rm "$f"; done
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const KEEP = '../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep';
mkdirSync(KEEP, { recursive: true });
const left = readdirSync(KEEP).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.orig'));
if (left.length > 0) {
  console.log(`REFUSED: ${left.join(', ')} in ${KEEP}. An earlier run was interrupted and a source may hold a mutant: restore as this file's header says.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const keepOf = (file) => `${KEEP}/${file.replaceAll('/', '__')}.orig`;
const restoreAll = () => {
  for (const n of readdirSync(KEEP)) {
    if (!n.endsWith('.orig')) continue;
    copyFileSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`, `../${n.slice(0, -'.orig'.length).replaceAll('__', '/')}`);
    rmSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`);
  }
};
// Every way out restores: the loop's end, process.exit and an uncaught throw all emit 'exit', and a signal is
// turned into an exit. A signal sent while the synchronous loop holds the thread is handled after the current
// child returns; a Ctrl-C also reaches the vitest child, and the loop stops on the child's signal below.
process.on('exit', restoreAll);
for (const s of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) process.on(s, () => process.exit(130));
// maxBuffer: past Node's default (1 MiB) spawnSync kills the child (ENOBUFS, signal SIGTERM, measured), which the
// loop below reads as an interrupt. Each large-operand case asserts a boolean or a length, so a red prints no big diff.
const vitest = (test, filter) => spawnSync('./node_modules/.bin/vitest', ['run', test, '-t', filter], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 });
const mutants = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
let bad = 0;
for (const m of mutants) {
  const target = `../${m.file}`;
  if (!existsSync(target)) { console.log(`NO SUCH FILE       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  const keep = keepOf(m.file);
  copyFileSync(target, keep);
  let src = readFileSync(keep, 'utf8');
  let unique = true;
  for (const e of m.edits) {
    const at = src.indexOf(e.anchor);
    if (at < 0 || src.indexOf(e.anchor, at + 1) >= 0) { unique = false; break; }
    src = src.slice(0, at) + e.replacement + src.slice(at + e.anchor.length);
  }
  if (!unique) { rmSync(keep); console.log(`ANCHOR NOT UNIQUE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  writeFileSync(target, src);
  const red = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  copyFileSync(keep, target);
  rmSync(keep);
  if (red.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${red.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  const failed = /Tests\s+(\d+) failed/.exec(red.stdout)?.[1] ?? '?';
  if (red.status === 0) { console.log(`STAYED GREEN       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`red (${failed} failed)   ${m.name}`);
  const green = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  if (green.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${green.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  if (green.status !== 0) { console.log(`RED AFTER RESTORE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`green              ${m.name}`);
}
console.log(bad === 0 ? 'every guard measured red, then green' : `${bad} guard(s) not measured`);
process.exit(bad === 0 ? 0 : 1);
EOF
```

```ts
// ===========================================================================
// W1-B2 Task 2: search primitives (spec §8.4 grep, §11 V2, P1, P8, P9, P10).

/** The store's blobs_fts definition (store.mjs FTS_DDL), on an in-memory DB. */
const ftsCorpus = (docs: ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, string]>): FtsDb => {

  db.exec("CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE blobs_fts USING fts5(body, content='', contentless_delete=1, tokenize='porter unicode61')");

    ['17 answers the empty phrase for an empty quoted phrase', '""', '""'],

describe('ftsOrderBy: hybrid over integer ts_ms, NULL last (spec 8.4; P8)', () => {
  const NOW = 1_760_000_000_000;
  const H = 3_600_000;
  it('spells each sort, and refuses an unknown sort or a column that is not a name', () => {
    expect(libSearch.GREP_SORTS).toEqual(['recency', 'relevance', 'hybrid']);
    expect(libSearch.ftsOrderBy('recency', 'e.ts_ms')).toBe('e.ts_ms DESC');
    expect(libSearch.ftsOrderBy('relevance', 'e.ts_ms')).toBe('rank ASC, e.ts_ms DESC');
    expect(libSearch.ftsOrderBy('hybrid', 'e.ts_ms')).toContain('COALESCE(e.ts_ms, 0)');
    expect(libSearch.ftsOrderBy('hybrid', 'e.ts_ms')).not.toContain('julianday');
    expect(() => libSearch.ftsOrderBy('newest', 'e.ts_ms')).toThrow(TypeError);
    for (const bad of ['e.ts_ms; DROP TABLE x', 'ts_ms)', '', '1ts']) expect(() => libSearch.ftsOrderBy('recency', bad), bad).toThrow(TypeError);
  });
  it('on real FTS5: relevance, recency and hybrid order a strong old hit, a weak new one and an undated one differently', () => {
    const db = ftsCorpus([
      [1, 'drain drain drain spool'], [2, 'drain then a long tail of other words about the store and its writer token and journal'],
      [3, 'drain drain drain spool'], ...Array.from({ length: 30 }, (_, k) => [10 + k, `unrelated filler ${k}`] as const),
    ]);
    db.exec('CREATE TABLE e (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ts_ms INTEGER)');
    const ts = db.prepare('INSERT INTO e (id, ts_ms) VALUES (?, ?)');
    ts.run(1, NOW - 2000 * H);
    ts.run(2, NOW - H);
    ts.run(3, null);
    // Only `hybrid` names `:now_ms`, and node:sqlite refuses a named parameter the statement lacks.
    const order = (sort: string): number[] => {
      const sql = `SELECT e.id AS id FROM blobs_fts JOIN e ON e.id = blobs_fts.rowid WHERE blobs_fts MATCH ? ORDER BY ${libSearch.ftsOrderBy(sort, 'e.ts_ms')}`;
      const st = db.prepare(sql);
      const rows = sql.includes(':now_ms') ? st.all({ now_ms: NOW }, '"drain"') : st.all('"drain"');
      return rows.map((r) => Number(r['id']));
    };
    expect(order('relevance')).toEqual([1, 3, 2]);
    expect(order('recency')).toEqual([2, 1, 3]);
    expect(order('hybrid'), 'the old strong hit outranks the new weak one; the undated one sorts last').toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
    expect(db.prepare('SELECT julianday(1760000000000) AS j').get()?.['j'], 'refuted candidate 2: julianday of an integer').toBeNull();
  });
});
```

```js

// ===========================================================================
// W1-B2 recall, Task 2: search primitives (spec §8.4 grep, §11 V2, P1, P8,
// P9, P10). Pure text and SQL-fragment decisions: the CLI runs the query and
// the regex worker runs the match. Task 1's module-private `escapeRe` is
// reused here.
// ===========================================================================

// derived from lossless-claw src/store/fts5-sanitize.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
/** The FTS5 MATCH text for plain `grep <words>` (§8.4, §11 P1). Every token
 *  is quoted, so FTS5 operators (`OR`, `NOT`, `NEAR(`), column filters and
 *  punctuation are literal text, and the terms are joined by spaces, which
 *  FTS5 reads as AND. A quoted phrase stays one phrase. ccrc's change: a token
 *  or phrase ENDING in `*` (inside or right after its closing quote) becomes
 *  a quoted term followed by `*`, an FTS5 prefix query, so `a0860d1f*` finds a
 *  SHA by its prefix with no trigram index; upstream kept the star inside the
 *  quotes, where it matches nothing. Porter stems a prefix query too, so a
 *  prefix cut inside a word's stem can miss (`runn*` does not find
 *  `running`, measured); a hex prefix is never stemmed. An empty query is
 *  `""`, which matches nothing and never errors. */
export function sanitizeFtsQuery(raw) {
  const text = String(raw);
  const parts = [];
  const bare = (chunk) => {
    for (const t of chunk.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)) parts.push(quoteFtsTerm(t.replace(/"/g, '')));
  };
  const phraseRe = /"([^"]+)"(\*?)/g;
  let last = 0;
  for (let m = phraseRe.exec(text); m !== null; m = phraseRe.exec(text)) {
    bare(text.slice(last, m.index));
    const phrase = m[1].replace(/"/g, '').trim();
    if (phrase) parts.push(quoteFtsTerm(m[2] === '*' ? `${phrase}*` : phrase));

function quoteFtsTerm(t) {

export function queryTerms(raw) {

 *  `$` only at a word edge. */
export function regexSyntaxIn(pattern) {

/** The regex worker's wall-clock kill, chosen (§8.4). */
export const REGEX_BUDGET_MS = 5000;

// derived from lossless-claw src/store/search-regex.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
const REGEX_QUANTIFIER = String.raw`(?:[+*?]|\{\d+(?:,\d*)?\})`;

/** A quantifier starting at `k`, as {len, min, max}, or null. */
function regexQuantifierAt(p, k) {

/** ccrc's structural ReDoS rule: a group repeated more than once (a

 *  nested groups included. Escapes and character classes are skipped, and a
 *  group's own `(?:`, `(?=`, `(?<name>` prefix is not a quantifier. It
 *  refuses some harmless patterns (`(a|b){2}`) to refuse every catastrophic
 *  one of that shape; the refusal names `--regex` and the pattern, so the
 *  session rewrites it. */
function repeatsVariableGroup(p) {
  const open = [];

    i += q.len;
    if (p[i] === '?') i += 1;

  while (i < p.length) {
    const c = p[i];
    if (c === '\\') { i += 2; continue; }
    if (c === '[') {
      i += 1;
      while (i < p.length && p[i] !== ']') i += p[i] === '\\' ? 2 : 1;
      i += 1;
      continue;
    }
    if (c === '(') {
      open.push(false);
      i += 1;
      if (p[i] === '?') {
        i += 1;
        if (p[i] === '<' && p[i + 1] !== '=' && p[i + 1] !== '!') {

          i += 1;
        } else {
          i += p[i] === '<' ? 2 : 1;

      continue;

    if (c === '|') {
      if (open.length > 0) open[open.length - 1] = true;
      i += 1;
      continue;
    }
    if (c === ')') {
      const variable = open.pop() === true;
      i += 1;
      const q = regexQuantifierAt(p, i);
      if (q !== null && q.max > 1 && variable) return true;
      if (open.length > 0 && (variable || (q !== null && q.min !== q.max))) open[open.length - 1] = true;
      if (q !== null) skipQuantifier(q);
      continue;
    }
    const q = regexQuantifierAt(p, i);
    if (q !== null) {
      if (q.min !== q.max && open.length > 0) open[open.length - 1] = true;

/** The FTS prefilter `--regex` runs before its worker (§8.4), or null for a
 *  full scan of the scope. It must never drop a true hit, so it names only a
 *  WHOLE-WORD literal every match contains: a top-level run of 3 or more
 *  ASCII letters or digits, each unquantified, bounded on both sides by an
 *  unquantified anchor (`^`, `$`), literal whitespace (` `, `\s`, `\t`,
 *  `\n`, `\r`) or literal ASCII punctuation, in a pattern with no top-level
 *  alternation. Those bounds are FTS5 separators, so the run is one whole
 *  token, and an exact-token query (no star) finds it: porter stems the query
 *  and the index alike. A prefix query (`"runn"*` misses `running`) and
 *  `\b` (which can sit beside a non-ASCII letter FTS5 keeps in the token)
 *  never make one. The longest such run wins; FTS5 folds case, so the
 *  prefilter is a superset of a case-sensitive pattern. */
export function regexPrefilter(pattern) {
  const atoms = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < pattern.length;) {
    const c = pattern[i];

    if (c === '\\') {

    } else if (c === '[') {
      i += 1;
      while (i < pattern.length && pattern[i] !== ']') i += pattern[i] === '\\' ? 2 : 1;
      i += 1;
      atoms.push({ t: 'other' });
    } else if (c === '(') {
      let depth = 0;
      for (; i < pattern.length; i += 1) {
        if (pattern[i] === '\\') { i += 1; continue; }
        if (pattern[i] === '[') {
          i += 1;
          while (i < pattern.length && pattern[i] !== ']') i += pattern[i] === '\\' ? 2 : 1;
          continue;
        }
        if (pattern[i] === '(') depth += 1;
        if (pattern[i] === ')' && --depth === 0) break;
      }
      i += 1;
      atoms.push({ t: 'other' });
    } else if (regexQuantifierAt(pattern, i) !== null) {
      const q = regexQuantifierAt(pattern, i);
      if (atoms.length > 0) atoms[atoms.length - 1] = { t: 'other' };
      i += q.len;
      if (pattern[i] === '?') i += 1;
    } else {
      if (/[A-Za-z0-9]/.test(c)) atoms.push({ t: 'word', ch: c });
      else if (c === '^' || c === '$' || c === ' ' || (/[!-/:-@[-`{-~]/.test(c) && c !== '.')) atoms.push({ t: 'sep' });
      else atoms.push({ t: 'other' });
      i += 1;
    }
  }
  let best = '';
  for (let k = 0; k < atoms.length;) {
    if (atoms[k].t !== 'word') { k += 1; continue; }
    let e = k;
    while (e < atoms.length && atoms[e].t === 'word') e += 1;
    const run = atoms.slice(k, e).map((a) => a.ch).join('');
    const bounded = k > 0 && atoms[k - 1].t === 'sep' && e < atoms.length && atoms[e].t === 'sep';

/** The sorts `grep --sort` takes (§8.4); `recency` is the default. */
export const GREP_SORTS = Object.freeze(['recency', 'relevance', 'hybrid']);
/** `--limit` (§8.4): at most 100; 20 when not given, chosen. */
export const GREP_LIMIT_MAX = 100;
export const GREP_LIMIT_DEFAULT = 20;
/** Every grep sort ranks and pages over the top 2,000 in-scope matches; §8.4 gives the pool to hybrid only (D-4681 (history-grep-pages-end-at-rank-pool)). */
export const RANK_POOL = 2000;
/** The hybrid sort's age decay per hour: upstream's AGE_DECAY_RATE (§11 P8). */
export const HYBRID_AGE_DECAY = 0.001;

// derived from lossless-claw src/store/full-text-sort.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
/** The ORDER BY of a ranked grep query (§8.4, §11 P8). `rank` is FTS5's
 *  BM25, lower is better. `hybrid` divides it by an age term in HOURS taken
 *  from the integer `ts_ms` and the statement's bound `:now_ms` parameter:
 *  upstream's `julianday(<ts>)` is NULL for an integer (measured, refuted
 *  candidate 2), which silently degrades the sort to recency. A NULL
 *  timestamp counts as the oldest, so it sorts last, never first; a
 *  timestamp ahead of the clock ages 0. `tsExpr` is interpolated into SQL,
 *  so only a (qualified) column name is accepted. */
export function ftsOrderBy(sort, tsExpr) {

    throw new TypeError(`ftsOrderBy: not a column name: ${JSON.stringify(tsExpr)}`);
  }
  switch (sort) {
    case 'recency':
      return `${tsExpr} DESC`;
    case 'relevance':
      return `rank ASC, ${tsExpr} DESC`;
    case 'hybrid':
      return `(rank / (1 + (MAX(0, :now_ms - COALESCE(${tsExpr}, 0)) / 3600000.0) * ${HYBRID_AGE_DECAY})) ASC, ${tsExpr} DESC`;
    default:
      throw new TypeError(`ftsOrderBy: sort outside GREP_SORTS: ${String(sort)}`);
  }
}

/** Word endings tried when a stemmed match leaves a literal term unfound. */
const SNIPPET_STEM_SUFFIXES = Object.freeze(['ing', 'ed', 'es', 's']);

/** A slice end that never splits a surrogate pair. */
function cutBefore(s, n) {

/** The grep snippet (§8.4, §11 P9): a window of 24 characters before and 40

 *  hit plus ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN on each side, redacted and cut back to the
 *  window, never the whole body (Task 12's displaySnippet, which hitSnippet

/** `--since` / `--before` (§8.4), plan-chosen grammar: `<n>d`, `<n>h` or

 *  `Z` or an offset. A date-time without a zone would depend on the box's
 *  timezone, and an impossible date (`2026-02-30`) would roll over, so both
 *  are null, which the CLI answers exit 2 `bad-args`. Minutes are `min`,
 *  never `m`, which `prune --older-than` reads as months. */

  const t = String(s).trim();

  if (m === null) return null;
  const day = new Date(Date.UTC(Number(m[1]), Number(m[2]) - 1, Number(m[3])));
  if (day.getUTCFullYear() !== Number(m[1]) || day.getUTCMonth() !== Number(m[2]) - 1 || day.getUTCDate() !== Number(m[3])) return null;

```

Two things the code depends on that a reviewer will ask about:
- `repeatsVariableGroup` is ccrc's own: upstream's guard (kept above it as a floor) inspects only the character before `)`, so it admits `(.*a){8}$`, which took 1,973 ms on 30 characters on Node 22.16.0 (measured here; the spec measured 1,235 ms).
- In `ftsOrderBy`'s `hybrid`, `MAX(0, …)` is SQLite's two-argument scalar `MAX`, and `COALESCE(<ts>, 0)` makes an undated row the oldest: without it the whole expression is NULL and SQLite sorts NULL FIRST under `ASC`.

Departures it implements: B1's D-4202 (`history-redaction-before-cut`), B1's D-4171 (`history-reasons-by-exit`), B1's D-4167 (`history-coverage-this-box`), B1's D-4169 (`history-exit-codes-4-and-9`), B1's D-4200 (`history-variant-cause`), B1's D-4221 (`history-apply-via-shim`), D-4682 (`history-skill-literal-path`).

Choices this task makes where the spec is silent (each is in the plan's open issues):
- The header keeps `transcripts`/`families` plural whatever N is, so the line has one grammar, and prints `lag=<n>s` the way B1's `status` already does.
- `costRow` and the relay and envelope builders are ccrc's own (P13 and P11 lend only their shape), so they carry no PROVENANCE entry; the cursor codec follows upstream's `args.ts` and does.
- `stripReadPrefix` strips only a leading run of consecutively numbered lines, so a data file whose rows begin with digits is never mangled, and a reminder Claude Code appends after a Read is kept.
- A `src` outside `RECALL_SRCS` prints as the controlled word `unknown` instead of throwing. `expand` and `grep` pass `entries.provenance` straight from the store, which has no CHECK, and the CLI may read a store a newer writer filled (§8.8, version-aware selects), so a provenance word this build does not know must never turn a read into exit 1; mapping it keeps every path and free text out of the attribute all the same.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the mutation runner.** It is a gitignored scratch tool (`.superpowers/` is in `.gitignore`), never committed. It is the ONE runner of the B2 tasks that measure guards with a mutants file: Tasks 1–7, 7A, 7B and 8 write this same file, byte for byte (Task 5 writes it at its Step 8), so each task stands alone and rewriting it changes nothing. It runs vitest with `maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024` (Tasks 7A and 7B carry cases over large strings, coordinator ruling R-runner). A mutant is `{name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}`, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. For each mutant the runner copies the pristine file to `.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/`, applies the edits and runs the named tests, which must fail; it then restores the file from the copy, removes the copy, and runs the same tests again, which must pass. Every exit the runner sees restores. Only a kill no handler sees (SIGKILL, a tool timeout that escalates) leaves a copy in `scratch/keep/`; the next run then refuses, and the runner's header gives the one-line restore. From the repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <<'EOF'
// .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs: measures each guard RED with it mutated, then GREEN with
// it restored (the B2 plan's mutation-pin rule). Run from server/, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least
// 600000 ms:
//   node ../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <mutants.json>
// A mutant is {name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}. `file` is repo-relative, `test` is
// server/-relative, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. The
// pristine file is copied to scratch/keep/<file with '/' as '__'>.orig BEFORE it is touched, and the copy is
// removed only after the file is restored from it. A kill no handler sees therefore leaves the original findable,
// and the next run REFUSES while any copy is left. To restore by hand, from the repository root:
//   for f in .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/*.orig; do t="$(basename "$f" .orig)"; cp "$f" "${t//__//}" && rm "$f"; done
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const KEEP = '../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep';
mkdirSync(KEEP, { recursive: true });
const left = readdirSync(KEEP).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.orig'));
if (left.length > 0) {
  console.log(`REFUSED: ${left.join(', ')} in ${KEEP}. An earlier run was interrupted and a source may hold a mutant: restore as this file's header says.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const keepOf = (file) => `${KEEP}/${file.replaceAll('/', '__')}.orig`;
const restoreAll = () => {
  for (const n of readdirSync(KEEP)) {
    if (!n.endsWith('.orig')) continue;
    copyFileSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`, `../${n.slice(0, -'.orig'.length).replaceAll('__', '/')}`);
    rmSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`);
  }
};
// Every way out restores: the loop's end, process.exit and an uncaught throw all emit 'exit', and a signal is
// turned into an exit. A signal sent while the synchronous loop holds the thread is handled after the current
// child returns; a Ctrl-C also reaches the vitest child, and the loop stops on the child's signal below.
process.on('exit', restoreAll);
for (const s of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) process.on(s, () => process.exit(130));
// maxBuffer: past Node's default (1 MiB) spawnSync kills the child (ENOBUFS, signal SIGTERM, measured), which the
// loop below reads as an interrupt. Each large-operand case asserts a boolean or a length, so a red prints no big diff.
const vitest = (test, filter) => spawnSync('./node_modules/.bin/vitest', ['run', test, '-t', filter], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 });
const mutants = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
let bad = 0;
for (const m of mutants) {
  const target = `../${m.file}`;
  if (!existsSync(target)) { console.log(`NO SUCH FILE       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  const keep = keepOf(m.file);
  copyFileSync(target, keep);
  let src = readFileSync(keep, 'utf8');
  let unique = true;
  for (const e of m.edits) {
    const at = src.indexOf(e.anchor);
    if (at < 0 || src.indexOf(e.anchor, at + 1) >= 0) { unique = false; break; }
    src = src.slice(0, at) + e.replacement + src.slice(at + e.anchor.length);
  }
  if (!unique) { rmSync(keep); console.log(`ANCHOR NOT UNIQUE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  writeFileSync(target, src);
  const red = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  copyFileSync(keep, target);
  rmSync(keep);
  if (red.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${red.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  const failed = /Tests\s+(\d+) failed/.exec(red.stdout)?.[1] ?? '?';
  if (red.status === 0) { console.log(`STAYED GREEN       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`red (${failed} failed)   ${m.name}`);
  const green = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  if (green.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${green.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  if (green.status !== 0) { console.log(`RED AFTER RESTORE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`green              ${m.name}`);
}
console.log(bad === 0 ? 'every guard measured red, then green' : `${bad} guard(s) not measured`);
process.exit(bad === 0 ? 0 : 1);
EOF
```

```ts

// ===========================================================================
// W1-B2 Task 3: output primitives (spec §8.3, §8.4, §11 P11, P12, P13, P17,
// P30). Property tests; the verb pins that use them (C12, C15, C45, C59, O54)

describe('the recall envelope: escaped attributes and text, one closing tag (spec 8.3; P30)', () => {
  it('escapes the ampersand first, then quotes and angle brackets', () => {

    expect(libOut.escapeXmlText('&lt;')).toBe('&amp;lt;');
  });

    const out = libOut.recallEnvelope({

    });

      + 'x&lt;/ccrc-recall&gt;&lt;ccrc-recall src="operator"&gt;y "z"</ccrc-recall>');
  });
  it('an unknown time or role prints empty, and src is a controlled word, never a path', () => {
    expect(libOut.recallEnvelope({ src: 'node', id: 'N7c1e2a', ts: null, role: null, text: 'g' }))
      .toBe('<ccrc-recall src="node" id="N7c1e2a" ts="" role="" trust="untrusted">g</ccrc-recall>');
    expect(libOut.RECALL_SRCS).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(['operator', 'model', 'tool', 'node', 'summary', 'sidecar', 'unknown']));
    expect(new Set(libOut.RECALL_SRCS).size, 'each word once').toBe(libOut.RECALL_SRCS.length);
  });
  it('a src outside RECALL_SRCS (a path, free text, a newer writer\'s provenance word) prints as unknown and never throws', () => {
    for (const src of ['/home/u/x', 'file', '', 'subagent', 'x" onload="y']) {
      expect(libOut.recallEnvelope({ src, id: 'x', ts: null, role: null, text: '' }), src)
        .toBe('<ccrc-recall src="unknown" id="x" ts="" role="" trust="untrusted"></ccrc-recall>');
    }
  });
});

    const { kept, shown } = libOut.capOutput(blocks, 500);

    expect(libOut.headerLine({ kind: 'family', id: 'claude-a-demo', project: 'demo', families: 1, transcripts: 3, indexedThroughMs: T, lagS: 42 }))
      .toBe('scope=family(claude-a-demo, 3 transcripts) coverage=this-box indexed-through=2026-10-06T12:00:00.000Z lag=42s');
    expect(libOut.headerLine({ kind: 'project', id: 'claude-a-demo', project: 'demo', families: 2, transcripts: 5, indexedThroughMs: null, lagS: null }))
      .toBe('scope=project(demo, 2 families) coverage=this-box indexed-through=unmeasured lag=unmeasured');
    expect(libOut.headerLine({ kind: 'workspace', id: 'claude-a-demo', project: 'demo', families: 1, transcripts: 1, indexedThroughMs: T, lagS: 0 }))
      .toBe('scope=workspace(demo, 1 families) coverage=this-box indexed-through=2026-10-06T12:00:00.000Z lag=0s');
    expect(() => libOut.headerLine({ kind: 'box' as 'family', id: 'a', project: null, families: 0, transcripts: 0, indexedThroughMs: null, lagS: null })).toThrow(TypeError);
  });
  it('lag is now minus the oldest end-of-file tick in scope; any file never at its end, none, or a recovery is unmeasured, never 0', () => {
    expect(libOut.scopeLag({ eofMs: [T - 5_000, T - 61_000], nowMs: T, recovering: false })).toEqual({ indexedThroughMs: T - 61_000, lagS: 61 });
    expect(libOut.scopeLag({ eofMs: [T - 5_000, null], nowMs: T, recovering: false })).toEqual({ indexedThroughMs: null, lagS: null });
    expect(libOut.scopeLag({ eofMs: [], nowMs: T, recovering: false })).toEqual({ indexedThroughMs: null, lagS: null });
    expect(libOut.scopeLag({ eofMs: [T - 5_000], nowMs: T, recovering: true })).toEqual({ indexedThroughMs: null, lagS: null });
    expect(libOut.scopeLag({ eofMs: [T + 9_000], nowMs: T, recovering: false })).toEqual({ indexedThroughMs: T + 9_000, lagS: 0 });
  });
});

describe('the read --json envelope: reason exactly where the exit carries one (spec 8.3; P11)', () => {
  const base = { storeId: '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0123456789ab', scope: { kind: 'family' }, header: { indexedThroughMs: 5, lagS: 1 }, items: [], shown: 0, total: 0, next: null };
  it('carries store_id, coverage and every item stamped untrusted, whatever the item said', () => {
    const env = libOut.readEnvelope({ ...base, exit: 0, items: [{ node_id: 'L03a9c000000000000001', trust: 'trusted' }], shown: 1, total: 1 });
    expect(env).toEqual({
      v: 1, exit: 0, store_id: base.storeId, coverage: 'this-box', scope: { kind: 'family' }, indexed_through_ms: 5, lag_s: 1,
      items: [{ node_id: 'L03a9c000000000000001', trust: 'untrusted' }], shown: 1, total: 1, next: null,
    });
    expect('reason' in env).toBe(false);
  });
  it('exits 2, 4, 5 and 7 need a reason word of their own code', () => {
    expect(libOut.readEnvelope({ ...base, exit: 2, reason: 'out-of-scope' }).reason).toBe('out-of-scope');
    expect(libOut.readEnvelope({ ...base, exit: 5, reason: 'store-unbound', header: null }).reason).toBe('store-unbound');
    expect(() => libOut.readEnvelope({ ...base, exit: 2 })).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => libOut.readEnvelope({ ...base, exit: 2, reason: 'store-unbound' })).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => libOut.readEnvelope({ ...base, exit: 7, reason: 'toString' })).toThrow(TypeError);

  it('exits 0, 1, 3, 6, 8 and 9 carry none, and a value outside EXIT is refused', () => {

    expect(() => libOut.readEnvelope({ ...base, exit: 10 })).toThrow(TypeError);

});

describe('the cursor: opaque, versioned, ids only (spec 8.4)', () => {
  it('round-trips, and refuses another resource, a tampered string or text', () => {
    const c = { v: 1 as const, resource: 'grep' as const, q: 'a'.repeat(64), after: { pos: 12, entryId: 9001 } };
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Implement the output primitives.** Append to the end of `ccd/history/lib.mjs`:

```js

// ===========================================================================
// W1-B2 recall, Task 3: output primitives (spec §8.3, §8.4 describe and
// expand, §11 P11, P12, P13, P17, P30). Task 2's module-private `cutBefore`
// makes every cut here surrogate-safe. Every recalled field reaches these
// ALREADY redacted (§8.3, D-4202; the plan's Global Constraints R2): a whole
// field through redactForDisplay, or, for a windowed display (a grep
// snippet, a describe or expand page, expand's outline input), the shown
// window through Task 12's redactDisplayWindow, which cuts it from the
// redactForDisplay reading of the window and ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN on each side
// (an inexact window under DISPLAY_INEXACT_NOTE), before any cut. They cut,
// escape, count and serialise, in that order, and the CLI runs redactFinal
// over the whole rendered output last.
// ===========================================================================

/** The output cap per call, in characters (§8.3; Claude Code's inline Bash
 *  cap is 30,000). */
export const OUTPUT_CAP = 20000;
/** `expand` cuts one big tool output to this many characters (§8.4). */
export const EXPLORE_CUT = 2000;
/** `describe` shows this much of a native summary; `--full` pages the rest (§8.4). */
export const DESCRIBE_EXCERPT = 4000;
/** A result over this many caps adds a `hint: delegate` line (§8.4). */
export const DELEGATE_FACTOR = 3;
/** One grep hit's snippet line, upstream's truncateSnippet bound (§11 P12). */
export const SNIPPET_MAX = 200;
/** The largest tool output the JSON explorer parses, chosen: above it the
 *  counts summary stands in, so one recalled multi-MiB output never costs a
 *  whole JSON.parse on a session's read path. */
export const EXPLORE_JSON_MAX = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
/** Every command ccrc prints for a session to run, by its literal path (§8.1,
 *  D-4682 (history-skill-literal-path)): `ccrc` is not on PATH inside sessions. */
export const HISTORY_CMD = '"$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc" history';
/** The shim's exit when an `--op` pass finds the lock held (§8.4); the CLI
 *  answers exit 4 `writer-busy`. */
export const SHIM_LOCK_HELD = 75;
/** The `src` attribute's words: a row's provenance, or the kind of node
 *  field (§8.3), each once (`summary` is already a PROVENANCE word), and
 *  `unknown` for a word outside the rest. Never a path. */
export const RECALL_SRCS = Object.freeze([...new Set([...PROVENANCE, 'node', 'summary', 'sidecar', 'unknown'])]);

/** Exit codes that carry a reason word: exactly the codes REASONS maps to. */
const REASON_EXITS = new Set(Object.values(REASONS));

// derived from lossless-claw src/assembler.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
export function escapeXmlAttr(value) {
  return value
    .replace(/&/g, '&amp;')
    .replace(/"/g, '&quot;')
    .replace(/</g, '&lt;')
    .replace(/>/g, '&gt;');
}

export function escapeXmlText(value) {
  return value
    .replace(/&/g, '&amp;')
    .replace(/</g, '&lt;')
    .replace(/>/g, '&gt;');
}

/** One recalled field in its untrusted envelope (§8.3, §11 P30): attributes
 *  and text XML-escaped, so a stored `</ccrc-recall>` cannot close it early.
 *  `ts` (ms) prints as ISO-8601 UTC, `''` when unknown; `role` likewise.
 *  `src` is a RECALL_SRCS word; anything else (a newer writer's provenance
 *  word, which the store's column does not CHECK) prints as `unknown`, so a
 *  stored value can neither put a path in the attribute nor fail the read. */
export function recallEnvelope({ src, id, ts, role, text }) {
  const word = RECALL_SRCS.includes(src) ? src : 'unknown';
  const when = typeof ts === 'number' && Number.isFinite(ts) && Math.abs(ts) <= 8.64e15 ? new Date(ts).toISOString() : '';
  return `<ccrc-recall src="${escapeXmlAttr(word)}" id="${escapeXmlAttr(String(id))}" ts="${escapeXmlAttr(when)}" `
    + `role="${escapeXmlAttr(role ?? '')}" trust="untrusted">${escapeXmlText(String(text))}</ccrc-recall>`;
}

// derived from lossless-claw src/tools/lcm-grep-tool.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
/** One grep hit as one line: newlines become spaces, and past `max` it is cut
 *  with `...` (upstream's truncateSnippet). */
export function snippetLine(text, max = SNIPPET_MAX) {
  const single = String(text).replace(/\n/g, ' ').trim();
  return single.length <= max ? single : `${single.slice(0, cutBefore(single, max - 3))}...`;
}

/** The output cap (§8.3, §11 P12): the rendered blocks, in order, while the
 *  running total (each block plus its newline) stays within `cap - reserve`;
 *  `reserve` holds room for the header and the `shown`/`next:` lines. The
 *  first block that does not fit ENDS the list: a later smaller block is not
 *  pulled forward, so the shown items are always a prefix of the ranked
 *  ones. No truncation marker is written into the output (§11 L10); the
 *  caller prints `shown K of N` with the TRUE count N, never the kept count.
 *  (Upstream's loop broke only its inner section and counted the post-LIMIT
 *  rows as the total.) */
export function capOutput(blocks, reserve, cap = OUTPUT_CAP) {
  const budget = cap - reserve;
  const kept = [];
  let used = 0;
  for (const block of blocks) {
    const cost = block.length + 1;
    if (used + cost > budget) break;
    kept.push(block);
    used += cost;
  }
  return { kept, shown: kept.length };
}

/** `shown K of N` (§8.3). K above N would be a lie about the count. */
export function shownLine(shown, total) {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(shown) || !Number.isSafeInteger(total) || shown < 0 || shown > total) {
    throw new TypeError(`shownLine: shown ${String(shown)} of ${String(total)} is not a count`);
  }
  return `shown ${shown} of ${total}`;
}

const SHELL_SAFE_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_./:=@%+,-]+$/;

/** The closing `next:` line (§8.3): the command that continues, by the
 *  literal path, each argument single-quoted unless it is plainly safe. The
 *  caller passes arguments it already redacted (C33). */
export function nextLine(args) {
  const quoted = args.map((a) => (SHELL_SAFE_RE.test(a) ? a : `'${String(a).replace(/'/g, "'\\''")}'`));
  return `next: ${HISTORY_CMD} ${quoted.join(' ')}`;
}

/** The header every read verb prints first (§8.3, D-4167):
 *  `scope=family(<id>, N transcripts)` or `scope=project|workspace(<p>, N families)`,
 *  then `coverage=this-box`, `indexed-through=<ISO>` and `lag=<s>s`, each
 *  `unmeasured` when no end-of-file tick backs it (never 0). The count words
 *  stay plural whatever N is, so the line keeps one grammar. */
export function headerLine(h) {
  if (!SCOPE_KINDS.includes(h.kind)) throw new TypeError(`headerLine: kind outside SCOPE_KINDS: ${String(h.kind)}`);
  const scope = h.kind === 'family'
    ? `family(${h.id}, ${h.transcripts} transcripts)`
    : `${h.kind}(${h.project}, ${h.families} families)`;
  const through = h.indexedThroughMs === null ? 'unmeasured' : new Date(h.indexedThroughMs).toISOString();
  const lag = h.lagS === null ? 'unmeasured' : `${h.lagS}s`;
  return `scope=${scope} coverage=${COVERAGE[0]} indexed-through=${through} lag=${lag}`;
}

/** The scope's lag (§8.3): now minus the OLDEST `ingest_files.eof_ms` among
 *  the files in scope, which is also `indexed-through`. Any file that has
 *  never reached its end, an empty scope, or a registered recovery step
 *  (§8.8: replay has not reached end-of-file) makes both unmeasured. */
export function scopeLag({ eofMs, nowMs, recovering }) {
  if (recovering || eofMs.length === 0) return { indexedThroughMs: null, lagS: null };
  let oldest = Infinity;
  for (const e of eofMs) {
    if (typeof e !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(e)) return { indexedThroughMs: null, lagS: null };
    if (e < oldest) oldest = e;
  }
  return { indexedThroughMs: oldest, lagS: Math.max(0, Math.floor((nowMs - oldest) / 1000)) };
}

/** A read verb's `--json` envelope (§8.3, §11 P11, D-4171,
 *  D-4169): one object, top-level `store_id` and
 *  `coverage`, every item stamped `trust:'untrusted'` (an item can never
 *  claim otherwise). A `reason` is present exactly when the exit is one
 *  REASONS maps to (2, 4, 5, 7), and it must be a word of THAT code; anything
 *  else throws, so no envelope can say two things at once. */
export function readEnvelope(o) {
  if (!Object.values(EXIT).includes(o.exit)) throw new TypeError(`readEnvelope: ${String(o.exit)} is not an EXIT value`);
  if (REASON_EXITS.has(o.exit)) {
    if (typeof o.reason !== 'string' || !Object.hasOwn(REASONS, o.reason) || REASONS[o.reason] !== o.exit) {
      throw new TypeError(`readEnvelope: exit ${o.exit} needs a reason word of its own code, got ${String(o.reason)}`);
    }
  } else if (o.reason !== undefined) {
    throw new TypeError(`readEnvelope: exit ${o.exit} carries no reason, got ${String(o.reason)}`);
  }
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(o.shown) || !Number.isSafeInteger(o.total) || o.shown < 0 || o.shown > o.total) {
    throw new TypeError(`readEnvelope: shown ${String(o.shown)} of ${String(o.total)} is not a count`);
  }
  return {
    v: 1,
    exit: o.exit,
    ...(o.reason === undefined ? {} : { reason: o.reason }),
    store_id: o.storeId,
    coverage: COVERAGE[0],
    scope: o.scope,
    indexed_through_ms: o.header === null ? null : o.header.indexedThroughMs,
    lag_s: o.header === null ? null : o.header.lagS,
    items: o.items.map((item) => ({ ...item, trust: 'untrusted' })),
    shown: o.shown,
    total: o.total,
    next: o.next,
  };
}

/** The resources a `--cursor` pages (§8.4). */
export const CURSOR_RESOURCES = Object.freeze(['grep', 'describe', 'expand']);
const CURSOR_MAX = 2048;
const CURSOR_TEXT_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}$/;

function cursorValueOk(v, depth) {
  if (v === null) return true;
  if (typeof v === 'number') return Number.isSafeInteger(v);
  if (typeof v === 'string') return CURSOR_TEXT_RE.test(v);
  if (typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v) && depth < 1) return Object.values(v).every((x) => cursorValueOk(x, depth + 1));
  return false;
}

function cursorShapeOk(c) {
  return c !== null && typeof c === 'object' && !Array.isArray(c) && c.v === 1 && CURSOR_RESOURCES.includes(c.resource)
    && Object.entries(c).every(([k, x]) => k === 'v' || k === 'resource' || cursorValueOk(x, 0));
}

// derived from lossless-claw src/cli/args.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
/** An opaque, versioned, URL-safe cursor (§8.4 `--cursor`): base64url JSON
 *  holding `v: 1`, its resource, and ids, integers and nested objects of
 *  them ONLY, never recalled text, so a cursor echoed in a `next:` line
 *  carries nothing to redact. */
export function encodeCursor(c) {
  if (!cursorShapeOk(c)) throw new TypeError('encodeCursor: a cursor holds v: 1, a CURSOR_RESOURCES word, and ids or integers only');
  const s = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(c), 'utf8').toString('base64url');
  if (s.length > CURSOR_MAX) throw new TypeError(`encodeCursor: ${s.length} characters, over ${CURSOR_MAX}`);
  return s;
}

/** The cursor back, or null (the CLI answers exit 2 `bad-args`) when it does
 *  not decode, names another resource, or holds anything but ids. */
export function decodeCursor(s, resource) {
  if (typeof s !== 'string' || s.length === 0 || s.length > CURSOR_MAX || !/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/.test(s)) return null;
  let c;
  try {
    c = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(s, 'base64url').toString('utf8'));
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
  return cursorShapeOk(c) && c.resource === resource ? c : null;
}

/** The CLI's answer for a writing form it ran through the shim (§8.4, O54's
 *  relay half, D-4221): the shim's exit 75 (lock held) is
 *  exit 4 `writer-busy`; otherwise the LAST stdout line must be exactly
 *  `{"rc":n}` or `{"rc":n,"reason":w}`, n an EXIT value equal to the process
 *  status, w present exactly when n carries reasons and of n's own code.
 *  A signal, a missing or malformed line, or any disagreement is exit 1:
 *  the CLI never reports a result the sweep did not state. */
export function decideRelay({ status, signal, lastLine }) {
  const internal = { exit: EXIT.INTERNAL };
  if (signal !== null) return internal;
  if (status === SHIM_LOCK_HELD) return { exit: EXIT.WRITER_BUSY, reason: 'writer-busy' };
  if (typeof lastLine !== 'string') return internal;
  let r;
  try {
    r = JSON.parse(lastLine);
  } catch {
    return internal;
  }
  if (r === null || typeof r !== 'object' || Array.isArray(r)) return internal;
  const keys = Object.keys(r).sort().join(',');
  if (keys !== 'rc' && keys !== 'rc,reason') return internal;
  if (!Object.values(EXIT).includes(r.rc) || r.rc !== status) return internal;
  if (REASON_EXITS.has(r.rc)) {
    return typeof r.reason === 'string' && Object.hasOwn(REASONS, r.reason) && REASONS[r.reason] === r.rc
      ? { exit: r.rc, reason: r.reason }
      : internal;
  }
  return r.reason === undefined ? { exit: r.rc } : internal;
}

// derived from lossless-claw src/large-files.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
const EXPLORE_CODE_EXTENSIONS = new Set([
  'c', 'cc', 'cpp', 'cs', 'go', 'h', 'hpp', 'java', 'js', 'jsx', 'kt', 'm', 'php', 'py', 'rb', 'rs', 'scala',
  'sh', 'sql', 'swift', 'ts', 'tsx',
]);

/** Claude Code's Read prefix, `<spaces><n>→` (or a tab in older versions). */
const READ_PREFIX_RE = /^\s*(\d+)(?:→|\t)/;

/** The text without Claude Code's Read line numbers (§8.4, refuted
 *  candidate 3: raw, the code outline finds 0 imports where it finds 27
 *  after stripping). Only a leading run of consecutively numbered lines is
 *  stripped, one prefix each; anything after it (a reminder Claude Code
 *  appended) is kept as it is, and text whose first line has no prefix is
 *  returned unchanged. */
export function stripReadPrefix(text) {
  const lines = String(text).split('\n');
  let prev = null;
  let k = 0;
  for (; k < lines.length; k += 1) {
    const m = READ_PREFIX_RE.exec(lines[k]);
    if (m === null || (prev !== null && Number(m[1]) !== prev + 1)) break;
    prev = Number(m[1]);
    lines[k] = lines[k].slice(m[0].length);
  }
  return k === 0 ? String(text) : lines.join('\n');
}

function fileNameExtension(fileName) {
  if (typeof fileName !== 'string' || fileName === '') return undefined;
  const base = fileName.trim().split(/[\\/]/).pop() ?? '';
  const idx = base.lastIndexOf('.');
  if (idx <= 0 || idx === base.length - 1) return undefined;
  const ext = base.slice(idx + 1).toLowerCase();
  return /^[a-z0-9]{1,10}$/.test(ext) ? ext : undefined;
}

/** Which explorer a tool output gets, from the paired tool_use's file path
 *  (§8.4): a Claude Code transcript carries no MIME type. */
export function exploreKindOf(path) {
  const ext = fileNameExtension(path);
  if (ext === 'json' || ext === 'csv' || ext === 'tsv') return ext;
  return ext !== undefined && EXPLORE_CODE_EXTENSIONS.has(ext) ? 'code' : null;
}

function normalizeTextForLine(text, maxLen) {
  const compact = text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
  if (compact.length <= maxLen) return compact;
  return `${compact.slice(0, cutBefore(compact, maxLen))}...`;
}

function uniqueOrdered(values) {
  const seen = new Set();
  const out = [];
  for (const value of values) {
    if (!seen.has(value)) {
      seen.add(value);
      out.push(value);
    }
  }
  return out;
}

function exploreJson(content) {
  const parsed = JSON.parse(content);
  const describe = (value, depth = 0) => {
    if (depth >= 2) return '...';
    if (Array.isArray(value)) {
      const sample = value.slice(0, 3).map((item) => describe(item, depth + 1));
      return `array(len=${value.length}${sample.length > 0 ? `, sample=[${sample.join(', ')}]` : ''})`;
    }
    if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return typeof value;
    const keys = Object.keys(value);
    const preview = keys.slice(0, 10).join(', ');
    return `object(keys=${keys.length}${preview ? `: ${preview}` : ''})`;
  };
  const topLevel = Array.isArray(parsed) ? 'array' : typeof parsed;
  return ['Structured summary (JSON):', `Top-level type: ${topLevel}.`, `Shape: ${describe(parsed)}.`].join('\n');
}

function parseDelimitedLine(line, delimiter) {
  return line.split(delimiter).map((item) => item.trim()).filter((item) => item.length > 0);
}

function exploreDelimited(content, delimiter, kind) {
  const lines = content.split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => line.trim()).filter((line) => line.length > 0);
  if (lines.length === 0) return `Structured summary (${kind}): no rows found.`;
  const headers = parseDelimitedLine(lines[0], delimiter);
  const rowCount = Math.max(0, lines.length - 1);
  const firstData = lines[1] ? normalizeTextForLine(lines[1], 180) : '(no data rows)';
  return [
    `Structured summary (${kind}):`,
    `Rows: ${rowCount.toLocaleString('en-US')}.`,
    `Columns (${headers.length}): ${headers.join(', ') || '(none detected)'}.`,
    `First row sample: ${firstData}.`,
  ].join('\n');
}

function exploreCode(content, fileName) {
  const lines = content.split(/\r?\n/);
  const imports = uniqueOrdered(
    lines
      .filter((line) => /^\s*(import\s+|from\s+\S+\s+import\s+|const\s+\w+\s*=\s*require\()/.test(line))
      .map((line) => normalizeTextForLine(line, 180))
      .slice(0, 12),
  );
  const signatures = uniqueOrdered(
    lines
      .map((line) => line.trim())
      .filter((line) => /^(export\s+)?(async\s+)?(function|class|interface|type|const\s+\w+\s*=\s*\(|def\s+\w+\(|struct\s+\w+)/.test(line))
      .map((line) => normalizeTextForLine(line, 200))
      .slice(0, 24),
  );
  return [
    `Code exploration summary${fileName ? ` (${fileName})` : ''}:`,
    `Lines: ${lines.length.toLocaleString('en-US')}.`,
    `Imports/dependencies (${imports.length}): ${imports.join(' | ') || 'none detected'}.`,
    `Top-level definitions (${signatures.length}): ${signatures.join(' | ') || 'none detected'}.`,
  ].join('\n');
}

function exploreCounts(content) {
  return [
    'Structured summary:',
    `Characters: ${content.length.toLocaleString('en-US')}.`,
    `Lines: ${content.split(/\r?\n/).length.toLocaleString('en-US')}.`,
  ].join('\n');
}

/** The deterministic summary beside an output `expand` cut to EXPLORE_CUT
 *  (§8.4, §11 P17): JSON keys, CSV or TSV columns, or a code outline, each
 *  taken after the Read prefix is stripped. JSON longer than
 *  EXPLORE_JSON_MAX, or that does not parse, gets counts instead. The text is
 *  the REDACTED full output; the caller escapes the result. */
export function explore(text, kind, fileName) {
  const content = stripReadPrefix(String(text));
  switch (kind) {
    case 'json':
      if (content.length > EXPLORE_JSON_MAX) return exploreCounts(content);
      try {
        return exploreJson(content);
      } catch {
        return 'Structured summary (JSON): failed to parse as valid JSON.';
      }
    case 'csv':
      return exploreDelimited(content, ',', 'CSV');
    case 'tsv':
      return exploreDelimited(content, '\t', 'TSV');
    case 'code':
      return exploreCode(content, fileName);
    default:
      throw new TypeError(`explore: kind outside json, csv, tsv and code: ${String(kind)}`);
  }
}

/** One child or source line's cost in `describe` (§8.4, §11 P13): its size in
 *  characters, and whether it fits one call's output cap. */
export function costRow(chars, cap = OUTPUT_CAP) {
  return { chars, fits: chars <= cap ? 'in' : 'over' };
}

/** Which body `expand` prints for an entry with variants (§6.1,
 *  D-4200, DM2b): when a variant marked `ccd-sanitize`
 *  really has ccd's sanitiser shape against the primary (variantCauseOf
 *  re-checks it, so a mislabelled row changes nothing), the body WITHOUT the
 *  `...` fill, the one the session actually wrote; otherwise the primary. */
export function pickExpandBody({ primary, variants }) {
  for (const v of variants) {
    if (v.cause !== 'ccd-sanitize' || variantCauseOf(primary, v.body) !== 'ccd-sanitize') continue;
    return sanitizedSideOf(primary, v.body) === 'a' ? v.body : primary;
  }
  return primary;
}

/** Which of two bodies of ccd's sanitiser shape carries the `...` fill. */
function sanitizedSideOf(a, b) {
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i += 1) {
    if (canonicalJson(a[i]) === canonicalJson(b[i])) continue;
    return a[i] !== null && typeof a[i] === 'object' && a[i].text === '...' ? 'a' : 'b';
  }
  return 'b';
}
```

`READ_PREFIX_RE` holds the single character U+2192 (`→`), written as itself. The explorers' regular expressions name `import`, `from` and `require` only as escaped regex text (`import\s+`, `require\(`), which B1's `lib.mjs is L1` ring case does not read as an import: it matches `import(`, `require(` and `from '…'` only.

Choices this task makes where the spec is silent (each is in the plan's open issues):
- The compact-card `export` keywords land here, not in Task 8: this task's tests inject the card's REAL heading rules, never a copy. Task 8 then imports them in `derive.mjs` and edits nothing in `compact-card.mjs`. Its Step 8A updates B1's ring census in `server/test/history-lib.test.ts` in the same commit: `RINGS` gains the one-line row `'derive.mjs'` (L4, forbidding `node:sqlite`, `./sweep.mjs` and `./cli.mjs`), and the `only L4 imports ../compact-card.mjs, and at most isBoundaryLine` case's blanket `{ isBoundaryLine }` check becomes the per-module table `CARD_FORMS` (`sweep.mjs`: `{ isBoundaryLine }`; `derive.mjs`: `{ HEADING_RE, fencedRanges, mineTokens }`; a module with no row takes nothing), the case renamed `only L4 imports ../compact-card.mjs, and only the forms CARD_FORMS names`, so the pin still refuses any other importer and any wider import. Without that step `every ccd/history/*.mjs has a ring` and the form pin go red the moment `derive.mjs` lands. Task 10 adds `recall.mjs`'s row and Task 14 `regex-worker.mjs`'s, each in the task that creates the file, with the `forbids` Global Constraints "Rings" spells; neither module imports the card, so `CARD_FORMS` keeps its two rows.
- Every `<analysis>` left in a STORED summary counts as surviving: Claude Code drops the first closed one before it stores the row (the card's `normalizeSummary` mirrors that), so what remains is the second, or one never closed.
- A key line is a lowercase `key:` at the start of a line, or `Expand for details about:`; another lowercase key starts a field that is ignored with its continuation lines, and a capitalised `Note: …` line continues the field above. The grammar needs one attribute after the tag name, so an id-less (generic) block carries one (`v="1"` in the fixtures); W3's generic template must print at least one.
- The native gist is `<Title>: <text>` per section, the two joined by a newline, each section's whitespace collapsed; topics are the list items (`-`, `*`, `+`) of the LAST sections numbered 2 and 3, compared by their collapsed text.
- When the direction names a pair the text does not hold, the other pair is used; with no direction and both pairs held, the pair whose heading comes later wins.
- The body's end: §7.4 item 8 names no close, so a `</summary>` ends the body only when it is the LAST one after the last `<summary>` open and comes after the last heading there. A close quoted inside a section's text is content, so a summary that quotes the tags (a session working on the card's `normalizeSummary` does) keeps its gist and topics, and a block after a real close stays out of the gist. One limit stays: an open quoted in a tag-less summary still moves the body's start past it (the spec's "after the last `<summary>` open"), so sections before it give no topics.
- Headings are the `HEADING_RE` matches at the smallest indentation seen (D-4686 (`history-native-gist-heading-indent-floor`)): an indented numbered list nested under a section (Pending Tasks' `   1. …`, a Current Work step list) is that section's text. A nested list at column 0 is still read as headings, as the card reads it. The rule "a number above the current section's starts a section" was rejected: an 8-item list under section 7 would make a false `8.` and lose Current Work.
- `gistSha` hashes the form the store keeps (trimmed, capped at `GIST_MAX` by `capText`, trailing whitespace dropped), so a carried copy of an over-cap gist is still caught; the derivation (Task 8) hashes the session's earlier stored gists with `gistSha` itself and counts `carried_copies` from `blockStatus`'s `reason`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the mutation runner.** It is a gitignored scratch tool (`.superpowers/` is in `.gitignore`), never committed. It is the ONE runner of the B2 tasks that measure guards with a mutants file: Tasks 1–7, 7A, 7B and 8 write this same file, byte for byte (Task 5 writes it at its Step 8), so each task stands alone and rewriting it changes nothing. It runs vitest with `maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024` (Tasks 7A and 7B carry cases over large strings, coordinator ruling R-runner). A mutant is `{name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}`, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. For each mutant the runner copies the pristine file to `.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/`, applies the edits and runs the named tests, which must fail; it then restores the file from the copy, removes the copy, and runs the same tests again, which must pass. Every exit the runner sees restores. Only a kill no handler sees (SIGKILL, a tool timeout that escalates) leaves a copy in `scratch/keep/`; the next run then refuses, and the runner's header gives the one-line restore. From the repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <<'EOF'
// .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs: measures each guard RED with it mutated, then GREEN with
// it restored (the B2 plan's mutation-pin rule). Run from server/, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least
// 600000 ms:
//   node ../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <mutants.json>
// A mutant is {name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}. `file` is repo-relative, `test` is
// server/-relative, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. The
// pristine file is copied to scratch/keep/<file with '/' as '__'>.orig BEFORE it is touched, and the copy is
// removed only after the file is restored from it. A kill no handler sees therefore leaves the original findable,
// and the next run REFUSES while any copy is left. To restore by hand, from the repository root:
//   for f in .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/*.orig; do t="$(basename "$f" .orig)"; cp "$f" "${t//__//}" && rm "$f"; done
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const KEEP = '../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep';
mkdirSync(KEEP, { recursive: true });
const left = readdirSync(KEEP).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.orig'));
if (left.length > 0) {
  console.log(`REFUSED: ${left.join(', ')} in ${KEEP}. An earlier run was interrupted and a source may hold a mutant: restore as this file's header says.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const keepOf = (file) => `${KEEP}/${file.replaceAll('/', '__')}.orig`;
const restoreAll = () => {
  for (const n of readdirSync(KEEP)) {
    if (!n.endsWith('.orig')) continue;
    copyFileSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`, `../${n.slice(0, -'.orig'.length).replaceAll('__', '/')}`);
    rmSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`);
  }
};
// Every way out restores: the loop's end, process.exit and an uncaught throw all emit 'exit', and a signal is
// turned into an exit. A signal sent while the synchronous loop holds the thread is handled after the current
// child returns; a Ctrl-C also reaches the vitest child, and the loop stops on the child's signal below.
process.on('exit', restoreAll);
for (const s of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) process.on(s, () => process.exit(130));
// maxBuffer: past Node's default (1 MiB) spawnSync kills the child (ENOBUFS, signal SIGTERM, measured), which the
// loop below reads as an interrupt. Each large-operand case asserts a boolean or a length, so a red prints no big diff.
const vitest = (test, filter) => spawnSync('./node_modules/.bin/vitest', ['run', test, '-t', filter], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 });
const mutants = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
let bad = 0;
for (const m of mutants) {
  const target = `../${m.file}`;
  if (!existsSync(target)) { console.log(`NO SUCH FILE       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  const keep = keepOf(m.file);
  copyFileSync(target, keep);
  let src = readFileSync(keep, 'utf8');
  let unique = true;
  for (const e of m.edits) {
    const at = src.indexOf(e.anchor);
    if (at < 0 || src.indexOf(e.anchor, at + 1) >= 0) { unique = false; break; }
    src = src.slice(0, at) + e.replacement + src.slice(at + e.anchor.length);
  }
  if (!unique) { rmSync(keep); console.log(`ANCHOR NOT UNIQUE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  writeFileSync(target, src);
  const red = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  copyFileSync(keep, target);
  rmSync(keep);
  if (red.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${red.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  const failed = /Tests\s+(\d+) failed/.exec(red.stdout)?.[1] ?? '?';
  if (red.status === 0) { console.log(`STAYED GREEN       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`red (${failed} failed)   ${m.name}`);
  const green = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  if (green.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${green.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  if (green.status !== 0) { console.log(`RED AFTER RESTORE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`green              ${m.name}`);
}
console.log(bad === 0 ? 'every guard measured red, then green' : `${bad} guard(s) not measured`);
process.exit(bad === 0 ? 0 : 1);
EOF
```

```ts

// --- W1-B2 Task 4: summary text and steered blocks (spec 2026-10-05 §7.4) ---
/** The sections of Claude Code's full (and partial `from`) compaction prompt,
 *  and of its partial `up_to` prompt. MEASURED: the last two titles of each
 *  (spec §7.4 item 8, from the prompt text); the others are fixture-chosen. */
export const FULL_SECTIONS = [
  'Primary Request and Intent', 'Key Technical Concepts', 'Files and Code Sections', 'Errors and fixes',
  'Problem Solving', 'All user messages', 'Pending Tasks', 'Current Work', 'Optional Next Step',
] as const;
export const UP_TO_SECTIONS = [
  'Primary Request and Intent', 'Key Technical Concepts', 'Files and Code Sections', 'Errors and fixes',
  'Problem Solving', 'All user messages', 'Work Completed', 'Context for Continuing Work',
] as const;

export interface SummaryTextOpts {
  /** Section titles in order, numbered from 1; FULL_SECTIONS when omitted. */
  sections?: readonly string[];
  /** A section's text by title; `- fixture point for <title>` when omitted. */
  body?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  /** `8. Current Work:` (plain), `## 8. Current Work` (hash) or `**8. Current Work:**` (bold). */
  style?: 'plain' | 'hash' | 'bold';
  /** No tags (a stored Claude-run summary), `<summary>…</summary>`, or an open never closed. */
  wrap?: 'none' | 'closed' | 'unclosed';
  before?: string;
  after?: string;
}

/** A summary row's text in the nine-section shape the native gist reads. */
export const summaryText = (o: SummaryTextOpts = {}): string => {
  const heading = (n: number, t: string): string =>
    (o.style === 'hash' ? `## ${n}. ${t}` : o.style === 'bold' ? `**${n}. ${t}:**` : `${n}. ${t}:`);
  const text = (o.sections ?? FULL_SECTIONS)
    .map((t, k) => `${heading(k + 1, t)}\n${o.body?.[t] ?? `- fixture point for ${t.toLowerCase()}`}\n`)
    .join('\n');
  const wrapped = o.wrap === 'closed' ? `<summary>\n${text}</summary>\n` : o.wrap === 'unclosed' ? `<summary>\n${text}` : text;
  return `${o.before ?? ''}${wrapped}${o.after ?? ''}`;
};

/** A steered `<ccrc-leaf|node>` block as W3's template asks for it (spec §7.4
 *  item 3). An id-less block carries `v="1"`, because the grammar needs one
 *  attribute after the tag name. */
export const steeredBlock = (o: {
  kind?: 'leaf' | 'node'; id?: string; gist: string; expand?: string; refs?: string | null; extra?: string;
}): string => {
  const kind = o.kind ?? 'leaf';
  return [
    `<ccrc-${kind} ${o.id === undefined ? 'v="1"' : `id="${o.id}"`}>`,
    `gist: ${o.gist}`,
    ...(o.expand === undefined ? [] : [`Expand for details about: ${o.expand}`]),
    ...(o.refs === undefined || o.refs === null ? [] : [`refs: ${o.refs}`]),
    ...(o.extra === undefined ? [] : [o.extra]),
    `</ccrc-${kind}>`,
  ].join('\n');
};
```
