- [ ] **Step 5: Implement them.** Append to the end of `ccd/history/lib.mjs`:

```js

// ===========================================================================
// Spans, leaf ids, readiness, fan-in and parent rollups (spec §6.1 "Span
// rule: an exact partition" and "Two forks after one head"; §6.3; W1-B2
// Task 5). Pure: derive.mjs (L4) reads ONE copy's rows in file order
// (memberships.line, a byte offset) with its boundaries' metadata and hands
// them in; nothing here reads the store. D-4687 (history-span-exact-partition)
// D-4688 (history-span-per-boundary-copy) D-4689 (history-leaf-id-fork-qualified)
// ===========================================================================

/** The leaves one copy's boundaries make, and its live tail (§6.1).
 *  `rows` are the copy's stored rows in any order: they are sorted by `pos`, the row's byte offset in that copy.
 *  `boundaries` are the SAME copy's boundary rows, each with:
 *  - `headUuid` (preservedSegment.headUuid);
 *  - `kept` (the members of preservedMessages.allUuids; a member absent from the copy is never tested);
 *  - `summaryUuid` (the summary row the parser chose, or null).
 *  Leaf N covers [head(N-1), boundary(N)), an epoch's first leaf from the copy's first row, minus:
 *  - boundary and summary rows;
 *  - the rows of [head(N-1), boundary(N-1)) absent from kept(N-1). Leaf N-1 claimed them: compaction N-1
 *    summarised them although they sit after its head (G12, ruled Q5);
 *  - the rows of [head(N), boundary(N)) in kept(N). Compaction N kept them verbatim: they belong to leaf N+1.
 *  The live tail is what no leaf covers yet: the last compaction's kept rows and every row after it.
 *  logicalParentUuid is never an input: it names the preserved tail's END (§6.1, M). A head absent from the copy
 *  (or, against every measurement, after its boundary) makes the boundary itself the edge, flagged `headMissing`,
 *  and the leaf's span start still names head(N-1): ids never change. */
export function planSpans({ rows, boundaries }) {
  const order = [...rows].sort((a, b) => a.pos - b.pos);
  const at = new Map(order.map((r, i) => [r.uuid, i]));
  const summaries = new Set(boundaries.map((b) => b.summaryUuid).filter((u) => typeof u === 'string'));
  const structural = (r) => r.isBoundary || r.isSummary || summaries.has(r.uuid);
  const bs = boundaries.filter((b) => at.has(b.uuid)).sort((x, y) => at.get(x.uuid) - at.get(y.uuid));
  // A boundary's preserved-tail window [head, boundary), or null when its head is not before it in this copy.
  const windowOf = (b) => {
    const to = at.get(b.uuid);
    const from = typeof b.headUuid === 'string' ? at.get(b.headUuid) : undefined;
    return from === undefined || from > to ? null : { from, to };
  };
  const leaves = [];
  for (let k = 0; k < bs.length; k += 1) {
    const b = bs[k];
    const prev = k === 0 ? null : bs[k - 1];
    const prevWin = prev === null ? null : windowOf(prev);
    const own = windowOf(b);
    // Leaf N starts at head(N-1): the rows compaction N-1 kept verbatim are its own.
    const start = prev === null ? 0 : prevWin === null ? at.get(prev.uuid) : prevWin.from;
    const sources = [];
    for (let i = start; i < at.get(b.uuid); i += 1) {
      const r = order[i];
      if (structural(r)) continue;
      // Leaf N-1 claimed these (G12).
      if (prevWin !== null && i < prevWin.to && !prev.kept.has(r.uuid)) continue;
      // Compaction N keeps these verbatim: leaf N+1's.
      if (own !== null && i >= own.from && b.kept.has(r.uuid)) continue;
      sources.push(r.uuid);
    }
    leaves.push({
      boundaryUuid: b.uuid,
      spanStartUuid: prev === null ? order[0].uuid : (prev.headUuid ?? prev.uuid),
      sources,
      headMissing: prev !== null && prevWin === null,
    });
  }
  const last = bs.length === 0 ? null : bs[bs.length - 1];
  const lastWin = last === null ? null : windowOf(last);
  const tailFrom = last === null ? 0 : lastWin === null ? at.get(last.uuid) + 1 : lastWin.from;
  const liveTail = [];
  for (let i = tailFrom; i < order.length; i += 1) {
    const r = order[i];
    if (structural(r)) continue;
    if (lastWin !== null && i < lastWin.to && !last.kept.has(r.uuid)) continue;
    liveTail.push(r.uuid);
  }
  return { leaves, liveTail };
}

/** A leaf's id (§6.1 "Two forks after one head"). The plain id hashes (ccrc id, cc uuid, span start). When that
 *  id is already bound to ANOTHER boundary (two forked copies each compacted after the same head), the first bound
 *  keeps it, as "the first claim stands" does for uuids, and this boundary's leaf takes the boundary-qualified id
 *  (`leaf_id_forked`). */
export function decideLeafId({ ccrcId, ccUuid, spanStartUuid, boundaryUuid, plainBoundOther }) {
  if (plainBoundOther) return { id: leafId(ccrcId, ccUuid, spanStartUuid, boundaryUuid), forked: true };
  return { id: leafId(ccrcId, ccUuid, spanStartUuid), forked: false };
}

/** How long after a boundary's own time a file read to its end proves the boundary has no summary row coming.
 *  Claude Code appends the summary within moments of the boundary; a tick that read in between must not make
 *  the leaf raw for good. *Chosen*. D-4690 (history-raw-leaf-grace) */
export const RAW_LEAF_GRACE_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;

/** Whether the file holding a boundary was read to its end late enough to say its summary row is missing. `eofMs`
 *  is the holding file's ingest_files.eof_ms: the start of the last tick that left its cursor at end-of-file.
 *  `boundaryTsMs` is the boundary's time; derive.mjs passes the newest stamped row before a boundary that has none
 *  of its own. With no time known at all the answer is false: end-of-file alone is exactly the race the grace
 *  closes, so such a boundary waits rather than going raw for good. */
export function eofAfterBoundary({ eofMs, boundaryTsMs }) {
  if (eofMs === null || boundaryTsMs === null) return false;
  return eofMs >= boundaryTsMs + RAW_LEAF_GRACE_MS;
}

/** A leaf is derived once it is final (§7.4 item 1, §6.3 "only leaves whose status is final"): its summary row is
 *  stored (native, or steered from W3), or its file shows it never will be (a raw leaf). Never earlier: a raw
 *  leaf is never written while it could still be a native one. */
export function leafReady({ summaryStored, fileAtEofAfterBoundary }) {
  return summaryStored === true || fileAtEofAfterBoundary === true;
}

/** The plugin's tested fan-in (§6.3, §11 P23; the 2 is a pressure arm ccrc has no consumer for): 8 leaves make a
 *  depth-1 parent, 4 nodes make each level above. */
export const FAN_IN = Object.freeze({ leaf: 8, condensed: 4 });

/** The groups of `width` slots that become parents now (§6.3). `slots` are ONE holding copy's nodes of one depth
 *  within one epoch, in boundaries.ord order (RB4): fan-in never crosses a /clear epoch and a parent never mixes
 *  forks. A slot is `nodeId: null` while its node does not exist yet (a boundary not ready), `final: false` while
 *  it may still change, `parented` once a parent holds it.
 *  Grouping starts at the first unparented slot and stops at the first group holding a null, non-final or
 *  parented slot: the nodes after a gap wait for it. */
export function planFanIn({ slots, width }) {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(width) || width < 2) throw new TypeError(`planFanIn: width must be an integer of at least 2, got ${String(width)}`);
  const groups = [];
  let i = slots.findIndex((s) => !s.parented);
  if (i < 0) return groups;
  while (i + width <= slots.length) {
    const g = slots.slice(i, i + width);
    if (g.some((s) => s.nodeId === null || !s.final || s.parented)) break;
    groups.push(g.map((s) => s.nodeId));
    i += width;
  }
  return groups;
}

/** A gist's first sentence (§6.3): up to and including the first `.`, `!` or `?` that ends the text or is
 *  followed by whitespace, else up to the first newline, else the whole gist; trimmed. So `v1.2` stays inside it. */
export function firstSentence(text) {
  const t = String(text ?? '').trim();
  const m = /[.!?](?=\s|$)|\n/.exec(t);
  if (m === null) return t;
  return t.slice(0, m[0] === '\n' ? m.index : m.index + 1).trim();
}

/** A parent from its children (§6.3), deterministic and rebuildable (a W3 steered <ccrc-node> gist replaces only
 *  the gist):
 *  - gist: each child's first sentence, joined with a space, cut at GIST_MAX by capText; null when no child has
 *    one (the leaves' own spelling of "no gist", never '');
 *  - topics: the union in first-seen order through capTopics (each once, at most TOPICS_MAX of at most TOPIC_CHARS);
 *  - refs: the union through capRefs (each (kind, value) once, the first origin kept, at most REFS_MAX);
 *  - time: the earliest child start to the latest child end;
 *  - srcChars: the children's; descCount: every descendant node; descChars: the descendants' gist chars.
 *  The three caps are Task 4's, the ones a leaf is cut by, so a parent and a leaf never disagree about a cut.
 *  A cut sets `capped`; no marker is ever inserted. D-4691 (history-node-char-counts) */
export function parentRollup(children) {
  const sentences = [];
  for (const c of children) {
    const s = typeof c.gist === 'string' ? firstSentence(c.gist) : '';
    if (s !== '') sentences.push(s);
  }
  const joined = sentences.join(' ');
  const gist = capText(joined, GIST_MAX);
  const topics = capTopics(children.flatMap((c) => c.topics));
  const cut = capRefs(children.flatMap((c) => c.refs));
  let earliestMs = null;
  let latestMs = null;
  let srcChars = 0;
  let descCount = 0;
  let descChars = 0;
  for (const c of children) {
    if (c.earliestMs !== null && (earliestMs === null || c.earliestMs < earliestMs)) earliestMs = c.earliestMs;
    if (c.latestMs !== null && (latestMs === null || c.latestMs > latestMs)) latestMs = c.latestMs;
    srcChars += c.srcChars;
    descCount += c.descCount + 1;
    descChars += c.descChars + (typeof c.gist === 'string' ? c.gist.length : 0);
  }
  return {
    gist: joined === '' ? null : gist.text, topics: topics.topics, refs: cut.refs, earliestMs, latestMs, srcChars, descCount, descChars,
    capped: gist.capped || topics.capped || cut.capped,
  };
}
```

  - `GIST_MAX`, `capText`, `capTopics` and `capRefs` are Task 4's declarations in the same module, and `cutBefore` (inside `capText`) is Task 2's. `leafId` is B1's. `parentRollup` spells no dedupe key of its own: `capRefs` is the one (kind, value) rule.

```ts
export interface SpanRow { readonly uuid: string; readonly pos: number; readonly isBoundary: boolean; readonly isSummary: boolean }
export interface SpanBoundary { readonly uuid: string; readonly headUuid: string | null; readonly kept: ReadonlySet<string>; readonly summaryUuid: string | null }

export const RAW_LEAF_GRACE_MS: number;

export const FAN_IN: Readonly<{ leaf: 8; condensed: 4 }>;
export interface FanInSlot { readonly nodeId: string | null; readonly final: boolean; readonly parented: boolean }
export function planFanIn(i: { slots: readonly FanInSlot[]; width: number }): string[][];
export function firstSentence(text: string): string;
export interface RollupChild {
  gist: string | null; topics: readonly string[]; refs: readonly { kind: string; value: string; origin: string }[];
  earliestMs: number | null; latestMs: number | null; srcChars: number; descCount: number; descChars: number;
}
export function parentRollup(children: readonly RollupChild[]): {
  gist: string | null; topics: string[]; refs: { kind: string; value: string; origin: string }[];

};
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Write the mutation runner.** It is a gitignored scratch tool at `.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs`. Tasks 1–7, 7A, 7B and 8 write this same file, byte for byte, so each task stands alone and rewriting it changes nothing. Like every copy, it spawns vitest with `maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024` (coordinator ruling R-runner). A mutant is `{name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}, …]}`, a list of exact edits. Its leftover check reads `scratch/keep/` only: a pristine copy any other tool leaves elsewhere is not its to find. From the repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <<'EOF'
// .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs: measures each guard RED with it mutated, then GREEN with
// it restored (the B2 plan's mutation-pin rule). Run from server/, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least
// 600000 ms:
//   node ../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <mutants.json>
// A mutant is {name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}. `file` is repo-relative, `test` is
// server/-relative, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. The
// pristine file is copied to scratch/keep/<file with '/' as '__'>.orig BEFORE it is touched, and the copy is
// removed only after the file is restored from it. A kill no handler sees therefore leaves the original findable,
// and the next run REFUSES while any copy is left. To restore by hand, from the repository root:
//   for f in .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/*.orig; do t="$(basename "$f" .orig)"; cp "$f" "${t//__//}" && rm "$f"; done
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const KEEP = '../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep';
mkdirSync(KEEP, { recursive: true });
const left = readdirSync(KEEP).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.orig'));
if (left.length > 0) {
  console.log(`REFUSED: ${left.join(', ')} in ${KEEP}. An earlier run was interrupted and a source may hold a mutant: restore as this file's header says.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const keepOf = (file) => `${KEEP}/${file.replaceAll('/', '__')}.orig`;
const restoreAll = () => {
  for (const n of readdirSync(KEEP)) {
    if (!n.endsWith('.orig')) continue;
    copyFileSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`, `../${n.slice(0, -'.orig'.length).replaceAll('__', '/')}`);
    rmSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`);
  }
};
// Every way out restores: the loop's end, process.exit and an uncaught throw all emit 'exit', and a signal is
// turned into an exit. A signal sent while the synchronous loop holds the thread is handled after the current
// child returns; a Ctrl-C also reaches the vitest child, and the loop stops on the child's signal below.
process.on('exit', restoreAll);
for (const s of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) process.on(s, () => process.exit(130));
// maxBuffer: past Node's default (1 MiB) spawnSync kills the child (ENOBUFS, signal SIGTERM, measured), which the
// loop below reads as an interrupt. Each large-operand case asserts a boolean or a length, so a red prints no big diff.
const vitest = (test, filter) => spawnSync('./node_modules/.bin/vitest', ['run', test, '-t', filter], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 });
const mutants = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
let bad = 0;
for (const m of mutants) {
  const target = `../${m.file}`;
  if (!existsSync(target)) { console.log(`NO SUCH FILE       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  const keep = keepOf(m.file);
  copyFileSync(target, keep);
  let src = readFileSync(keep, 'utf8');
  let unique = true;
  for (const e of m.edits) {
    const at = src.indexOf(e.anchor);
    if (at < 0 || src.indexOf(e.anchor, at + 1) >= 0) { unique = false; break; }
    src = src.slice(0, at) + e.replacement + src.slice(at + e.anchor.length);
  }
  if (!unique) { rmSync(keep); console.log(`ANCHOR NOT UNIQUE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  writeFileSync(target, src);
  const red = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  copyFileSync(keep, target);
  rmSync(keep);
  if (red.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${red.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  const failed = /Tests\s+(\d+) failed/.exec(red.stdout)?.[1] ?? '?';
  if (red.status === 0) { console.log(`STAYED GREEN       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`red (${failed} failed)   ${m.name}`);
  const green = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  if (green.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${green.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  if (green.status !== 0) { console.log(`RED AFTER RESTORE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`green              ${m.name}`);
}
console.log(bad === 0 ? 'every guard measured red, then green' : `${bad} guard(s) not measured`);
process.exit(bad === 0 ? 0 : 1);
EOF
```

**Spec:**
- §6.6: the prune floor (*chosen* 30 days), dry run by default.
- §6.9: the binding table, `store-unbound`, `store-recoverable`, `store-wal-orphaned`.
- §8.3: "Which no-store answer", the writing-verb row `writer-absent` ("never 9, because the store exists"), "an unreadable one answers 5 `store-unmeasured` … never read as absent".
- §8.4: the operator verbs; `doctor --adopt`, `--restore <file>` and `--rebuild [--store-id <uuid>]` preconditions; `reparse` limits.
- §11 P15: `parseDuration`, ported; §11 L8: reparse's preflight limit.
- No pin is owned whole here. This task ships the pure halves of DM21, DM22, C57, C58, C62 and C67, whose verb halves are Tasks 20, 21, 27, 28 and 10.

  - D-4693 (`history-restore-verb`)
  - D-4694 (`history-rebuild-verb`)
  - B1's D-4188 (`history-store-wal-orphaned`)
  - B1's D-4185 (`history-store-recoverable`)
  - D-4695 (`history-backup-preflight-and-rename`)
  - B1's D-4183 (`history-shim-role-gated`)
  - B1's D-4171 (`history-reasons-by-exit`)
  - D-4696 (`history-reasons-repair-backup`) (NEW): §8.3 names no exit-2 word for `doctor --repair` refused on `integrity_check` or on a new foreign-key violation, nor for `doctor --backup` refused for room. Each is a refusal with nothing written, so each gets a word of its own at exit 2.
  - D-4697 (`history-reparse-targets`) (NEW): §8.4 sets reparse's limit, not its target grammar. `--node <full id>` (a leaf, or a parent's leaves), `--session <id>` (that id's leaves) or neither (every leaf).
  - D-4698 (`history-ops-refused-while-recovering`) (NEW; coordinator rulings RB6 and RB12-RB14, confirmed by RB16): §9.14 says drain and ingest wait and cursors do not move while a recovery step runs, but names no rule for the operator's own writing verbs. While a `('recover', ms)` step is registered, the writing `--op` forms (`import --apply`, `prune --apply`, `reparse --apply`, `doctor --repair|--backup|--adopt|--migrate`) are refused exit 2 `recovering`, decided in `decideOpGate`, authoritative in its sweep half. `restore` and `rebuild` replace the registered step and are never refused; W2's `recall-off` forms are exempt (RB12); `--migrate` is refused only while the stored `user_version` equals the code's (RB13); `--adopt` is exempt on an unbound store, `store.id` absent (RB14). Dry runs and read verbs still answer.

Rulings this task applies (coordinator, 2026-10-06):
- **RB12.** W2's `recall-off` and `recall-off-clear-all` forms are not refused `recovering`: a privacy switch moves no cursor. B2 refuses them `bad-args` anyway (`parseOpVerbArgs`), and W2's rows inherit the exemption.
- **RB13.** `doctor --migrate` is refused `recovering` only when the stored `user_version` already equals the code's. A restored backup older than the code (a `pre-v<N>.db`) would otherwise wait on its own recovery step, which runs only at the code's version, while the step waits on the migration.
- **RB14.** `doctor --adopt` is exempt on an unbound store (`store.id` absent). The scheduled pass refuses such a store `store-unbound`, so its step could never run until something binds it.
- **RB17.** Adopt's newer-schema refusal is `decideBind`'s (L1), over the stored version as a fact; Task 26's `adoptArm` (L4) only measures and relays.

Choices this task makes where the rulings are silent (listed in the PR body):
- An unmeasured fact never exempts. A stored version that is absent or unreadable, a missing code version, or a `store.id` that is unreadable rather than absent keeps the `recovering` refusal, because IV5 never reads unmeasured as absent or as a value. Such a store would fail migrate's or adopt's own open anyway.

```ts
  /** RB6 allows restore and rebuild (they replace the step); RB12 exempts W2's recall-off forms. */
  const ALLOWED = ['restore', 'rebuild', 'recall-off', 'recall-off-clear-all'];
  const recovering = { claudecode: false, historyOff: false, recovering: true };
  const S = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000e1';
  const ver = (value: number): libOps.Presence<number> => ({ state: 'value', value });
  const sid = (value: string): libOps.Presence<string> => ({ state: 'value', value });
  const absent = { state: 'absent' } as const;
  const unreadable = { state: 'unreadable' } as const;
  const refusedRecovering = { ok: false, rc: 2, reason: 'recovering' };

  it('CONTROL: the two lists cover every WRITING_FORMS key exactly once', () => {
    expect([...REFUSED, ...ALLOWED].sort()).toEqual(Object.keys(FORMS).sort());
  });
  it('each RB6 form answers recovering; restore, rebuild and the recall-off forms (RB12) pass; a dry run passes', () => {
    for (const f of REFUSED) expect(libOps.decideOpGate(f, recovering, true, null), f).toEqual(refusedRecovering);
    for (const f of ALLOWED) expect(libOps.decideOpGate(f, recovering, true, null), f).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(libOps.decideOpGate(null, recovering, false, 'cc-demo-quiet-basin')).toEqual({ ok: true });
  });
  it("RB13: migrate is refused only while the stored user_version equals the code's; an older or a newer store passes; an unmeasured version keeps the refusal", () => {
    // codeVersion null builds an env with NO codeVersion key ("not measured"); undefined would select the default 2.
    const at = (storedVersion: libOps.Presence<number> | undefined, codeVersion: number | null = 2) => ({ ...recovering, storedVersion, ...(codeVersion === null ? {} : { codeVersion }) });
    expect(libOps.decideOpGate('migrate', at(ver(2)), true, null), 'stored = code').toEqual(refusedRecovering);
    expect(libOps.decideOpGate('migrate', at(ver(1)), true, null), 'a restored older backup').toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(libOps.decideOpGate('migrate', at(ver(3)), true, null), 'newer: openStore answers it, not this row').toEqual({ ok: true });
    for (const sv of [unreadable, absent, undefined]) {
      expect(libOps.decideOpGate('migrate', at(sv), true, null), `storedVersion ${JSON.stringify(sv)}`).toEqual(refusedRecovering);
    }
    expect(libOps.decideOpGate('migrate', at(ver(1), null), true, null), 'no code version measured').toEqual(refusedRecovering);
    // The version facts exempt migrate alone.
    for (const f of REFUSED.filter((x) => x !== 'migrate')) expect(libOps.decideOpGate(f, at(ver(1)), true, null), f).toEqual(refusedRecovering);
  });
  it('RB14: adopt is exempt only on an unbound store (store.id absent); a store.id present, unreadable or unmeasured keeps the refusal', () => {
    const with_ = (storeId: libOps.Presence<string> | undefined) => ({ ...recovering, storeId });
    expect(libOps.decideOpGate('adopt', with_(absent), true, null), 'unbound').toEqual({ ok: true });
    for (const p of [sid(S), unreadable, undefined]) {
      expect(libOps.decideOpGate('adopt', with_(p), true, null), `storeId ${JSON.stringify(p)}`).toEqual(refusedRecovering);
    }
    // store.id absent exempts adopt alone.
    for (const f of REFUSED.filter((x) => x !== 'adopt')) expect(libOps.decideOpGate(f, with_(absent), true, null), f).toEqual(refusedRecovering);
    // The exemption sits after B1's bumps: adopt still needs a TTY and refuses a cc- pane.
    expect(libOps.decideOpGate('adopt', with_(absent), false, null)).toEqual({ ok: false, rc: 2, reason: 'needs-tty' });
    expect(libOps.decideOpGate('adopt', with_(absent), true, 'cc-demo-quiet-basin')).toEqual({ ok: false, rc: 2, reason: 'irreversible-in-pane' });
  });
  it("B1's bumps still answer first: CLAUDECODE, the TTY, a cc- pane, history-off", () => {
    expect(libOps.decideOpGate('repair', { ...recovering, claudecode: true }, true, null)).toEqual({ ok: false, rc: 2, reason: 'apply-in-session' });
    expect(libOps.decideOpGate('repair', recovering, false, null)).toEqual({ ok: false, rc: 2, reason: 'needs-tty' });
    expect(libOps.decideOpGate('repair', recovering, true, 'cc-demo-quiet-basin')).toEqual({ ok: false, rc: 2, reason: 'irreversible-in-pane' });
    expect(libOps.decideOpGate('backup', { ...recovering, historyOff: true }, true, null)).toEqual({ ok: false, rc: 2, reason: 'history-off' });
  });
  it('recovering absent (the CLI half) or false refuses nothing new', () => {
    for (const f of REFUSED) {
      expect(libOps.decideOpGate(f, { claudecode: false, historyOff: false }, true, null), f).toEqual({ ok: true });
      expect(libOps.decideOpGate(f, { claudecode: false, historyOff: false, recovering: false }, true, null), f).toEqual({ ok: true });
    }
  });
});

describe("parseOpVerbArgs: each verb's argv, decided once for both doors (spec 8.4)", () => {
  const ok = (op: string, args: string[]): libOps.OpArgs => {
    const r = libOps.parseOpVerbArgs(op, args);
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`${op} ${args.join(' ')}: ${r.reason}`);
    return r.args;
  };
  const why = (op: string, args: string[]): string => {
    const r = libOps.parseOpVerbArgs(op, args);
    return r.ok ? 'ok' : r.reason;
  };
  const FILE = '/home/u/.claude/projects/-home-u-worktrees-p-quiet-basin/0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-000000000001.jsonl';

  it("import keeps B1's grammar: --apply, and --session with --file, both or neither", () => {
    expect(ok('import', [])).toEqual({ op: 'import', apply: false, session: null, file: null });
    expect(ok('import', ['--apply'])).toEqual({ op: 'import', apply: true, session: null, file: null });
    expect(ok('import', ['--session', 'claude-demo', '--file', FILE, '--apply'])).toEqual({ op: 'import', apply: true, session: 'claude-demo', file: FILE });
    expect(why('import', ['--session', 'claude-demo'])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('import', ['--apply', '--apply'])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('import', ['stray'])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('import', ['--session'])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('import', ['--session', '../x', '--file', FILE])).toBe('bad-id');
    expect(why('import', ['--session', 'claude-demo', '--file', '/home/u/notes.txt'])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('import', ['--session', 'claude-demo', '--file', '/home/u/x/not-a-uuid.jsonl'])).toBe('bad-args');
  });

  it('migrate, repair, backup and adopt take no arguments', () => {
    for (const op of ['migrate', 'repair', 'backup', 'adopt']) {
      expect(ok(op, []), op).toEqual({ op });
      expect(why(op, ['--apply']), op).toBe('bad-args');
    }
  });

  it('prune needs --older-than; under 30 days is older-than-floor (DM22 pure half)', () => {
    expect(ok('prune', ['--older-than', '90d'])).toEqual({ op: 'prune', days: 90, apply: false });
    expect(ok('prune', ['--older-than', '3m', '--apply'])).toEqual({ op: 'prune', days: 90, apply: true });
    expect(ok('prune', ['--apply', '--older-than', '30d'])).toEqual({ op: 'prune', days: 30, apply: true });
    expect(why('prune', ['--older-than', '7d'])).toBe('older-than-floor');
    expect(why('prune', ['--older-than', '29 days'])).toBe('older-than-floor');
    expect(why('prune', [])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('prune', ['--apply'])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('prune', ['--older-than', 'soon'])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('prune', ['--older-than'])).toBe('bad-args');
  });

  it('reparse takes a full 20-hex node id or a session, never both, plus --apply', () => {
    const NODE = 'L0123456789abcdef0123';
    expect(ok('reparse', [])).toEqual({ op: 'reparse', node: null, session: null, apply: false });
    expect(ok('reparse', ['--node', NODE, '--apply'])).toEqual({ op: 'reparse', node: NODE, session: null, apply: true });
    expect(ok('reparse', ['--node', 'N0123456789abcdef0123'])).toMatchObject({ node: 'N0123456789abcdef0123' });
    expect(ok('reparse', ['--session', 'claude-demo'])).toEqual({ op: 'reparse', node: null, session: 'claude-demo', apply: false });
    expect(why('reparse', ['--node', 'L0123ab'])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('reparse', ['--node', NODE.toUpperCase()])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('reparse', ['--node', NODE, '--session', 'claude-demo'])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('reparse', ['--session', '..'])).toBe('bad-id');
  });

  it('restore takes exactly one bare backup name; a path, a temp or another name is restore-refused (C57 pure half)', () => {
    expect(ok('restore', ['20261001T000000Z.db'])).toEqual({ op: 'restore', name: '20261001T000000Z.db' });
    expect(ok('restore', ['pre-v2.db'])).toEqual({ op: 'restore', name: 'pre-v2.db' });
    for (const n of ['../20261001T000000Z.db', 'backups/20261001T000000Z.db', '.20261001T000000Z.db.tmp',
      '20261001T000000Z.db.tmp', 'pre-v0.db', 'history.db', '/home/u/x.db']) {
      expect(why('restore', [n]), n).toBe('restore-refused');
    }
    expect(why('restore', [])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('restore', ['pre-v2.db', 'pre-v3.db'])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('restore', ['--apply'])).toBe('bad-args');
  });

  it('rebuild takes an optional --store-id of the uuid grammar', () => {
    const S = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000e1';
    expect(ok('rebuild', [])).toEqual({ op: 'rebuild', storeId: null });
    expect(ok('rebuild', ['--store-id', S])).toEqual({ op: 'rebuild', storeId: S });
    expect(why('rebuild', ['--store-id', S.toUpperCase()])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('rebuild', ['--store-id'])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('rebuild', [S])).toBe('bad-args');
  });

  it('a verb B2 does not run is bad-args (recall-off ships in W2)', () => {
    expect(why('recall-off', ['claude-demo'])).toBe('bad-args');
    expect(why('frobnicate', [])).toBe('bad-args');
  });
});

describe('parseDuration, backupNameOf and restoreNameOk (spec 6.6, 8.4; P15)', () => {
  it("parseDuration reads upstream's units: d, w, m (30 days), y (365), any case and spacing; nothing else", () => {
    expect(libOps.parseDuration('90d')).toBe(90);
    expect(libOps.parseDuration('1w')).toBe(7);
    expect(libOps.parseDuration('3m')).toBe(90);
    expect(libOps.parseDuration('1y')).toBe(365);
    expect(libOps.parseDuration(' 2 WEEKS ')).toBe(14);
    expect(libOps.parseDuration('45 days')).toBe(45);
    for (const s of ['0d', '-5d', '5', '', 'd', '1.5d', 'ninety days']) expect(libOps.parseDuration(s), s).toBeNull();
    expect(libOps.PRUNE_FLOOR_DAYS).toBe(30);
  });
  it('backupNameOf is the UTC second (`YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ.db`, §8.4), and restoreNameOk accepts it', () => {
    expect(libOps.backupNameOf(Date.parse('2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z'))).toBe('20261001T000000Z.db');
    expect(libOps.backupNameOf(Date.parse('2026-12-31T23:59:59.999Z'))).toBe('20261231T235959Z.db');
    expect(libOps.restoreNameOk(libOps.backupNameOf(Date.now()))).toBe(true);
    expect(libOps.restoreNameOk('pre-v12.db')).toBe(true);
    expect(() => libOps.backupNameOf(-1)).toThrow(TypeError);
  });
});

describe('decideOpDoor: which no-store answer a writing verb gets before any spawn (spec 8.3 "Which no-store answer", 8.4)', () => {
  const S = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000e1';
  const absent = { state: 'absent' as const };
  const unreadable = { state: 'unreadable' as const };
  const id = { state: 'value' as const, value: S };
  /** decideCliStore's input, as Task 10's cliFactsOf(measureReach(home)) builds it. */
  const reach = (o: Partial<libOps.CliStoreFacts> = {}): libOps.CliStoreFacts => ({
    darwin: false, role: 'fleet', statSettled: true, dbDir: 'dir', shim: 'present',
    storeId: absent, pending: absent, writer: absent, db: 'absent', dbStoreId: absent,
    wal: false, shm: false, journalStoreDirs: [], backupsDb: [], ...o,
  });
  const stored = { storeId: id, db: 'present' as const, dbStoreId: id };
  it('macOS and a recorded server role are exit 9, whatever is on disk', () => {
    expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach({ darwin: true, ...stored }))).toEqual({ ok: false, exit: 9 });
    expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach({ role: 'server', ...stored }))).toEqual({ ok: false, exit: 9 });
    expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach({ role: 'server', shim: 'unmeasured' }))).toEqual({ ok: false, exit: 9 });
  });
  it('no shim, no store.id and no DB: never installed, exit 9, whatever else the history root holds', () => {
    expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach({ shim: 'absent' }))).toEqual({ ok: false, exit: 9 });
    expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach({ shim: 'absent', journalStoreDirs: [S] })), 'a journal directory is not a store').toEqual({ ok: false, exit: 9 });
  });
  it('a store.id or a DB with no shim is exit 2 writer-absent, never 9: a plain uninstall kept the data', () => {
    for (const o of [stored, { storeId: id }, { db: 'present' as const, dbStoreId: id }, { db: 'zero-byte' as const }]) {
      expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach({ shim: 'absent', ...o })), JSON.stringify(o)).toEqual({ ok: false, exit: 2, reason: 'writer-absent' });
    }
  });
  it('an unmeasured shim, store.id or DB, a dangling db/ or an unsettled stat is exit 5 with its own word, never read as absent (IV5)', () => {
    expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach({ shim: 'unmeasured' }))).toEqual({ ok: false, exit: 5, reason: 'store-unmeasured' });
    expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach({ shim: 'absent', storeId: unreadable }))).toEqual({ ok: false, exit: 5, reason: 'store-unmeasured' });
    expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach({ shim: 'absent', db: 'unmeasured' }))).toEqual({ ok: false, exit: 5, reason: 'store-unmeasured' });
    expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach({ shim: 'absent', dbDir: 'dangling' }))).toEqual({ ok: false, exit: 5, reason: 'store-root-dangling' });
    expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach({ shim: 'absent', statSettled: false }))).toEqual({ ok: false, exit: 5, reason: 'store-unreachable' });
  });
  it('a shim present goes on to the gate and the shim\'s own pass, with a store or not', () => {
    expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach())).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(libOps.decideOpDoor(reach(stored))).toEqual({ ok: true });
  });
});

describe("decideBind: the binding verbs' preconditions, unreadable never read as absent (spec 6.9, 8.4; C57, C58, C67 pure halves)", () => {
  const S = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000e1';
  const T = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000e2';
  const v = (value: string) => ({ state: 'value' as const, value });
  const absent = { state: 'absent' as const };
  const unreadable = { state: 'unreadable' as const };
  const facts = (o: Partial<libOps.BindFacts> = {}): libOps.BindFacts => ({
    role: 'fleet', dbDir: 'dir', storeId: absent, pending: absent, writer: absent, db: 'absent', dbStoreId: absent,
    wal: false, shm: false, journalStoreDirs: [], backupsDb: [],
    codeVersion: 1, storedVersion: absent, storeIdArg: null, journalDirs: [], backup: null, ...o,
  });
  const backup = (o: Partial<libOps.BindBackup> = {}): libOps.BindBackup =>
    ({ regular: true, storeId: v(S), userVersion: 1, integrityOk: true, ...o });
  const refused = (kind: 'adopt' | 'restore' | 'rebuild', o: Partial<libOps.BindFacts>) =>
    libOps.decideBind(kind, facts(o));
  /** history.db's own user_version, as Task 26's bindFactsOf measures it (storedVersionAt). */
  const ver = (value: number): libOps.Presence<number> => ({ state: 'value', value });
  /** A DB adopt can bind: present, with a readable store_id, at this build's version. */
  const adoptable = { db: 'present' as const, dbStoreId: v(S), storedVersion: ver(1) };

  it('C67: an unreadable store.id, pending marker or store.writer, or an unmeasured db/ or DB, is exit 5 store-unmeasured for every binding verb', () => {
    for (const kind of ['adopt', 'restore', 'rebuild'] as const) {
      for (const o of [{ storeId: unreadable }, { pending: unreadable }, { writer: unreadable }, { dbDir: 'unmeasured' as const }, { db: 'unmeasured' as const }]) {
        expect(refused(kind, o), `${kind} ${JSON.stringify(o)}`).toMatchObject({ ok: false, rc: 5, reason: 'store-unmeasured' });
      }
    }
  });

  it('a dangling db/ is exit 5 store-root-dangling', () => {
    expect(refused('restore', { dbDir: 'dangling' })).toMatchObject({ ok: false, rc: 5, reason: 'store-root-dangling' });
  });

  it('adopt binds a present DB with a readable store_id and no store.id, at or below this build\'s version', () => {
    expect(libOps.decideBind('adopt', facts(adoptable))).toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: S });
    expect(libOps.decideBind('adopt', facts({ ...adoptable, pending: v(T) }))).toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: S });
    expect(libOps.decideBind('adopt', facts({ ...adoptable, codeVersion: 2 })), 'an older store: its migration is the writer\'s').toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: S });
  });

  it("adopt refuses a store newer than this build, and an unreadable user_version is exit 5 (G9; RB17: lib decides, the arm relays)", () => {
    const newer = refused('adopt', { ...adoptable, storedVersion: ver(2) });
    expect(newer).toMatchObject({ ok: false, rc: 2, reason: 'adopt-refused' });
    if (!newer.ok) expect(newer.detail).toBe('history.db is schema 2; this build knows 1: adopt it with the build that wrote it');
    for (const sv of [unreadable, absent]) {
      expect(refused('adopt', { ...adoptable, storedVersion: sv }), JSON.stringify(sv)).toMatchObject({ ok: false, rc: 5, reason: 'store-unmeasured' });
    }
    // The version is adopt's own fact: restore and rebuild never read it (their DB must be absent).
    expect(libOps.decideBind('restore', facts({ storedVersion: unreadable, backup: backup() }))).toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: S });
    expect(libOps.decideBind('rebuild', facts({ storedVersion: unreadable, storeId: v(S) }))).toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: S });
  });

  it('adopt refuses: store.id present (equal or different), no readable store_id, no DB, or its own pending marker', () => {
    for (const o of [
      { db: 'present' as const, dbStoreId: v(S), storeId: v(S) },
      { db: 'present' as const, dbStoreId: v(S), storeId: v(T) },
      { db: 'present' as const, dbStoreId: absent },
      { db: 'present' as const, dbStoreId: unreadable },
      { db: 'absent' as const },
      { db: 'zero-byte' as const },
      { db: 'present' as const, dbStoreId: v(S), pending: v(S) },
    ]) {
      expect(refused('adopt', o), JSON.stringify(o)).toMatchObject({ ok: false, rc: 2, reason: 'adopt-refused' });
    }
  });

  it('restore binds the backup onto a box with no DB, or whose store.id names the backup\'s store', () => {
    expect(libOps.decideBind('restore', facts({ backup: backup() }))).toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: S });
    expect(libOps.decideBind('restore', facts({ storeId: v(S), backup: backup() }))).toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: S });
    expect(libOps.decideBind('restore', facts({ journalStoreDirs: [S], backupsDb: ['20261001T000000Z.db'], backup: backup() })),
      'store-recoverable evidence is what a restore exists for').toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: S });
  });

  it('restore passes the pre-copy check with version and integrity not yet measured', () => {
    expect(libOps.decideBind('restore', facts({ backup: backup({ userVersion: null, integrityOk: null }) }))).toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: S });
  });

  it('restore refuses: a DB present, a leftover WAL, a non-regular or unnamed backup, an unreadable or foreign store_id, a newer schema, a failed integrity_check', () => {
    for (const o of [
      { db: 'present' as const, dbStoreId: v(S), backup: backup() },
      { db: 'zero-byte' as const, backup: backup() },
      { wal: true, backup: backup() },
      { shm: true, backup: backup() },
      { backup: null },
      { backup: backup({ regular: false }) },
      { backup: backup({ storeId: unreadable }) },
      { backup: backup({ storeId: absent }) },
      { backup: backup({ storeId: v('not-a-uuid') }) },
      { storeId: v(T), backup: backup() },
      { backup: backup({ userVersion: 2 }) },
      { backup: backup({ integrityOk: false }) },
    ]) {
      expect(refused('restore', o), JSON.stringify(o)).toMatchObject({ ok: false, rc: 2, reason: 'restore-refused' });
    }
  });

  it("rebuild's store_id: store.id's; else the one journal directory whose heads agree; else --store-id among several", () => {
    expect(libOps.decideBind('rebuild', facts({ storeId: v(S) }))).toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: S });
    expect(libOps.decideBind('rebuild', facts({ journalStoreDirs: [S], journalDirs: [{ storeId: S, headsAgree: true }] }))).toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: S });
    const two = { journalStoreDirs: [S, T], journalDirs: [{ storeId: S, headsAgree: true }, { storeId: T, headsAgree: true }] };
    expect(libOps.decideBind('rebuild', facts({ ...two, storeIdArg: T }))).toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: T });
    expect(libOps.decideBind('rebuild', facts({ ...two, storeId: v(T), storeIdArg: T }))).toEqual({ ok: true, storeId: T });
  });

  it('rebuild refuses: a DB, a leftover WAL, nothing naming a store, store.id against --store-id, several directories unnamed, a --store-id naming no directory, heads naming another store', () => {
    const two = { journalStoreDirs: [S, T], journalDirs: [{ storeId: S, headsAgree: true }, { storeId: T, headsAgree: true }] };
    for (const o of [
      { db: 'present' as const, dbStoreId: v(S), storeId: v(S) },
      { wal: true, storeId: v(S) },
      {},
      { ...two, storeId: v(S), storeIdArg: T },
      { ...two },
      { ...two, storeIdArg: '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000e3' },
      { journalStoreDirs: [S], journalDirs: [{ storeId: S, headsAgree: false }] },
      { journalStoreDirs: [S], journalDirs: [{ storeId: S, headsAgree: false }], storeIdArg: S },
    ]) {
      expect(refused('rebuild', o), JSON.stringify(o)).toMatchObject({ ok: false, rc: 2, reason: 'rebuild-refused' });
    }
  });

  it("rebuild's refusal names the candidate directories", () => {
    const r = libOps.decideBind('rebuild', facts({ journalStoreDirs: [S, T], journalDirs: [{ storeId: S, headsAgree: true }, { storeId: T, headsAgree: true }] }));
    expect(r.ok).toBe(false);
    if (!r.ok) {
      expect(r.detail).toContain(S);
      expect(r.detail).toContain(T);
    }
  });

  it('rebuild with an unlistable journal/ is exit 5 store-unmeasured', () => {
    expect(refused('rebuild', { journalStoreDirs: ['(unlistable)'] })).toMatchObject({ ok: false, rc: 5, reason: 'store-unmeasured' });
  });

  it('a kind outside BIND_KINDS is a programming error', () => {
    expect(() => libOps.decideBind('import' as 'adopt', facts())).toThrow(TypeError);
  });
});

describe('decideReparse: the preflight limits (spec 8.4, 11 L8; DM21, C62 pure halves)', () => {
  it('up to REPARSE_MAX_TARGETS runs; one more is reparse-too-many; any pruned span is span-pruned', () => {
    expect(libOps.decideReparse({ targets: libOps.REPARSE_MAX_TARGETS, prunedSpans: 0 })).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(libOps.decideReparse({ targets: 0, prunedSpans: 0 })).toEqual({ ok: true });
    expect(libOps.decideReparse({ targets: libOps.REPARSE_MAX_TARGETS + 1, prunedSpans: 0 })).toEqual({ ok: false, reason: 'reparse-too-many' });
```

```js

// ===========================================================================
// Operator-verb decisions (spec §6.6, §6.9, §8.3 "Which no-store answer",
// §8.4; W1-B2 Task 6). Pure: the CLI's door and the sweep's --op dispatch
// both call them, so the two doors answer the same words (C64).
// D-4692 (history-adopt-verb) D-4693 (history-restore-verb) D-4694 (history-rebuild-verb)
// ===========================================================================

/** A restorable backup's bare name under db/backups/ (§8.4, §6.11): doctor --backup's `<ts>.db` or the
 *  writer's `pre-v<N>.db`. A `/`, a dot-prefixed temp, a `.tmp` or any other name never matches. */
const RESTORE_NAME_RE = /^(?:[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z|pre-v[1-9][0-9]*)\.db$/;

/** argv after `--op <verb>`, read against `spec` (flag -> 'bool' | 'value'): each flag at most once, a value
 *  flag followed by its value, anything not starting with `-` a positional. null on an unknown or repeated
 *  flag, or a value flag with nothing after it. */
function readOpFlags(args, spec) {
  const flags = {};
  const positional = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
    const a = args[i];
    if (!Object.hasOwn(spec, a)) {
      if (typeof a !== 'string' || a.startsWith('-')) return null;
      positional.push(a);
      continue;
    }
    if (Object.hasOwn(flags, a)) return null;
    if (spec[a] === 'bool') { flags[a] = true; continue; }
    if (i + 1 >= args.length) return null;
    i += 1;
    flags[a] = args[i];
  }
  return { flags, positional };
}

/** One operator verb's argv (§8.4), as both doors read it. `import` keeps B1's grammar (`--apply`, and
 *  `--session <id> --file <path>` both or neither, the session an idOk id and the file a `<uuid>.jsonl`).
 *  `prune` needs `--older-than <dur>` at or above PRUNE_FLOOR_DAYS. `reparse` takes `--node <full id>` (Task 1's
 *  HISTORY_NODE_ID_RE, the one spelling of a full node id) or `--session <id>`, never both
 *  D-4697 (history-reparse-targets). `restore` takes one bare backup name, refused
 *  `restore-refused` when it is not one (C57). `rebuild` takes `--store-id <uuid>`. A verb B2 does not run
 *  (recall-off is W2's) is `bad-args`. */
export function parseOpVerbArgs(op, args) {
  const refuse = (reason) => ({ ok: false, reason });
  const ok = (a) => ({ ok: true, args: Object.freeze(a) });
  switch (op) {
    case 'import': {
      const r = readOpFlags(args, { '--apply': 'bool', '--session': 'value', '--file': 'value' });
      if (r === null || r.positional.length > 0) return refuse('bad-args');
      const session = r.flags['--session'] ?? null;
      const file = r.flags['--file'] ?? null;
      if ((session === null) !== (file === null)) return refuse('bad-args');
      if (session !== null) {
        if (!idOk(session)) return refuse('bad-id');
        const base = file.slice(file.lastIndexOf('/') + 1);
        if (!base.endsWith('.jsonl') || !UUID_RE.test(base.slice(0, -'.jsonl'.length))) return refuse('bad-args');
      }
      return ok({ op, apply: r.flags['--apply'] === true, session, file });
    }
    case 'migrate':
    case 'repair':
    case 'backup':
    case 'adopt':
      return args.length === 0 ? ok({ op }) : refuse('bad-args');
    case 'prune': {
      const r = readOpFlags(args, { '--apply': 'bool', '--older-than': 'value' });
      if (r === null || r.positional.length > 0 || r.flags['--older-than'] === undefined) return refuse('bad-args');
      const days = parseDuration(r.flags['--older-than']);
      if (days === null) return refuse('bad-args');
      if (days < PRUNE_FLOOR_DAYS) return refuse('older-than-floor');
      return ok({ op, days, apply: r.flags['--apply'] === true });
    }
    case 'reparse': {
      const r = readOpFlags(args, { '--apply': 'bool', '--node': 'value', '--session': 'value' });
      if (r === null || r.positional.length > 0) return refuse('bad-args');
      const node = r.flags['--node'] ?? null;
      const session = r.flags['--session'] ?? null;
      if (node !== null && session !== null) return refuse('bad-args');
      if (node !== null && !HISTORY_NODE_ID_RE.test(node)) return refuse('bad-args');
      if (session !== null && !idOk(session)) return refuse('bad-id');
      return ok({ op, node, session, apply: r.flags['--apply'] === true });
    }
    case 'restore': {
      const r = readOpFlags(args, {});
      if (r === null || r.positional.length !== 1) return refuse('bad-args');
      const name = r.positional[0];
      if (!restoreNameOk(name)) return refuse('restore-refused');
      return ok({ op, name });
    }
    case 'rebuild': {
      const r = readOpFlags(args, { '--store-id': 'value' });
      if (r === null || r.positional.length > 0) return refuse('bad-args');
      const storeId = r.flags['--store-id'] ?? null;
      if (storeId !== null && !UUID_RE.test(storeId)) return refuse('bad-args');
      return ok({ op, storeId });
    }
    default:
      return refuse('bad-args');
  }
}

/** The no-store table's answers a writing verb keeps as they are: what could not be measured or reached. */
const DOOR_UNMEASURED = Object.freeze(['store-unreachable', 'store-root-dangling', 'store-unmeasured']);

/** Which no-store answer a WRITING verb gets before the CLI spawns the shim (§8.3's table, its writing-verb
 *  row), over exactly decideCliStore's input, so "is there a store here" is decided by that one table, from
 *  store.id and the DB, never from whether ~/.ccrc/history exists:
 *  - macOS or a recorded server role is 9, whatever is on disk;
 *  - a shim present goes on to decideOpGate and the shim's own pass, which decides the store rows itself;
 *  - otherwise the table answers. Its 9 (no store.id and no DB: never installed) stays 9. Its unreachable,
 *    dangling and unmeasured words (5) stand: an input that could not be measured is never read as absent (IV5).
 *    Any other answer means a store exists, and a writing verb with no shim is 2 `writer-absent`, never 9 (a
 *    plain uninstall kept the data). D-4183 */
export function decideOpDoor(f) {
  if (f.darwin || f.role === 'server') return { ok: false, exit: EXIT.NO_STORE };
  if (f.shim === 'present') return { ok: true };
  const t = decideCliStore(f);
  if (t.exit === EXIT.NO_STORE) return { ok: false, exit: EXIT.NO_STORE };
  if (t.exit === EXIT.DB && DOOR_UNMEASURED.includes(t.reason)) return { ok: false, exit: EXIT.DB, reason: t.reason };
  return { ok: false, exit: EXIT.REFUSED, reason: 'writer-absent' };
}

// derived from lossless-claw src/prune.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
const PRUNE_DURATION_RE = /^(\d+)\s*(d|day|days|w|week|weeks|m|month|months|y|year|years)$/i;
const PRUNE_UNIT_DAYS = Object.freeze({
  d: 1, day: 1, days: 1, w: 7, week: 7, weeks: 7, m: 30, month: 30, months: 30, y: 365, year: 365, years: 365,
});

/** A human duration (`90d`, `3m`, `1y`) as days, or null when it is not one (§11 P15, upstream's grammar: a month
 *  is 30 days, a year 365). */
export function parseDuration(input) {
  if (typeof input !== 'string') return null;
  const trimmed = input.trim().toLowerCase();
  const match = PRUNE_DURATION_RE.exec(trimmed);
  if (!match) {
    return null;
  }
  const amount = Number(match[1]);
  const unit = match[2].toLowerCase();
  const multiplier = PRUNE_UNIT_DAYS[unit];
  if (multiplier == null || !Number.isFinite(amount) || amount <= 0) {
    return null;
  }
  return amount * multiplier;
}

/** `prune --older-than` under this many days is refused `older-than-floor` (§6.6, *chosen*). */
export const PRUNE_FLOOR_DAYS = 30;

/** doctor --backup's file name for the UTC second `nowMs` (§8.4): `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ.db`, the form `--op backup`
 *  publishes under db/backups/ and `doctor --restore` takes. D-4695 (history-backup-preflight-and-rename) */
export function backupNameOf(nowMs) {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(nowMs) || nowMs < 0) throw new TypeError(`backupNameOf: a time in ms, got ${String(nowMs)}`);
  const iso = new Date(nowMs).toISOString();
  return `${iso.slice(0, 19).replace(/[-:]/g, '')}Z.db`;
}

/** Whether `name` is a bare backup name `doctor --restore` may open under db/backups/ (§8.4). */
export function restoreNameOk(name) {
  return typeof name === 'string' && RESTORE_NAME_RE.test(name);
}

const BIND_REFUSALS = Object.freeze({ adopt: 'adopt-refused', restore: 'restore-refused', rebuild: 'rebuild-refused' });

/** The binding verbs' preconditions (§8.4, §6.9; the "which also decides the binding verbs' preconditions" arm
 *  of the store-open decision, §6.4). `f` is the store's measured facts (B1's StoreFacts) plus what the verb
 *  names: the code's schema version, history.db's own user_version (`storedVersion`), a --store-id, the journal
 *  directories with whether every head in each names that directory's store, and, for restore, the backup. Before
 *  anything kind-specific, an input that could not be measured answers 5 `store-unmeasured` (C67): store.id, its
 *  pending marker, store.writer, db/, history.db. A db/ link to nothing answers 5 `store-root-dangling`. Then:
 *  - adopt: history.db present with a readable meta.store_id, and store.id absent (equal is nothing to adopt,
 *    different is two stores claiming this box), and not this box's own interrupted binding (a pending marker
 *    naming the same store, which the next tick finishes). Last, its user_version: one that is not a measured value
 *    is 5 `store-unmeasured`, and one above the code's is refused before anything is written, as openStore refuses
 *    it before its writer's open (G9; DM17 "no write"). That refusal is decided here, never in the L4 arm (RB17);
 *  - restore: no history.db, no leftover -wal or -shm (SQLite would replay it into the restored file), a regular
 *    backup with a readable uuid store_id, store.id absent or naming that store, the backup's user_version not
 *    newer than the code's and its integrity_check not failed. Before the copy, version and integrity may be
 *    null (not measured yet), and they pass;
 *  - rebuild: no history.db and no leftover -wal or -shm. Its store_id is store.id's; else the one journal
 *    directory whose heads agree; else --store-id, which must name one of several. A --store-id disagreeing with
 *    store.id, naming no directory, or naming one whose heads name another store is refused, with the
 *    candidates named.
 *  D-4188 D-4185 D-4186 */
export function decideBind(kind, f) {
  if (!Object.hasOwn(BIND_REFUSALS, kind)) throw new TypeError(`decideBind: kind outside BIND_KINDS: ${String(kind)}`);
  const unmeasured = (detail) => ({ ok: false, rc: EXIT.DB, reason: 'store-unmeasured', detail });
  const refuse = (detail) => ({ ok: false, rc: EXIT.REFUSED, reason: BIND_REFUSALS[kind], detail });
  if (f.dbDir === 'dangling') return { ok: false, rc: EXIT.DB, reason: 'store-root-dangling', detail: 'db/ is a link to nothing: recreate its target or remove the link' };
  if (f.dbDir === 'unmeasured' || f.db === 'unmeasured') return unmeasured('db/ or history.db could not be measured');
  if (presenceUnreadable(f.storeId)) return unmeasured('store.id exists and cannot be read');
  if (presenceUnreadable(f.pending)) return unmeasured('store.id.pending exists and cannot be read');
  if (presenceUnreadable(f.writer)) return unmeasured('store.writer exists and cannot be read');
  const marker = presenceValue(f.storeId);
  if (kind === 'adopt') {
    if (f.db !== 'present') return refuse(f.db === 'zero-byte' ? 'history.db is 0 bytes: there is no store to adopt' : 'there is no history.db to adopt');
    const inDb = presenceValue(f.dbStoreId);
    if (inDb === null) return refuse('history.db has no readable meta.store_id');
    if (marker !== null) return refuse(marker === inDb ? 'store.id already names this store: nothing to adopt' : `store.id names ${marker} and history.db is ${inDb}: two stores claim this box`);
    if (presenceValue(f.pending) === inDb) return refuse("store.id.pending names this store: it is this box's own interrupted binding, which the next tick finishes");
    const stored = presenceValue(f.storedVersion);
    if (stored === null) return unmeasured("history.db's user_version cannot be read");
    if (stored > f.codeVersion) return refuse(`history.db is schema ${stored}; this build knows ${f.codeVersion}: adopt it with the build that wrote it`);
    return { ok: true, storeId: inDb };
  }
  if (kind === 'restore') {
    if (f.db === 'present' || f.db === 'zero-byte') return refuse("history.db is present: a live store is never overwritten; move the old store's three files aside together first");
    if (f.wal || f.shm) return refuse("a history.db-wal or -shm is left with no history.db: SQLite would replay it into the restored file; move the old store's three files aside together");
    const bk = f.backup;
    if (bk === null || !bk.regular) return refuse('the backup is not a regular file under db/backups/');
    const bkId = presenceValue(bk.storeId);
    if (bkId === null || !UUID_RE.test(bkId)) return refuse(bk.storeId.state === 'unreadable' ? "the backup's meta.store_id cannot be read" : 'the backup has no meta.store_id');
    if (marker !== null && marker !== bkId) return refuse(`store.id names ${marker}; the backup is ${bkId}`);
    if (bk.userVersion !== null && bk.userVersion > f.codeVersion) return refuse(`the backup is schema ${bk.userVersion}; this build knows ${f.codeVersion}`);
    if (bk.integrityOk === false) return refuse("the backup's integrity_check is not ok");
    return { ok: true, storeId: bkId };
  }
  if (f.db === 'present' || f.db === 'zero-byte') return refuse('history.db is present: rebuild recreates a lost database only');
  if (f.wal || f.shm) return refuse("a history.db-wal or -shm is left with no history.db: move the old store's three files aside together");
  if (f.journalStoreDirs.includes('(unlistable)')) return unmeasured('journal/ could not be listed');
  const dirs = f.journalDirs;
  const names = dirs.length === 0 ? 'none' : dirs.map((d) => d.storeId).join(', ');
  const arg = f.storeIdArg;
  if (arg !== null) {
    if (marker !== null && marker !== arg) return refuse(`store.id names ${marker}; --store-id names ${arg}`);
    const d = dirs.find((x) => x.storeId === arg);
    if (d === undefined) return refuse(`--store-id ${arg} names no journal directory (journal directories: ${names})`);
    if (!d.headsAgree) return refuse(`journal/${arg}/ holds head records naming another store`);
    return { ok: true, storeId: arg };
  }
  if (marker !== null) return { ok: true, storeId: marker };
  if (dirs.length === 0) return refuse('nothing names a store_id: no store.id and no journal directory');
  if (dirs.length > 1) return refuse(`several journal directories: name one with --store-id (journal directories: ${names})`);
  if (!dirs[0].headsAgree) return refuse(`journal/${dirs[0].storeId}/ holds head records naming another store`);
  return { ok: true, storeId: dirs[0].storeId };
}

/** reparse's preflight (§8.4, §11 L8): more than REPARSE_MAX_TARGETS leaves is `reparse-too-many`, and any target
 *  with a tombstoned source or summary is `span-pruned` (§6.6). Either refuses the whole run, so nothing is
 *  rewritten. */
export function decideReparse({ targets, prunedSpans }) {
  if (targets > REPARSE_MAX_TARGETS) return { ok: false, reason: 'reparse-too-many' };
  if (prunedSpans > 0) return { ok: false, reason: 'span-pruned' };
  return { ok: true };
}
```

```ts
export type OpArgs =
  | { readonly op: 'import'; readonly apply: boolean; readonly session: string | null; readonly file: string | null }
  | { readonly op: 'migrate' }
  | { readonly op: 'prune'; readonly days: number; readonly apply: boolean }

  | { readonly op: 'repair' }

  | { readonly op: 'rebuild'; readonly storeId: string | null };
export function parseOpVerbArgs(op: string, args: readonly string[]):

export function restoreNameOk(name: string): boolean;

export function decideBind(kind: 'adopt' | 'restore' | 'rebuild', f: BindFacts):
  { ok: true; storeId: string } | { ok: false; rc: 2 | 5; reason: string; detail: string };
export function decideReparse(i: { targets: number; prunedSpans: number }): { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: 'reparse-too-many' | 'span-pruned' };
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Write the mutation runner.** It is the same gitignored scratch tool as Task 5's: Tasks 1–7, 7A, 7B and 8 write this same file, byte for byte, so each task stands alone and rewriting it changes nothing. Like every copy, it spawns vitest with `maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024` (coordinator ruling R-runner). From the repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <<'EOF'
// .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs: measures each guard RED with it mutated, then GREEN with
// it restored (the B2 plan's mutation-pin rule). Run from server/, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least
// 600000 ms:
//   node ../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <mutants.json>
// A mutant is {name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}. `file` is repo-relative, `test` is
// server/-relative, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. The
// pristine file is copied to scratch/keep/<file with '/' as '__'>.orig BEFORE it is touched, and the copy is
// removed only after the file is restored from it. A kill no handler sees therefore leaves the original findable,
// and the next run REFUSES while any copy is left. To restore by hand, from the repository root:
//   for f in .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/*.orig; do t="$(basename "$f" .orig)"; cp "$f" "${t//__//}" && rm "$f"; done
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const KEEP = '../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep';
mkdirSync(KEEP, { recursive: true });
const left = readdirSync(KEEP).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.orig'));
if (left.length > 0) {
  console.log(`REFUSED: ${left.join(', ')} in ${KEEP}. An earlier run was interrupted and a source may hold a mutant: restore as this file's header says.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const keepOf = (file) => `${KEEP}/${file.replaceAll('/', '__')}.orig`;
const restoreAll = () => {
  for (const n of readdirSync(KEEP)) {
    if (!n.endsWith('.orig')) continue;
    copyFileSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`, `../${n.slice(0, -'.orig'.length).replaceAll('__', '/')}`);
    rmSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`);
  }
};
// Every way out restores: the loop's end, process.exit and an uncaught throw all emit 'exit', and a signal is
// turned into an exit. A signal sent while the synchronous loop holds the thread is handled after the current
// child returns; a Ctrl-C also reaches the vitest child, and the loop stops on the child's signal below.
process.on('exit', restoreAll);
for (const s of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) process.on(s, () => process.exit(130));
// maxBuffer: past Node's default (1 MiB) spawnSync kills the child (ENOBUFS, signal SIGTERM, measured), which the
// loop below reads as an interrupt. Each large-operand case asserts a boolean or a length, so a red prints no big diff.
const vitest = (test, filter) => spawnSync('./node_modules/.bin/vitest', ['run', test, '-t', filter], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 });
const mutants = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
let bad = 0;
for (const m of mutants) {
  const target = `../${m.file}`;
  if (!existsSync(target)) { console.log(`NO SUCH FILE       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  const keep = keepOf(m.file);
  copyFileSync(target, keep);
  let src = readFileSync(keep, 'utf8');
  let unique = true;
  for (const e of m.edits) {
    const at = src.indexOf(e.anchor);
    if (at < 0 || src.indexOf(e.anchor, at + 1) >= 0) { unique = false; break; }
    src = src.slice(0, at) + e.replacement + src.slice(at + e.anchor.length);
  }
  if (!unique) { rmSync(keep); console.log(`ANCHOR NOT UNIQUE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  writeFileSync(target, src);
  const red = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  copyFileSync(keep, target);
  rmSync(keep);
  if (red.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${red.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  const failed = /Tests\s+(\d+) failed/.exec(red.stdout)?.[1] ?? '?';
  if (red.status === 0) { console.log(`STAYED GREEN       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`red (${failed} failed)   ${m.name}`);
  const green = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  if (green.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${green.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  if (green.status !== 0) { console.log(`RED AFTER RESTORE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`green              ${m.name}`);
}
console.log(bad === 0 ? 'every guard measured red, then green' : `${bad} guard(s) not measured`);
process.exit(bad === 0 ? 0 : 1);
EOF
```

### Task 7: lib: recovery and repair decisions: RECOVER_PHASES and the cursor grammar, journal-file order, replayStep and planReplay, the unmoved-tick rule, the FK baseline diff (P21), FTS shadow health (P24)

**Files:**

  - Add three import lines directly below the file's last top-of-file `import` line.
  - Append the describes at the end of the file.
- Scratch, gitignored: `.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs` and `mutants-task7.json`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (B1 `lib.mjs`, same module):
  - `parseJournalRecord(line)`, which answers `{kind:'record', rec} | {kind:'malformed'} | {kind:'unknown'} | {kind:'newer'}`;
  - `journalRecord(kind, t, fields)` (tests only), `eventKey(drainingName, ordinal)`, `canonicalJson(value)`;
  - the types `JournalRecord`, `JournalRead`, `JournalKind` (`lib.d.mts`).
- Consumes (tests only): B1 `store.mjs`'s `FTS_DDL`, and `node:sqlite`'s `DatabaseSync` on `:memory:`.
- Produces (`lib.mjs`, each declared once in `lib.d.mts`):
  - `export const RECOVER_PHASES: readonly string[]` (`['index', 'apply', 'reindex']`, frozen). B4 inserts its export phases between `apply` and `reindex`.
  - `export interface RecoverCursor { phase: string; file: string | null; offset: number; blobId: number | null; pairsAdded: boolean }`
  - `export function formatRecoverCursor(c: RecoverCursor): string` and `export function parseRecoverCursor(s: string | null): RecoverCursor | null`. The grammar:
    - `<phase>`;
    - `<phase>:<YYYY-MM>.<writer>.jsonl:<offset>` for `index` and `apply`;
    - `reindex:<blobId>`;
    - each optionally followed by `+pairs`.
    A NULL cursor is the step's start.
  - `export interface JournalFileFacts { name: string; month: string; writer: string; headT: number | null; lastT: number | null }`
  - `export function orderJournalFiles(files: readonly JournalFileFacts[]): string[][]`. These are merge groups in apply order. Files of one month whose `[headT, lastT]` ranges overlap form one group, merged by record time `t`.
  - `export type ReplayAction`:
    - `{ do: 'file'; name: string; t: number }`
    - `{ do: 'receipt'; key: string; ord: number; rec: Record<string, unknown>; recvMs: number; verdicts: JournalRecord[] }`
    - `{ do: 'skip-undrained'; file: string }`
    - `{ do: 'verdict'; rec: JournalRecord }`
    - `{ do: 'redact'; len: number; sha256: string; t: number }`
    - `{ do: 'tick'; t: number; lagMs: number | null }`
    - `{ do: 'skip'; counter: 'journal_line_malformed' | 'journal_record_unknown' | 'journal_head_mismatch' }`
  - `export interface ReplayState { storeId: string; file: string | null; recvMs: number; drained: ReadonlySet<string>; verdictsByKey: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly JournalRecord[]>; ticksAfter: number; ticksBefore?: number | null }`. A `tick` record applies only when `ticksAfter < t` and, when `ticksBefore` is a number, `t < ticksBefore`: the store already holds the ticks up to `ticksAfter` (its newest tick below the bind when the step began), and a tick at or after the step's bind ms is a recovery pass's own record (D-4701 (`history-replay-skips-post-bind-ticks`)). An absent or null `ticksBefore` sets no upper bound.
  - `export function indexRecord(r: JournalRead): { redact?: { len: number; sha256: string; t: number }; verdictKey?: string; drainedFile?: string }`
  - `export function replayStep(state: ReplayState, r: JournalRead): { state: ReplayState; actions: ReplayAction[] }`
  - `export function planReplay(i: { storeId: string; files: readonly { name: string; month: string; writer: string; lines: readonly string[] }[]; ticksAfter: number; ticksBefore?: number | null }): ReplayAction[]` (`ticksBefore` defaults to null)
  - `export function nextUnmovedTicks(i: { prev: number; moved: boolean; held: boolean }): number`
  - `export interface FkRow { table: string | null; rowid: number | null; parent: string | null; fkid: number | null }`
  - `export function diffForeignKeys(baseline: readonly FkRow[], current: readonly FkRow[]): { newViolations: FkRow[]; preExisting: number }`
  - `export const FTS_SHADOWS` and `export const FTS_COLUMNS`, each `Readonly<{ blobs_fts: readonly string[]; nodes_fts: readonly string[] }>`, frozen with frozen rows
  - `export function ftsTablesHealthy(m: { tables: ReadonlySet<string>; columns: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>> }): { blobs: boolean; nodes: boolean }`
- Contract for the streaming executor (Task 25), which must agree with `planReplay`:
  - Read each journal file's first line first. Drop a file whose head names another store, counting `journal_head_mismatch` once.
  - Order what is left with `orderJournalFiles`. Merge each group by record time, ties to the earlier file in the group, keeping each file's own line order. This keeps a `file` record and its `spool` records contiguous, because one block shares one `t`.
  - Index pass: `indexRecord` over that stream, applying redact pairs.
  - Apply pass: `replayStep` over the same stream, its state's `ticksBefore` the step's version (the bind ms), so the executor applies every action `replayStep` answers and decides no tick bound of its own. `planReplay` is the whole-journal order O56 pins; Task 25's tests pin the executor's agreement with it over the cases they name, and its O48 case the executor's own order.
- Later consumers: Task 25 (recovery step), Task 23 (`diffForeignKeys`, `FTS_SHADOWS`, `ftsTablesHealthy`), Task 29 (`pairsAdded`).

**Spec:**
- §9.14 "Recovery: one step for `--restore` and `--rebuild`": the cursor; "Redaction first"; "Journal replay" (month, then head time; overlapping writers merged by `t`; a first pass indexing redact records, drain-time verdicts and `drained` records; the second applying records in order, a drain-time verdict at its line's position, a later verdict at its own); "Only drained files replay"; "Unknown records".
- §9.6: `recovery-stalled` (a cursor unmoved for 15 ticks while neither the floor nor `history-off` holds it).
- §8.4 `doctor --repair`: integrity_check, a `foreign_key_check` baseline diff refusing NEW violations (P21), the FTS self-heal (P24, no `_content` shadow for a contentless table).
- §6.4: `planReplay` is a lib decision.
- Pins: **O56** (the `planReplay` half: the apply order O48 asserts, with its two CONTROLs). This task also ships O48's replay-order pure half (Task 25 owns its tick half) and C61's pure half (Task 23 owns the verb).
- Departures:
  - D-4699 (`history-recovery-replay`)
  - B1's D-4230 (`history-journal-drained-record`)
  - B1's D-4241 (`history-redaction-journaled`)
  - B1's D-4190 (`history-epoch-confirmation`)
  - B1's D-4251 (`history-doctor-state-words`)
  - D-4700 (`history-b4-after-b2`)
  - D-4701 (`history-replay-skips-post-bind-ticks`) (NEW; defined with Task 25, which journals the tick record it skips): the upper tick bound is decided here, in `replayStep`, so the executor never decides it.
- RB7 (repair's foreign-key check): `diffForeignKeys` is the pure diff. Task 23 takes the baseline ONCE, before the repair's first chunk, persists it with the resumable cursor, and runs the second `foreign_key_check` ONCE, at completion, never per chunk; a resumed repair diffs against the original baseline.

```ts
// ===========================================================================
const RP_STORE = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000c1';
const RP_OTHER = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000c2';

const RP_S3 = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000d3';   // a later-tick confirmation's sid

const rpLine = (k: libReplay.JournalKind, t: number, f: Record<string, unknown>): string => libReplay.journalRecord(k, t, f);

  const r = libReplay.parseJournalRecord(line);

  return r.rec;
};
const rpHead = (t: number, writer = '0a1b2c3d', store = RP_STORE): string => rpLine('head', t, { store_id: store, month: '2026-10', writer });
const rpStartup = { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: RP_ID, sid: RP_S1, src: 'startup', reg: RP_S1, gen: RP_G };
const rpClear = { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: RP_ID, sid: RP_C1, src: 'clear', gen: RP_G };
const rpRecall = { v: 1, ev: 'recall', id: RP_ID, cmd: 'grep', rc: 0, ms: 40 };
const rpFile = (name: string, lines: string[]) => ({ name, month: name.slice(0, 7), writer: name.slice(8, 16), lines });

/** One writer's month: a drained file holding a startup line S then a clear line C, both decided at drain; a
 *  held file (journaled, never drained); a tick before the step's start; a later-tick confirmation; a drained
 *  file holding a recall line; a redact record; a tick after the step's start; a bind. */
function rpJournal() {

  const kC = libReplay.eventKey(RP_D1, 2);
```
