```ts
    vChainC: rpLine('verdict', 2100, { event_key: kC, kind: 'epoch-chained', ccrc_id: RP_ID, generation: RP_G, cc_session_uuid: RP_C1, cause: 'clear' }),
    vDrained1: rpLine('verdict', 2100, { event_key: 'none', kind: 'drained', file: RP_D1 }),
    fileD2: rpLine('file', 2500, { name: RP_D2 }),
    spHeld: rpLine('spool', 2500, { ord: 1, rec: { v: 1, ev: 'Stop', id: RP_ID } }),
    tickOld: rpLine('tick', 2900, { lag_ms: 800 }),
    vLater: rpLine('verdict', 3000, { event_key: 'none', kind: 'epoch-confirmed', ccrc_id: RP_ID, generation: RP_G, cc_session_uuid: RP_S3, cause: 'resume', declared_by: 'hook', by: 'later-tick' }),
    fileD3: rpLine('file', 3500, { name: RP_D3 }),
    spD3: rpLine('spool', 3500, { ord: 1, rec: rpRecall }),
    vDrained3: rpLine('verdict', 3600, { event_key: 'none', kind: 'drained', file: RP_D3 }),
    redact: rpLine('redact', 3700, { len: 40, sha256: 'a'.repeat(64) }),
    tickNew: rpLine('tick', 3800, { lag_ms: 1200 }),
    vBind: rpLine('verdict', 3900, { event_key: 'none', kind: 'bind', bind: 'restore', writer: '0a1b2c3d' }),
  };
  return { l, kS, kC, kR };
}

describe('RecoverCursor: the recovery step cursor grammar (spec 9.14; B4 adds export phases)', () => {
  it('RECOVER_PHASES is index, apply, reindex, frozen', () => {
    expect([...libReplay.RECOVER_PHASES]).toEqual(['index', 'apply', 'reindex']);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(libReplay.RECOVER_PHASES)).toBe(true);
  });
  it("round-trips each phase's form, with and without +pairs", () => {
    for (const s of ['index', 'index:2026-10.0a1b2c3d.jsonl:4096', 'apply:2026-09.0a1b2c3d.jsonl:0+pairs', 'apply+pairs', 'reindex', 'reindex:812', 'reindex:812+pairs']) {
      const c = libReplay.parseRecoverCursor(s);
      expect(c, s).not.toBeNull();
      expect(libReplay.formatRecoverCursor(c!), s).toBe(s);
    }
    expect(libReplay.parseRecoverCursor('apply:2026-10.0a1b2c3d.jsonl:96+pairs'))
      .toEqual({ phase: 'apply', file: '2026-10.0a1b2c3d.jsonl', offset: 96, blobId: null, pairsAdded: true });
  });
  it("a NULL cursor is the step's start", () => {
    expect(libReplay.parseRecoverCursor(null)).toEqual({ phase: 'index', file: null, offset: 0, blobId: null, pairsAdded: false });
  });
  it('anything else is null, never a guess', () => {
    for (const s of ['journal:120', 'index:2026-13.0a1b2c3d.jsonl:1', 'index:notes.jsonl:1', 'apply:2026-10.0a1b2c3d.jsonl:01', 'reindex:-1', 'export-blobs', '', 'index:2026-10.0a1b2c3d.jsonl:99999999999999999']) {
      expect(libReplay.parseRecoverCursor(s), s).toBeNull();
    }
    expect(() => libReplay.formatRecoverCursor({ phase: 'export-blobs', file: null, offset: 0, blobId: null, pairsAdded: false })).toThrow(TypeError);
  });
});

describe('orderJournalFiles: month, then head time, then name; overlapping files of one month merge (O56; spec 9.14)', () => {
  const f = (name: string, headT: number | null, lastT: number | null): libReplay.JournalFileFacts =>
    ({ name, month: name.slice(0, 7), writer: name.slice(8, 16), headT, lastT });
  it('O56 CONTROL: months in order, then head times; never the lexical order of the writer token', () => {
    expect(libReplay.orderJournalFiles([
      f('2026-10.00000000.jsonl', 5000, 6000), f('2026-10.ffffffff.jsonl', 1000, 1500), f('2026-09.77777777.jsonl', 10, 900),
    ])).toEqual([['2026-09.77777777.jsonl'], ['2026-10.ffffffff.jsonl'], ['2026-10.00000000.jsonl']]);
  });
  it('two writers whose time ranges overlap in one month are one group, the earlier head first', () => {
    expect(libReplay.orderJournalFiles([f('2026-10.0000000b.jsonl', 2000, 4000), f('2026-10.0000000a.jsonl', 1000, 3000)]))
      .toEqual([['2026-10.0000000a.jsonl', '2026-10.0000000b.jsonl']]);
  });
  it('a file with no head sorts last in its month, alone; another month never merges', () => {
    expect(libReplay.orderJournalFiles([f('2026-10.0000000c.jsonl', null, null), f('2026-10.0000000a.jsonl', 1000, 9000), f('2026-11.0000000a.jsonl', 100, 200)]))
      .toEqual([['2026-10.0000000a.jsonl'], ['2026-10.0000000c.jsonl'], ['2026-11.0000000a.jsonl']]);
  });
});

describe('planReplay: the journal apply order (O56 planReplay half; O48 order; spec 9.14)', () => {
  it('O56: S then C in one drained file replay in that order, each with its drain-time verdicts; a held file is skipped; a later-tick confirmation applies at its own position; redaction first', () => {
    const { l, kS, kC, kR } = rpJournal();
    const actions = libReplay.planReplay({ storeId: RP_STORE, files: [rpFile('2026-10.0a1b2c3d.jsonl', Object.values(l))], ticksAfter: 3000, ticksBefore: 3900 });
    expect(actions).toEqual([
      { do: 'redact', len: 40, sha256: 'a'.repeat(64), t: 3700 },
      { do: 'file', name: RP_D1, t: 2000 },
      { do: 'receipt', key: kS, ord: 1, rec: rpStartup, recvMs: 2000, verdicts: [rpRec(l.vFamily), rpRec(l.vConfS)] },
      { do: 'receipt', key: kC, ord: 2, rec: rpClear, recvMs: 2000, verdicts: [rpRec(l.vChainC)] },
      { do: 'file', name: RP_D2, t: 2500 },
      { do: 'skip-undrained', file: RP_D2 },
      { do: 'verdict', rec: rpRec(l.vLater) },
      { do: 'file', name: RP_D3, t: 3500 },
      { do: 'receipt', key: kR, ord: 1, rec: rpRecall, recvMs: 3500, verdicts: [] },
      { do: 'tick', t: 3800, lagMs: 1200 },
    ]);
  });

  it('O56: two writers of one month apply the earlier head first, and a tie in time goes to that file', () => {
    const DA = `${RP_ID}.1759313100000.4242.jsonl`;
    const DB = `${RP_ID}.1759313200000.4242.jsonl`;
    const a = rpFile('2026-10.ffffffff.jsonl', [
      rpHead(1000, 'ffffffff'), rpLine('file', 5000, { name: DA }), rpLine('spool', 5000, { ord: 1, rec: rpRecall }),
      rpLine('verdict', 5000, { event_key: 'none', kind: 'drained', file: DA }),
    ]);
    const b = rpFile('2026-10.00000000.jsonl', [
      rpHead(5000, '00000000'), rpLine('file', 5000, { name: DB }), rpLine('spool', 5000, { ord: 1, rec: rpRecall }),
      rpLine('verdict', 5000, { event_key: 'none', kind: 'drained', file: DB }),
    ]);
    const order = libReplay.planReplay({ storeId: RP_STORE, files: [b, a], ticksAfter: 0 })
      .flatMap((x) => (x.do === 'file' ? [`file ${x.name}`] : x.do === 'receipt' ? [`receipt ${x.key}`] : []));
    expect(order).toEqual([`file ${DA}`, `receipt ${libReplay.eventKey(DA, 1)}`, `file ${DB}`, `receipt ${libReplay.eventKey(DB, 1)}`]);
  });

  it('two writers whose times overlap merge by record time, each file in its own order', () => {
    const X1 = `${RP_ID}.1759313300000.4242.jsonl`;
    const X2 = `${RP_ID}.1759313400000.4242.jsonl`;
    const Y = `${RP_ID}.1759313500000.4242.jsonl`;
    const block = (name: string, t: number): string[] => [
      rpLine('file', t, { name }), rpLine('spool', t, { ord: 1, rec: rpRecall }), rpLine('verdict', t + 50, { event_key: 'none', kind: 'drained', file: name }),
    ];
    const x = rpFile('2026-10.0000000a.jsonl', [rpHead(1000, '0000000a'), ...block(X1, 1100), ...block(X2, 3100)]);
    const y = rpFile('2026-10.0000000b.jsonl', [rpHead(2000, '0000000b'), ...block(Y, 2100)]);
    const files = libReplay.planReplay({ storeId: RP_STORE, files: [x, y], ticksAfter: 0 })
      .filter((v): v is Extract<libReplay.ReplayAction, { do: 'file' }> => v.do === 'file').map((v) => v.name);
    expect(files).toEqual([X1, Y, X2]);
  });

  it('a file whose head names another store is skipped whole, counted once', () => {
    const foreign = rpFile('2026-10.0b0b0b0b.jsonl', [
      rpHead(1000, '0b0b0b0b', RP_OTHER), rpLine('redact', 1100, { len: 40, sha256: 'b'.repeat(64) }), rpLine('tick', 1200, { lag_ms: 5 }),
    ]);
    expect(libReplay.planReplay({ storeId: RP_STORE, files: [foreign], ticksAfter: 0 })).toEqual([{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_head_mismatch' }]);
  });

  it('a torn line, an unknown k and a v of 2 are skipped and counted; replay never throws', () => {
    const f = rpFile('2026-10.0a1b2c3d.jsonl', [rpHead(1000), '{"v":1,"k":"tick"', '{"v":1,"k":"nope","t":5}', '{"v":2,"k":"tick","t":5,"lag_ms":null}', '']);
    expect(libReplay.planReplay({ storeId: RP_STORE, files: [f], ticksAfter: 0 })).toEqual([
      { do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_line_malformed' },
      { do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_record_unknown' },
      { do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_line_malformed' },
    ]);
  });

  it("a tick at or after ticksBefore (the step's bind ms) is a recovery pass's own record: never applied (NEW history-replay-skips-post-bind-ticks)", () => {
    const { l } = rpJournal();
    const ticks = (ticksBefore: number | null) => libReplay.planReplay({ storeId: RP_STORE, files: [rpFile('2026-10.0a1b2c3d.jsonl', Object.values(l))], ticksAfter: 3000, ticksBefore })
      .filter((x) => x.do === 'tick');
    expect(ticks(3801)).toEqual([{ do: 'tick', t: 3800, lagMs: 1200 }]);
    expect(ticks(3800)).toEqual([]);
    expect(ticks(null), 'null sets no upper bound').toEqual([{ do: 'tick', t: 3800, lagMs: 1200 }]);
  });

  it('a block journaled twice gives two receipts with one key, and a re-appended verdict is indexed once', () => {
    const { l, kS } = rpJournal();
    const f = rpFile('2026-10.0a1b2c3d.jsonl', [l.head, l.fileD1, l.spS, l.fileD1, l.spS, l.vConfS, l.vConfS, l.vDrained1]);
    const receipts = libReplay.planReplay({ storeId: RP_STORE, files: [f], ticksAfter: 0 }).filter((x) => x.do === 'receipt');
    expect(receipts).toHaveLength(2);
    for (const r of receipts) expect(r).toMatchObject({ key: kS, verdicts: [rpRec(l.vConfS)] });
  });
});

describe('replayStep: one journal line, one decision, never a throw (spec 9.14 "Unknown records")', () => {
  const state = (o: Partial<libReplay.ReplayState> = {}): libReplay.ReplayState =>
    ({ storeId: RP_STORE, file: null, recvMs: 0, drained: new Set([RP_D1]), verdictsByKey: new Map(), ticksAfter: 0, ticksBefore: null, ...o });
  const read = (line: string): libReplay.JournalRead => libReplay.parseJournalRecord(line);

  it('a torn line or a newer v counts journal_line_malformed; an unknown k journal_record_unknown', () => {
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state(), read('{"v":1,"k":"tick"')).actions).toEqual([{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_line_malformed' }]);
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state(), read('{"v":2,"k":"tick","t":5,"lag_ms":null}')).actions).toEqual([{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_line_malformed' }]);
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state(), read('{"v":1,"k":"nope","t":5}')).actions).toEqual([{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_record_unknown' }]);
  });
  it('a head naming another store counts journal_head_mismatch; any head clears the draining file', () => {
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state({ file: RP_D1 }), read(rpHead(1, '0a1b2c3d', RP_OTHER))))
      .toEqual({ state: state({ file: null }), actions: [{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_head_mismatch' }] });
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state({ file: RP_D1 }), read(rpHead(1)))).toEqual({ state: state({ file: null }), actions: [] });
  });
  it('a file record sets the draining name and its receive time', () => {
    const r = libReplay.replayStep(state(), read(rpLine('file', 2000, { name: RP_D1 })));
    expect(r.state).toMatchObject({ file: RP_D1, recvMs: 2000 });
    expect(r.actions).toEqual([{ do: 'file', name: RP_D1, t: 2000 }]);
  });
  it('a spool record of a drained file is a receipt with its drain-time verdicts in journal order; of an undrained file, skip-undrained; with no file before it, malformed', () => {
    const { l, kS } = rpJournal();
    const vs = [rpRec(l.vFamily), rpRec(l.vConfS)];
    const s = state({ file: RP_D1, recvMs: 2000, verdictsByKey: new Map([[kS, vs]]) });
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(s, read(l.spS)).actions).toEqual([{ do: 'receipt', key: kS, ord: 1, rec: rpStartup, recvMs: 2000, verdicts: vs }]);
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state({ file: RP_D2 }), read(l.spHeld)).actions).toEqual([{ do: 'skip-undrained', file: RP_D2 }]);
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state(), read(l.spS)).actions).toEqual([{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_line_malformed' }]);
  });
  it('bind and drained verdicts apply nothing; a verdict keyed to a line waits for it; a verdict keyed none applies here', () => {
    const { l } = rpJournal();
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state(), read(l.vBind)).actions).toEqual([]);
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state(), read(l.vDrained1)).actions).toEqual([]);
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state(), read(l.vConfS)).actions).toEqual([]);
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state(), read(l.vLater)).actions).toEqual([{ do: 'verdict', rec: rpRec(l.vLater) }]);
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state(), read(l.redact)).actions).toEqual([]);
  });
  it('a tick at or before ticksAfter is already in the store; a later one is applied', () => {
    const { l } = rpJournal();
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state({ ticksAfter: 2900 }), read(l.tickOld)).actions).toEqual([]);
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state({ ticksAfter: 2899 }), read(l.tickOld)).actions).toEqual([{ do: 'tick', t: 2900, lagMs: 800 }]);
  });
  it("a tick at or after ticksBefore is the recovery pass's own; one before it is applied", () => {
    const { l } = rpJournal();
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state({ ticksBefore: 2900 }), read(l.tickOld)).actions).toEqual([]);
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state({ ticksBefore: 2901 }), read(l.tickOld)).actions).toEqual([{ do: 'tick', t: 2900, lagMs: 800 }]);
    expect(libReplay.replayStep(state({ ticksBefore: undefined }), read(l.tickOld)).actions, 'an absent bound bounds nothing')
      .toEqual([{ do: 'tick', t: 2900, lagMs: 800 }]);
  });
});

describe('indexRecord: the first pass indexes redact pairs, drain-time verdicts and drained files (spec 9.14)', () => {
  it('answers only for those three', () => {
    const { l, kS } = rpJournal();
    const read = (line: string): libReplay.JournalRead => libReplay.parseJournalRecord(line);
    expect(libReplay.indexRecord(read(l.redact))).toEqual({ redact: { len: 40, sha256: 'a'.repeat(64), t: 3700 } });
    expect(libReplay.indexRecord(read(l.vDrained1))).toEqual({ drainedFile: RP_D1 });
    expect(libReplay.indexRecord(read(l.vFamily))).toEqual({ verdictKey: kS });
    for (const x of [l.vLater, l.vBind, l.spS, l.fileD1, l.head, l.tickNew, '{"v":1']) expect(libReplay.indexRecord(read(x)), x).toEqual({});
  });
});

describe('nextUnmovedTicks: what recovery-stalled counts (spec 9.6, 9.14)', () => {
  it('a moved cursor resets; a hold (the floor, history-off) keeps the count; otherwise one more', () => {
    expect(libReplay.nextUnmovedTicks({ prev: 14, moved: true, held: false })).toBe(0);
    expect(libReplay.nextUnmovedTicks({ prev: 14, moved: false, held: true })).toBe(14);
    expect(libReplay.nextUnmovedTicks({ prev: 14, moved: false, held: false })).toBe(15);
  });
});

describe('diffForeignKeys: a repair refuses NEW violations only (spec 8.4 doctor --repair; P21; C61 pure half)', () => {
  const row = (table: string, rowid: number | null, parent = 'p', fkid = 0): libReplay.FkRow => ({ table, rowid, parent, fkid });
  it('rows in the baseline are pre-existing; rows outside it are new', () => {
    expect(libReplay.diffForeignKeys([row('c', 1)], [row('c', 1), row('c', 2)])).toEqual({ newViolations: [row('c', 2)], preExisting: 1 });
    expect(libReplay.diffForeignKeys([row('c', 1)], [row('c', 1)])).toEqual({ newViolations: [], preExisting: 1 });
    expect(libReplay.diffForeignKeys([], [])).toEqual({ newViolations: [], preExisting: 0 });
  });
  it('the key is (table, rowid, parent, fkid): any part differing is a different violation', () => {
    expect(libReplay.diffForeignKeys([row('c', 1)], [row('c', 1, 'q')]).newViolations).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(libReplay.diffForeignKeys([row('c', 1)], [row('c', 1, 'p', 1)]).newViolations).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(libReplay.diffForeignKeys([row('c', null)], [row('c', null)]).newViolations).toHaveLength(0);
  });
  it("SQLite's foreign_key_check rows have FkRow's shape, and the diff reads them", () => {
    const db = new ReplaySqlite(':memory:');
    try {
      db.exec('PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF');
      db.exec('CREATE TABLE p (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY); CREATE TABLE c (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, p INTEGER REFERENCES p(id))');
      db.exec('INSERT INTO c (id, p) VALUES (1, 7)');
      const before = db.prepare('PRAGMA foreign_key_check').all() as unknown as libReplay.FkRow[];
      expect(before).toEqual([row('c', 1)]);
      db.exec('INSERT INTO c (id, p) VALUES (2, 8)');
      const after = db.prepare('PRAGMA foreign_key_check').all() as unknown as libReplay.FkRow[];
      expect(libReplay.diffForeignKeys(before, after)).toEqual({ newViolations: [row('c', 2)], preExisting: 1 });
    } finally {
      db.close();
    }
  });
});

describe('FTS self-heal checks: ftsTablesHealthy over per-table shadows (spec 8.4 doctor --repair; P24)', () => {
  const measure = (db: InstanceType<typeof ReplaySqlite>) => {
    const tables = new Set((db.prepare("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table'").all() as unknown as { name: string }[]).map((r) => r.name));
    const cols = (t: string): string[] => (db.prepare('SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info(?)').all(t) as unknown as { name: string }[]).map((r) => r.name);
    return { tables, columns: { blobs_fts: tables.has('blobs_fts') ? cols('blobs_fts') : [], nodes_fts: tables.has('nodes_fts') ? cols('nodes_fts') : [] } };
  };
  it("the per-table shadow list is exactly what SQLite makes for B1's FTS_DDL: the contentless blobs_fts has no _content", () => {
    const db = new ReplaySqlite(':memory:');
    try {

      }

  it('a missing table, a missing shadow or a missing column reads broken, table by table', () => {

      expect(libReplay.ftsTablesHealthy(without('blobs_fts'))).toEqual({ blobs: false, nodes: true });
      expect(libReplay.ftsTablesHealthy(without('blobs_fts_idx'))).toEqual({ blobs: false, nodes: true });
      expect(libReplay.ftsTablesHealthy(without('nodes_fts_content'))).toEqual({ blobs: true, nodes: false });
      expect(libReplay.ftsTablesHealthy({ ...m, columns: { ...m.columns, nodes_fts: ['gist', 'topics'] } })).toEqual({ blobs: true, nodes: false });
      expect(libReplay.ftsTablesHealthy({ tables: new Set(), columns: {} })).toEqual({ blobs: false, nodes: false });
    } finally {
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement them.** Append to the end of `ccd/history/lib.mjs`:

```js

// ===========================================================================
// Recovery and repair decisions (spec §9.14 "Recovery", "Journal replay",
// "Only drained files replay", "Unknown records"; §9.6 recovery-stalled;
// §8.4 doctor --repair; §11 P21, P24; W1-B2 Task 7). Pure: the sweep's
// recovery step (Task 25) streams the journal and applies every action
// replayStep answers, deciding nothing of its own (the tick bounds included);
// planReplay is the same order over a whole journal in memory, which O56 pins;
// Task 25's tests pin the executor's agreement with it over the cases they
// name.
// D-4699 (history-recovery-replay) D-4230
// D-4241 D-4190
// D-4701 (history-replay-skips-post-bind-ticks)
// ===========================================================================

/** The recovery step's phases, in order (§9.14). `index` applies the redact records and indexes drain-time
 *  verdicts and drained files; `apply` replays the journal; `reindex` re-runs the FTS derivation when the index
 *  pass learned a pair the store lacked. B4 inserts its export phases between `apply` and `reindex` (§9.14
 *  "Export replay"): this list is that seam. D-4700 (history-b4-after-b2) */
export const RECOVER_PHASES = Object.freeze(['index', 'apply', 'reindex']);

const RECOVER_JOURNAL_CURSOR_RE = /^(index|apply)(?::([0-9]{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])\.[0-9a-f]{8}\.jsonl):(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,15}))?(\+pairs)?$/;
const RECOVER_REINDEX_CURSOR_RE = /^reindex(?::(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,15}))?(\+pairs)?$/;

/** The recovery step's cursor as derivation_state ('recover', <bind ms>) keeps it and status prints it (§9.14):
 *  `<phase>` at a phase's start, `index:<YYYY-MM>.<writer>.jsonl:<byte offset>` or `apply:…` inside the journal,
 *  `reindex:<blob_id>` inside the FTS re-derivation, then `+pairs` once the index pass learned a pair the store
 *  lacked. It is advanced in the same transaction as the records it applies. */
export function formatRecoverCursor(c) {
  if (!RECOVER_PHASES.includes(c.phase)) throw new TypeError(`formatRecoverCursor: phase outside RECOVER_PHASES: ${String(c.phase)}`);
  let s = c.phase;
  if (c.phase === 'reindex') {
    if (c.blobId !== null) s += `:${c.blobId}`;
  } else if (c.file !== null) {
    s += `:${c.file}:${c.offset}`;
  }
  return c.pairsAdded ? `${s}+pairs` : s;
}

/** The cursor back, or null when it is not one: never a guess at where to resume. A NULL column (a step just
 *  registered by a binding verb) is the step's start. */
export function parseRecoverCursor(s) {
  if (s === null) return { phase: RECOVER_PHASES[0], file: null, offset: 0, blobId: null, pairsAdded: false };
  if (typeof s !== 'string') return null;
  const j = RECOVER_JOURNAL_CURSOR_RE.exec(s);
  if (j !== null) {
    const offset = j[3] === undefined ? 0 : Number(j[3]);
    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(offset)) return null;
    return { phase: j[1], file: j[2] ?? null, offset, blobId: null, pairsAdded: j[4] !== undefined };
  }
  const r = RECOVER_REINDEX_CURSOR_RE.exec(s);
  if (r !== null) {
    const blobId = r[1] === undefined ? null : Number(r[1]);
    if (blobId !== null && !Number.isSafeInteger(blobId)) return null;
    return { phase: 'reindex', file: null, offset: 0, blobId, pairsAdded: r[2] !== undefined };
  }
  return null;
}

const journalCmpText = (a, b) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0);
const journalCmpHead = (a, b) => (a === b ? 0 : a === null ? 1 : b === null ? -1 : a - b);
const journalFileOrder = (a, b) => journalCmpText(a.month, b.month) || journalCmpHead(a.headT, b.headT) || journalCmpText(a.name, b.name);

/** The journal files' apply order (§9.14 "Journal replay"): by the month in the name, then by the head
 *  record's time, then by name (code-unit order, never the locale's: DM8). Files of one month whose
 *  [headT, lastT] ranges overlap (a store run on two boxes at once, against §6.9's rule) form ONE group, which
 *  the caller merges by record time. A file with no readable head sorts last in its month, alone. */
export function orderJournalFiles(files) {
  const groups = [];
  let cur = null;
  for (const f of [...files].sort(journalFileOrder)) {
    const hi = f.lastT ?? f.headT;
    if (cur !== null && cur.month === f.month && f.headT !== null && cur.hi !== null && f.headT <= cur.hi) {
      cur.names.push(f.name);
      if (hi !== null && hi > cur.hi) cur.hi = hi;
      continue;
    }
    cur = { month: f.month, hi, names: [f.name] };
    groups.push(cur);
  }
  return groups.map((g) => g.names);
}

/** The first pass over one record (§9.14): a `redact` pair, a drain-time verdict (one keyed to its spool line's
 *  event_key) to apply at that line, or a `drained` record naming a file whose spool records may replay. */
export function indexRecord(r) {
  if (r.kind !== 'record') return {};
  const rec = r.rec;
  if (rec.k === 'redact') return { redact: { len: rec.len, sha256: rec.sha256, t: rec.t } };
  if (rec.k !== 'verdict') return {};
  if (rec.kind === 'drained') return { drainedFile: rec.file };
  if (rec.kind === 'bind' || rec.event_key === 'none') return {};
  return { verdictKey: rec.event_key };
}

/** The second pass over one record (§9.14). It never reads $REG and never re-decides: a spool record of a
 *  drained file becomes a receipt carrying the verdicts the drain took from it, in journal order, which the
 *  executor applies through decideEpochLine and the drain's own receipt functions; a verdict keyed to a line
 *  waits for that line; a verdict keyed `none` (a later confirmation, a backfill mapping, an operator's import)
 *  applies at its own position. A spool record whose file has no `drained` record is skipped: the file is still
 *  in .draining/ with its sidecar, and the live drain decides it after the step, or B1 set it aside after journaling
 *  it, into .draining/rejected/ or .draining/planted/<area>/, where nothing drains it; either way the lost store held
 *  none of its lines (the executor, Task 25's undrainedFileKept, tells a kept file from a gone one). A tick at or before the newest
 *  tick the store held when the step began (`ticksAfter`) is already there; one at or after the step's bind ms
 *  (`ticksBefore`, when it is a number) is a recovery pass's own record, journaled after the bind
 *  D-4701 (history-replay-skips-post-bind-ticks). A line that does not parse, or a `v` newer than
 *  this build, counts journal_line_malformed; an unknown kind journal_record_unknown; a head naming another
 *  store journal_head_mismatch. Nothing here throws on a record. */
export function replayStep(state, r) {
  if (r.kind === 'malformed' || r.kind === 'newer') return { state, actions: [{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_line_malformed' }] };
  if (r.kind === 'unknown') return { state, actions: [{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_record_unknown' }] };
  const rec = r.rec;
  switch (rec.k) {
    case 'head':
      if (rec.store_id !== state.storeId) return { state: { ...state, file: null }, actions: [{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_head_mismatch' }] };
      return { state: { ...state, file: null }, actions: [] };
    case 'file':
      return { state: { ...state, file: rec.name, recvMs: rec.t }, actions: [{ do: 'file', name: rec.name, t: rec.t }] };
    case 'spool': {
      if (state.file === null) return { state, actions: [{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_line_malformed' }] };
      if (!state.drained.has(state.file)) return { state, actions: [{ do: 'skip-undrained', file: state.file }] };
      const key = eventKey(state.file, rec.ord);
      return { state, actions: [{ do: 'receipt', key, ord: rec.ord, rec: rec.rec, recvMs: state.recvMs, verdicts: [...(state.verdictsByKey.get(key) ?? [])] }] };
    }
    case 'verdict':
      if (rec.kind === 'bind' || rec.kind === 'drained') return { state, actions: [] };
      if (rec.event_key !== 'none') return { state, actions: [] };
      return { state, actions: [{ do: 'verdict', rec }] };
    case 'redact':
      return { state, actions: [] };
    case 'tick': {
      const before = typeof state.ticksBefore !== 'number' || rec.t < state.ticksBefore;
      return { state, actions: rec.t > state.ticksAfter && before ? [{ do: 'tick', t: rec.t, lagMs: rec.lag_ms }] : [] };
    }
    default:
      return { state, actions: [{ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_record_unknown' }] };
  }
}

/** One merge group's records by record time, each file's own order kept, a tie to the earlier file in the group.
 *  A journal block (a `file` record and its `spool` records) shares one `t`, so a block is never split. */
function mergeJournalByTime(files) {
  const pos = files.map(() => 0);
  const out = [];
  for (;;) {
    let pick = -1;
    for (let f = 0; f < files.length; f += 1) {
      if (pos[f] >= files[f].recs.length) continue;
      if (pick < 0 || files[f].recs[pos[f]].t < files[pick].recs[pos[pick]].t) pick = f;
    }
    if (pick < 0) return out;
    out.push(files[pick].recs[pos[pick]].read);
    pos[pick] += 1;
  }
}

/** The whole replay of one store's journal, in memory (§9.14; the O56 pin). A file whose head names another
 *  store is dropped, counted once. The rest run in orderJournalFiles' order, each group merged by record time. A
 *  first pass indexes every redact pair (applied before anything else: "Redaction first"), every drain-time
 *  verdict by event_key (an identical re-appended verdict once) and every drained file; the second runs
 *  replayStep over the same stream. Duplicate receipts are left to the executor's receipt upsert. `ticksBefore`
 *  (the step's bind ms) defaults to null, no upper tick bound. */
export function planReplay({ storeId, files, ticksAfter, ticksBefore = null }) {
  const skips = [];
  const kept = [];
  for (const f of files) {
    const recs = [];
    let headT = null;
    let lastT = null;
    let foreign = false;
    for (const line of f.lines) {
      if (line === '') continue;
      const read = parseJournalRecord(line);
      if (recs.length === 0 && read.kind === 'record' && read.rec.k === 'head') {
        if (read.rec.store_id !== storeId) { foreign = true; break; }
        headT = read.rec.t;
      }
      const t = read.kind === 'record' ? read.rec.t : (lastT ?? headT ?? 0);
      if (read.kind === 'record') lastT = lastT === null ? t : Math.max(lastT, t);
      recs.push({ read, t });
    }
    if (foreign) {
      skips.push({ do: 'skip', counter: 'journal_head_mismatch' });
      continue;
    }
    kept.push({ name: f.name, month: f.month, writer: f.writer, headT, lastT, recs });
  }
  const byName = new Map(kept.map((f) => [f.name, f]));
  const stream = orderJournalFiles(kept).flatMap((g) => mergeJournalByTime(g.map((n) => byName.get(n))));
  const redacts = [];
  const seenPairs = new Set();
  const seenVerdicts = new Set();
  const verdictsByKey = new Map();
  const drained = new Set();
  for (const read of stream) {
    const ix = indexRecord(read);
    if (ix.redact !== undefined) {
      const pair = `${ix.redact.len}:${ix.redact.sha256}`;
      if (!seenPairs.has(pair)) {
        seenPairs.add(pair);
        redacts.push({ do: 'redact', ...ix.redact });
      }
    }
    if (ix.drainedFile !== undefined) drained.add(ix.drainedFile);
    if (ix.verdictKey !== undefined) {
      const same = canonicalJson(read.rec);
      if (!seenVerdicts.has(same)) {
        seenVerdicts.add(same);
        const list = verdictsByKey.get(ix.verdictKey) ?? [];
        list.push(read.rec);
        verdictsByKey.set(ix.verdictKey, list);
      }
    }
  }
  let state = { storeId, file: null, recvMs: 0, drained, verdictsByKey, ticksAfter, ticksBefore };
  const applied = [];
  for (const read of stream) {
    const step = replayStep(state, read);
    state = step.state;
    applied.push(...step.actions);
  }
  return [...skips, ...redacts, ...applied];
}

/** The recovery step's unmoved-tick count, kept in meta HEALTH_META.recoverUnmovedTicks (§9.6: FAIL
 *  recovery-stalled at RECOVERY_STALL_TICKS). A moved cursor resets it; a tick the floor or history-off held
 *  leaves it; any other tick adds one. */
export function nextUnmovedTicks({ prev, moved, held }) {
  if (moved) return 0;
  return held ? prev : prev + 1;
}

// derived from lossless-claw src/plugin/lcm-doctor-rollover-splits.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
const foreignKeyKey = (row) => [row.table ?? '', row.rowid ?? '', row.parent ?? '', row.fkid ?? ''].join('\0');

/** doctor --repair's foreign-key proof (§8.4, P21): the violations `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` reports at the
 *  repair's completion, against the baseline taken ONCE before its first chunk and persisted with its resumable
 *  cursor, so a resumed repair diffs against the original baseline (RB7; Task 23 runs the check twice per repair,
 *  never per chunk). A violation is keyed by (table, rowid, parent, fkid); one
 *  outside the baseline is NEW, and a repair that made one is refused. No v1 table is WITHOUT ROWID, so rowid is
 *  never NULL for a v1 row. */
export function diffForeignKeys(baseline, current) {
  const base = new Set(baseline.map(foreignKeyKey));
  const newViolations = [];
  let preExisting = 0;
  for (const row of current) {
    if (base.has(foreignKeyKey(row))) preExisting += 1;
    else newViolations.push(row);
  }
  return { newViolations, preExisting };
}

// derived from lossless-claw src/db/migration.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
/** Each FTS table's shadow tables, listed per table (P24): the contentless blobs_fts (content='',
 *  contentless_delete=1) has no `_content` shadow, so a list naming one for every table would read a healthy
 *  index as broken and rebuild it on every repair. */
export const FTS_SHADOWS = Object.freeze({
  blobs_fts: Object.freeze(['blobs_fts_config', 'blobs_fts_data', 'blobs_fts_docsize', 'blobs_fts_idx']),
  nodes_fts: Object.freeze(['nodes_fts_config', 'nodes_fts_content', 'nodes_fts_data', 'nodes_fts_docsize', 'nodes_fts_idx']),
});
/** Each FTS table's columns, as B1's FTS_DDL creates them. */
export const FTS_COLUMNS = Object.freeze({
  blobs_fts: Object.freeze(['body']),
  nodes_fts: Object.freeze(['gist', 'topics', 'refs']),
});

/** Whether each FTS table is whole (§8.4 doctor --repair's self-heal, P24): the table, every shadow it should
 *  have, and every column. The store adapter measures `tables` (sqlite_master) and `columns` (pragma_table_info);
 *  the repair rebuilds a table this answers false for. */
export function ftsTablesHealthy({ tables, columns }) {
  const healthy = (t) => tables.has(t) && FTS_SHADOWS[t].every((s) => tables.has(s))
    && FTS_COLUMNS[t].every((c) => (columns[t] ?? []).includes(c));
  return { blobs: healthy('blobs_fts'), nodes: healthy('nodes_fts') };
}
```

  - The `\0` in `foreignKeyKey` is the two-character escape in source, never a raw NUL byte.
  - The two `derived from lossless-claw` comments are the P21 and P24 markers. B1's `license.test.ts` pins them against Step 6's entries: one entry per (ours, upstream) pair.

```ts
export const RECOVER_PHASES: readonly string[];
export interface RecoverCursor { phase: string; file: string | null; offset: number; blobId: number | null; pairsAdded: boolean }

export interface JournalFileFacts { name: string; month: string; writer: string; headT: number | null; lastT: number | null }

export type ReplayAction =
  | { do: 'file'; name: string; t: number }
  | { do: 'receipt'; key: string; ord: number; rec: Record<string, unknown>; recvMs: number; verdicts: JournalRecord[] }
  | { do: 'skip-undrained'; file: string }

  | { do: 'redact'; len: number; sha256: string; t: number }
  | { do: 'tick'; t: number; lagMs: number | null }
  | { do: 'skip'; counter: 'journal_line_malformed' | 'journal_record_unknown' | 'journal_head_mismatch' };
export interface ReplayState {
  storeId: string; file: string | null; recvMs: number;
  drained: ReadonlySet<string>; verdictsByKey: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly JournalRecord[]>; ticksAfter: number;
  ticksBefore?: number | null;
}
export function indexRecord(r: JournalRead): { redact?: { len: number; sha256: string; t: number }; verdictKey?: string; drainedFile?: string };
export function replayStep(state: ReplayState, r: JournalRead): { state: ReplayState; actions: ReplayAction[] };
export function planReplay(i: {
  storeId: string; files: readonly { name: string; month: string; writer: string; lines: readonly string[] }[]; ticksAfter: number;
  ticksBefore?: number | null;
}): ReplayAction[];
export function nextUnmovedTicks(i: { prev: number; moved: boolean; held: boolean }): number;
export interface FkRow { table: string | null; rowid: number | null; parent: string | null; fkid: number | null }
export function diffForeignKeys(baseline: readonly FkRow[], current: readonly FkRow[]): { newViolations: FkRow[]; preExisting: number };

export const FTS_COLUMNS: Readonly<{ blobs_fts: readonly string[]; nodes_fts: readonly string[] }>;
export function ftsTablesHealthy(m: { tables: ReadonlySet<string>; columns: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>> }): { blobs: boolean; nodes: boolean };
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Write the mutation runner.** It is the same gitignored scratch tool as Task 5's: Tasks 1–7, 7A, 7B and 8 write this same file, byte for byte, so each task stands alone and rewriting it changes nothing. Like every copy, it spawns vitest with `maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024` (coordinator ruling R-runner). From the repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <<'EOF'
// .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs: measures each guard RED with it mutated, then GREEN with
// it restored (the B2 plan's mutation-pin rule). Run from server/, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least
// 600000 ms:
//   node ../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <mutants.json>
// A mutant is {name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}. `file` is repo-relative, `test` is
// server/-relative, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. The
// pristine file is copied to scratch/keep/<file with '/' as '__'>.orig BEFORE it is touched, and the copy is
// removed only after the file is restored from it. A kill no handler sees therefore leaves the original findable,
// and the next run REFUSES while any copy is left. To restore by hand, from the repository root:
//   for f in .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/*.orig; do t="$(basename "$f" .orig)"; cp "$f" "${t//__//}" && rm "$f"; done
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const KEEP = '../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep';
mkdirSync(KEEP, { recursive: true });
const left = readdirSync(KEEP).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.orig'));
if (left.length > 0) {
  console.log(`REFUSED: ${left.join(', ')} in ${KEEP}. An earlier run was interrupted and a source may hold a mutant: restore as this file's header says.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const keepOf = (file) => `${KEEP}/${file.replaceAll('/', '__')}.orig`;
const restoreAll = () => {
  for (const n of readdirSync(KEEP)) {
    if (!n.endsWith('.orig')) continue;
    copyFileSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`, `../${n.slice(0, -'.orig'.length).replaceAll('__', '/')}`);
    rmSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`);
  }
};
// Every way out restores: the loop's end, process.exit and an uncaught throw all emit 'exit', and a signal is
// turned into an exit. A signal sent while the synchronous loop holds the thread is handled after the current
// child returns; a Ctrl-C also reaches the vitest child, and the loop stops on the child's signal below.
process.on('exit', restoreAll);
for (const s of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) process.on(s, () => process.exit(130));
// maxBuffer: past Node's default (1 MiB) spawnSync kills the child (ENOBUFS, signal SIGTERM, measured), which the
// loop below reads as an interrupt. Each large-operand case asserts a boolean or a length, so a red prints no big diff.
const vitest = (test, filter) => spawnSync('./node_modules/.bin/vitest', ['run', test, '-t', filter], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 });
const mutants = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
let bad = 0;
for (const m of mutants) {
  const target = `../${m.file}`;
  if (!existsSync(target)) { console.log(`NO SUCH FILE       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  const keep = keepOf(m.file);
  copyFileSync(target, keep);
  let src = readFileSync(keep, 'utf8');
  let unique = true;
  for (const e of m.edits) {
    const at = src.indexOf(e.anchor);
    if (at < 0 || src.indexOf(e.anchor, at + 1) >= 0) { unique = false; break; }
    src = src.slice(0, at) + e.replacement + src.slice(at + e.anchor.length);
  }
  if (!unique) { rmSync(keep); console.log(`ANCHOR NOT UNIQUE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  writeFileSync(target, src);
  const red = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  copyFileSync(keep, target);
  rmSync(keep);
  if (red.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${red.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  const failed = /Tests\s+(\d+) failed/.exec(red.stdout)?.[1] ?? '?';
  if (red.status === 0) { console.log(`STAYED GREEN       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`red (${failed} failed)   ${m.name}`);
  const green = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  if (green.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${green.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  if (green.status !== 0) { console.log(`RED AFTER RESTORE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`green              ${m.name}`);
}
console.log(bad === 0 ? 'every guard measured red, then green' : `${bad} guard(s) not measured`);
process.exit(bad === 0 ? 0 : 1);
EOF
```

Departures: none (rev 3.5 is the rule, §8.3 "Where it runs" and §6.2 included).

Choices this task makes (each listed in the PR body):
- **K per unit, from its own folded alphabet:** 72 bits, at most the unit's length, rounded down to the ladder. Rounding down only masks more, and the ladder bounds a reading to five passes.
- **Seeds:** a gram seeds only with a third of its characters distinct and a digit or both cases. This keeps a padding run, a wordy unit or a token's wordy prefix from masking prose. Its price depends on the unit's alphabet (measured on the prototype, 2000 random 40-character values each, and 5.4M grams of `randomBytes(30).toString('base64url')`, spec §8.3 "Seeds", review finding V36): a mixed-case token's K-wide gram fails it about once in 10^4, a base64url one's about once in 5 × 10^4 (measured 2.07e-5, 112 of 5.4M grams, where the 2000-value sample had seen none), but a one-case `[a-z0-9]` token's about once in 100 (9.8e-3) and a base32 `[A-Z2-7]` one's about once in 18 (5.6e-2), because a digit-free stretch of one case seeds nothing. A whole value, or any print of it that holds one seeding gram, is still masked to its run; what a one-case unit leaves is a partial print of a digit-free K-window alone (the case `the seed rule's price` pins both halves). Relaxing the rule for one-case units would let a wordy one-case unit (`production-database-01`) mask its words in prose, so the price is named instead (spec §8.3 "What it cannot see").
- **unicode61's own fold (ruling R-fold).** `beltFold` drops exactly the 25 combining marks unicode61 drops at remove_diacritics 1, folds a character whose canonical decomposition is an ASCII letter or digit alone, or that and one such mark, and folds U+017F and U+1E9B to `s`, as unicode61's case fold does. Every other mark is a boundary, as it is to unicode61 (the `\p{Mn}` rule this replaces joined 1,794 marks unicode61 splits at, and folded 114 letters with two marks that unicode61 keeps). One case compares it with node:sqlite's tokenizer on every code point U+0080..U+2FFFF.
- **Linear widening (ruling R-linear).** A cover that starts at or before the end its span was widened to joins that span, so no character is widened over twice. The old rule pushed a new span for a cover inside an already widened run and rescanned the rest of the run at each one: `(v.slice(0, 14) + 'x').repeat(n)` cost 1.1 s at 64 KiB and 56 s at 512 KiB (review measurement); now 2.6-2.9 ms and 18 ms on the prototype. The pin's glue letter never equals the gram's next character, `v[14]` case folded (it is `z` when `v[14]` is `x` or `X`): with an equal one, about 3% of draws, every window across a glue matched a gram, the run was one cover and the old rule's mutant (t) stayed green (finding V10).
- **No mark after a bare backslash.** The left widening stops before a JSON escape's letter or hex digit, and a span that starts inside an escape takes the whole escape, so `redactFinal` over a `--json` envelope never leaves `\[redacted]` (finding R31: `JSON.parse` threw `Bad escaped character`). B1's layer 1 still marks a run that IS a pair whole, so a registered value whose first character is an escape letter, printed right after that escape's backslash, is B1's case and not changed here.
- **Three escape readings:** as written, sequences removed, introducers removed. Fields also read each JSON decode. An index reading does not, because `redactForIndex` decodes level by level, each level through this belt.
- **Mask extent:** a window union widened to its run. Where the run IS the value, that is layer 1's own output.
- **Glue windows are hash-only.** They need no value, so a rotated value and a sessions.json hash glued by `_` or `-` are redacted by their pair. A run past either budget is marked whole: its hash count (`GLUE_HASH_FLOOR` plus a quarter of its length) or its hashed window characters (`GLUE_HASH_BYTES_FLOOR`, 64 KiB, *chosen*, plus 4 × its length, each window charged its length before it is hashed; spec §8.3, review R69). A count bound alone costs the count times the longest registered pair: 4.2 s of sha256 for 1 MiB of runs twice a 16 KiB unit's length on Node 24.14.1 (measured), 5 ms with the byte budget. The case `the glue windows are bounded in hashed bytes` pins it, with mutant (k2).
- **`beltAll`:** a re-derivation probe counts every layer-4 and glue-window hit as owed. Both depend on loaded values and on code BELT_VERSION tags, which the owed-pair argument does not cover.
- **A generation records the version it opened under (ruling R-version).** `fts_belt` keeps `gv` beside an open `gen`. `decideBelt` keeps `gen` only when `gv` is the code's BELT_VERSION, and when the belt is due and the open generation's record is absent or another version's it answers `restart`, which makes `rederivePlan` start a belt generation from cursor 0. `beltAfterGeneration` stamps `gv`, the version the walk ran under. So a version that deploys mid-walk is stamped only after a walk that ran wholly under it; the reviewers measured the old rule stamping `{"v":2,"rids":[3,4],"gen":null}` over a walk opened under version 1.
- **A witness, not a tick count (the lib half of ruling R-rollback).** `beltWitnessMoved(state, witness)` is the pure comparison; Task 7B measures the witness and records it. A state with no `w` claims nothing.
- **B1's F2 case is reshaped, not flipped.** The glue windows now clean its `v_tail` rows, which would leave its phrase-path mutant nothing to find. Its value is printed with its own `-` as spaces, a shape no layer removes and a phrase still finds, so the pin keeps biting.
- **Fixture values start `QP` and end in a digit.** A random first character flakes the exact-text case about 7% of the time, and porter stemming may rewrite a term that ends in a letter. In the lib describe they also hold `e`, `A` and `o` at offsets 9, 19 and 29, so the precomposed shape (finding R16) has a precomposed acute form at each of its three offsets on every draw; the `base64url` width fixture ends in `0_-`, so its folded alphabet is always 38 characters (a random draw without a digit, `_` or `-` answered 16 about once in 1,300, finding R12).
- **Display shows what the index holds.** The belt's decoded readings find only a unit this process loaded. A value known as a pair alone (a rotated value, a `sessions.json` hash) glued to a literal escape (B1's review 316 F2 shape, `\n<value>`) is separated only by the index's escape readings. So up to `DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX`, `redactForDisplay` IS `redactForIndex`: a field is shown as it came, redacted, unless a deeper JSON-escape reading removed something; then that reading is shown, decoded. A field whose escapes hide nothing is shown byte for byte as `redactField` shows it.
- **Past the bound, span by span.** A longer field (expand reads a sidecar up to `SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX`) is redacted once by `redactField`. Then each maximal span of `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` characters and backslashes that holds a backslash and a run character is read through `redactForIndex` alone, and replaced by the mark when any of its readings removed something. The cost stays linear, and a long JSON text's ordinary escapes print as they are. Residual, past the bound only: a value that only the context layer sees after a decode, with no backslash touching it.
- **`nodes_fts` takes each column through `entryIndexText`.** The gist, each topic and each ref value are read one by one, then topics and refs are joined one per line, as Tasks 8 and 9 index them. The stored fields keep the derivation's `redactField` (Tasks 4 and 8): the escape readings run where text leaves the store, as display or as an index term. So a `nodes_fts` row is a function of its node's stored fields and the pair index's answers alone, which is what lets Task 29's node step recompute and compare it.
- What stays is spec rev 3.5's named residual (§6.2 "What the belt cannot see"): a hash-only unit glued by a letter or digit. Glued on its right (`<value>x`), its index term starts with the value, so a prefix `MATCH` of the value, or of any prefix of it, answers it, and a read verb prints it. Glued on its left only, its term is a different word and no `MATCH` on the value answers it.

```ts
// ── W1-B2 Task 7A: the substring belt (spec §8.3 layer 4 and layer 1's glue windows, §6.2 "The belt"; rev 3.5; O59) ──
// Coordinator rulings 4019 and 4043, reviews 344 F9 and 351. Every fixture value is minted at runtime. The leak shapes
// are the ones B1 measured (review 351; fr2's "For the coordinator" items 1-2): a stray `ESC[` whose final byte takes a
// value's second character behind a mid-span `ESC[0m` (31 of 32 characters one term; 27 when a closing sequence splits
// off the last four), and a value glued to a neighbour by `_`, `-` or a letter. A "belt leak" is a stretch of
// beltWidth(value) consecutive characters of the value, ASCII case folded (unicode61 folds case).
describe('the substring belt (W1-B2 Task 7A; spec §8.3 layer 4, §6.2; O59 lib half)', () => {
  const ESC = String.fromCharCode(27);
  const BS = String.fromCharCode(92);
  const AL = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789';
  const alnum = (n: number): string => Array.from(historyCrypto.randomBytes(n), (b) => AL[b % 62]!).join('');
  /** 32 characters: `Q`, then `P` (a CSI final byte a stray `ESC[` takes), then 29 more, then a digit (review 351's shape).
   *  Offsets 9, 19 and 29 are `e`, `A` and `o`, each with a precomposed acute form (the precomposed shape, finding R16). */
  const mint = (): string => `QP${alnum(7)}e${alnum(9)}A${alnum(9)}o${alnum(1)}7`;
  const ACUTE = String.fromCharCode(0x301);
  /** The longest stretch `out` shares with `v`, case folded and with every nonspacing mark dropped. That is unicode61's
   *  fold for every character these fixtures print (U+0301 and precomposed acute letters); beltFold's own case pins the
   *  exact fold over every code point. */
  const shared = (out: string, v: string): number => {
    const o = out.normalize('NFD').replace(/\p{Mn}/gu, '').toLowerCase();
    const w = v.toLowerCase();
    let best = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < w.length; i += 1) for (let j = i + best + 1; j <= w.length && o.includes(w.slice(i, j)); j += 1) best = j - i;
    return best;
  };
  const strip = (s: string): string => s.replace(new RegExp(`${ESC}\\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]`, 'g'), '');
  const decoded = (s: string): string => s.replace(/\\u([0-9a-fA-F]{4})/g, (_m, h: string) => String.fromCharCode(parseInt(h, 16)));
  const shapes = (v: string): Array<[string, string]> => [
    ['a stray ESC[ behind a mid-span ESC[0m takes the second character (31 of 32)', `w ${v[0]}${ESC}[0m${ESC}[${v.slice(1)} y`],
    ['the same, a closing ESC[0m before the last four (27 of 32)', `w ${v[0]}${ESC}[0m${ESC}[${v.slice(1, 28)}${ESC}[0m${v.slice(28)} y`],
    ['glued to letters with no separator', `note ab${v}cd end`],
    ['printed in upper case', `note ${v.toUpperCase()} end`],
    ['glued by _', `note ab_${v}_tail end`],
    ['glued by - on both sides', `note ab-${v}-tail end`],
    ['three stray ESC[ each take a character', `note ${v.slice(0, 8)}${ESC}[${v.slice(8, 18)}${ESC}[${v.slice(18)} end`],
    ['a combining mark after every tenth character', `note ${[...v].map((c, i) => (i % 10 === 9 ? `${c}${ACUTE}` : c)).join('')} end`],
    // é, Á and ó as one code point each: unicode61 folds each to its letter, so the term holds the value whole.
    ['every tenth character precomposed with an acute, glued by letters', `note ab${[...v].map((c, i) => (i % 10 === 9 ? `${c}${ACUTE}`.normalize('NFC') : c)).join('')}cd end`],
  ];
  const beltIdx = (values: string[]): libRedact.PairIndex =>
    libRedact.makePairIndex(libRedact.secretPairs(values).pairs, libRedact.makeBelt(libRedact.beltUnits(values)));
  const pairIdx = (values: string[]): libRedact.PairIndex => libRedact.makePairIndex(libRedact.secretPairs(values).pairs);

  it('CONTROL: with pairs alone, the measured shapes still leak 31, 27, 32 and 32 characters', () => {
    const v = mint();
    const idx = pairIdx([v]);
    expect(shapes(v).slice(0, 4).map(([, t]) => shared(libRedact.entryIndexText(t, idx), v))).toEqual([31, 27, 32, 32]);

  it('beltFold is unicode61\'s own fold: node:sqlite\'s tokenizer agrees on every code point U+0080..U+2FFFF', async () => {
    const { DatabaseSync } = await import('node:sqlite');
    const db = new DatabaseSync(':memory:');
    try {
      // B1's tables use 'porter unicode61'; porter only stems ASCII words, so unicode61 alone is the fold.
      db.exec("CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE t USING fts5(b, tokenize='unicode61')");
      db.exec("CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE tv USING fts5vocab(t, 'instance')");
      const ins = db.prepare('INSERT INTO t (rowid, b) VALUES (?, ?)');
      const cps: number[] = [];
      db.exec('BEGIN');
      for (let cp = 0x80; cp <= 0x2ffff; cp += 1) {
        if (cp >= 0xd800 && cp <= 0xdfff) continue;   // a lone surrogate is no character
        cps.push(cp);
        ins.run(cp, `q${String.fromCodePoint(cp)}q`);
      }
      db.exec('COMMIT');
      const terms = new Map<number, string[]>();
      for (const r of db.prepare('SELECT doc, term FROM tv').all() as { doc: number; term: string }[]) {
        const a = terms.get(Number(r.doc)) ?? [];
        a.push(r.term);
        terms.set(Number(r.doc), a);
      }
      const AL = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789';
      /** unicode61's reading of `q<cp>q`: dropped (-1: one term `qq`), an ASCII letter or digit (its belt code, 1-36),
       *  or anything else (0: a boundary, or a character no ASCII term can hold). */
      const sqlite = (cp: number): number => {
        const a = terms.get(cp) ?? [];
        if (a.length === 1 && a[0] === 'qq') return -1;
        const m = a.length === 1 ? a[0]!.slice(1, -1) : '';
        return m.length === 1 && AL.includes(m) ? AL.indexOf(m) + 1 : 0;
      };
      expect(cps.length, 'CONTROL: every code point was read').toBe(0x2ffff - 0x80 + 1 - 0x800);
      expect([0xe9, 0x301, 0x305, 0x17f, 0x1d5, 0x2010].map(sqlite), 'CONTROL: é is e, U+0301 dropped, U+0305 a boundary, ſ is s, Ǖ (two marks) kept, a hyphen a boundary')
        .toEqual([5, -1, 0, 19, 0, 0]);
      const diverge = cps.filter((cp) => libRedact.beltFold(cp) !== sqlite(cp)).map((cp) => cp.toString(16));
      expect(diverge.length, `diverging code points (first 20): ${diverge.slice(0, 20).join(' ')}`).toBe(0);
    } finally { db.close(); }
  });

  it('the widening is linear: a run that repeats a 14-wide gram glued by an uncovered letter, 8x longer, costs under 16x', () => {
    const v = mint();
    const idx = beltIdx([v]);
    // The glue letter never equals the gram's next character, case folded: were it v[14] (x or X, 8 draws in 256),
    // the window crossing each glue would match a gram of v, the run would be one cover, and mutant (t) stayed green
    // (finding V10 measured it: 117 ms and 238 ms).
    const g = v[14]!.toLowerCase() === 'x' ? 'z' : 'x';
    const shape = (bytes: number): string => `${v.slice(0, 14)}${g}`.repeat(Math.ceil(bytes / 15));
    const best = (t: string): number => {
      let m = Infinity;
      for (let k = 0; k < 5; k += 1) {
        const t0 = performance.now();
        const out = libRedact.beltMask(t, idx.belt, true);
        m = Math.min(m, performance.now() - t0);
        expect(out === libRedact.REDACTED_MARK, 'the whole run is one mark').toBe(true);
      }
      return m;
    };
    best(shape(4096));   // warm-up
    const small = best(shape(64 * 1024));
    const large = best(shape(512 * 1024));
    // Measured on the prototype (Node 24.14.1): 2.6-2.9 ms and 18 ms, a ratio near 7. The per-cover rescan this
    // replaces cost 0.6 s and 37 s here (review: 1.1 s and 56 s), a ratio near 64.
    expect(large / Math.max(small, 0.5), `64 KiB ${small.toFixed(1)} ms, 512 KiB ${large.toFixed(1)} ms`).toBeLessThan(16);
    expect(large, '512 KiB within the bound').toBeLessThan(2_000);
  });

  it('a --json string stays valid: no widening takes a JSON escape\'s letter or hex digit, and a span that starts inside an escape takes it whole', () => {
    const v = mint();
    const idx = beltIdx([v]);
    const w = libRedact.beltWidth(v);
    for (const pre of ['a\n', 'a\u0001', 'grep x\t', 'q"']) {
      const s = libRedact.redactFinal(JSON.stringify({ t: `${pre}${v}y`, u: `x${v}\n` }), idx);
      let o: { t: string; u: string } | null = null;
      try { o = JSON.parse(s); } catch { o = null; }
      expect(o, `${JSON.stringify(pre)}: ${s}`).not.toBeNull();
      expect(Math.max(shared(o!.t, v), shared(o!.u, v)), s).toBeLessThan(w);
      expect(s).toContain(libRedact.REDACTED_MARK);
    }
    expect(libRedact.redactFinal(JSON.stringify({ t: `a\n${v}` }), idx), 'the escape stays, the value goes').toBe(`{"t":"a\\n${libRedact.REDACTED_MARK}"}`);
    // A unit that begins with `n`, printed after a backslash-n: the literal reading's cover starts on the escape's
    // letter, and the span takes the whole escape.
    const nv = `n${v}`;
    const s2 = libRedact.redactFinal(JSON.stringify({ t: `a\n${v}zz` }), beltIdx([nv]));
    expect(s2, 'the span took the escape whole').toBe(`{"t":"a${libRedact.REDACTED_MARK}"}`);
  });
});

// ── W1-B2 Task 7A: the index's escape readings for display and nodes_fts (spec §8.3 "Where it runs", §6.2, rev 3.5;
// B1's D-4343 and D-4419; B1's run 302 notes) ──
describe('lib: nodeIndexTexts and redactForDisplay read every escape level the index reads (W1-B2 Task 7A)', () => {
  /** A 40-character value built at runtime (no key-shaped literal in a public repo): one run, registered as a pair.
   *  The index below holds its pair and no belt, as a rotated value or a sessions.json hash is held. */
  const V = Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, i) => 'abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789'[(i * 7 + 3) % 31]).join('');
  const idx = libRedact.makePairIndex(libRedact.secretPairs([V]).pairs);
  /** What a tool printing JSON leaves in a row: a literal backslash and `n` glued onto the value (B1's review 316 F2). */
  const glued = JSON.stringify({ text: `\n${V}` });
  /** A backslash-u-005c chain: two decodes separate the value. */
  const nested = `x \\u005cn${V} y`;

  it('up to its bound redactForDisplay is redactForIndex: a value glued to a literal escape is masked where redactField leaves it', () => {
    expect(libRedact.redactField(glued, idx), 'CONTROL: one reading leaves the glued value').toContain(V);
    expect(libRedact.redactField(nested, idx), 'CONTROL: and the chained one').toContain(V);
    for (const t of [glued, nested, `plain ${V} text`]) {
      const shown = libRedact.redactForDisplay(t, idx);
      expect(shown, t).not.toContain(V);
      expect(shown, t).toContain(libRedact.REDACTED_MARK);
      expect(shown, 'the text the index would hold').toBe(libRedact.redactForIndex(t, idx));
    }
  });

  it('text whose escapes hide nothing is shown exactly as it came: a Windows path, LaTeX, a JSON line break', () => {
    for (const t of ['C:\\new_folder\\table.txt', '\\begin{document} and \\n twice', '{"a":"b\\nc"}', 'no escapes at all']) {
      expect(libRedact.redactForDisplay(t, idx), t).toBe(t);
    }
  });

  it('past DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX each escape-glued span is masked only when its own readings remove something', () => {
    expect(libRedact.DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX).toBe(libRedact.ENTRY_FTS_BYTES + libRedact.ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN);
    const big = `${'w '.repeat(libRedact.DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX / 2)}${glued} and \\nfoo and ${nested} end`;
    expect(big.length, 'CONTROL: past the bound').toBeGreaterThan(libRedact.DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX);
    // Booleans, never the 1 MiB strings: a red must not print a 1 MiB diff (ruling R-runner).
    expect(libRedact.redactField(big, idx).includes(V), 'CONTROL: one reading leaves the glued values').toBe(true);
    const shown = libRedact.redactForDisplay(big, idx);
    expect(shown.includes(V), 'no glued value is shown').toBe(false);
    expect(shown.includes(' and \\nfoo and '), 'an escape that hides nothing prints as it came').toBe(true);
    expect(shown.endsWith(' end')).toBe(true);
  });

  it('nodeIndexTexts takes the gist, each topic and each ref value through entryIndexText, topics and refs one per line', () => {
    const t = libRedact.nodeIndexTexts({ gist: `zqgist ${glued}`, topics: [`zqtopic ${nested}`, 'plain topic'], refs: ['src/a.ts', glued] }, idx);
    for (const col of [t.gist, t.topics, t.refs]) expect(col).not.toContain(V);
    expect(t.gist).toBe(libRedact.entryIndexText(`zqgist ${glued}`, idx));
    expect(t.topics.split('\n').at(-1)).toBe('plain topic');
    expect(t.refs.split('\n')[0]).toBe('src/a.ts');
    expect(libRedact.nodeIndexTexts({ gist: null, topics: null, refs: [] }, idx)).toEqual({ gist: '', topics: '', refs: '' });
  });

  it('nodeIndexTexts depends on the pairs only through the index\'s answers: a probe index returns the same texts and counts the owed hit', () => {
    const pairs = libRedact.secretPairs([V]).pairs.map((p, i) => ({ ...p, rid: i + 1 }));
    const probe = libRedact.makeProbeIndex(pairs, 0);
    const fields = { gist: `zqgist ${glued}`, topics: [], refs: [] };
    expect(libRedact.nodeIndexTexts(fields, probe)).toEqual(libRedact.nodeIndexTexts(fields, idx));
    expect(probe.probe.hits, 'the owed pair was asked and answered yes').toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```

```js
export function rederivePlan(mark, top, maxBlobId, state, beltDue = false, restart = false) {
  // `restart` (decideBelt's, R-version): the belt is due and the open generation carries no record of its units under
  // this BELT_VERSION (one opened under another version, by a build without the belt, or whose record a due record
  // cleared), so its walk is begun again rather than finished under a stamp it could not earn.

  // own mark until its completion writes the state without ` b`.
  if (top > mark || beltDue) return { target: Math.max(top, mark), cursor: 0, end: maxBlobId, ...(beltDue ? { belt: true } : {}) };
  return null;
}
```
