- [ ] **Step 5: Append the belt block** at the end of `ccd/history/lib.mjs`, exactly as measured on the judge's prototype:

```js
// ===========================================================================
// The substring belt (spec §8.3 layer 4 and layer 1's glue windows, §6.2 "The belt"; rev 3.5; W1-B2 Task 7A;
// coordinator rulings 4019 and 4043, reviews 344 F9 and 351). Layer 1 matches a registered unit only as a whole
// `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` run, so a unit glued to a neighbour (`ab_<v>`, `ab<v>`) or a run an escape sequence took a character
// of (`ESC[` + `P…`) kept most of a secret as one FTS term and printed it (B1's D-4344
// (history-reindex-mark-by-rederivation) and D-4307 (history-redaction-csi-joined-belt) name both limits). Two repairs,
// both inside redactField so every caller has them:
// layer 1's glue windows (by hash, so a rotated value and a sessions.json hash are covered), and layer 4, which masks
// every stretch sharing beltWidth(unit) or more consecutive characters, folded, with a unit this process loaded.
// ===========================================================================

/** The belt's derivation version (meta fts_belt's `v`). A store whose recorded version differs, a B1 store's absent
 *  state included, re-derives its whole index once (decideBelt, rederivePlan); a generation open across a bump is
 *  restarted, and a completion stamps the version its walk ran under (`gv`, ruling R-version). Bump it with any change
 *  to layer 4, to the glue windows, to beltWidth, to beltFold or to the seed rule. */
export const BELT_VERSION = 1;
/** The bits a matched stretch must carry in its unit's folded alphabet: SECRET_SEGMENT_MIN base64url characters'
 *  72 bits, the bound §8.3 already sets on a segment. */
export const BELT_BITS = 72;
/** The widths the belt scans at, ascending; the floor is SECRET_SEGMENT_MIN, the shortest unit. */
export const BELT_K_LADDER = Object.freeze([12, 14, 16, 18, 21]);
/** The most grams one belt holds (about 15 MiB); a unit past it stays in layer 1 only and is counted. */
export const BELT_GRAMS_MAX = 65536;
/** meta key: the belt state, formatBeltState's JSON (rowids only, never a value). */
export const BELT_META = 'fts_belt';
/** The derivation step that re-redacts every node's stored fields when a re-derivation generation opens. */
export const BELT_NODES_STEP = 'nodes-belt';
/** meta key: the declared secretsFile paths the last tick read (JSON array, paths only). */
export const REDACT_SOURCES_META = 'redact_sources';
/** The belt's counter words (sweep.mjs writes them). */
export const BELT_COUNTERS = Object.freeze({ overflow: 'redact_belt_overflow', generations: 'redact_belt_generations' });
/** The glue windows one run may hash before it is replaced whole (fail closed): this plus a quarter of its length. */
const GLUE_HASH_FLOOR = 64;
/** The window characters one run may hash before it is replaced whole (fail closed): this plus 4 × its length, each
 *  window charged its length before it is hashed (spec §8.3, review R69; *chosen*). A count bound alone costs
 *  (64 + n/4) × the longest registered pair. */
const GLUE_HASH_BYTES_FLOOR = 64 * 1024;

/** A character's belt code: 1-38 for `[a-z0-9_-]` (an upper-case letter folds to its lower case), 0 for any other
 *  ASCII character, a boundary no gram crosses. */
const BELT_CODE = (() => {
  const t = new Uint8Array(128);
  let c = 1;
  for (const ch of 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_-') { t[ch.charCodeAt(0)] = c; c += 1; }
  for (let u = 0x41; u <= 0x5a; u += 1) t[u] = t[u + 0x20];
  return t;
})();
const FOLD_MEMO = new Map();
const FOLD_MEMO_MAX = 4096;
/** The combining marks FTS5 unicode61 drops inside a token at remove_diacritics 1, the default B1's `porter unicode61`
 *  tables use: U+0300-0304, U+0306-030C, U+030F, U+0311, U+031B, U+0323-0328, U+032D-032E, U+0330-0331. Measured
 *  against node:sqlite on every code point U+0080..U+2FFFF (the case `beltFold is unicode61's own fold`); every other
 *  mark is a boundary to unicode61, so it is one to the belt. */
const isDroppedMark = (c) => (c >= 0x300 && c <= 0x304) || (c >= 0x306 && c <= 0x30c) || c === 0x30f || c === 0x311
  || c === 0x31b || (c >= 0x323 && c <= 0x328) || c === 0x32d || c === 0x32e || c === 0x330 || c === 0x331;
const isAsciiAlnum = (b) => (b >= 0x30 && b <= 0x39) || (b >= 0x41 && b <= 0x5a) || (b >= 0x61 && b <= 0x7a);

/** A non-ASCII code point's belt code, exactly as FTS5 unicode61 (remove_diacritics 1) folds it inside a token
 *  (coordinator ruling R-fold): one of the marks it drops is dropped (-1); a character whose canonical decomposition is
 *  an ASCII letter or digit alone, or that and one dropped mark, folds to that character's code; U+017F and U+1E9B
 *  (long s, and long s with a dot above) fold to `s`, as unicode61's case fold takes them; anything else is a
 *  boundary (0), a letter with two marks included, which unicode61 keeps as itself. Memoised per code point
 *  (bounded), so CJK-dense text costs one lookup a character. */
export function beltFold(cp) {
  const hit = FOLD_MEMO.get(cp);
  if (hit !== undefined) return hit;
  let c = 0;
  if (isDroppedMark(cp)) c = -1;
  else if (cp === 0x17f || cp === 0x1e9b) c = BELT_CODE[0x73];
  else {
    const d = String.fromCodePoint(cp).normalize('NFD');
    const b = d.charCodeAt(0);
    if (isAsciiAlnum(b) && (d.length === 1 || (d.length === 2 && isDroppedMark(d.charCodeAt(1))))) c = BELT_CODE[b];
  }
  if (FOLD_MEMO.size < FOLD_MEMO_MAX) FOLD_MEMO.set(cp, c);
  return c;
}

/** The width a unit is masked at: the stretch its folded alphabet needs to carry BELT_BITS, never more than the unit,
 *  rounded DOWN to BELT_K_LADDER (rounding down only masks more). */
export function beltWidth(unit) {
  const u = unit.toLowerCase();
  let size;
  if (/^[0-9]+$/.test(u)) size = 10;
  else if (/^[0-9a-f]+$/.test(u)) size = 16;
  else size = (/[0-9]/.test(u) ? 10 : 0) + (/[a-z]/.test(u) ? 26 : 0) + (u.includes('_') ? 1 : 0) + (u.includes('-') ? 1 : 0);
  const need = size < 2 ? u.length : Math.min(u.length, Math.ceil(BELT_BITS / Math.log2(size)));
  let w = BELT_K_LADDER[0];
  for (const s of BELT_K_LADDER) if (s <= need) w = s;
  return w;
}

/** Whether the gram of `unit` at `off`, `w` long, may seed a mask: at least a third of its folded characters are
 *  distinct (a padding run seeds nothing), and it holds a digit or both an upper- and a lower-case letter. So a
 *  snake_case, kebab-case or CONSTANT_CASE word, or the wordy part of a token (`claude-sonnet-`), seeds nothing. The
 *  price depends on the unit's alphabet (measured, 2000 random 40-character values each, and 5.4M base64url grams):
 *  a token's gram fails this about once in 10^4 when it is mixed-case, about once in 5 × 10^4 when it is base64url
 *  (measured 2.07e-5), but a one-case `[a-z0-9]` token's about once in 100 and
 *  a base32 `[A-Z2-7]` one's about once in 18. A print that holds any seeding gram is still masked to its run; a
 *  partial print of a one-case unit's digit-free window alone is left (spec §8.3 "What it cannot see"). A value of
 *  one-case letters only is left to layer 1 (its pair and its glue windows). */
function beltSeeds(unit, off, w) {
  let digit = false;
  let lower = false;
  let upper = false;
  const seen = new Set();
  for (let k = off; k < off + w; k += 1) {
    const c = unit.charCodeAt(k);
    if (c >= 0x30 && c <= 0x39) digit = true;
    else if (c >= 0x61 && c <= 0x7a) lower = true;
    else if (c >= 0x41 && c <= 0x5a) upper = true;
    seen.add(BELT_CODE[c]);
  }
  if (seen.size * 3 < w) return false;
  return digit || (lower && upper);
}

const BELT_BASE = 0x01000193;
function beltPow(e) {
  let r = 1;
  for (let i = 0; i < e; i += 1) r = Math.imul(r, BELT_BASE);
  return r;
}
function beltSame(a, ai, b, bi, w) {
  for (let k = 0; k < w; k += 1) if (a[ai + k] !== b[bi + k]) return false;
  return true;
}

/** The units the belt masks for `values`: secretUnits' rule, so layer 4, layer 1 and the late-pair search agree. */
export function beltUnits(values) {
  return [...new Set([...values].flatMap((v) => secretUnits(v)))];
}

/** The belt over `units` (secretUnits' runs of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, SECRET_SEGMENT_MIN or more). Each width holds a table
 *  from a seeding gram's 32-bit rolling hash (high 30 bits) to the grams with it; every candidate is compared code by
 *  code, so a collision never changes an answer. Units are taken in sorted order until BELT_GRAMS_MAX; the rest are
 *  counted in `overflow`. Held in this process's memory only; `texts` is what the --regex child is handed. */
export function makeBelt(units) {
  const codesOf = [];
  const texts = [];
  const byWidth = new Map();
  let grams = 0;
  let overflow = 0;
  for (const unit of [...new Set(units)].sort()) {
    const w = beltWidth(unit);
    const n = unit.length - w + 1;
    if (n < 1 || !/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/.test(unit)) continue;
    if (grams + n > BELT_GRAMS_MAX) { overflow += 1; continue; }
    const codes = new Uint8Array(unit.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < unit.length; i += 1) codes[i] = BELT_CODE[unit.charCodeAt(i)];
    const at = codesOf.length;
    codesOf.push(codes);
    texts.push(unit);
    let t = byWidth.get(w);
    if (t === undefined) {
      t = { w, pw: beltPow(w - 1), table: new Map() };
      byWidth.set(w, t);
    }
    let h = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < unit.length; i += 1) {
      if (i >= w) h = (h - Math.imul(codes[i - w], t.pw)) | 0;
      h = (Math.imul(h, BELT_BASE) + codes[i]) | 0;
      if (i < w - 1) continue;
      const off = i - w + 1;
      if (!beltSeeds(unit, off, w)) continue;
      const key = h >>> 2;
      const list = t.table.get(key);
      if (list !== undefined && list.some((g) => beltSame(codesOf[g.unit], g.off, codes, off, w))) continue;
      if (list === undefined) t.table.set(key, [{ unit: at, off }]);
      else list.push({ unit: at, off });
      grams += 1;
    }
  }
  return { units: codesOf, texts, widths: [...byWidth.values()].sort((a, b) => a.w - b.w), grams, overflow };
}

/** A reading of a text: a string and, per UTF-16 unit of it, the range of the text it came from (null: itself). */
const readFrom = (r, i) => (r.from === null ? i : r.from[i]);
const readTo = (r, i) => (r.to === null ? i + 1 : r.to[i]);

/** `r` with every match of `re` (global) replaced by `fn(match)`, each replacement character mapped to the match. */
function mapReading(r, re, fn) {
  const parts = [];
  const from = [];
  const to = [];
  let last = 0;
  re.lastIndex = 0;
  for (let m = re.exec(r.s); m !== null; m = re.exec(r.s)) {
    for (let i = last; i < m.index; i += 1) { from.push(readFrom(r, i)); to.push(readTo(r, i)); }
    parts.push(r.s.slice(last, m.index));
    const rep = fn(m);
    const a = readFrom(r, m.index);
    const b = readTo(r, m.index + m[0].length - 1);
    for (let i = 0; i < rep.length; i += 1) { from.push(a); to.push(b); }
    parts.push(rep);
    last = m.index + m[0].length;
    if (m[0].length === 0) re.lastIndex += 1;
  }
  if (last === 0 && parts.length === 0) return r;
  for (let i = last; i < r.s.length; i += 1) { from.push(readFrom(r, i)); to.push(readTo(r, i)); }
  parts.push(r.s.slice(last));
  return { s: parts.join(''), from: Int32Array.from(from), to: Int32Array.from(to) };
}

/** The bytes of one escape sequence that introduce it: a 7-bit ESC, its fill and the `[`, `P`, `N` or `O` after it
 *  when a byte follows that, or the one 8-bit introducer. The rest (parameters, intermediates, the final byte) is what
 *  a stray introducer may have taken from a value. */
function introducerLen(seq) {
  if (seq.charCodeAt(0) !== 0x1b) return 1;
  let k = 1;
  while (k < seq.length && SEQ_FILL_RE.test(seq[k])) k += 1;
  return k < seq.length - 1 && '[PNO'.includes(seq[k]) ? k + 1 : k;
}

/** Scan one reading: every window equal to a seeding gram of its width adds its source range to `cover` (a difference
 *  array over the masked text) and calls `onHit` (the re-derivation's probe). Linear per width. */
function scanReading(r, belt, cover, onHit) {
  const s = r.s;
  const codes = new Uint8Array(s.length);
  const from = new Int32Array(s.length);
  const to = new Int32Array(s.length);
  let n = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length;) {
    const u = s.charCodeAt(i);
    let len = 1;
    let c;
    if (u < 0x80) c = BELT_CODE[u];
    else {
      const cp = s.codePointAt(i);
      if (cp > 0xffff) len = 2;
      c = beltFold(cp);
    }
    if (c >= 0) {
      codes[n] = c;
      if (r.from === null) { from[n] = i; to[n] = i + len; } else { from[n] = r.from[i]; to[n] = r.to[i + len - 1]; }
      n += 1;
    }
    i += len;
  }
  for (const t of belt.widths) {
    const w = t.w;
    let h = 0;
    let run = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i += 1) {
      const c = codes[i];
      if (c === 0) { run = 0; h = 0; continue; }
      if (run >= w) h = (h - Math.imul(codes[i - w], t.pw)) | 0;
      else run += 1;
      h = (Math.imul(h, BELT_BASE) + c) | 0;
      if (run < w) continue;
      const list = t.table.get(h >>> 2);
      if (list === undefined) continue;
      if (!list.some((x) => beltSame(belt.units[x.unit], x.off, codes, i - w + 1, w))) continue;
      cover[from[i - w + 1]] += 1;
      cover[to[i]] -= 1;
      if (onHit !== null) onHit();
    }
  }
}

/** Layer 4 (spec §8.3): `text` with every stretch sharing a seeding gram with a unit of `belt` replaced by
 *  REDACTED_MARK. Readings: the text, and when it holds an escape introducer, the text with every ANSI sequence removed
 *  and the text with every sequence's introducer removed (what a stray `ESC[` took stays in place); with `decode`, the
 *  same three of each JSON-escape decode, up to INDEX_UNESCAPE_PASSES, stopping at the first that changes nothing. Each
 *  reading is folded (ASCII case, unicode61's diacritics, beltFold) and maps every character back to the range of
 *  `text` it came from. The masked ranges are their union, each widened to the `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` run around it but never
 *  over a JSON escape's letter or hex digit, then each replaced by one mark; a span that starts inside an escape takes
 *  the whole escape, so no mark follows a bare backslash. A mark holds no unit's width of run characters, so the result
 *  is a fixed point. Cost: at most 3 * (1 + INDEX_UNESCAPE_PASSES) readings, each scanned once per width
 *  (BELT_K_LADDER.length at most) with an exact comparison of at most the width per hash hit, and one widening pass
 *  that reads each character at most once (a cover inside an already widened span joins it, ruling R-linear): O(text),
 *  pinned by the case `the widening is linear`. `onHit` (or null) is called once per matched window. */
export function beltMask(text, belt, decode, onHit = null) {
  if (belt === null || belt === undefined || belt.widths.length === 0 || text.length < BELT_K_LADDER[0]) return text;
  const cover = new Int32Array(text.length + 1);
  let r = { s: text, from: null, to: null };
  for (let level = 0; ; level += 1) {
    scanReading(r, belt, cover, onHit);
    if (ESCAPE_INTRODUCER_RE.test(r.s)) {
      scanReading(mapReading(r, ANSI_ESCAPE_RE, () => ''), belt, cover, onHit);
      scanReading(mapReading(r, ANSI_ESCAPE_RE, (m) => m[0].slice(introducerLen(m[0]))), belt, cover, onHit);
    }
    if (!decode || level >= INDEX_UNESCAPE_PASSES || !r.s.includes('\\')) break;
    const d = mapReading(r, JSON_ESCAPE_RE, (m) => (m[1] !== undefined ? JSON_ESCAPE_CHAR[m[1]] : String.fromCharCode(parseInt(m[2], 16))));
    if (d === r || d.s === r.s) break;
    r = d;
  }
  // The masked spans: each union of covered ranges, widened to the `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` run around it. The widening is
  // linear (ruling R-linear): a cover that starts at or before the end the last span was widened to joins that span,
  // so no character is widened over twice. (A cover inside an already widened run used to push a span of its own and
  // rescan the rest of the run, quadratic in it.) A left widening never takes a JSON escape's letter or hex digit, and
  // a span that starts inside an escape takes the whole escape, so no mark follows a bare backslash and a `--json`
  // string stays valid, as REDACTED_MARK promises (finding R31).
  const n = text.length;
  const spans = [];
  let depth = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i += 1) {
    const was = depth;
    depth += cover[i];
    if (depth > 0) {
      const last = spans.length === 0 ? null : spans[spans.length - 1];
      if (was === 0 && (last === null || i > last[1])) {
        const floor = last === null ? 0 : last[1];
        let s = i;
        while (s > floor && isRunByte(text.charCodeAt(s - 1)) && jsonEscapeAt(text, s - 1) < 0) s -= 1;
        if (last !== null && s === floor) last[1] = i + 1;
        else spans.push([s, i + 1]);
      } else if (i + 1 > last[1]) last[1] = i + 1;
    } else if (was > 0) widenRun(text, spans[spans.length - 1]);
  }
  if (spans.length === 0) return text;
  widenRun(text, spans[spans.length - 1]);
  let out = '';
  let last = 0;
  for (const [s0, e] of spans) {
    if (e <= last) continue;
    const at = jsonEscapeAt(text, s0);
    const s = at < 0 ? s0 : at;
    out += text.slice(last, Math.max(s, last)) + REDACTED_MARK;
    last = e;
  }
  return out + text.slice(last);
}

/** A span's right widening over the `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` run after it. A backslash ends it, so it never enters an escape. */
function widenRun(text, sp) {
  while (sp[1] < text.length && isRunByte(text.charCodeAt(sp[1]))) sp[1] += 1;
}

const isHexByte = (b) => (b >= 0x30 && b <= 0x39) || (b >= 0x41 && b <= 0x46) || (b >= 0x61 && b <= 0x66);

/** The index of the backslash of the JSON escape whose letter or hex digit `text[k]` is (`\n`, `A`), or -1. A
 *  backslash opens an escape only after an even number of backslashes (`\\n` is an escaped backslash, then a letter).
 *  Cost: at most five characters back, and the backslash run there. */
function jsonEscapeAt(text, k) {
  for (let b = k - 1; b >= 0 && b >= k - 5; b -= 1) {
    if (text.charCodeAt(b) !== 0x5c) continue;
    let r = b;
    while (r > 0 && text.charCodeAt(r - 1) === 0x5c) r -= 1;
    if ((b - r) % 2 === 1) return -1;
    if (k === b + 1) return JSON_ESCAPE_CHAR[text[k]] !== undefined || text[k] === 'u' ? b : -1;
    if (text[b + 1] !== 'u') return -1;
    for (let h = b + 2; h <= k; h += 1) if (!isHexByte(text.charCodeAt(h))) return -1;
    return b;
  }
  return -1;
}

/** The probe callback of a re-derivation index (makeProbeIndex with beltAll): every layer-4 and glue-window hit is an
 *  owed hit, because both depend on the loaded values and on BELT_VERSION's code, which the owed-pair argument does
 *  not cover. Null for every other index. */
function beltHit(idx) {
  return idx.beltAll === true && idx.probe !== undefined ? () => { idx.probe.hits += 1; } : null;
}

/** One index reading's redaction (redactForIndex's readings, the sidecar's raw pass): the three layers, then the belt
 *  over the literal and escape readings only. An FTS term is a run of the literal text, and redactForIndex decodes
 *  the deeper levels itself, each through this. */
function redactIndexReading(text, idx) {
  return beltMask(redactLayered(text, idx), idx.belt, false, beltHit(idx));
}

const isGlueSep = (c) => c === 0x5f || c === 0x2d;
const GLUE_SEP_RE = /[_-]/;

/** `text` with each maximal union of the [start, end) pairs in `iv` (non-empty) replaced by the mark. */
function maskIntervals(text, iv) {
  const pairs = [];
  for (let k = 0; k < iv.length; k += 2) pairs.push([iv[k], iv[k + 1]]);
  pairs.sort((x, y) => x[0] - y[0] || x[1] - y[1]);
  let out = '';
  let at = 0;
  let a = pairs[0][0];
  let b = pairs[0][1];
  for (let k = 1; k < pairs.length; k += 1) {
    if (pairs[k][0] <= b) { b = Math.max(b, pairs[k][1]); continue; }
    out += text.slice(at, a) + REDACTED_MARK;
    at = b;
    a = pairs[k][0];
    b = pairs[k][1];
  }
  return out + text.slice(at, a) + REDACTED_MARK + text.slice(b);
}

/** Layer 1's glue windows (§8.3, rev 3.5): in a `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` run that is not itself a pair, every window that starts
 *  at the run's start or at or right after a `_` or `-`, ends at the run's end or at or right before one, holds a
 *  letter or digit, and has a length some pair has, is tested by (length, sha256) as a run is. A value glued by `_` or
 *  `-` (which unicode61 splits off as its own terms) is matched by its pair alone, a rotated value and a sessions.json
 *  hash included. One run takes at most GLUE_HASH_FLOOR plus a quarter of its length in hashes, and hashes at most
 *  GLUE_HASH_BYTES_FLOOR plus 4 × its length in window characters, each window charged before it is hashed; past
 *  either budget it is replaced whole, fail closed. One run's glue cost is then linear in its length plus a constant,
 *  whatever the registered lengths. */
function glueRedact(run, idx) {
  const n = run.length;
  if (n <= SECRET_SEGMENT_MIN || idx.byLen.size === 0 || !GLUE_SEP_RE.test(run)) return run;
  const starts = [];
  const isEnd = new Uint8Array(n + 1);
  const alnum = new Int32Array(n + 1);
  isEnd[n] = 1;
  for (let k = 0; k < n; k += 1) {
    const sep = isGlueSep(run.charCodeAt(k));
    alnum[k + 1] = alnum[k] + (sep ? 0 : 1);
    if (k === 0 || sep || isGlueSep(run.charCodeAt(k - 1))) starts.push(k);
    if (sep) { isEnd[k] = 1; isEnd[k + 1] = 1; }
  }
  const hit = beltHit(idx);
  let budget = GLUE_HASH_FLOOR + (n >>> 2);
  let bytes = GLUE_HASH_BYTES_FLOOR + 4 * n;
  const iv = [];
  for (const [len, shas] of idx.byLen) {
    if (len >= n) continue;
    for (const i of starts) {
      const j = i + len;
      if (j > n) break;
      if (isEnd[j] === 0 || alnum[j] === alnum[i]) continue;
      budget -= 1;
      bytes -= len;
      if (budget < 0 || bytes < 0) {
        if (hit !== null) hit();
        return REDACTED_MARK;
      }
      if (shas.has(sha256Hex(run.slice(i, j)))) {
        iv.push(i, j);
        if (hit !== null) hit();
      }
    }
  }
  return iv.length === 0 ? run : maskIntervals(run, iv);
}

/** fts_belt's witness is a short JSON array (sweep's beltWitness); a longer string is no state. */
const BELT_WITNESS_MAX = 512;

/** meta fts_belt's grammar: `{"v":<int>,"rids":[<rid>…],"gen":null|[<rid>…]}`, then `"gv":<int>` exactly when `gen` is
 *  a list (the BELT_VERSION the open generation opened under, ruling R-version), then optionally `"w":"<witness>"`
 *  (sweep's beltWitness when a belt-aware pass last wrote the state, ruling R-rollback). Every rid is a positive
 *  integer. Anything else (undefined included) is null, which decideBelt reads as due. */
export function parseBeltState(text) {
  let o;
  try { o = JSON.parse(text ?? ''); } catch { return null; }
  const rids = (a) => Array.isArray(a) && a.every((x) => Number.isSafeInteger(x) && x > 0);
  if (o === null || typeof o !== 'object' || !Number.isSafeInteger(o.v) || !rids(o.rids)) return null;
  if (o.gen === null ? o.gv !== undefined : !(rids(o.gen) && Number.isSafeInteger(o.gv))) return null;
  if (o.w !== undefined && !(typeof o.w === 'string' && o.w.length <= BELT_WITNESS_MAX)) return null;
  return { v: o.v, rids: [...o.rids], gen: o.gen === null ? null : [...o.gen], ...(o.gen === null ? {} : { gv: o.gv }), ...(o.w === undefined ? {} : { w: o.w }) };
}
/** The text parseBeltState reads back: `gv` only beside a list `gen`, `w` only when set, so the due record
 *  `{ v: 0, rids: [], gen: null }` (Tasks 21 and 23 write it) is `{"v":0,"rids":[],"gen":null}` exactly. */
export function formatBeltState(s) {
  return JSON.stringify({ v: s.v, rids: s.rids, gen: s.gen, ...(s.gen === null ? {} : { gv: s.gv }), ...(s.w === undefined ? {} : { w: s.w }) });
}

/** The belt's decision for one tick (§6.2 "The belt"). `live`: the redact_hashes rowids of the units this tick's belt
 *  holds. `rids`: the units every indexed row is known to carry the belt of, at version `v`. `gen`: the units live at
 *  every tick of the open generation, which opened under version `gv`.
 *  - A unit no longer live leaves `rids` and `gen`: a row indexed while its value is not loaded lacks its belt.
 *  - Due: the version differs (a B1 store's absent state, and the `v: 0` due record, included), or a live unit at or
 *    below the mark is not in `rids` (its file readable again). A unit above the mark is the pair generation's.
 *  - Restart (ruling R-version): when due, an open generation whose `gen` is absent (one a build without the belt
 *    opened, or one a due record cleared) or was recorded under another BELT_VERSION covers nothing this version can
 *    stamp, so rederivePlan begins its walk again from cursor 0 rather than finishing one that ran partly under other
 *    code.
 *  `next` is the state to write, without `w` (the sweep adds it). Pure. */
export function decideBelt(state, live, mark) {
  if (state === null) return { due: true, restart: true, next: { v: 0, rids: [], gen: null } };
  const L = new Set(live);
  const keep = (a) => a.filter((r) => L.has(r));
  const genOk = state.gen !== null && state.gv === BELT_VERSION;
  const next = { v: state.v, rids: state.v === BELT_VERSION ? keep(state.rids) : [], gen: genOk ? keep(state.gen) : null, ...(genOk ? { gv: BELT_VERSION } : {}) };
  const covered = new Set(next.rids);
  const due = state.v !== BELT_VERSION || live.some((r) => r <= mark && !covered.has(r));
  return { due, restart: due && !genOk, next };
}
/** The state a completed generation leaves: the units live at every one of its ticks (`gen`), at the version its walk
 *  ran under (`gv`, which decideBelt keeps only when it is BELT_VERSION). A generation with no `gen` (one a B1 pass
 *  opened, or one whose record a due record cleared) covers nothing new, so the belt stays due. */
export function beltAfterGeneration(next) {
  return next.gen === null ? { v: next.v, rids: next.rids, gen: null } : { v: next.gv, rids: [...next.gen].sort((a, b) => a - b), gen: null };
}
/** Whether a build that writes index rows without the belt (B1, after a rollback) wrote since a belt-aware pass last
 *  recorded the store's witness (ruling R-rollback): `witness` (sweep's beltWitness, measured now) differs from the
 *  state's `w`. A state with no `w` (none recorded yet, or the due record Tasks 21 and 23 write) claims nothing: it is
 *  due already, or about to be stamped. Pure. */
export function beltWitnessMoved(state, witness) {
  return state !== null && state.w !== undefined && state.w !== witness;
}

/** meta redact_sources: a JSON array of at most 256 absolute paths; anything else names none. */
export function parseRedactSources(text) {
  let a;
  try { a = JSON.parse(text ?? '[]'); } catch { return []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(a) || a.length > 256) return [];
  return a.every((p) => typeof p === 'string' && p.startsWith('/') && p.length < 4096 && !p.includes('\0')) ? a : [];
}
```

```js

// ===========================================================================
// The index's escape readings for display and nodes_fts (spec §8.3 "Where it runs", §6.2 `nodes_fts`, rev 3.5;
// W1-B2 Task 7A; B1's D-4343 and D-4419,
// and B1's run 302 notes to B2). The belt's decoded readings find only a unit this process loaded; a value held as a
// pair alone (a rotated value, a sessions.json hash) glued to a literal escape is separated only by redactForIndex's
// readings. So a read verb shows a field as the index holds it, and nodes_fts indexes what blobs_fts would.
// ===========================================================================

/** The longest field redactForDisplay reads through every escape reading, in UTF-16 units: the window an entry's index
 *  text is redacted over (B1's D-4419). */
export const DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX = ENTRY_FTS_BYTES + ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN;

/** A recalled field as a read verb shows it, so no output shows a value the index masked (§8.3's field pass, with the
 *  escape readings B1 gave the index).
 *  - Up to DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX it IS redactForIndex: the field as it came, redacted, unless a deeper JSON-escape
 *    reading removed something; then that reading is shown, decoded. A field whose escapes hide nothing is shown
 *    exactly as redactField shows it.
 *  - Past it (expand reads a sidecar up to SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX), the field is redacted once, and each maximal span of
 *    `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` characters and backslashes that holds a backslash and a run character (the spans B1's
 *    exhaustion rule marks) is read through redactForIndex alone and replaced by the mark when any of its readings
 *    removed something. The cost stays linear, and a long JSON text's ordinary escapes print as they are. Residual,
 *    past the bound only: a value only the context layer sees after a decode, with no backslash touching it.
 *  It calls nothing but redactField and redactForIndex (whose readings are redactIndexReading's, the belt included),
 *  so it fails closed as they do (R2). */
export function redactForDisplay(text, idx) {
  if (text.length <= DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX) return redactForIndex(text, idx);
  const t = redactField(text, idx);
  if (!t.includes('\\')) return t;
  return t.replace(/[A-Za-z0-9_.\\-]+/g, (span) => (span.includes('\\') && /[A-Za-z0-9_-]/.test(span) && redactForIndex(span, idx) !== span ? REDACTED_MARK : span));
}

/** A nodes_fts row's three column texts (§6.2): the gist, each topic and each ref value through entryIndexText (B1's
 *  escape readings and window, the belt included), topics and refs then joined one per line, as Tasks 8 and 9 index
 *  them. Every nodes_fts writer calls it (Task 8's indexNode, Task 9's insertNodeFts, Task 29's redactNodeFields), so
 *  a row is a function of its node's stored fields and the pair index's answers alone, which Task 29's node step
 *  recomputes and compares. */
export function nodeIndexTexts(fields, idx) {
  const one = (s) => entryIndexText(String(s), idx);
  return {
    gist: fields.gist === null || fields.gist === undefined ? '' : one(fields.gist),
    topics: (fields.topics ?? []).map(one).join('\n'),
    refs: (fields.refs ?? []).map(one).join('\n'),
  };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Write the mutation runner.** It is the same gitignored scratch tool as Task 5's: Tasks 1–7, 7A, 7B and 8 write this same file, byte for byte, so each task stands alone and rewriting it changes nothing. Every copy in this plan spawns vitest with `maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024` (ruling R-runner; finding R09 measured `r.error.code === 'ENOBUFS'` under mutants (c) and (k) with the 1 MiB default). From the repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <<'EOF'
// .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs: measures each guard RED with it mutated, then GREEN with
// it restored (the B2 plan's mutation-pin rule). Run from server/, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least
// 600000 ms:
//   node ../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <mutants.json>
// A mutant is {name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}. `file` is repo-relative, `test` is
// server/-relative, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. The
// pristine file is copied to scratch/keep/<file with '/' as '__'>.orig BEFORE it is touched, and the copy is
// removed only after the file is restored from it. A kill no handler sees therefore leaves the original findable,
// and the next run REFUSES while any copy is left. To restore by hand, from the repository root:
//   for f in .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/*.orig; do t="$(basename "$f" .orig)"; cp "$f" "${t//__//}" && rm "$f"; done
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const KEEP = '../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep';
mkdirSync(KEEP, { recursive: true });
const left = readdirSync(KEEP).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.orig'));
if (left.length > 0) {
  console.log(`REFUSED: ${left.join(', ')} in ${KEEP}. An earlier run was interrupted and a source may hold a mutant: restore as this file's header says.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const keepOf = (file) => `${KEEP}/${file.replaceAll('/', '__')}.orig`;
const restoreAll = () => {
  for (const n of readdirSync(KEEP)) {
    if (!n.endsWith('.orig')) continue;
    copyFileSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`, `../${n.slice(0, -'.orig'.length).replaceAll('__', '/')}`);
    rmSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`);
  }
};
// Every way out restores: the loop's end, process.exit and an uncaught throw all emit 'exit', and a signal is
// turned into an exit. A signal sent while the synchronous loop holds the thread is handled after the current
// child returns; a Ctrl-C also reaches the vitest child, and the loop stops on the child's signal below.
process.on('exit', restoreAll);
for (const s of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) process.on(s, () => process.exit(130));
// maxBuffer: past Node's default (1 MiB) spawnSync kills the child (ENOBUFS, signal SIGTERM, measured), which the
// loop below reads as an interrupt. Each large-operand case asserts a boolean or a length, so a red prints no big diff.
const vitest = (test, filter) => spawnSync('./node_modules/.bin/vitest', ['run', test, '-t', filter], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 });
const mutants = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
let bad = 0;
for (const m of mutants) {
  const target = `../${m.file}`;
  if (!existsSync(target)) { console.log(`NO SUCH FILE       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  const keep = keepOf(m.file);
  copyFileSync(target, keep);
  let src = readFileSync(keep, 'utf8');
  let unique = true;
  for (const e of m.edits) {
    const at = src.indexOf(e.anchor);
    if (at < 0 || src.indexOf(e.anchor, at + 1) >= 0) { unique = false; break; }
    src = src.slice(0, at) + e.replacement + src.slice(at + e.anchor.length);
  }
  if (!unique) { rmSync(keep); console.log(`ANCHOR NOT UNIQUE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  writeFileSync(target, src);
  const red = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  copyFileSync(keep, target);
  rmSync(keep);
  if (red.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${red.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  const failed = /Tests\s+(\d+) failed/.exec(red.stdout)?.[1] ?? '?';
  if (red.status === 0) { console.log(`STAYED GREEN       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`red (${failed} failed)   ${m.name}`);
  const green = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  if (green.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${green.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  if (green.status !== 0) { console.log(`RED AFTER RESTORE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`green              ${m.name}`);
}
console.log(bad === 0 ? 'every guard measured red, then green' : `${bad} guard(s) not measured`);
process.exit(bad === 0 ? 0 : 1);
EOF
```

### Task 7B: sweep: the belt in the tick — the tick's belt and live units, meta `redact_sources`, the belt generation in `rederiveFts`, the node step opened (spec §6.2 "The belt", §8.3, rev 3.5; O59 store half)

**Files:**
- Modify: `ccd/history/sweep.mjs` (B1-created), in place:
  - the `./lib.mjs` import block;
  - `secretStmts` (one statement);

  - `recordTick`: one line inside its transaction (the witness stamp);
  - `rederiveFts`, its plan lines and its commit's meta writes;
  - and four functions added directly above `rederiveFts`'s doc comment: `beltWitness`, the module-private `ftsIndexWitness` (it uses B1's existing `import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';`, so no import changes), `stampBeltWitness` and `recordBeltDueIfWitnessMoved` (the witness check, written once: secretsStep calls it, and so does Task 27's `RESTORE_BELT.check`; coordinator ruling on the pass-6 cross-file items).
  `tick`'s body gains no call, so B1's F39 docstring pin and Tasks 8 and 29's renumbering are untouched.
- Test: `server/test/history-ingest.test.ts`: append one describe.
- Scratch, gitignored: `.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs` (Step 5 writes it again, byte for byte, so this task stands alone) and `mutants-task7b.json`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - Task 7A's lib names;
  - B1 sweep: `loadSecrets`, `recordPairs`, `secretStmts`, `derivStmts` (its existing `pairRid`, `pairTop`, `maxBlob` and `sel`), `FTS_STEP`, `getMeta` (which answers null when absent), `setMeta`, `bump`, `withTx`, `REINDEX_META`, `REDERIVE_META`, `recordTick`;
  - B1's `tick`, unchanged. It sets `ictx.pairIdx = secrets.pairIdx`, so ingest, the backfill, the phrase path, the re-derivation and Task 8's derivation read the belt; it calls `recordTick` last but `markScan`, which carries the stamp.
- Produces:
  - `secretsStep`'s `pairIdx` is `{ byLen, belt, beltLive }`. `beltLive` holds the sorted `redact_hashes` rowids of the belt's units.
  - `secretsStep` writes meta `redact_sources` (the shim's declared paths) only when the shim passed any, and counts `redact_belt_overflow`.
  - `secretsStep`, first of all (ruling R-rollback): it calls `recordBeltDueIfWitnessMoved(db)` in a transaction of its own, so when `beltWitnessMoved(parseBeltState(fts_belt), beltWitness(db))` it records meta `fts_belt` as the due record `{"v":0,"rids":[],"gen":null}` before it records a pair or any step writes a row.
  - `export function recordBeltDueIfWitnessMoved(db): boolean`, inside the caller's transaction (it opens no `withTx`): the writer order's check (spec §6.2 "The belt"; rulings R-rollback and R-witness-restore), written once. When the witness moved it writes the due record and answers true; otherwise it writes nothing and answers false. Its callers are `secretsStep` and Task 27's `RESTORE_BELT.check` (inside `commitRestore`'s FULL bind transaction), so the rule has one spelling.
  - `export function beltWitness(db): string`: the JSON array `[max(blob_id), max(redact_hashes rowid), meta fts_reindex_rid, meta fts_rederive, [('fts', 1)'s cursor, completed_ms] or null, ftsIndexWitness(db)]`.
  - module-private `ftsIndexWitness(db): string | null`: the sha256 hex of `blobs_fts_data`'s FTS5 averages record (id 1) and structure record (id 10), which every committed `blobs_fts` insert or delete rewrites; null when `blobs_fts_data` does not exist. Inside a transaction that wrote `blobs_fts` it may answer anything from the pre-transaction value up to the committed one (a contentless delete writes its tombstone and record 10 at once; a hash-size overflow or a SAVEPOINT flushes early), never a value ahead of the commit; a stamp taken there is behind or exact, never ahead.
  - `export function stampBeltWitness(db): void`, inside the caller's transaction: a parseable `fts_belt` gets `w: beltWitness(db)`; called by `recordTick`, so every pass that writes a `ticks` row (the tick, Task 25's `recoverPass`) ends stamped. A caller stamps in a transaction that wrote no `blobs_fts` row (recordTick's writes none), or its stamp may be behind its own index writes (never ahead of them) and costs one belt generation.
  - `rederiveFts`:
    - reads meta `fts_belt` through `decideBelt`;
    - opens a belt generation when it is due, and restarts an open generation from cursor 0 when `decideBelt` answers `restart` (ruling R-version);
    - on any generation that opens, restarts `('nodes-belt', 1)` (Task 29 runs it) and counts `redact_belt_generations` when a recorded state at a real version fell due (`stored.v !== 0`, finding R15);
    - records `gen` and `gv: BELT_VERSION` when it opens a generation;
    - probes with `{ belt, beltAll: true }`;
    - writes `fts_belt` with every commit, `beltAfterGeneration` at completion, each with `w: beltWitness(db)` measured after the commit's own meta writes;
    - drops ` b` at completion.

**Spec:** §6.2 "The belt"; §8.3 layer 1 (`redact_sources`) and layer 4. Pin: O59 (store half). Coordinator rulings: R-version (the store half), R-rollback, R-runner and R-filter; findings R10/R17, R11, R15, R22 and R24 of the B1-refreshed review. Departures: D-4702 (`history-loader-values-in-tick-memory`) (the tick builds its belt from the values its loader read, held in its own memory only).

Choices this task makes:
- **The mark still only rises.** A due belt opens a generation at the current mark, flagged ` b`, instead of lowering `fts_reindex_rid`. B1's D-4344 (`history-reindex-mark-by-rederivation`) rule, "only a completed generation moves the mark", stands.
- **A unit not loaded leaves the covered set at once**, and its return opens a belt generation. A file that keeps failing keeps doctor's existing WARN `redact-source-unreadable`.
- **`redact_belt_generations` counts only a recorded state at a real version that fell due** (`stored !== null && stored.v !== 0`, finding R15). A new store's first belt generation, a B1 store's, and the one after a due record (`v: 0`: Task 23's rebuild, Task 21's op-pass rule, or a witness that moved) are no event; counting a store's first generation turned B1's FU8 drain cases red (they expect no counters), as measured on the prototype. `getMeta` answers null, not undefined.
- **A generation open at a version change, or with no record of its units, is restarted (ruling R-version).** `decideBelt`'s `restart` makes `rederivePlan` replace it with a belt generation from cursor 0, so a B1 store whose pair generation is open at upgrade (finding R15) is walked once, from 0, under the belt, and its first belt generation opens with no recorded state (no event).
- **A build without the belt is detected by a witness (ruling R-rollback).** B2 runs on schema v1, so `ccrc rollback` or the update watchdog can put B1 back on a store B2 wrote. B1 never reads or writes `fts_belt`, and its ingest, backfill, phrase path and re-derivation write index rows with the three layers alone (review 351's shapes keep 27-32 characters as terms). B1 advances no meta on every tick (`last_zero_behind_ms` only with nothing behind, `scan_ms` only at a scan), and its `ticks` row is skipped by a tick that ends on a busy store after its re-index steps ran. Nor does `max(blob_id)` with `fts_reindex_rid` suffice, the fallback the ruling named: B1's backfill indexes blobs B2 left unindexed without a new blob id, and B1's re-derivation rewrites rows and moves only `fts_rederive`'s cursor until it completes. Nor do B1's ids and metas alone: B1's ingest also indexes a blob ALREADY stored whose `fts_indexed` is 0 (`writeChunk`'s `if (b.fts_indexed === 0) indexBlob(...)`, and the sidecar path's `unindexed(sha)`), and two kinds stay at 0 after the backfill completes (a blob first stored from a row of non-searchable provenance, which the backfill does not select, and B1's D-4346 (`history-permanent-failures-classified`) undecodable blob, which it passes over), so that write moves no id, pair, mark, cursor or time (finding V13). So the witness is the tuple each of B1's index writers moves when it writes: `max(blob_id)` (its ingest; `AUTOINCREMENT` ids are never reused), the top `redact_hashes` rowid (a pair it records, which its phrase path then searches), `fts_reindex_rid` and `fts_rederive` (its re-derivation, which opens with a different state string because B1 cannot parse the ` b` grammar or opens its own on a new pair), `('fts', 1)`'s cursor and `completed_ms` (its backfill), and the index itself: a hash of `blobs_fts_data`'s averages record (id 1) and structure record (id 10), which FTS5 rewrites on every committed insert or delete, the rewrite of a row with the same text included (its structure cookie moves; measured on Node 24.14.1's SQLite, about 0.2 ms per `beltWitness` call). Each part is pinned by its own row of the case `the witness moves with each value a build without the belt writes`, and the index part also by `a build without the belt that indexes a blob already stored`. Every belt-aware write of `fts_belt` carries the witness, and `secretsStep`, the first step of every pass that writes rows, compares it before anything is written: a moved witness records the due record, which also clears any open generation's record so the generation restarts. Inside a transaction that wrote `blobs_fts`, the index part may read anywhere from the pre-transaction state up to the committed one (a contentless delete writes its tombstone and record 10 at once; a hash-size overflow or a SAVEPOINT flushes early; an insert alone leaves both records as they were until the commit), never ahead of the commit, so a witness measured there is behind its own index writes or exact, never ahead: `rederiveFts`'s commit records one (its chunk deletes and inserts, so its reading is a mix), and `recordTick`'s stamp, in a transaction that writes no index row, is what witnesses them. The price is a false positive, never a miss: a tick that ends on a busy store after its ingest or its re-derivation committed index rows leaves `w` behind its own writes; an operator pass that writes witnessed values, `blobs_fts` rows included, and does not end with `stampBeltWitness` in a transaction of its own (it runs `secretsStep`'s check first, so stamping at its end hides nothing) leaves the same, and so does any merge step a build without the belt runs; each costs one extra belt generation.
- **`redact_sources` keeps the last list when a pass is handed none.** A pass with an unreadable roster keeps it, and a stale path can only mask more.

```ts
        const end = Number((w.prepare('SELECT max(blob_id) AS b FROM blobs').get() as { b: number }).b);
        w.prepare('DELETE FROM meta WHERE k = ?').run(lib.BELT_META);
        const upsert = w.prepare('INSERT INTO meta (k, v) VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT (k) DO UPDATE SET v = excluded.v');
        upsert.run('fts_reindex_rid', '0');
        upsert.run('fts_rederive', `${top} ${rows[0]!.blob_id} ${end}`);
      } finally { w.close(); }
      let db = openStoreRO(box);
      try {
        expect(btShared(db, v), 'CONTROL: the escape and letter shapes are terms again').toBe(32);
        expect(lib.parseRederiveState(btMeta(db, 'fts_rederive'))?.cursor, 'CONTROL: B1\'s generation is open past the first blob').toBeGreaterThan(0);
      } finally { db.close(); }
      btHint(box);
      const r = runSweep(box);
      expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
      db = openStoreRO(box);
      try {
        expect(btShared(db, v), 'the first blob too: the walk began again at cursor 0').toBeLessThan(lib.beltWidth(v));
        expect(lib.parseBeltState(btMeta(db, lib.BELT_META))?.v).toBe(lib.BELT_VERSION);
        expect(lib.parseRederiveState(btMeta(db, 'fts_rederive'))?.belt, 'the completed belt generation is closed').toBeUndefined();
        expect(btMeta(db, 'fts_reindex_rid'), 'its completion moved the mark').toBe(String((db.prepare('SELECT max(rowid) AS r FROM redact_hashes').get() as { r: number }).r));
        expect((db.prepare('SELECT n FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get(lib.BELT_COUNTERS.generations) as { n: number } | undefined)?.n,
          'a store with no state is no event').toBeUndefined();
      } finally { db.close(); }
    } finally { fs.rmSync(box.home, { recursive: true, force: true }); }
  });

  it('a value whose file was unreadable while a row was indexed is no longer covered, and its return opens a belt generation that rewrites that row', async (ctx) => {
    if (process.getuid?.() === 0) ctx.skip();                       // root reads a 0000 file regardless of its mode
    const { lib } = await IX.api();
    const box = IX.newBox('ccrc-hist-belt-d-');
    try {

      const file = btSecret(box, 'ret.env', `ZQ_RET=${v}\n`);

      IX.sweepTwice(box);
      fs.chmodSync(file, 0o000);

        fs.appendFileSync(p, IX.jsonl([IX.user(IX.uuidN(2), IX.uuidN(1), `zqbelt gap abP${v}x end`, 2)]));
        btHint(box);
        const r = runSweep(box);
        expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
      } finally { fs.chmodSync(file, 0o600); }
      let db = openStoreRO(box);
      try { expect(btShared(db, v), 'CONTROL: glued by letters, the row indexed in the gap holds the value').toBe(32); } finally { db.close(); }
      btHint(box);
      const r = runSweep(box);
      expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
      db = openStoreRO(box);

        expect(btShared(db, v)).toBeLessThan(lib.beltWidth(v));

          'the return is counted').toBe(1);

  it('a belt past BELT_GRAMS_MAX counts the units it left to layer 1 in redact_belt_overflow', async () => {
    const { lib } = await IX.api();
    const box = IX.newBox('ccrc-hist-belt-f-');
    try {
      // 3000 forty-character values: 27 grams each at width 14, 81,000 in all, past BELT_GRAMS_MAX (65,536).
      btSecret(box, 'many.env', Array.from({ length: 3000 }, (_, i) => `ZQ_MANY_${i}=QP${alnum(37)}7\n`).join(''));
      IX.plantCopy(box.homes[0]!, IX.U, IX.jsonl([IX.user(IX.uuidN(1), null, 'zqbelt many', 1)]));
      IX.sweepTwice(box);

        expect((db.prepare('SELECT n FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get(lib.BELT_COUNTERS.overflow) as { n: number } | undefined)?.n ?? 0,
          'the units past the bound are counted').toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Finding V13: B1's writeChunk and sidecar path index a blob ALREADY stored whose fts_indexed is 0 (a row of
  // non-searchable provenance stored it first, or the backfill passed over it, B1's D-4346), moving no id or meta.
  it('a build without the belt that indexes a blob already stored moves only the index witness, and the next pass rewrites that row', async () => {
    const { sweep, store, lib } = await IX.api();
    const S = sweep as unknown as {
      ftsTextOfBlob(z: Uint8Array, s: boolean, i: unknown, n: number): Promise<{ text: string | null }>;
      beltWitness(db: DatabaseSync): string;
      stampBeltWitness(db: DatabaseSync): void;
    };
    const box = IX.newBox('ccrc-hist-belt-g-');
    try {
      const v = mint();
      btSecret(box, 'belt.env', `ZQ_BELT=${v}\n`);
      IX.plantCopy(box.homes[0]!, IX.U, IX.jsonl(btRows(v)));
      IX.sweepTwice(box);
      let before = '';
      const w = store.openWriter(lib.historyPaths(box.home).dbFile);
      try {
        // The state such a blob is in when B2 last stamped the store: stored, fts_indexed 0, no index row.
        const first = Number((w.prepare('SELECT min(blob_id) AS b FROM blobs WHERE fts_indexed = 1 AND z IS NOT NULL').get() as { b: number }).b);
        w.prepare('DELETE FROM blobs_fts WHERE rowid = ?').run(first);
        w.prepare('UPDATE blobs SET fts_indexed = 0 WHERE blob_id = ?').run(first);
        S.stampBeltWitness(w);
        before = S.beltWitness(w);
        // What B1's indexBlob then does, with the three layers alone: one index row, and fts_indexed 1.
        const bare = lib.makePairIndex((w.prepare('SELECT len, sha256 FROM redact_hashes').all() as { len: number; sha256: Uint8Array }[])
          .map((p) => ({ len: Number(p.len), sha256: Buffer.from(p.sha256).toString('hex') })));
        const b = w.prepare('SELECT z, raw_len FROM blobs WHERE blob_id = ?').get(first) as { z: Uint8Array; raw_len: number };
        const t = await S.ftsTextOfBlob(b.z, false, bare, Number(b.raw_len));
        expect(t.text, 'CONTROL: the blob decodes').not.toBeNull();
        w.prepare('INSERT INTO blobs_fts (rowid, body) VALUES (?, ?)').run(first, lib.entryIndexText(t.text!, bare));
        w.prepare('UPDATE blobs SET fts_indexed = 1 WHERE blob_id = ?').run(first);
      } finally { w.close(); }
      let db = openStoreRO(box);
      try {
        expect(btShared(db, v), 'CONTROL: the row the other build indexed holds the value').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(lib.beltWidth(v));
        expect((JSON.parse(S.beltWitness(db)) as unknown[]).slice(0, 5), 'CONTROL: no blob id, pair, mark, re-derivation state or backfill step moved')
          .toEqual((JSON.parse(before) as unknown[]).slice(0, 5));
      } finally { db.close(); }
      btHint(box);
      const r = runSweep(box);
      expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
      db = openStoreRO(box);
      try {
        expect(btShared(db, v), 'the moved index witness opened a belt generation, which rewrote the row').toBeLessThan(lib.beltWidth(v));
      } finally { db.close(); }
    } finally { fs.rmSync(box.home, { recursive: true, force: true }); }
  });

  // Finding V14: each part of the witness is pinned by the write that moves only it.
  it('the witness moves with each value a build without the belt writes: a blob, a pair, the mark, the re-derivation state, the backfill step and an index row', async () => {
    const { sweep, store, lib } = await IX.api();
    const W = sweep as unknown as { beltWitness(db: DatabaseSync): string };
    const box = IX.newBox('ccrc-hist-belt-h-');
    try {
      IX.plantCopy(box.homes[0]!, IX.U, IX.jsonl([IX.user(IX.uuidN(1), null, 'zqbelt witness parts', 1)]));
      IX.sweepTwice(box);
      const w = store.openWriter(lib.historyPaths(box.home).dbFile);
      try {
        const upsert = w.prepare('INSERT INTO meta (k, v) VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT (k) DO UPDATE SET v = excluded.v');
        const first = Number((w.prepare('SELECT min(blob_id) AS b FROM blobs WHERE z IS NOT NULL').get() as { b: number }).b);
        let added = 0;
        const moves: [string, () => number][] = [
          ['a blob it stores, unindexed', () => {
            const n = Number(w.prepare('INSERT INTO blobs (sha256, codec, z, raw_len, fts_indexed) SELECT ?, codec, z, raw_len, 0 FROM blobs WHERE blob_id = ?')
              .run(randomBytes(32), first).changes);
            added = Number((w.prepare('SELECT max(blob_id) AS b FROM blobs').get() as { b: number }).b);
            return n;
          }],
          ['a pair it records', () => Number(w.prepare('INSERT INTO redact_hashes (len, sha256, first_seen_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?)').run(40, randomBytes(32), 1).changes)],
          ['the mark its re-derivation moves', () => Number(upsert.run('fts_reindex_rid', '987654').changes)],
          ['its re-derivation state', () => Number(upsert.run('fts_rederive', '987654 1 2').changes)],
          ["its backfill's cursor", () => Number(w.prepare("UPDATE derivation_state SET cursor = '987654' WHERE step = 'fts' AND version = 1").run().changes)],
          ['an index row for a blob already stored', () => Number(w.prepare('INSERT INTO blobs_fts (rowid, body) VALUES (?, ?)').run(added, 'zqwitness parts').changes)],
        ];
        for (const [what, move] of moves) {
          const was = W.beltWitness(w);
          expect(move(), `CONTROL: ${what} was written`).toBe(1);
          expect(W.beltWitness(w), what).not.toBe(was);
        }
      } finally { w.close(); }
    } finally { fs.rmSync(box.home, { recursive: true, force: true }); }
  });
});
```

  6. Directly above `rederiveFts`'s doc comment, whose first line is B1's `/** The hash re-derivation that moves the re-index mark (§6.2 "A pair learned after its text was indexed", D-4344,`, insert:

```js
/** The store's witness for the belt (§6.2 "The belt", coordinator ruling R-rollback): the values each index writer of a
 *  build without the belt (B1, after a rollback) moves when it writes a row, so a belt-aware pass that finds them moved
 *  since it last recorded them knows another build wrote. Its ingest raises max(blob_id) (AUTOINCREMENT: an id is never
 *  reused); a pair it records raises the top redact_hashes rowid, and only then does its phrase path write; its
 *  re-derivation moves meta fts_rederive (a cursor, or a generation of its own, since it cannot parse ` b`) and, at
 *  completion, fts_reindex_rid; its backfill moves ('fts', 1)'s cursor and completed_ms; and every index row it
 *  writes or deletes moves ftsIndexWitness, including its ingest's row for a blob ALREADY stored with fts_indexed 0,
 *  which moves none of the others (finding V13). B1 advances no meta on every tick, and its ticks row is skipped by a
 *  tick that ends on a busy store after its re-index steps ran, so neither serves; nor do max(blob_id) and
 *  fts_reindex_rid alone, which miss its backfill and an incomplete re-derivation. A short JSON array: never a value,
 *  only ids, a mark, a cursor, a time and a hash of FTS5's own bookkeeping. Each part is on its own line, and each
 *  line's `witness (...)` tag is the anchor of the mutant that removes it (Step 6). */
export function beltWitness(db) {
  const d = derivStmts(db);
  const fts = d.sel.get(FTS_STEP, 1);
  return JSON.stringify([
    d.maxBlob.get().id ?? 0,  // witness (blob): its ingest stores a blob
    d.pairTop.get().rid ?? 0,  // witness (pair): it records a pair, and only then does its phrase path write
    getMeta(db, REINDEX_META) ?? '',  // witness (mark): its re-derivation completes
    getMeta(db, REDERIVE_META) ?? '',  // witness (rederive): its re-derivation's cursor, or a generation of its own
    fts === undefined ? null : [fts.cursor ?? null, fts.completed_ms ?? null],  // witness (backfill): ('fts', 1)
    ftsIndexWitness(db),  // witness (index): every committed blobs_fts write
  ]);
}

/** The index part of beltWitness: the sha256 hex of blobs_fts_data's FTS5 averages record (id 1) and structure record
 *  (id 10). FTS5 rewrites both on every committed insert or delete into blobs_fts, a rewrite of a row with the same
 *  text included (the structure record's cookie moves), so it moves with every index write any build makes, whatever
 *  else that write leaves alone. Inside a transaction that wrote blobs_fts this may read anywhere from the records'
 *  pre-transaction state up to the committed one: FTS5 holds inserts in memory until the commit, but a contentless
 *  delete writes its tombstone and record 10 at once, and a hash-size overflow or a SAVEPOINT flushes early. It never
 *  reads ahead of the commit, so a witness recorded there is behind or exact, never ahead; one behind reads as moved
 *  at the next check, a false positive and never a miss. null when blobs_fts_data does not exist (FTS5 absent, or the tables
 *  not created yet). Both records are small (the structure record lists the segments), so this is O(segments). */
function ftsIndexWitness(db) {
  if (db.prepare("SELECT 1 AS x FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'blobs_fts_data'").get() === undefined) return null;
  const h = createHash('sha256');
  for (const r of db.prepare('SELECT id, block FROM blobs_fts_data WHERE id IN (1, 10) ORDER BY id').all()) h.update(`${r.id}:`).update(r.block);
  return h.digest('hex');
}

/** Inside the caller's transaction, as a pass ends: a parseable meta fts_belt gets `w: beltWitness(db)`, so the
 *  pass's own writes never read as another build's at the next pass (ruling R-rollback). A store with no parseable
 *  state is left as it is: it is due already. recordTick calls it, so the tick and every pass that writes a ticks row
 *  end stamped; each such pass ran secretsStep's witness check first, so a stamp never hides another build's writes.
 *  The caller's transaction writes no blobs_fts row (recordTick's writes none): in one that does, the index part may
 *  read behind those rows, never ahead (ftsIndexWitness), and the stamp costs one belt generation at the next check. */
export function stampBeltWitness(db) {
  const s = parseBeltState(getMeta(db, BELT_META));
  if (s === null) return;
  const next = formatBeltState({ ...s, w: beltWitness(db) });
  if (next !== getMeta(db, BELT_META)) setMeta(db, BELT_META, next);
}

/** The writer order's check (spec §6.2 "The belt"; rulings R-rollback and R-witness-restore), written once: when the
 *  store's witness moved since a belt-aware pass last recorded it (lib's beltWitnessMoved), a pass this build did not
 *  stamp wrote since, so meta fts_belt is recorded due (`{"v":0,"rids":[],"gen":null}`), which also clears an open
 *  generation's record so that it restarts. Inside the caller's transaction; it opens none. secretsStep calls it first
 *  of all, and Task 27's RESTORE_BELT.check inside commitRestore's FULL bind transaction, each before its pass writes
 *  a witnessed value. Answers whether it recorded the due record. */
export function recordBeltDueIfWitnessMoved(db) {
  const moved = beltWitnessMoved(parseBeltState(getMeta(db, BELT_META)), beltWitness(db));
  if (moved) setMeta(db, BELT_META, formatBeltState({ v: 0, rids: [], gen: null }));
  return moved;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Write the mutation runner.** It is the same gitignored scratch tool as Task 5's: Tasks 1–7, 7A, 7B and 8 write this same file, byte for byte, so each task stands alone and rewriting it changes nothing. Like every copy, it spawns vitest with `maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024` (ruling R-runner). From the repository root:

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <<'EOF'
// .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs: measures each guard RED with it mutated, then GREEN with
// it restored (the B2 plan's mutation-pin rule). Run from server/, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least
// 600000 ms:
//   node ../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/mutate.mjs <mutants.json>
// A mutant is {name, file, test, filter, edits: [{anchor, replacement}]}. `file` is repo-relative, `test` is
// server/-relative, and each anchor must occur exactly once in the file as the earlier edits leave it. The
// pristine file is copied to scratch/keep/<file with '/' as '__'>.orig BEFORE it is touched, and the copy is
// removed only after the file is restored from it. A kill no handler sees therefore leaves the original findable,
// and the next run REFUSES while any copy is left. To restore by hand, from the repository root:
//   for f in .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep/*.orig; do t="$(basename "$f" .orig)"; cp "$f" "${t//__//}" && rm "$f"; done
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const KEEP = '../.superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/keep';
mkdirSync(KEEP, { recursive: true });
const left = readdirSync(KEEP).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.orig'));
if (left.length > 0) {
  console.log(`REFUSED: ${left.join(', ')} in ${KEEP}. An earlier run was interrupted and a source may hold a mutant: restore as this file's header says.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const keepOf = (file) => `${KEEP}/${file.replaceAll('/', '__')}.orig`;
const restoreAll = () => {
  for (const n of readdirSync(KEEP)) {
    if (!n.endsWith('.orig')) continue;
    copyFileSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`, `../${n.slice(0, -'.orig'.length).replaceAll('__', '/')}`);
    rmSync(`${KEEP}/${n}`);
  }
};
// Every way out restores: the loop's end, process.exit and an uncaught throw all emit 'exit', and a signal is
// turned into an exit. A signal sent while the synchronous loop holds the thread is handled after the current
// child returns; a Ctrl-C also reaches the vitest child, and the loop stops on the child's signal below.
process.on('exit', restoreAll);
for (const s of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) process.on(s, () => process.exit(130));
// maxBuffer: past Node's default (1 MiB) spawnSync kills the child (ENOBUFS, signal SIGTERM, measured), which the
// loop below reads as an interrupt. Each large-operand case asserts a boolean or a length, so a red prints no big diff.
const vitest = (test, filter) => spawnSync('./node_modules/.bin/vitest', ['run', test, '-t', filter], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 });
const mutants = JSON.parse(readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8'));
let bad = 0;
for (const m of mutants) {
  const target = `../${m.file}`;
  if (!existsSync(target)) { console.log(`NO SUCH FILE       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  const keep = keepOf(m.file);
  copyFileSync(target, keep);
  let src = readFileSync(keep, 'utf8');
  let unique = true;
  for (const e of m.edits) {
    const at = src.indexOf(e.anchor);
    if (at < 0 || src.indexOf(e.anchor, at + 1) >= 0) { unique = false; break; }
    src = src.slice(0, at) + e.replacement + src.slice(at + e.anchor.length);
  }
  if (!unique) { rmSync(keep); console.log(`ANCHOR NOT UNIQUE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; continue; }
  writeFileSync(target, src);
  const red = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  copyFileSync(keep, target);
  rmSync(keep);
  if (red.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${red.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  const failed = /Tests\s+(\d+) failed/.exec(red.stdout)?.[1] ?? '?';
  if (red.status === 0) { console.log(`STAYED GREEN       ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`red (${failed} failed)   ${m.name}`);
  const green = vitest(m.test, m.filter);
  if (green.signal !== null) { console.log(`INTERRUPTED (${green.signal})  ${m.name}`); process.exit(130); }
  if (green.status !== 0) { console.log(`RED AFTER RESTORE  ${m.name}`); bad += 1; } else console.log(`green              ${m.name}`);
}
console.log(bad === 0 ? 'every guard measured red, then green' : `${bad} guard(s) not measured`);
process.exit(bad === 0 ? 0 : 1);
EOF
```

The order is the guard: every text is redacted WHOLE before any cut (the steered block's text before `parseBlocks`, so before `blockFields` cuts the gist at GIST_MAX and each topic at TOPIC_CHARS, and each mined token before it is classified and stored), because a pair matches a whole run and never a prefix. Reparse clears the markers (Task 21), and a new `NODE_PARSER_VERSION` retries them.

    - `('rows-unspanned', <transcript_pk>)`, whose cursor is `<rows_unspanned already folded>:<live bytes read when folded>`. Every tick recounts a main transcript with two or more live copies whose bytes read changed since, or which gained a leaf;
    - `('transcript-forked', <transcript_pk>)`, present once that transcript is counted;
    - `('leaf-crashed', <boundary entry_id>)`, above.

**Spec:**
- §6.1: the span rule (positions from the copy holding each boundary; rows absent from it join no leaf, counted `rows_unspanned`; a copy with no uuid-superset counts `transcript_forked` once); two forks after one head (`leaf_id_forked`); node kinds.
- §6.2: `nodes`, `node_sources`, `node_refs`, `nodes_fts` (redacted gists, topics and refs); the producer of boundary N (the first non-unknown assistant row after its summary row, in the copy that holds it).
- §6.4: compact-card reuse by import plus two in-place `export` keywords; lib stays L1 with the toolkit injected.
- §7.4:
  - item 1: the summary row via `anchorUuid`; `anchor_is_boundary`; the echo row never read; a missing anchor row is `raw_leaf`;
  - item 2: blocks only with a steer receipt, otherwise `not-requested`;
  - items 6-10: caps, refs mined from the span's tool_use rows (origin `tool_use`), the native gist from the last two sections chosen by `summarizeMetadata.direction`, `directive_flag` only, and the counters stratified by producer.
- §9.2 step 6: derive.
- Pins: **PX1**, **PX7**, **PX25**, **DM25**, **DM36**, **DM37**.
- Departures:

  - D-4689 (`history-leaf-id-fork-qualified`)
  - D-4684 (`history-summary-anchor-is-boundary`)
  - D-4683 (`history-native-gist-last-summary-open`)
  - B1's D-4196 (`history-producer-backend`)
  - D-4685 (`history-steer-receipt`)
  - B1's D-4224 (`history-tick-order`)
  - D-4703 (`history-node-indexes-by-derivation`) (NEW). v1 has no index on `nodes(boundary_entry_id)` (which "has this boundary a leaf" reads every tick) or `node_children(child_id)` (who is a node's parent). A schema migration would escalate to `snapshot-needs-op` on every real store (§6.11). So derivation creates them, IF NOT EXISTS, as it creates the FTS tables.
  - D-4704 (`history-summary-direction-from-source-line`) (NEW). B1 stores a summary row's message only, not `summarizeMetadata`. The direction is read from the row's own line in its holding file:
    - through B1's admission (`O_NOFOLLOW`, realpath under a rostered `projects/` root);
    - at its membership byte offset;
    - bounded at `LINE_MAX`;
    - only when the line's uuid matches.
    A file gone or changed gives `null`, and the pair then follows the text.
  - D-4705 (`history-native-refs-no-prlink`) (NEW). §7.4 item 7 also unions `pr-link` metadata refs (origin `meta`). B1 never stores uuid-less rows (G13), so there is no such row to mine. Native refs are the span's `tool_use` paths only.
  - D-4690 (`history-raw-leaf-grace`) (Task 5's): a boundary row with no time of its own takes the newest stamped row before it in the holding copy.
  - D-4706 (`history-parser-crash-recorded`) (NEW, RB5). §9.2's `parser_crash` rule (roll back, hold the cursor, retry next tick) is the transcript reader's; applied to node derivation it would re-parse a poison boundary every 90 s tick, grow `parser_crash` without bound and stall that copy's fan-in. A node-parser throw instead writes its leaf `parse-failed` (a NEW `PARSE_STATUS` word: none of `ok`, `degraded`, `invalid`, `absent`, `not-requested` means "the parser threw"), or a `leaf-crashed` marker when no leaf can be written; it is counted once, and only reparse retries it.
  - D-4707 (`history-summary-size-counters-from-store`) (NEW). §7.4 item 10 also names block chars, and summary chars and duration with versus without steering. Every input is a stored column: the summary blob's `raw_len` through `nodes.summary_blob_id`, `boundaries.duration_ms`, and `steer_receipts` for the arm. Every W1 leaf is the without-steering arm, so W3 reads both arms from the store, and W1 folds no such counter.

```js

// ===========================================================================
// Leaf helpers derive.mjs composes (spec §6.1 "The copy", §7.4 items 2-8;
// W1-B2 Task 8). Pure.
// ===========================================================================

/** A summary row's `summarizeMetadata.direction` (§7.4 item 8): `from` or `up_to`, else null. derive.mjs reads
 *  the row from the line it came from, because the store keeps a summary row's message only.
 *  D-4704 (history-summary-direction-from-source-line) */
export function directionOfSummaryRow(row) {
  const meta = row !== null && typeof row === 'object' && !Array.isArray(row) ? row.summarizeMetadata : undefined;
  const d = meta !== null && typeof meta === 'object' ? meta.direction : undefined;
  return d === 'from' || d === 'up_to' ? d : null;
}

/** A selected block's stored fields (§7.4 items 3, 6, 7). The block was parsed from REDACTED text, so every cut
 *  below lands on redacted text (§8.3, SE1):
 *  - the gist, trimmed, cut at GIST_MAX by Task 4's capText, then trimmed at its end again: the form Task 4's
 *    gistSha hashes, so a later block carrying this gist word for word is a carried copy even past the cap; empty
 *    is null;
 *  - topics: the `Expand for details about:` field split on commas, through capTopics (each once, at most
 *    TOPICS_MAX of at most TOPIC_CHARS);
 *  - refs: the `refs:` values classifyRef recognises, origin `model` (capRefs runs over the leaf's union).
 *  Both cuts are surrogate-safe. A cut sets `capped`; no marker is ever inserted. */
export function blockFields(block) {
  const gist = capText(typeof block.gist === 'string' ? block.gist.trim() : '', GIST_MAX);
  const topics = capTopics((typeof block.expand === 'string' ? block.expand : '').split(','));
  const refs = [];
  for (const v of Array.isArray(block.refs) ? block.refs : []) {
    const kind = typeof v === 'string' ? classifyRef(v) : null;
    if (kind !== null) refs.push({ kind, value: v, origin: 'model' });
  }
  const text = gist.text.trimEnd();
  return { gist: text === '' ? null : text, topics: topics.topics, refs, capped: gist.capped || topics.capped };
}

/** The steer receipt a leaf's span carries (§7.4 item 2): the receipt naming this leaf's id, else a generic one
 *  (leafId '') received after the previous boundary and no later than this one; null when neither. An epoch's
 *  first leaf has no lower bound. D-4685 (history-steer-receipt) */
export function pickReceipt(receipts, { id, afterMs, uptoMs }) {
  const exact = receipts.find((r) => r.leafId === id);
  if (exact !== undefined) return exact;
  return receipts.find((r) => r.leafId === '' && (afterMs === null || r.tsMs > afterMs) && (uptoMs === null || r.tsMs <= uptoMs)) ?? null;
}

/** The copy that holds a boundary (§6.1 "The copy"): among a transcript's files that have the boundary row as a
 *  member, a live one (source_key '') before a retired or exported one, then the smallest file_id; null when no file
 *  holds it. derive.mjs measures `live` and `holds`; Task 9's fan-in splits its slots by this same answer.
 *  D-4688 (history-span-per-boundary-copy) */
export function pickHoldingCopy(files) {
  let best = null;
  for (const f of files) {
    if (!f.holds) continue;
    if (best === null || (f.live && !best.live) || (f.live === best.live && f.fileId < best.fileId)) best = f;
  }
  return best === null ? null : best.fileId;
}

/** A main transcript's fork counts (§6.1), from what derive.mjs measured over its LIVE copies: each copy's row
 *  count, the rows in any of them, the rows in a copy that holds one of its leaves' boundaries, and how many copies
 *  hold one. `unspanned` is how many rows no holding copy has: they join no leaf (none while no copy holds a leaf,
 *  when every row is still live tail). `forked` is true when two or more live copies exist and none holds every row
 *  (no uuid-superset). */
export function forkCounts({ liveSizes, unionSize, coveredSize, holdingCopies }) {
  return {
    unspanned: holdingCopies === 0 ? 0 : Math.max(0, unionSize - coveredSize),
    forked: liveSizes.length > 1 && !liveSizes.some((n) => n === unionSize),
  };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Add the derivation_state helpers to the store.** Append to the end of `ccd/history/store.mjs`:

```js

// ── W1-B2 Task 8: derivation_state steps by name (§6.2 `derivation_state`) ─────────────────────────────────────

/** One derivation step's row: its cursor (TEXT, as the step wrote it) and when it completed; null when the step
 *  has no row. */
export function getStep(db, step, version) {
  const r = db.prepare('SELECT cursor, completed_ms FROM derivation_state WHERE step = ? AND version = ?').get(step, version);
  if (r === undefined) return null;
  return { cursor: r.cursor === null ? null : String(r.cursor), completedMs: r.completed_ms === null ? null : Number(r.completed_ms) };
}

/** Upsert one derivation step's row; the caller holds the transaction. An omitted `completedMs` leaves an
 *  existing completed_ms as it is (a new row gets NULL); a number or null sets it. */
export function setStep(db, step, version, cursor, completedMs) {
  if (completedMs === undefined) {
    db.prepare(`INSERT INTO derivation_state (step, version, cursor, completed_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?, NULL)
      ON CONFLICT (step, version) DO UPDATE SET cursor = excluded.cursor`).run(step, version, cursor);
    return;
  }
  db.prepare(`INSERT INTO derivation_state (step, version, cursor, completed_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
    ON CONFLICT (step, version) DO UPDATE SET cursor = excluded.cursor, completed_ms = excluded.completed_ms`)
    .run(step, version, cursor, completedMs);
}
```
