```bash
if (file === undefined || anchor === undefined || pairs.length === 0 || pairs.length % 2 !== 0) {
  console.error('usage: node mut-after.mjs <file> <anchor> <needle> <replacement> [<needle> <replacement> ...]');
  process.exit(2);
}
const scratch = join('.superpowers', 'sdd', 'history-w1-b2', 'scratch');
mkdirSync(scratch, { recursive: true });
const orig = join(scratch, `${basename(file)}.orig`);
if (existsSync(orig)) {
  console.error(`mut-after: ${orig} exists: restore the earlier mutant first (mv ${orig} ${file})`);
  process.exit(1);
}
let text = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
const at = text.indexOf(anchor);
if (at < 0) { console.error(`mut-after: anchor not found in ${file}: ${anchor}`); process.exit(1); }
for (let i = 0; i < pairs.length; i += 2) {
  const k = text.indexOf(pairs[i], at);
  if (k < 0) { console.error(`mut-after: needle not found after the anchor: ${pairs[i]}`); process.exit(1); }
  text = text.slice(0, k) + pairs[i + 1] + text.slice(k + pairs[i].length);
}
copyFileSync(file, orig);
writeFileSync(file, text);
console.log(`mut-after: mutated ${file}; restore with: mv ${orig} ${file}`);
EOF
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement the lineage in store.mjs.** Append this section to the END of `ccd/history/store.mjs`, after B1's `createFtsTables`:

```js
// ── Lineage: the range CTE and the two edge lookups (spec §6.3; W1-B2 Task 9) ────────────────────────────
// The edge names are directional (§6.3):
//   - node_sources is leaf → its entries, ordered;
//   - node_children is parent → the nodes it condenses, ordered.
// The lineage walks DOWN, from a node to what it condenses and then to those nodes' source entries. The
// upstream subtree CTE walks toward a summary's CONSUMERS with UNION ALL (summary-store.ts:780-822); it is not
// ported (§11, refuted candidate 4). UNION, not UNION ALL, so a cycle in node_children ends the walk.
// derived from lossless-claw src/store/summary-store.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw
// From getSummaryMessageSeqRange, upstream lines 595-621. SQLite keeps a CROSS JOIN's order, so this visits
// the lineage before it looks up any link. A reordered join could scan every family's links once per node.
const LINEAGE_SQL = `WITH RECURSIVE source_nodes(node_id) AS (
  SELECT ?
  UNION
  SELECT nc.child_id
  FROM node_children nc
  JOIN source_nodes s ON s.node_id = nc.node_id
)
SELECT ns.node_id AS node_id, ns.entry_id AS entry_id, ns.ord AS ord, e.ts_ms AS ts_ms
FROM source_nodes s
CROSS JOIN node_sources ns ON ns.node_id = s.node_id
CROSS JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = ns.entry_id
ORDER BY ns.node_id, ns.ord`;

/** Every source entry under `nodeId`: a leaf's own, or every leaf's below a parent. Rows come grouped by leaf id
 *  and in each leaf's `ord`. Ordering the leaves themselves (by `boundaries.ord`) is the caller's job. */
export function lineageEntries(db, nodeId) {
  return db.prepare(LINEAGE_SQL).all(nodeId).map((r) => ({
    nodeId: r.node_id, entryId: Number(r.entry_id), ord: Number(r.ord), tsMs: r.ts_ms === null ? null : Number(r.ts_ms),
  }));
}

/** What `nodeId` condenses, in order (empty for a leaf). */
export function childrenOf(db, nodeId) {
  return db.prepare('SELECT child_id, ord FROM node_children WHERE node_id = ? ORDER BY ord').all(nodeId)
    .map((r) => ({ childId: r.child_id, ord: Number(r.ord) }));
}

/** The node that condenses `nodeId`, or null. Fan-in gives a node one parent; ORDER BY keeps the answer
 *  deterministic over a hand-damaged table. */
export function parentOf(db, nodeId) {
  const r = db.prepare('SELECT node_id FROM node_children WHERE child_id = ? ORDER BY node_id LIMIT 1').get(nodeId);
  return r === undefined ? null : r.node_id;
}
```

```ts
// ── W1-B2 Task 9: parents (fan-in per epoch, final leaves only), the nodes_fts backfill, a re-key moves nodes ──
// DM26 (spec 2026-10-05 §6.3, §6.7):
//   - through real ticks: 8 leaves in one epoch make one depth-1 parent; 8 leaves spanning a /clear make none,
//     and the /clear epoch, confirmed only at a later tick, has no node before it is confirmed (review focus 4);
//   - in-process: a boundary whose leaf is not derived yet stops the group; fan-in is 4 per level above;
//   - in-process: fan-in is per holding copy, so two forks of one transcript never share a parent (ruling RB4).
// Plus (not pins): the nodes_fts backfill indexes redacted text once, and mergeFamily re-points nodes.
import * as v9 from 'vitest';
import * as tmp9 from './tmpHelpers.js';
import * as lib9 from '../../ccd/history/lib.mjs';
import * as store9 from '../../ccd/history/store.mjs';
import * as h9 from './historyHelpers.js';
import * as fx9 from './historyFixtures.js';
import type { DatabaseSync as Db9 } from 'node:sqlite';

interface Derive9 {
  deriveParents(db: Db9, ictx: object, budget: object): number;
  indexNodesFts(db: Db9, ictx: object, budget: object): number;
  rerollParents(db: Db9, ictx: object, nodeIds: readonly string[]): number;
}
interface Sweep9 {
  newBudget(): object;
  mergeFamily(db: Db9, fromPk: number, toPk: number): void;
}
const derive9 = async (): Promise<Derive9> => (await import('../../ccd/history/derive.mjs')) as unknown as Derive9;
const sweep9 = async (): Promise<Sweep9> => (await import('../../ccd/history/sweep.mjs')) as unknown as Sweep9;

const ID9 = 'claude-a-demo';
const E9 = 'd9e00000-1111-4111-8111-111111111111';
const T0_9 = Date.UTC(2026, 9, 1, 10, 0, 0);
const CWD9 = '/home/u/worktrees/p/quiet-basin';
const uid9 = (p: string, n: number): string => `${p}-0000-4000-8000-${n.toString(16).padStart(12, '0')}`;
const NO_PAIRS9 = lib9.makePairIndex([]);

/** A fresh store: one family, one confirmed epoch, one transcript with `n` boundaries, and a native leaf at
 *  every boundary except those in `missing` (a leaf the derivation has not reached yet). The transcript has
 *  `copies` live files (file_id 1, 2, …), and boundary k is a member of the files `holders(k)` names, so fan-in,
 *  which groups per holding copy, finds each boundary's copy the way Task 8's holdingCopy does. By default one
 *  copy holds every boundary. */
function epochFixture9(prefix: string, n: number, missing: ReadonlySet<number>,
  copies = 1, holders: (k: number) => readonly number[] = () => [1]): { db: Db9; leafIds: string[] } {
  const home = tmp9.mkTmp(prefix);
  store9.createStore(home);
  const db = store9.openWriter(lib9.historyPaths(home).dbFile);
  const leafIds: string[] = [];
  db.exec('BEGIN');
  db.prepare("INSERT INTO sessions (session_pk, ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms) VALUES (1, ?, '', 'demo', 1)").run(ID9);
  db.prepare("INSERT INTO epochs (session_pk, seq, cc_session_uuid, cause, declared_by, confirmed_ms) VALUES (1, 1, ?, 'startup', 'hook', 1)").run(E9);
  db.prepare('INSERT INTO transcripts (transcript_pk, cc_session_uuid) VALUES (1, ?)').run(E9);
  const file = db.prepare("INSERT INTO ingest_files (file_id, dev, ino, transcript_pk, status, parser_version) VALUES (?, 1, ?, 1, 'live', 1)");
  for (let f = 1; f <= copies; f += 1) file.run(f, 9000 + f);
  db.prepare("INSERT INTO blobs (blob_id, sha256, codec, z, raw_len) VALUES (1, ?, 'br5', ?, 1)").run(Buffer.alloc(32, 9), Buffer.from([0]));
  const ent = db.prepare("INSERT INTO entries (entry_id, uuid, transcript_pk, type, subtype, provenance, prov_version, struct_rank_ns, struct_file_id, blob_id, ts_ms) VALUES (?, ?, 1, 'system', 'compact_boundary', 'harness', 1, 0, 0, 1, ?)");
  const bnd = db.prepare('INSERT INTO boundaries (entry_id, transcript_pk, ord) VALUES (?, 1, ?)');
  const member = db.prepare('INSERT INTO memberships (file_id, entry_id, line) VALUES (?, ?, ?)');
  for (let k = 1; k <= n; k += 1) {
    ent.run(k, uid9('d9e00000', k), 1000 * k);
    bnd.run(k, k);
    for (const f of holders(k)) member.run(f, k, k);
    const id = lib9.leafId(ID9, E9, `span-${k}`);
    leafIds.push(id);
    if (!missing.has(k)) addLeaf9(db, k, id);
  }
  db.exec('COMMIT');
  return { db, leafIds };
}
function addLeaf9(db: Db9, k: number, id: string): void {
  db.prepare("INSERT INTO nodes (node_id, session_pk, epoch_seq, transcript_pk, kind, depth, status, gist, topics, boundary_entry_id, earliest_ms, latest_ms, src_chars, desc_count, desc_chars, parser_version, created_ms) VALUES (?, 1, 1, 1, 'native_leaf', 0, 'not-requested', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 100, 0, 0, 1, 1)")
    .run(id, `Leaf ${k} did part ${k}. It also did more.`, JSON.stringify([`topic ${k}`]), k, 1000 * k, 1000 * k + 500);
}
interface Parent9 { node_id: string; kind: string; status: string; gist: string | null; topics: string | null; earliest_ms: number; latest_ms: number; desc_count: number }
const parents9 = (db: Db9, depth: number): Parent9[] =>
  (db.prepare('SELECT node_id, kind, status, gist, topics, earliest_ms, latest_ms, desc_count FROM nodes WHERE depth = ? ORDER BY earliest_ms').all(depth) as unknown as Parent9[]).map((r) => ({ ...r }));
const children9 = (db: Db9, id: string): string[] =>
  (db.prepare('SELECT child_id FROM node_children WHERE node_id = ? ORDER BY ord').all(id) as { child_id: string }[]).map((r) => r.child_id);

/** `n` manual compactions in one transcript. Each cycle is a user turn, an answer, a kept follow-up, the
 *  boundary (head = the follow-up, kept = [the follow-up]) and the summary row right after it (§6.1's manual
 *  shape: the anchor is the summary, one row past the boundary). Row uuids carry the 8-hex prefix `p`, so two
 *  transcripts never share one. */
function cycles9(p: string, sid: string, n: number, t0: number): fx9.Row[] {
  const rows: fx9.Row[] = [];
  let k = 0;
  let t = t0;
  const ts = (): string => new Date((t += 1000)).toISOString();
  for (let c = 1; c <= n; c += 1) {
    const u = uid9(p, ++k); const a = uid9(p, ++k); const x = uid9(p, ++k); const b = uid9(p, ++k); const s = uid9(p, ++k);
    rows.push(fx9.userRow({ uuid: u, ts: ts(), sessionId: sid, cwd: CWD9, text: `fixture request ${c}` }));
    rows.push(fx9.assistantRow({ uuid: a, ts: ts(), sessionId: sid, cwd: CWD9, text: `Fixture answer ${c}. More detail follows.`, requestId: `req_${p}_${c}`, msgId: `msg_${p}_${c}` }));
    rows.push(fx9.userRow({ uuid: x, ts: ts(), sessionId: sid, cwd: CWD9, text: `fixture follow-up ${c}` }));
    rows.push(fx9.boundaryRow({ uuid: b, ts: ts(), sessionId: sid, cwd: CWD9, trigger: 'manual', headUuid: x, anchorUuid: s, tailUuid: x, allUuids: [x] }));
    rows.push(fx9.summaryRow({ uuid: s, ts: ts(), sessionId: sid, cwd: CWD9, text: [
      'This session is being continued from a previous conversation. The summary below covers the earlier portion.',
      '<summary>', '1. Primary Request and Intent:', `   Fixture request ${c}.`,
      '8. Current Work:', `   Wrote part ${c} of the fixture.`,
      '9. Optional Next Step:', `   Continue with part ${c + 1}.`, '</summary>',
    ].join('\n') }));
  }
  return rows;
}

v9.describe('DM26: parents by fan-in, never across an epoch, only over final leaves (W1-B2 Task 9)', () => {
  v9.it('a boundary whose leaf is not derived yet stops the group: 9 boundaries, leaf 4 missing, no parent; leaf 4 derived, one parent over leaves 1-8', async () => {
    const d = await derive9();

    const ictx = { nowMs: 5_000, fts: false, pairIdx: NO_PAIRS9 };
    try {
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget());
      v9.expect(parents9(fx.db, 1), 'slot 4 is not final: slots 1-3 and 5-9 are never one group').toEqual([]);
      addLeaf9(fx.db, 4, fx.leafIds[3]!);
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget());
      const p = parents9(fx.db, 1);
      v9.expect(p).toHaveLength(1);
      v9.expect(p[0]!.node_id, 'parentId over the children in boundary order').toBe(lib9.parentId(fx.leafIds.slice(0, 8)));
      v9.expect(children9(fx.db, p[0]!.node_id)).toEqual(fx.leafIds.slice(0, 8));
      v9.expect([p[0]!.kind, p[0]!.status]).toEqual(['condensed', 'ok']);
      v9.expect(p[0]!.gist).toContain('Leaf 1 did part 1');
      v9.expect(p[0]!.gist).toContain('Leaf 8 did part 8');
      v9.expect([p[0]!.earliest_ms, p[0]!.latest_ms]).toEqual([1000, 8500]);
      v9.expect(p[0]!.desc_count).toBe(8);
      v9.expect(JSON.parse(p[0]!.topics ?? '[]')).toEqual(v9.expect.arrayContaining(['topic 1', 'topic 8']));
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget());
      v9.expect(parents9(fx.db, 1), 'a rerun mints nothing again').toHaveLength(1);
    } finally {
      fx.db.close();
    }
  });

  v9.it('fan-in is 4 per level above the leaves: 32 leaves give four depth-1 parents and one depth-2 parent over them, in order', async () => {
    const d = await derive9();
    const s = await sweep9();
    const fx = epochFixture9('ccrc-hist-dm26-d2-', 32, new Set());
    try {
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, { nowMs: 5_000, fts: false, pairIdx: NO_PAIRS9 }, s.newBudget());
      const level1 = [0, 8, 16, 24].map((i) => lib9.parentId(fx.leafIds.slice(i, i + 8)));
      v9.expect(parents9(fx.db, 1).map((r) => r.node_id)).toEqual(level1);
      const top = parents9(fx.db, 2);

      v9.expect(children9(fx.db, top[0]!.node_id)).toEqual(level1);

    } finally {

  v9.it('a parent never mixes forks: two copies share a head, fork, and interleave in ord; each copy gets its own parent, and a leaf not derived in one stops only that copy (RB4)', async () => {
    const d = await derive9();
    const s = await sweep9();
    // Boundaries 1-2: the shared head, in both copies, so held by file 1 (both are live: the smaller file_id).
    // Then the forks arrive interleaved: odd k from 3 to 17 is copy A's (file 1 only), even k from 4 to 18 copy
    // B's (file 2 only). boundaries.ord is per transcript, so the two forks' ords interleave as they do on a box.
    const holders = (k: number): number[] => (k <= 2 ? [1, 2] : k % 2 === 1 ? [1] : [2]);
    const fx = epochFixture9('ccrc-hist-dm26-fork-', 18, new Set([7]), 2, holders);
    const ictx = { nowMs: 5_000, fts: false, pairIdx: NO_PAIRS9 };
    const leaf = (k: number): string => fx.leafIds[k - 1]!;
    const copyA = [1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13].map(leaf);
    const copyB = [4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18].map(leaf);
    try {
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget());
      v9.expect(parents9(fx.db, 1).map((p) => p.node_id), 'leaf 7 (copy A) is not derived yet: copy B still gets its parent')
        .toEqual([lib9.parentId(copyB)]);
      addLeaf9(fx.db, 7, leaf(7));
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget());
      const made = parents9(fx.db, 1).map((p) => p.node_id).sort();
      v9.expect(made).toEqual([lib9.parentId(copyA), lib9.parentId(copyB)].sort());
      v9.expect(children9(fx.db, lib9.parentId(copyA)), 'the head and copy A\'s first six, in ord').toEqual(copyA);
      // Every parent's children sit in one holding copy: the smallest live file_id with the boundary as a member.
      const holderOf = (id: string): number => {
        const b = (fx.db.prepare('SELECT boundary_entry_id AS e FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?').get(id) as { e: number }).e;
        return Number((fx.db.prepare('SELECT min(file_id) AS f FROM memberships WHERE entry_id = ?').get(b) as { f: number }).f);
      };
      for (const p of made) v9.expect(new Set(children9(fx.db, p).map(holderOf)).size, `${p}: one holding copy`).toBe(1);
    } finally {
      fx.db.close();
    }
  });

  v9.it('rerollParents re-rolls every parent above a changed leaf from its children as stored now, ids kept (Tasks 21 and 29 call it)', async () => {
    const d = await derive9();
    const s = await sweep9();
    const fx = epochFixture9('ccrc-hist-reroll-', 32, new Set());
    const ictx = { nowMs: 5_000, fts: false, pairIdx: NO_PAIRS9 };
    try {
      d.deriveParents(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget());

      const before = ids();
      fx.db.prepare('UPDATE nodes SET gist = ? WHERE node_id = ?').run('Leaf 3 was re-derived. Its tail is dropped.', fx.leafIds[2]!);
      v9.expect(d.rerollParents(fx.db, ictx, [fx.leafIds[2]!]), 'its depth-1 parent, then the depth-2 parent above that').toBe(2);
      const p1 = parents9(fx.db, 1);

      v9.expect(p1[0]!.gist).not.toContain('Leaf 3 did part 3');

      v9.expect(ids(), 'no parent id changes').toEqual(before);

    } finally {

    }

  v9.it('through real ticks: 8 leaves in one epoch make one parent; 8 leaves spanning a /clear make none, and the late-confirmed /clear epoch has no node before it is confirmed', () => {
    const one = h9.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-dm26-one-');
    const acct = Object.keys(one.accountHome)[0]!;
    const T = 'd26a0000-1111-4111-8111-111111111111';
    h9.plantSession(one, ID9, { uuid: T, project: 'demo' });
    h9.plantTranscript(one, acct, '-home-u-tree-demo', T, cycles9('d26a1a00', T, 8, T0_9));
    h9.spoolLine(one, ID9, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: ID9, sid: T, src: 'startup', reg: T });
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) v9.expect(h9.runSweep(one).code).toBe(0);
    const db1 = h9.openStoreRO(one);
    try {
      const leaves = (db1.prepare('SELECT n.node_id AS id FROM nodes n JOIN boundaries b ON b.entry_id = n.boundary_entry_id WHERE n.depth = 0 ORDER BY b.ord').all() as { id: string }[]).map((r) => r.id);
      v9.expect(leaves).toHaveLength(8);
      v9.expect(parents9(db1, 1).map((r) => r.node_id)).toEqual([lib9.parentId(leaves)]);
    } finally {
      db1.close();
    }

    const two = h9.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-dm26-clear-');
    const acct2 = Object.keys(two.accountHome)[0]!;
    const T1 = 'd26c1000-1111-4111-8111-111111111111';
    const T2 = 'd26c2000-2222-4222-8222-222222222222';
    // B1 renames a spool line at the END of a tick and drains it at the NEXT (sweep.mjs's listDraining loop, then
    // renameAndObserve), and the first tick also runs the registry scan, which books a planted .uuid as an 'import'
    // epoch. So the box is primed first: that tick spends the scan, and epoch 1 is the hook's 'startup'.
    v9.expect(h9.runSweep(two).code).toBe(0);   // prime: spends the first tick's registry scan, so epoch 1 is the hook's 'startup'
    h9.plantSession(two, ID9, { uuid: T1, project: 'demo' });
    h9.plantTranscript(two, acct2, '-home-u-tree-demo', T1, cycles9('d26c1a00', T1, 4, T0_9));
    h9.spoolLine(two, ID9, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: ID9, sid: T1, src: 'startup', reg: T1 });
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) v9.expect(h9.runSweep(two).code).toBe(0);
    // The /clear line drains while .uuid still names T1 and no .workdir is set: B1 chains its epoch UNCONFIRMED
    // (SE5; decideEpochLine, then confirmClear waits), out of every scope. .uuid names T2 only after that tick, so
    // a LATER tick confirms it ('later-tick'), and only then do its leaves appear, in that epoch (review focus 4).
    h9.plantTranscript(two, acct2, '-home-u-tree-demo', T2, cycles9('d26c2a00', T2, 4, T0_9 + 3_600_000));
    h9.spoolLine(two, ID9, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: ID9, sid: T2, src: 'clear' });
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) v9.expect(h9.runSweep(two).code).toBe(0);   // tick N renames the /clear line, tick N+1 drains it and chains the unconfirmed epoch
    const early = h9.openStoreRO(two);
    try {
      const ep = early.prepare('SELECT seq, confirmed_ms FROM epochs ORDER BY seq').all() as { seq: number; confirmed_ms: number | null }[];
      v9.expect(ep.map((e) => [e.seq, e.confirmed_ms !== null]), 'the /clear epoch waits unconfirmed').toEqual([[1, true], [2, false]]);
      v9.expect((early.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM nodes WHERE epoch_seq = 2').get() as { n: number }).n, 'no node in an unconfirmed epoch').toBe(0);
    } finally {
      early.close();
    }
    h9.plantSession(two, ID9, { uuid: T2 });
    h9.spoolLine(two, ID9, { v: 1, ev: 'Stop', id: ID9 });   // a renamed line for the id hints its confirmed epochs and .uuid at ingest; without one, T2 waits for the 30-minute scan
    for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) v9.expect(h9.runSweep(two).code).toBe(0);
    const db2 = h9.openStoreRO(two);
    try {
      const epochs = (db2.prepare('SELECT seq, cause, confirmed_ms FROM epochs ORDER BY seq').all() as { seq: number; cause: string; confirmed_ms: number | null }[]);
      v9.expect(epochs.map((e) => [e.seq, e.cause, e.confirmed_ms !== null])).toEqual([[1, 'startup', true], [2, 'clear', true]]);
      v9.expect((db2.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM nodes WHERE depth = 0').get() as { n: number }).n).toBe(8);
      v9.expect((db2.prepare('SELECT epoch_seq AS e, count(*) AS n FROM nodes WHERE depth = 0 GROUP BY epoch_seq ORDER BY epoch_seq').all() as { e: number; n: number }[])
        .map((r) => [r.e, r.n]), 'the late-confirmed epoch\'s leaves sit in it').toEqual([[1, 4], [2, 4]]);
      v9.expect(parents9(db2, 1), 'four leaves in each epoch: never one group across the /clear').toEqual([]);
    } finally {
      db2.close();
    }
  }, 120_000);
});

  v9.it('indexNodesFts indexes each node once, on redacted text, and a rerun adds nothing', async (ctx) => {

      const plain = 'fixtureonlylowercasevalueqwrt';

      fx.db.prepare('UPDATE nodes SET gist = ? WHERE node_id = ?').run(`Leaf 2 did part 2 with ${secret} and {"t":"a\\n${plain}"}.`, fx.leafIds[1]!);
      // Leaf 1: the value glued to letters (§8.3 layer 4, Task 7A): one run no pair matches, which the belt masks.
      fx.db.prepare('UPDATE nodes SET gist = ? WHERE node_id = ?').run(`Leaf 1 did part 1 with zq${secret}x.`, fx.leafIds[0]!);
      const ictx = { nowMs: 5_000, fts: true, pairIdx: lib9.makePairIndex(lib9.secretPairs([secret, plain]).pairs,
        lib9.makeBelt(lib9.beltUnits([secret, plain]))) };
      v9.expect(d.indexNodesFts(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget())).toBe(2);
      const hits = (q: string): number => (fx.db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM nodes_fts WHERE nodes_fts MATCH ?').get(q) as { n: number }).n;
      v9.expect(hits('"part"')).toBe(2);
      v9.expect(hits(`"${secret}"`), 'the value was redacted before indexing').toBe(0);
      v9.expect(hits(`"zq${secret}x"`), 'the glued value was masked by the belt before indexing (§8.3 layer 4)').toBe(0);
      v9.expect(hits(`"n${plain}"`), 'the escape-glued value was redacted on its decoded reading before indexing').toBe(0);
      v9.expect(hits(`"${plain}"`)).toBe(0);
      const nodeBytes = (fx.db.prepare('SELECT block FROM nodes_fts_data').all() as { block: Uint8Array }[])
        .map((r) => Buffer.from(r.block).toString('latin1')).join('');
      v9.expect(nodeBytes.includes(secret.slice(4, 18)), 'no 14 characters of the value are an index byte').toBe(false);
      v9.expect(d.indexNodesFts(fx.db, ictx, s.newBudget()), 'a rerun inserts no duplicate rowid').toBe(0);
      v9.expect((fx.db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM nodes_fts').get() as { n: number }).n).toBe(2);
    } finally {
      fx.db.close();
    }

    const s = await sweep9();

    store9.createStore(home);
    const db = store9.openWriter(lib9.historyPaths(home).dbFile);
    const U = ['e1000000-1111-4111-8111-111111111111', 'e2000000-2222-4222-8222-222222222222',
      'e3000000-3333-4333-8333-333333333333', 'e4000000-4444-4444-8444-444444444444'];
    const G = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0123456789ab';
    try {
      db.exec('BEGIN');
      db.prepare("INSERT INTO sessions (session_pk, ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms) VALUES (1, ?, '', 'demo', 1)").run(ID9);
      db.prepare("INSERT INTO sessions (session_pk, ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms) VALUES (2, ?, ?, 'demo', 2)").run(ID9, G);
      U.forEach((u, i) => { db.prepare('INSERT INTO transcripts (transcript_pk, cc_session_uuid) VALUES (?, ?)').run(i + 1, u); });
      const ep = db.prepare("INSERT INTO epochs (session_pk, seq, cc_session_uuid, cause, declared_by, confirmed_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'startup', 'hook', 1)");
      ep.run(1, 1, U[0]!); ep.run(1, 2, U[1]!); ep.run(2, 1, U[2]!);
      const node = db.prepare("INSERT INTO nodes (node_id, session_pk, epoch_seq, transcript_pk, kind, depth, status, parser_version, created_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'ok', 1, 1)");
      node.run('L1aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', 1, 1, 1, 'native_leaf', 0);
      node.run('N1aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', 1, 1, 1, 'condensed', 1);
      node.run('L2aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', 1, 2, 2, 'native_leaf', 0);
      node.run('L3aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', 2, 1, 3, 'native_leaf', 0);
      node.run('L4aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', 1, 1, 4, 'native_leaf', 0);

      s.mergeFamily(db, 1, 2);

      const where = (id: string): number[] => {

        return [r.session_pk, r.epoch_seq];

        .map((e) => [e.seq, e.cc_session_uuid])).toEqual([[1, U[0]], [2, U[1]], [3, U[2]]]);

      v9.expect((db.prepare("SELECT n FROM counters WHERE name = 'nodes_unrepointed'").get() as { n: number }).n).toBe(1);
```

Merge these names into derive.mjs's existing import clauses, adding only those absent (Task 8 already imports some):
- from `'./lib.mjs'`: `parentId, planFanIn, parentRollup, FAN_IN, directiveFlag, nodeIndexTexts, NODE_PARSER_VERSION, withinBudget` (Task 8 already imports `nodeIndexTexts`; this section calls no `redactField`);
- from `'./store.mjs'`: `withTx, getStep, setStep, parentOf`.

Then append this section to the END of `ccd/history/derive.mjs`:

```js
// ── Parents: fan-in per epoch, deterministic rollups (spec §6.3; W1-B2 Task 9) ───────────────────────────
//
// Which leaves group:
//   - 8 leaves make a depth-1 parent, and 4 nodes per level above (FAN_IN; lib's planFanIn decides each group);
//   - never across a /clear epoch: an epoch's slots are its own main transcript's boundaries, in `ord`;
//   - never across two forks: those slots are split per HOLDING COPY, the transcript file Task 8's holdingCopy
//     picks for each boundary, and fan-in runs per copy, so a parent's children share one copy (the
//     coordinator's ruling RB4; slug history-span-per-boundary-copy, extended to fan-in);
//   - only over FINAL leaves: a boundary whose leaf is not derived yet is a null slot, and a null slot stops the
//     group of its own copy, so a parent never skips a span to fill itself.
// What a parent is:
//   - its id is parentId(child ids, in order), so a retry, a reparse or a rebuild re-derives the same id (§6.1);
//   - its gist, topics, refs, time range and counts come from lib's parentRollup over the children's stored
//     fields. No model summarises anything (§6.3: "always deterministic and rebuildable").
// Writes: each parent, its node_children and node_refs rows, and (when the FTS tables exist) its nodes_fts row
// commit in ONE NORMAL transaction. A node is derived and rebuildable, never journaled (§9.14).
// Cursor (slug history-parents-cursor-by-rowid, NEW): ('parents', NODE_PARSER_VERSION) holds the highest
// nodes.rowid already considered. Only an epoch that gained a node since then is walked again; a budget that
// ends mid-walk leaves the cursor where it was, so the next tick walks those epochs again.

const PARENTS_STEP = 'parents';
/** The nodes_fts backfill's derivation step. Exported: doctor --repair (W1-B2 Task 23) resets its cursor when it
 *  recreates nodes_fts. */
export const NODES_FTS_STEP = 'nodes-fts';
const NODES_FTS_STEP_VERSION = 1;
/** The nodes_fts backfill's page: one NORMAL transaction each. */
const NODES_FTS_BATCH = 256;
/** A walk never climbs past this depth. 4^31 leaves is no store this code will meet; the bound only keeps a
 *  hand-damaged node_children table from looping. */
const MAX_FAN_DEPTH = 32;

function parentsBudgetLeft(budget) {
  return withinBudget({ elapsedMs: budget.now() - budget.startMs, bytes: budget.bytes, maxMs: budget.maxMs, maxBytes: budget.maxBytes });
}

/** A node's `topics` column as a list. A parent writes a JSON array; a column that is not one reads as one
 *  topic per line. */
function topicsOfColumn(text) {
  if (text === null || text === undefined || text === '') return [];
  try {
    const v = JSON.parse(text);
    if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.filter((x) => typeof x === 'string');
  } catch {
    // not JSON: one topic per line, below
  }
  return String(text).split('\n').map((t) => t.trim()).filter((t) => t !== '');
}

const PARENT_STMTS = new WeakMap();
function parentStmts(db) {
  let s = PARENT_STMTS.get(db);
  if (s === undefined) {
    s = {
      maxRow: db.prepare('SELECT max(rowid) AS r FROM nodes'),
      touched: db.prepare('SELECT DISTINCT session_pk, epoch_seq FROM nodes WHERE rowid > ?'),
      epochTranscripts: db.prepare('SELECT t.transcript_pk AS transcript_pk FROM epochs e JOIN transcripts t ON t.cc_session_uuid = e.cc_session_uuid '
        + "WHERE e.session_pk = ? AND e.seq = ? AND t.agent_id = '' ORDER BY t.transcript_pk"),
      bounds: db.prepare('SELECT entry_id, transcript_pk FROM boundaries WHERE transcript_pk = ? ORDER BY ord'),
      leafAt: db.prepare('SELECT node_id FROM nodes WHERE boundary_entry_id = ? AND depth = 0'),
      exists: db.prepare('SELECT 1 AS x FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?'),
      node: db.prepare('SELECT node_id, session_pk, epoch_seq, transcript_pk, gist, topics, earliest_ms, latest_ms, src_chars, desc_count, desc_chars FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?'),
      refs: db.prepare('SELECT kind, value, origin FROM node_refs WHERE node_id = ? ORDER BY rowid'),
      rowidOf: db.prepare('SELECT rowid AS r FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?'),
      insNode: db.prepare('INSERT INTO nodes (node_id, session_pk, epoch_seq, transcript_pk, kind, depth, status, gist, topics, '
        + 'summary_blob_id, boundary_entry_id, span_start_uuid, earliest_ms, latest_ms, src_chars, desc_count, desc_chars, '
        + 'directive_flag, capped, parser_version, created_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, NULL, NULL, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)'),
      insChild: db.prepare('INSERT INTO node_children (node_id, child_id, ord) VALUES (?, ?, ?)'),
      insRef: db.prepare('INSERT INTO node_refs (node_id, kind, value, origin) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT (node_id, kind, value) DO NOTHING'),
    };
    PARENT_STMTS.set(db, s);
  }
  return s;
}

/** A node's stored fields, as parentRollup and the nodes_fts row read them. */
function storedNode(db, id) {
  const s = parentStmts(db);
  const r = s.node.get(id);
  return {
    row: r,
    rollup: {
      gist: typeof r.gist === 'string' ? r.gist : null,
      topics: topicsOfColumn(r.topics),
      refs: s.refs.all(id).map((x) => ({ kind: x.kind, value: x.value, origin: x.origin })),
      earliestMs: r.earliest_ms === null ? null : Number(r.earliest_ms),
      latestMs: r.latest_ms === null ? null : Number(r.latest_ms),
      srcChars: Number(r.src_chars ?? 0),
      descCount: Number(r.desc_count ?? 0),
      descChars: Number(r.desc_chars ?? 0),
    },
  };
}

/** One nodes_fts row: the gist, the topics one per line and the ref values one per line, through lib's nodeIndexTexts
 *  with this tick's pairs (W1-B2 Task 7A: B1's entryIndexText on each column, so redactForIndex's escape readings and
 *  the belt, §8.3 layer 4; spec §6.2 `nodes_fts`, rev 3.5). It is the one index-text rule B1 applies to
 *  blobs_fts, and Task 8's indexNode writes through it too. The parts are taken from redacted text already (§6.2);
 *  this pass also catches a pair learned since. */
function insertNodeFts(db, ictx, rowid, gist, topics, refs) {
  const t = nodeIndexTexts({ gist, topics, refs: refs.map((r) => r.value) }, ictx.pairIdx);
  db.prepare('INSERT INTO nodes_fts (rowid, gist, topics, refs) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)').run(rowid, t.gist, t.topics, t.refs);
}

/** The parent of `childIds` at `depth`, unless it exists. Returns its id, or null when it was there. */
function createParent(db, ictx, childIds, depth) {
  const s = parentStmts(db);
  const id = parentId(childIds);
  if (s.exists.get(id) !== undefined) return null;
  const kids = childIds.map((c) => storedNode(db, c));
  const first = kids[0].row;
  const r = parentRollup(kids.map((k) => k.rollup));
  withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
    s.insNode.run(id, first.session_pk, first.epoch_seq, first.transcript_pk, 'condensed', depth, 'ok', r.gist, JSON.stringify(r.topics),
      r.earliestMs, r.latestMs, r.srcChars, r.descCount, r.descChars, directiveFlag(r.gist ?? '') ? 1 : 0, r.capped ? 1 : 0,
      NODE_PARSER_VERSION, ictx.nowMs);
    childIds.forEach((c, i) => { s.insChild.run(id, c, i); });
    for (const ref of r.refs) s.insRef.run(id, ref.kind, ref.value, ref.origin);
    if (ictx.fts === true) insertNodeFts(db, ictx, s.rowidOf.get(id).r, r.gist, r.topics, r.refs);
  });
  return id;
}

/** Fan-in over ONE holding copy's level-0 slots, level by level (§6.3). Each slot holds its leaf or null; each
 *  level above holds the parents of the level below, in their children's order. Returns the parents made. */
function fanInLevels(db, ictx, level0) {
  let made = 0;
  let level = level0;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < MAX_FAN_DEPTH && level.length > 0; depth += 1) {
    const width = depth === 0 ? FAN_IN.leaf : FAN_IN.condensed;
    const slots = level.map((id) => ({ nodeId: id, final: id !== null, parented: id !== null && parentOf(db, id) !== null }));
    for (const group of planFanIn({ slots, width })) {
      if (createParent(db, ictx, group, depth + 1) !== null) made += 1;
    }
    const next = [];
    for (const id of level) {
      if (id === null) continue;
      const p = parentOf(db, id);
      if (p !== null && !next.includes(p)) next.push(p);
    }
    level = next;
  }
  return made;
}

/** Every parent one epoch can have now (§6.3; the coordinator's ruling RB4). Level 0 is split PER HOLDING COPY:
 *  each boundary of the epoch's main transcript, in `ord`, joins the slot list of the file Task 8's holdingCopy
 *  picks for it (a live file first, then the smallest file_id, among the files that have it as a member).
 *  - Why: `boundaries.ord` is numbered per transcript in arrival order, so two forks of one transcript
 *    interleave in it. One list for the whole transcript would let a parent take leaves of both forks, and a
 *    leaf not derived yet in one fork would stop the other's grouping. Per copy, a null slot stops only its own
 *    copy, and a parent's children share one copy.
 *  - A shared head falls to the copy that holds it (the smaller file_id when both are live), so the other fork's
 *    list starts after the fork.
 *  - A boundary no file holds has no leaf (Task 8 waits on it) and joins no list.
 *  - The split is read when a parent is minted. A parent minted earlier keeps its children: they read parented
 *    (parentOf), and planFanIn never regroups a parented slot.
 *  The lists run in ascending file_id. Returns the parents made. */
function deriveEpochParents(db, ictx, sessionPk, epochSeq) {
  const s = parentStmts(db);
  const ds = stmts(db);
  const pass = { files: new Map() };
  const copies = new Map();   // holding file_id → its level-0 slots, in ord
  for (const t of s.epochTranscripts.all(sessionPk, epochSeq)) {
    for (const b of s.bounds.all(t.transcript_pk)) {
      const holding = holdingCopy(ds, pass, b);
      if (holding === null) continue;
      const copyKey = holding.file_id;
      if (!copies.has(copyKey)) copies.set(copyKey, []);
      const leaf = s.leafAt.get(b.entry_id);
      copies.get(copyKey).push(leaf === undefined ? null : leaf.node_id);
    }
  }
  let made = 0;
  for (const key of [...copies.keys()].sort((x, y) => Number(x) - Number(y))) made += fanInLevels(db, ictx, copies.get(key));
  return made;
}

/** Fan-in for every epoch that gained a node since the cursor (§6.3). Returns how many parents it made. */
export function deriveParents(db, ictx, budget) {
  const s = parentStmts(db);
  const step = getStep(db, PARENTS_STEP, NODE_PARSER_VERSION);
  const from = step === null || step.cursor === null ? 0 : Number(step.cursor);
  const top = s.maxRow.get().r;
  if (top === null || Number(top) <= from) return 0;
  let made = 0;
  for (const e of s.touched.all(from)) {
    if (!parentsBudgetLeft(budget)) return made;
    made += deriveEpochParents(db, ictx, e.session_pk, e.epoch_seq);
  }
  setStep(db, PARENTS_STEP, NODE_PARSER_VERSION, String(top), null);
  return made;
}

/** The nodes_fts backfill (§6.2): every node past the ('nodes-fts', 1) cursor with no nodes_fts row gets one.
 *  This covers a node derived while the FTS tables did not exist, or after doctor --repair recreated them.
 *  A node indexed at derivation is skipped, never inserted twice: a second insert of one rowid throws.
 *  Returns the rows added. */
export function indexNodesFts(db, ictx, budget) {
  if (ictx.fts !== true) return 0;
  const step = getStep(db, NODES_FTS_STEP, NODES_FTS_STEP_VERSION);
  let cursor = step === null || step.cursor === null ? 0 : Number(step.cursor);
  const page = db.prepare('SELECT rowid AS rid, node_id FROM nodes WHERE rowid > ? ORDER BY rowid LIMIT ?');
  const has = db.prepare('SELECT 1 AS x FROM nodes_fts WHERE rowid = ?');
  let added = 0;
  while (parentsBudgetLeft(budget)) {
    const rows = page.all(cursor, NODES_FTS_BATCH);
    if (rows.length === 0) break;
    withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
      for (const r of rows) {
        if (has.get(r.rid) !== undefined) continue;
        const n = storedNode(db, r.node_id).rollup;
        insertNodeFts(db, ictx, r.rid, n.gist, n.topics, n.refs);
        added += 1;
      }
      cursor = Number(rows[rows.length - 1].rid);
      setStep(db, NODES_FTS_STEP, NODES_FTS_STEP_VERSION, String(cursor), null);
    });
  }
  return added;
}

/** Every condensed node above `nodeIds`, re-rolled from its children as they are stored now (§6.3), for a reparse
 *  (W1-B2 Task 21) or a pair learned late (Task 29). Ids and node_children never change; a parent's rollup fields,
 *  node_refs and nodes_fts row do. Lower levels go first, so each level reads children already re-rolled. Returns
 *  how many parents it rewrote. */
export function rerollParents(db, ictx, nodeIds) {
  const s = parentStmts(db);
  const depthOf = db.prepare('SELECT depth FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?');
  const kidsOf = db.prepare('SELECT child_id FROM node_children WHERE node_id = ? ORDER BY ord');
  const setParent = db.prepare('UPDATE nodes SET gist = ?, topics = ?, earliest_ms = ?, latest_ms = ?, src_chars = ?, '
    + 'desc_count = ?, desc_chars = ?, directive_flag = ?, capped = ?, parser_version = ? WHERE node_id = ?');
  const dropRefs = db.prepare('DELETE FROM node_refs WHERE node_id = ?');
  const above = new Map();
  for (const id of nodeIds) {
    let p = parentOf(db, id);
    for (let k = 0; p !== null && k < MAX_FAN_DEPTH && !above.has(p); k += 1) {
      const d = depthOf.get(p);
      if (d === undefined) break;
      above.set(p, Number(d.depth));
      p = parentOf(db, p);
    }
  }
  const order = [...above.entries()].sort((x, y) => x[1] - y[1] || (x[0] < y[0] ? -1 : x[0] > y[0] ? 1 : 0)).map(([id]) => id);
  let n = 0;
  for (const id of order) {
    const kids = kidsOf.all(id).map((r) => storedNode(db, r.child_id));
    if (kids.length === 0) continue;
    const r = parentRollup(kids.map((k) => k.rollup));
    withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
      setParent.run(r.gist, JSON.stringify(r.topics), r.earliestMs, r.latestMs, r.srcChars, r.descCount, r.descChars,
        directiveFlag(r.gist ?? '') ? 1 : 0, r.capped ? 1 : 0, NODE_PARSER_VERSION, id);
      dropRefs.run(id);
      for (const ref of r.refs) s.insRef.run(id, ref.kind, ref.value, ref.origin);
      if (ictx.fts === true) {
        const rowid = s.rowidOf.get(id).r;
        db.prepare('DELETE FROM nodes_fts WHERE rowid = ?').run(rowid);
        insertNodeFts(db, ictx, rowid, r.gist, r.topics, r.refs);
      }
    });
    n += 1;
  }
  return n;
}
```

```bash
mkdir -p .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch
cat > .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/mut-after.mjs <<'EOF'
// mut-after.mjs: apply ONE mutant for a mutation pin (W1-B2 plan, Tasks 9-11), in place.
// usage: node .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/mut-after.mjs <file> <anchor> <needle> <replacement> [<needle> <replacement> ...]
// For each pair, replace the FIRST occurrence of <needle> that follows the first occurrence of <anchor>.
// - The clean file is saved first to .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/<basename>.orig.
// - The script exits 1 and writes nothing when the anchor or any needle is missing, so a mutant never applies half.
// - It also exits 1 while an earlier .orig is still there (an unrestored mutant).
// Restore: mv .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/scratch/<basename>.orig <file>
import { copyFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { basename, join } from 'node:path';
const [file, anchor, ...pairs] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (file === undefined || anchor === undefined || pairs.length === 0 || pairs.length % 2 !== 0) {
  console.error('usage: node mut-after.mjs <file> <anchor> <needle> <replacement> [<needle> <replacement> ...]');
  process.exit(2);
}
const scratch = join('.superpowers', 'sdd', 'history-w1-b2', 'scratch');
mkdirSync(scratch, { recursive: true });
const orig = join(scratch, `${basename(file)}.orig`);
if (existsSync(orig)) {
  console.error(`mut-after: ${orig} exists: restore the earlier mutant first (mv ${orig} ${file})`);
  process.exit(1);
}
let text = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
const at = text.indexOf(anchor);
if (at < 0) { console.error(`mut-after: anchor not found in ${file}: ${anchor}`); process.exit(1); }
for (let i = 0; i < pairs.length; i += 2) {
  const k = text.indexOf(pairs[i], at);
  if (k < 0) { console.error(`mut-after: needle not found after the anchor: ${pairs[i]}`); process.exit(1); }
  text = text.slice(0, k) + pairs[i + 1] + text.slice(k + pairs[i].length);
}
copyFileSync(file, orig);
writeFileSync(file, text);
console.log(`mut-after: mutated ${file}; restore with: mv ${orig} ${file}`);
EOF
git check-ignore -q .superpowers/sdd/history-w1-b2/mut-after.mjs && echo ignored
```

```ts
// ── W1-B2 Task 10: the CLI runner, the pane fixtures, and a captured family ─────────────────────────────
/** The pane every read-verb case runs in. */
export const PANE = '%1';

/** A working tmux in <home>/.local/bin, over the poison: it records its argv in $HOME/tmux-calls and answers
 *  `cc-<id>` (or `opts.name` verbatim) as the pane's session name. Returns the env a CLI child needs. */
export function withPane(box: HistoryBox, id: string, opts: { name?: string } = {}): Record<string, string> {
  const name = opts.name ?? `cc-${id}`;
  const bin = path.join(box.home, '.local', 'bin', 'tmux');
  fs.writeFileSync(bin, `#!/bin/sh\nprintf '%s\\n' "$*" >> "$HOME/tmux-calls"\nprintf '%s\\n' '${name}'\n`);
  fs.chmodSync(bin, 0o755);
  return { TMUX_PANE: PANE };
}

/** A tmux that never answers: `exec sleep` keeps one pid, so the CLI's SIGKILL at its deadline ends it (a child
 *  `sleep` would keep the pipe open past the kill). */
export function sleepyTmux(box: HistoryBox, seconds: number): Record<string, string> {
  const bin = path.join(box.home, '.local', 'bin', 'tmux');
  fs.writeFileSync(bin, `#!/bin/sh\nexec sleep ${String(seconds)}\n`);
  fs.chmodSync(bin, 0o755);
  return { TMUX_PANE: PANE };
}

/** `node --no-warnings cli.mjs <args>` in the box, on the statfs preload, capped like every spawn here. `json` is
 *  the last stdout line parsed, or null when it is not a JSON object. */
export function runCli(box: HistoryBox, args: string[], opts: SpawnOpts = {}): SpawnResult & { json: Record<string, unknown> | null } {
  const r = timed(() => spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--no-warnings', CLI, ...args],
    { env: childEnv(box, opts), cwd: box.home, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: opts.timeoutMs ?? SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS, killSignal: 'SIGTERM' }));
  let json: Record<string, unknown> | null = null;
  try {
    const v: unknown = JSON.parse(r.stdout.trim().split('\n').at(-1) ?? '');
    if (v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v)) json = v as Record<string, unknown>;
  } catch {
    // a human-format answer
  }
  return { ...r, json };
}

/** The project slug a seeded transcript sits under. */
export const SEED_SLUG = '-home-u-tree-demo';
export interface SeedSpec {
  id: string; project: string; uuid: string; rows: object[];
  workdir?: string; generation?: string | null; accountId?: string;
}

/** One family, captured as the box captures one:
 *  - one priming sweep first, which spends the first tick's registry scan so the epoch is the hook's 'startup' and
 *    not the scan's 'import' (B1's scanDue is true while meta scan_ms is null; registryBackfill books a planted .uuid);
 *  - its registry fields;
 *  - its transcript, under the roster's first account unless `accountId` names another;
 *  - a SessionStart(startup) line whose `reg` is the uuid; B1 drains it one tick after renaming it, so the epoch
 *    appears on the second sweep (§6.1);
 *  - sweep ticks until one leaves the transcript at end-of-file AND its epoch confirmed.
 *  A string `generation` is written to the registry and carried on the line; null writes none (a gen-less line).
 *  Throws when four ticks do not get there: a seed that stops short would make every case built on it vacuous. */
export function seedFamily(box: HistoryBox, f: SeedSpec): { uuid: string; transcript: string } {
  const prime = runSweep(box);
  if (prime.code !== 0) throw new Error(`seedFamily(${f.id}): the priming sweep exited ${String(prime.code)}: ${prime.stderr}${prime.stdout}`);
  plantSession(box, f.id, {
    uuid: f.uuid, project: f.project,
    ...(f.generation === undefined ? {} : { generation: f.generation }),
    ...(f.workdir === undefined ? {} : { workdir: f.workdir }),
  });
  const transcript = plantTranscript(box, f.accountId ?? Object.keys(box.accountHome)[0]!, SEED_SLUG, f.uuid, f.rows);
  spoolLine(box, f.id, {
    v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: f.id, sid: f.uuid, src: 'startup', reg: f.uuid,
    ...(typeof f.generation === 'string' ? { gen: f.generation } : {}),
  });
  for (let i = 0; i < 4; i += 1) {
    const r = runSweep(box);
    if (r.code !== 0) throw new Error(`seedFamily(${f.id}): the sweep exited ${String(r.code)}: ${r.stderr}${r.stdout}`);
    if (atEndOfFile(box, f.uuid)) return { uuid: f.uuid, transcript };
  }
  throw new Error(`seedFamily(${f.id}): four ticks left ${f.uuid} short of end-of-file`);
}

function atEndOfFile(box: HistoryBox, uuid: string): boolean {
  const db = openStoreRO(box);
  try {
    const row = db.prepare("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM ingest_files f JOIN transcripts t ON t.transcript_pk = f.transcript_pk WHERE t.cc_session_uuid = ? AND f.source_key = '' AND f.eof_ms IS NOT NULL")
      .get(uuid) as { n: number };
    // B1 reaches the transcript's EOF through hintedUuids in the tick that RENAMES the line, but drains the line (and so
    // books the family and its epoch) only in the next: EOF alone would return before the family exists.
    const ep = db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM epochs WHERE cc_session_uuid = ? AND confirmed_ms IS NOT NULL').get(uuid) as { n: number };
    return Number(row.n) > 0 && Number(ep.n) > 0;
  } finally {
    db.close();
  }
}
```

```ts
// server/test/history-recall.test.ts — the read verbs of `ccrc history` (W1-B2), run as a session runs them
// (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-ccrc-history-lossless-dag-design.md §8.1–§8.4, §8.8, §8.9).

//   - The fixture poisons tmux, gh, ssh, curl and the managers, and scrubs CLAUDECODE, TMUX, TMUX_PANE,

const ID = 'claude-a-demo';
const ID_B = 'claude-b-demo';

const G1 = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0123456789ab';
const G2 = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0123456789ac';
const TA = 'a1a1a1a1-1111-4111-8111-111111111111';
const TB = 'b2b2b2b2-2222-4222-8222-222222222222';
const U9 = '99999999-9999-4999-8999-999999999999';
const LIB = path.join(REPO, 'ccd', 'history', 'lib.mjs');
const T0 = Date.UTC(2026, 9, 1, 10, 0, 0);
/** A case that seeds stores and spawns the CLI several times runs past vitest's 20 s default. */
const HEAVY = 120_000;

/** A row uuid: the transcript's first eight hex digits and a counter. Two transcripts never share one, because
 *  entries.uuid is store-wide (§6.1). */
const rid = (transcript: string, n: number): string => `${transcript.slice(0, 8)}-0000-4000-8000-${n.toString(16).padStart(12, '0')}`;
const iso = (k: number): string => new Date(T0 + k * 1000).toISOString();

/** `n` plain turns, each a question and its answer: no compaction, so no node. */
function turns(transcript: string, n: number, cwd = '/home/u/worktrees/p/quiet-basin'): Row[] {
  const rows: Row[] = [];
  for (let i = 1; i <= n; i += 1) {
    rows.push(userRow({ uuid: rid(transcript, 2 * i - 1), ts: iso(2 * i - 1), sessionId: transcript, cwd, text: `fixture question ${i}` }));
    rows.push(assistantRow({ uuid: rid(transcript, 2 * i), ts: iso(2 * i), sessionId: transcript, cwd, text: `Fixture answer ${i}.`,
      requestId: `req_${transcript.slice(0, 8)}_${i}`, msgId: `msg_${transcript.slice(0, 8)}_${i}` }));
  }
  return rows;
}

/** `n` manual compactions, each cycle being a turn, its answer, a kept follow-up, the boundary and its summary
 *  row. The summary names Current Work and Optional Next Step, so each native leaf has a gist. */
function cycles(transcript: string, n: number): Row[] {
  const rows: Row[] = [];
  const cwd = '/home/u/worktrees/p/quiet-basin';
  let k = 0;
  for (let c = 1; c <= n; c += 1) {
    const u = rid(transcript, ++k); const a = rid(transcript, ++k); const x = rid(transcript, ++k);
    const b = rid(transcript, ++k); const s = rid(transcript, ++k);
    const base = { sessionId: transcript, cwd };
    rows.push(userRow({ ...base, uuid: u, ts: iso(5 * c), text: `fixture request ${c}` }));
    rows.push(assistantRow({ ...base, uuid: a, ts: iso(5 * c + 1), text: `Fixture answer ${c}.`, requestId: `req_c_${c}`, msgId: `msg_c_${c}` }));
    rows.push(userRow({ ...base, uuid: x, ts: iso(5 * c + 2), text: `fixture follow-up ${c}` }));
    rows.push(boundaryRow({ ...base, uuid: b, ts: iso(5 * c + 3), trigger: 'manual', headUuid: x, anchorUuid: s, tailUuid: x, allUuids: [x] }));
    rows.push(summaryRow({ ...base, uuid: s, ts: iso(5 * c + 4), text: [
      'This session is being continued from a previous conversation. The summary below covers the earlier portion.',
      '<summary>', '1. Primary Request and Intent:', `   Fixture request ${c}.`,
      '8. Current Work:', `   Wrote part ${c} of the fixture.`,
      '9. Optional Next Step:', `   Continue with part ${c + 1}.`, '</summary>',
    ].join('\n') }));
  }
  return rows;
}

    expect(parse('tree', ['--session', '..']).ok, 'the id grammar is decideScope\'s, after the parse').toBe(true);
    expect(parse('touched', [])).toEqual(bad);
    expect([...libRead.READ_VERBS]).toEqual(['grep', 'describe', 'expand', 'tree']);
  });

  it('selectColumns names what the store\'s version has and NULLs what it lacks; an unknown table or column throws', () => {
    expect(libRead.selectColumns(1, 'nodes', ['node_id', 'gist'])).toBe('node_id, gist');
    expect(libRead.selectColumns(1, 'nodes', ['node_id'], libRead.SCHEMA_ADDED, 'n')).toBe('n.node_id');
    const seam = { ...libRead.SCHEMA_ADDED, 2: { heavy: false, tables: { nodes: ['seam_col'] } } };
    expect(libRead.selectColumns(1, 'nodes', ['node_id', 'seam_col'], seam)).toBe('node_id, NULL AS seam_col');
    expect(libRead.selectColumns(2, 'nodes', ['node_id', 'seam_col'], seam)).toBe('node_id, seam_col');
    expect(() => libRead.selectColumns(1, 'no_such_table', ['x'])).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => libRead.selectColumns(1, 'nodes', ['no_such_col'])).toThrow(TypeError);
  });

  it('decideRecallOffPreflight: the id grammar first, then the generation read, then W2\'s word', () => {
    const pre = libRead.decideRecallOffPreflight;
    expect(pre({ args: ['../x', '--clear'], generation: null })).toEqual({ done: true, exit: 2, reason: 'bad-id' });
    expect(pre({ args: [ID], generation: null })).toEqual({ done: false, id: ID });
    expect(pre({ args: [ID], generation: { state: 'unreadable' } })).toEqual({ done: true, exit: 2, reason: 'generation-unreadable' });
    expect(pre({ args: [ID, '--clear'], generation: { state: 'value', value: G1 } })).toEqual({ done: true, exit: 2, reason: 'bad-args' });
    expect(pre({ args: [ID], generation: { state: 'absent' } })).toEqual({ done: true, exit: 2, reason: 'bad-args' });
    expect(pre({ args: ['--clear-all'], generation: null })).toEqual({ done: true, exit: 2, reason: 'bad-args' });
    expect(pre({ args: [], generation: null })).toEqual({ done: true, exit: 2, reason: 'bad-args' });
    expect(pre({ args: [ID, '--bogus'], generation: null })).toEqual({ done: true, exit: 2, reason: 'bad-args' });
  });
});

describe('the read verbs: identity, §8.3\'s table, the read-only handle, the family (W1-B2 Task 10)', () => {
  beforeEach((ctx) => { if (process.platform === 'darwin') ctx.skip(); });

  it('C4 (no-pane half): with no TMUX_PANE a read verb answers 2 no-identity and never asks tmux', () => {
    const box = boundBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c4-');
    withPane(box, ID);   // a working tmux IS on PATH: the refusal is the missing pane
    const r = runCli(box, ['tree', '--json']);
    expect(answer(r)).toEqual([2, 'no-identity']);
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(box.home, 'tmux-calls'))).toBe(false);
  });

  it('C3: the identity is `tmux display-message -p -t "$TMUX_PANE" \'#S\'`, and only a cc- name is one', () => {
    const box = boundBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c3-');
    const ok = treeJson(box);
    expect(ok.code, `${ok.stderr}${ok.stdout}`).toBe(6);   // an identity, a bound store, no family yet
    expect(fs.readFileSync(path.join(box.home, 'tmux-calls'), 'utf8').trim().split('\n')).toEqual(['display-message -p -t %1 #S']);
    const bad = runCli(box, ['tree', '--json'], { env: withPane(box, ID, { name: ID }) });
    expect(answer(bad)).toEqual([2, 'no-identity']);
  });

  it('C65: a tmux that never answers is killed at the bound: 2 no-identity, well inside the spawn cap', () => {
    const box = boundBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c65-');
    const r = runCli(box, ['tree', '--json'], { env: sleepyTmux(box, 30) });
    expect(answer(r)).toEqual([2, 'no-identity']);
    // TMUX_DEADLINE_MS is 2000. The other 4 s allow for node's start and the stub's on a loaded box: an allowance,
    // not a measurement. A deadline raised to 8 s reds here, and so does no deadline at all (Step 9, review R28).
    expect(r.ms, 'TMUX_DEADLINE_MS is 2000').toBeLessThan(6_000);
  }, HEAVY);

  it('C36: §8.3\'s table, row by row, through tree in a pane', () => {
    const ask = (b: HistoryBox): unknown[] => answer(treeJson(b));
    const server = boundBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c36a-');
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(server.home, '.ccrc', 'ccrc.env'), 'CCRC_ROLE=server\n');
    expect(ask(server), 'a recorded server role, with a stale shim, store.id and DB').toEqual([9, undefined]);
    expect(ask(makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c36b-', { shim: false })), 'never installed').toEqual([9, undefined]);
    const shimOnly = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c36c-');
    expect(ask(shimOnly), 'the first tick has not created the store').toEqual([6, undefined]);
    fs.mkdirSync(hist(shimOnly, 'journal', U9), { recursive: true });
    expect(ask(shimOnly)).toEqual([5, 'store-recoverable']);
    const wal = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c36d-');
    fs.mkdirSync(hist(wal, 'db'), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    fs.writeFileSync(hist(wal, 'db', 'history.db-wal'), '');
    expect(ask(wal)).toEqual([5, 'store-wal-orphaned']);
    const missing = boundBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c36e-');
    for (const f of ['history.db', 'history.db-wal', 'history.db-shm']) fs.rmSync(hist(missing, 'db', f), { force: true });
    expect(ask(missing)).toEqual([5, 'store-missing']);
    expect(ask(boundBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c36f-')), 'a bound store holding no row of this family').toEqual([6, undefined]);
    const zero = boundBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c36g-');
    for (const f of ['history.db-wal', 'history.db-shm']) fs.rmSync(hist(zero, 'db', f), { force: true });
    fs.truncateSync(hist(zero, 'db', 'history.db'), 0);
    expect(ask(zero)).toEqual([5, 'store-zero-byte']);
    expect(fs.statSync(hist(zero, 'db', 'history.db')).size, 'never opened, never written').toBe(0);
  }, HEAVY);

  it('C1: the handle is read-only: a write through it throws; a shim-only box answers 6 and creates no file', () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c1-');
    seedFamily(box, { id: ID, project: PROJECT, uuid: TA, generation: G1, rows: turns(TA, 2) });
    const probe = [
      `const lib = await import(${JSON.stringify(pathToFileURL(LIB).href)});`,
      `const cli = await import(${JSON.stringify(pathToFileURL(CLI).href)});`,
      "const rc = await cli.readContext(process.env.HOME, 'tree', lib.parseReadArgs('tree', []));",
      "if (!('db' in rc)) { process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ out: 'refused', rc })); process.exit(0); }",
      "let out = 'wrote';",
      "try { rc.db.exec(\"INSERT INTO meta (k, v) VALUES ('c1-probe', 'x')\"); } catch (e) { out = 'threw: ' + e.message; }",
      'rc.db.close();',
      'process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ out }));',
      'process.exit(0);',
    ].join('\n');
    const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--no-warnings', '--input-type=module', '-e', probe], {
      cwd: box.home, encoding: 'utf8',
      env: { ...box.env, HISTORY_TEST_STATFS: 'plenty', NODE_OPTIONS: preloadOptions([PRELOADS.statfs]), ...withPane(box, ID) },
    });
    expect(r.status, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect((JSON.parse(r.stdout) as { out: string }).out).toMatch(/^threw: .*readonly/);
    const db = openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      expect(db.prepare("SELECT v FROM meta WHERE k = 'c1-probe'").get()).toBeUndefined();
    } finally {
      db.close();
    }
    const fresh = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c1b-');
    expect(treeJson(fresh).code).toBe(6);
    expect(fs.existsSync(hist(fresh, 'db')), 'no DB and no db/ directory is created').toBe(false);
  }, HEAVY);

  it('C2: the read-only open works with the WAL sidecars absent, and any sidecar it makes is 0600 under umask 0002', () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c2-');
    seedFamily(box, { id: ID, project: PROJECT, uuid: TA, generation: G1, rows: turns(TA, 2) });
    // seedFamily ends with atEndOfFile's read-only open, which creates -wal and -shm and cannot remove them (B1
    // Task 12, measured). The sole writer closes last: one more tick checkpoints and unlinks both.
    expect(runSweep(box).code).toBe(0);
    for (const f of ['history.db-wal', 'history.db-shm']) expect(fs.existsSync(hist(box, 'db', f)), `${f}: the sweep closed cleanly`).toBe(false);
    const r = spawnSync('bash', ['-c', 'umask 0002; exec "$0" "$@"', process.execPath, '--no-warnings', CLI, 'tree', '--json'], {
      cwd: box.home, encoding: 'utf8',
      env: { ...box.env, HISTORY_TEST_STATFS: 'plenty', NODE_OPTIONS: preloadOptions([PRELOADS.statfs]), ...withPane(box, ID) },
    });
    expect(r.status, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    for (const f of ['history.db', 'history.db-wal', 'history.db-shm']) {
      if (fs.existsSync(hist(box, 'db', f))) expect((fs.statSync(hist(box, 'db', f)).mode & 0o777).toString(8), f).toBe('600');
    }
  }, HEAVY);

  it('C54 + C67 (harness half): a harness with no table row is 2 harness-unsupported, never 6; unreadable is harness-unreadable; absent reads as claude-code', () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c54-');   // shim only: §8.3's table alone would answer 6
    const harness = path.join(box.reg, `${ID}.harness`);
    fs.writeFileSync(harness, 'codex');
    expect(answer(treeJson(box))).toEqual([2, 'harness-unsupported']);
    fs.rmSync(harness);
    fs.mkdirSync(harness);   // present, and no read of it succeeds
    expect(answer(treeJson(box))).toEqual([2, 'harness-unreadable']);
    fs.rmdirSync(harness);
    expect(answer(treeJson(box)), 'absent: claude-code, and the table answers').toEqual([6, undefined]);
    const seeded = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c54b-');
    seedFamily(seeded, { id: ID, project: PROJECT, uuid: TA, generation: G1, rows: turns(TA, 2) });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(seeded.reg, `${ID}.harness`), 'claude-code');
    expect(treeJson(seeded).code).toBe(0);
  }, HEAVY);

  it('C56: a stat of db/history.db that never settles answers 5 store-unreachable inside the 2 s bound, naming the store, and no DB open is attempted', async () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c56-');
    seedFamily(box, { id: ID, project: PROJECT, uuid: TA, generation: G1, rows: turns(TA, 2) });
    // §8.9's C56 also says "no DB open is attempted". The stat seam hangs fs.promises.stat only, so a SQLite open
    // would go unseen. The DB path is therefore made a directory: B1's openReader refuses that at once, before any
    // SQLite handle, with store-unmeasured. An open anywhere before the stat would answer that word, never
    // store-unreachable (review R28).
    const dbFile = hist(box, 'db', 'history.db');
    fs.renameSync(dbFile, `${dbFile}.aside`);
    fs.mkdirSync(dbFile);
    const store = (await import('../../ccd/history/store.mjs')) as unknown as { openReader(p: string): { close(): void } };
    expect(() => store.openReader(dbFile), 'CONTROL: an open of the planted path refuses').toThrow(/not a regular file/);
    const r = treeJson(box, ID, [], { HISTORY_TEST_STAT_HANG: 'history.db' });
    expect(answer(r)).toEqual([5, 'store-unreachable']);
    expect(r.json?.['store_id']).toBe(storeIdOf(box));
    // CLI_STAT_DEADLINE_MS is 2000. The other 4 s allow for node's start, the preload and the tmux stub on a loaded
    // box: an allowance, not a measurement. A deadline raised to 8 s reds here (Step 9).
    expect(r.ms, 'CLI_STAT_DEADLINE_MS is 2000').toBeLessThan(6_000);
  }, HEAVY);

  it('F11 (read verbs): a failed read of an admitted store is ONE exit-5 answer, store-read-failed with its store_id, as status gives; a TypeError stays exit 1', () => {
    // B1's rule for status (review 316 F11, history-cli.test.ts's RF5b F11 and M30 cases), for tree. The tables are
    // dropped with foreign keys off, so a derived row never blocks the drop.
    const drop = (b: HistoryBox, table: string): void => {
      const db = new DatabaseSync(hist(b, 'db', 'history.db'), { enableForeignKeyConstraints: false });
      try { db.exec(`DROP TABLE ${table}`); } finally { db.close(); }
    };
    // readContext's own read: the pair index's table is gone.
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-f11a-');
    seedFamily(box, { id: ID, project: PROJECT, uuid: TA, generation: G1, rows: turns(TA, 2) });
    drop(box, 'redact_hashes');
    const r = treeJson(box);
    expect(answer(r), r.stderr).toEqual([5, 'store-read-failed']);
    expect(r.stdout.trim().split('\n'), 'one answer').toHaveLength(1);
    expect(r.json?.['store_id']).toBe(storeIdOf(box));
    expect(r.json?.['coverage']).toBe('this-box');
    expect(r.stderr).toContain('no such table: redact_hashes');
    const human = runCli(box, ['tree'], { env: withPane(box, ID) });
    expect(human.code, human.stderr).toBe(5);
    expect(human.stdout).toContain('exit 5 store-read-failed');
    // A plain TypeError out of the same read is a defect: exit 1, no answer, never store-read-failed.
    const defect = runCli(box, ['tree', '--json'], {
      preloads: [PRELOADS.faults], env: { ...withPane(box, ID), HISTORY_TEST_THROW_PREPARE: 'TypeError@FROM redact_hashes' },
    });
    expect(defect.code, defect.stderr).toBe(1);
    expect(defect.stdout.trim(), 'no answer for a defect').toBe('');
    expect(defect.stderr).toContain('ccrc history: internal error: fixture-planted');
    expect(defect.stderr).not.toContain('store-read-failed');
    // The verb's own read (runTree's nodes select), past readContext: the same ONE answer.
    const verb = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-f11b-');
    seedFamily(verb, { id: ID, project: PROJECT, uuid: TA, generation: G1, rows: turns(TA, 2) });
    drop(verb, 'nodes');
    const v = treeJson(verb);
    expect(answer(v), v.stderr).toEqual([5, 'store-read-failed']);
    expect(v.stdout.trim().split('\n'), 'one answer').toHaveLength(1);
    expect(v.json?.['store_id']).toBe(storeIdOf(verb));
    expect(v.stderr).toContain('no such table: nodes');
  }, HEAVY);

  it('C66 (B2 half): an id off ccd\'s grammar is bad-id before any path is formed from it', () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c66-');
    seedFamily(box, { id: ID, project: PROJECT, uuid: TA, generation: G1, rows: turns(TA, 2) });
    expect(answer(treeJson(box, ID, ['--session', '..']))).toEqual([2, 'bad-id']);
    const victim = hist(box, 'x');   // where recall-off/../x would land
    fs.writeFileSync(victim, 'keep');
    const ro = runCli(box, ['recall-off', '../x', '--clear', '--json']);
    expect(answer(ro)).toEqual([2, 'bad-id']);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(victim, 'utf8'), 'nothing unlinked, nothing written').toBe('keep');
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(box.reg, `${ID_B}.generation`));
    expect(answer(runCli(box, ['recall-off', ID_B, '--json'])), 'C67\'s recall-off clause').toEqual([2, 'generation-unreadable']);
    expect(answer(runCli(box, ['recall-off', ID, '--json'])), 'the writing verb ships with W2').toEqual([2, 'bad-args']);
  }, HEAVY);

  it('C48: with no CCRC_SESSION_GENERATION and $REG/<id>.generation = G, the scope is (id, G), not the newest family', () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-c48-');
    seedFamily(box, { id: ID, project: PROJECT, uuid: TA, generation: G1, rows: turns(TA, 2) });
    seedFamily(box, { id: ID, project: PROJECT, uuid: TB, generation: G2, rows: turns(TB, 2) });
    plantSession(box, ID, { generation: G1 });
    const older = treeJson(box);
    expect(older.code, `${older.stderr}${older.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    expect(scopeOf(older).families.map((f) => f.generation)).toEqual([G1]);
    plantSession(box, ID, { generation: G2 });
    expect(scopeOf(treeJson(box)).families.map((f) => f.generation)).toEqual([G2]);
    const viaEnv = treeJson(box, ID, [], { CCRC_SESSION_GENERATION: G1 });
    expect(scopeOf(viaEnv).families.map((f) => f.generation), 'the env generation comes first').toEqual([G1]);
  }, HEAVY);

  it('DM18b (CLI half): after a re-key merged the gen-less family into (id, G), default recall answers 0 on (id, G), never 6, and reads the nodes derived before the merge', () => {
    // Review focus 4: the '' family's leaves and parent are derived BEFORE the re-key, then merged into (id, G).
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-dm18b-');
    seedFamily(box, { id: ID, project: PROJECT, uuid: TA, generation: null, rows: cycles(TA, 8) });   // the '' family
    expect(runSweep(box).code).toBe(0);   // one more tick: derivation shares the run budget
    const idsOf = (r: CliRun): string[] => ((r.json?.['items'] ?? []) as { node_id: string }[]).map((i) => i.node_id).sort();
    const before = treeJson(box);
    expect(before.code, `${before.stderr}${before.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    const nodeIds = idsOf(before);
    expect(nodeIds, 'one parent and its eight leaves, derived before the re-key').toHaveLength(9);
    plantSession(box, ID, { generation: G1 });
    spoolLine(box, ID, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: ID, sid: TA, src: 'resume', reg: TA });
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) expect(runSweep(box).code).toBe(0);   // tick N renames the resume line, tick N+1 drains it and re-keys
    expect(counters(box)['family_rekeyed']).toBe(1);
    const r = treeJson(box);
    expect(r.code, `${r.stderr}${r.stdout}`).toBe(0);
    const scope = scopeOf(r);
    expect(scope.families.map((f) => [f.ccrc_id, f.generation])).toEqual([[ID, G1]]);
    expect(scope.transcripts).toBe(1);
    expect(idsOf(r), 'the same nine ids after the merge: node ids never change (§6.1)').toEqual(nodeIds);
    const db = openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      const split = db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM node_children c JOIN nodes p ON p.node_id = c.node_id '
        + 'JOIN nodes k ON k.node_id = c.child_id WHERE p.session_pk <> k.session_pk OR p.epoch_seq <> k.epoch_seq').get() as { n: number };
      expect(Number(split.n), 'no parent spans two families or two epochs after the merge').toBe(0);
      const gens = db.prepare('SELECT DISTINCT s.generation AS g FROM nodes n JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = n.session_pk').all() as { g: string }[];
      expect(gens.map((x) => x.g), 'every node now sits in (id, G)').toEqual([G1]);
    } finally {
      db.close();
    }
    expect(counters(box)['nodes_unrepointed'] ?? 0).toBe(0);
  }, HEAVY);

  it('tree renders the family, its epochs and its nodes in envelopes, with true counts and a next line', () => {
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-rcl-tree-');
    seedFamily(box, { id: ID, project: PROJECT, uuid: TA, generation: G1, rows: cycles(TA, 8) });
    expect(runSweep(box).code).toBe(0);   // one more tick: derivation shares the run budget
    const human = runCli(box, ['tree'], { env: withPane(box, ID) });
    expect(human.code, human.stderr).toBe(0);
    const lines = human.stdout.trimEnd().split('\n');
    expect(lines[0]).toMatch(new RegExp(`^scope=family\\(${ID}, 1 transcripts\\) coverage=this-box indexed-through=\\S+ lag=\\S+$`));
    expect(lines[1]).toMatch(new RegExp(`^family ${ID} generation=${G1} first-seen=\\S+$`));
    expect(lines[2]).toMatch(/^ {2}epoch 1 startup started=\S+ session=a1a1a1a1$/);
    // Display prefixes are at least 6 hex after L/N (NODE_ID_DISPLAY_MIN; ruled).
    const nodeLines = lines.filter((l) => /^ {4,}[LN][0-9a-f]{6,20} (native_leaf|steered_leaf|raw_leaf|condensed) depth=\d/.test(l));
    expect(nodeLines, 'one parent and its eight leaves').toHaveLength(9);
    for (const l of nodeLines) expect(l).toMatch(/<ccrc-recall src="node" .*trust="untrusted">.*<\/ccrc-recall>$/);
    expect(lines).toContain('shown 9 of 9');
    expect(lines.at(-1)).toMatch(/^next: "\$HOME\/\.local\/bin\/ccrc" history describe N[0-9a-f]{6,20}$/);
    const json = runCli(box, ['tree', '--json'], { env: withPane(box, ID) }).json!;
    const items = json['items'] as { node_id: string; trust: string }[];
    expect(items).toHaveLength(9);
    for (const i of items) {
      expect(i.node_id, '--json ids are always the full 20 hex').toMatch(/^[LN][0-9a-f]{20}$/);
      expect(i.trust).toBe('untrusted');
    }
    expect([json['shown'], json['total'], json['store_id'], json['coverage']]).toEqual([9, 9, storeIdOf(box), 'this-box']);
    const shallow = runCli(box, ['tree', '--depth', '1', '--json'], { env: withPane(box, ID) }).json!;
    expect([shallow['shown'], shallow['total']]).toEqual([1, 9]);
    expect(String(shallow['next'])).toContain('history tree --depth 2');
  }, HEAVY);
});
```

```js
// ── recall: the read verbs' arguments, selects by store version, recall-off's B2 refusals (W1-B2 Task 10) ──
//
// THE ARGUMENT WHITELIST is one table per read verb: §8.2 builds the whitelist from that one list. These are
// exit 2 bad-args before anything is measured:
//   - an option the table does not name;
//   - a repeated option;
//   - an option missing its value;
//   - a value off its grammar.
// `--` ends the options, so a word that starts with `--` is still searchable (`grep -- --force`; slug
// history-read-args-terminator, NEW). Ids are not checked here: the id grammar is decideScope's (idOk), which
// runs before any path is formed from one.
export const TREE_DEPTH_DEFAULT = 2;
export const TREE_DEPTH_MAX = 8;
/** expand --around's window on each side (chosen: §8.4 names the option, not its bound). */
export const AROUND_DEFAULT = 5;
export const AROUND_MAX = 50;

const readOpt = (kind, key, extra = {}) => Object.freeze({ kind, key, ...extra });
/** Options every read verb takes (§8.2). */
const COMMON_READ_OPTIONS = Object.freeze({
  '--json': readOpt('flag', 'json'),
  '--session': readOpt('value', 'session'),
});
const ANY_COUNT = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
export const READ_OPTIONS = Object.freeze({
  grep: Object.freeze({
    options: Object.freeze({
      ...COMMON_READ_OPTIONS,
      '--regex': readOpt('value', 'regex'),
      '--role': readOpt('value', 'role'),
      '--tool': readOpt('value', 'tool'),
      '--since': readOpt('value', 'since'),
      '--before': readOpt('value', 'before'),
      '--node': readOpt('value', 'node'),
      '--sort': readOpt('enum', 'sort', { values: GREP_SORTS }),
      '--limit': readOpt('int', 'limit', { min: 1, max: GREP_LIMIT_MAX }),
      '--cursor': readOpt('value', 'cursor'),
      '--include-recall': readOpt('flag', 'includeRecall'),
    }),
    defaults: Object.freeze({
      regex: null, role: null, tool: null, since: null, before: null, node: null,
      sort: GREP_SORTS[0], limit: GREP_LIMIT_DEFAULT, cursor: null, includeRecall: false,
    }),
    positional: Object.freeze({ min: 0, max: ANY_COUNT }),
  }),
  describe: Object.freeze({
    options: Object.freeze({
      ...COMMON_READ_OPTIONS,
      '--full': readOpt('flag', 'full'),
      '--cursor': readOpt('value', 'cursor'),
    }),
    defaults: Object.freeze({ full: false, cursor: null }),
    positional: Object.freeze({ min: 1, max: ANY_COUNT }),
  }),
  expand: Object.freeze({
    options: Object.freeze({
      ...COMMON_READ_OPTIONS,
      '--around': readOpt('value', 'around'),
      '--before': readOpt('int', 'before', { min: 0, max: AROUND_MAX }),
      '--after': readOpt('int', 'after', { min: 0, max: AROUND_MAX }),
      '--cursor': readOpt('value', 'cursor'),
    }),
    defaults: Object.freeze({ around: null, before: AROUND_DEFAULT, after: AROUND_DEFAULT, cursor: null }),
    positional: Object.freeze({ min: 0, max: ANY_COUNT }),
  }),
  tree: Object.freeze({
    options: Object.freeze({
      ...COMMON_READ_OPTIONS,
      '--depth': readOpt('int', 'depth', { min: 1, max: TREE_DEPTH_MAX }),
    }),
    defaults: Object.freeze({ depth: TREE_DEPTH_DEFAULT }),
    positional: Object.freeze({ min: 0, max: 0 }),
  }),
});
/** The read verbs (§8.2): derived from the whitelist, never listed twice. `touched` joins in W4. */
export const READ_VERBS = Object.freeze(Object.keys(READ_OPTIONS));

const BAD_READ_ARGS = Object.freeze({ ok: false, reason: 'bad-args' });

/** A read verb's argv (after the verb) against its whitelist. Every key the verb's table names has a value in
 *  `opts` (its default when not given), plus json, session, project and workspace. */
export function parseReadArgs(verb, argv) {
  if (typeof verb !== 'string' || !Object.hasOwn(READ_OPTIONS, verb) || !Array.isArray(argv)) return BAD_READ_ARGS;
  const spec = READ_OPTIONS[verb];
  const opts = { json: false, session: null, project: false, workspace: false, ...spec.defaults };
  const positional = [];
  const seen = new Set();
  let rest = false;
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i += 1) {
    const a = argv[i];
    if (typeof a !== 'string') return BAD_READ_ARGS;
    if (rest || !a.startsWith('--')) {
      positional.push(a);
      continue;
    }
    if (a === '--') {
      rest = true;
      continue;
    }
    if (!Object.hasOwn(spec.options, a) || seen.has(a)) return BAD_READ_ARGS;
    seen.add(a);
    const o = spec.options[a];
    if (o.kind === 'flag') {
      opts[o.key] = true;
      continue;
    }
    const v = argv[i + 1];
    if (typeof v !== 'string' || v === '') return BAD_READ_ARGS;
    i += 1;
    if (o.kind === 'value') {
      opts[o.key] = v;
      continue;
    }
    if (o.kind === 'enum') {
      if (!o.values.includes(v)) return BAD_READ_ARGS;
      opts[o.key] = v;
      continue;
    }
    if (!/^[0-9]{1,6}$/.test(v)) return BAD_READ_ARGS;
    const n = Number(v);
    if (n < o.min || n > o.max) return BAD_READ_ARGS;
    opts[o.key] = n;
  }
  if (positional.length < spec.positional.min || positional.length > spec.positional.max) return BAD_READ_ARGS;
  if (verb === 'grep' && positional.length === 0 && opts.regex === null) return BAD_READ_ARGS;
  if (verb === 'expand' && positional.length === 0 && opts.around === null && opts.cursor === null) return BAD_READ_ARGS;
  return { ok: true, verb, positional: Object.freeze(positional), opts: Object.freeze(opts) };
}

/** A select list naming only the columns the store's version has (§6.11, DM44). A column a later version added
 *  reads `NULL AS <col>`, so a store older than the code answers with that field null and never a SQL error.
 *  A table that version lacks throws, and so does a column no version declares (a typo, not an old store).
 *  The verbs that need a newer table refuse first with migration-pending. */
export function selectColumns(version, table, cols, schema = SCHEMA_ADDED, alias = null) {
  const have = new Set();
  const everywhere = new Set();
  let known = false;
  for (const [v, entry] of Object.entries(schema)) {
    const t = entry.tables[table];
    if (t === undefined) continue;
    for (const c of t) everywhere.add(c);
    if (Number(v) > version) continue;
    known = true;
    for (const c of t) have.add(c);
  }
  if (!known) throw new TypeError(`selectColumns: table ${table} is not in schema version ${version}`);
  const q = alias === null ? '' : `${alias}.`;
  return cols.map((c) => {
    if (!everywhere.has(c)) throw new TypeError(`selectColumns: ${table}.${c} is in no schema version`);
    return have.has(c) ? `${q}${c}` : `NULL AS ${c}`;
  }).join(', ');
}

/** `recall-off` in B2 (slug history-recall-off-preflight-b2, NEW): the verb that writes recall-off/<id> ships
 *  with W2 (§8.10), and B2 answers only its refusals, in this order:
 *   - an argv off `<id> [--clear]` or `--clear-all` is bad-args;
 *   - an id off ccd's grammar is bad-id, before any path is formed from it (C66);
 *   - then the caller reads $REG/<id>.generation (`generation` null asks it to): unreadable is
 *     generation-unreadable (C67);
 *   - anything else is bad-args, naming W2. */
export function decideRecallOffPreflight(i) {
  const a = i.args;
  const done = (reason) => ({ done: true, exit: EXIT.REFUSED, reason });
  if (a.length === 1 && a[0] === '--clear-all') return done('bad-args');
  const shapeOk = a.length >= 1 && a.length <= 2 && typeof a[0] === 'string' && !a[0].startsWith('--')
    && (a.length === 1 || a[1] === '--clear');
  if (!shapeOk) return done('bad-args');
  if (!idOk(a[0])) return done('bad-id');
  if (i.generation === null) return { done: false, id: a[0] };
  if (i.generation.state === 'unreadable') return done('generation-unreadable');
  return done('bad-args');
}
```

```ts
export const TREE_DEPTH_DEFAULT: 2;
export const TREE_DEPTH_MAX: 8;
export const AROUND_DEFAULT: 5;
export const AROUND_MAX: 50;
export interface ReadOptionSpec {
  readonly kind: 'flag' | 'value' | 'enum' | 'int'; readonly key: string;
  readonly values?: readonly string[]; readonly min?: number; readonly max?: number;
}
export interface ReadVerbSpec {
  readonly options: Readonly<Record<string, ReadOptionSpec>>;
  readonly defaults: Readonly<Record<string, string | number | boolean | null>>;

}
```
