```ts
    for (const bad of [
      [], ['--json'], ['--limit', '0', 'zq'], ['--limit', String(libGrep.GREP_LIMIT_MAX + 1), 'zq'], ['--limit', 'x', 'zq'],
      ['--sort', 'best', 'zq'], ['--since', 'yesterday', 'zq'], ['--before', 'soon', 'zq'], ['--role', 'User!', 'zq'],
      ['--tool', 'a b', 'zq'], ['--json', '--json', 'zq'], ['--frob', 'zq'], ['zq', '--role'],
      ['--regex', 'x', 'word'], ['--regex', 'x', '--sort', 'relevance'],
    ]) {
      expect(libGrep.parseGrepArgs(bad, NOW), JSON.stringify(bad)).toEqual({ ok: false, reason: 'bad-args' });
    }
  });

  it("SEARCH_REACH says how far grep reaches, from the two window constants (B1's history-entry-index-text-windowed and history-sidecar-redact-before-cut)", () => {
    expect(libGrep.ENTRY_FTS_BYTES).toBe(1024 * 1024);
    expect(libGrep.SIDECAR_FTS_BYTES).toBe(512 * 1024);
    expect(libGrep.SEARCH_REACH).toBe("grep reaches at most the first 1 MiB of each message's redacted text and the first 512 KiB of each tool output Claude Code saved to its own file; text past that is stored but not searched");
    expect([libGrep.reachSize(3 * 1024 * 1024), libGrep.reachSize(1536 * 1024), libGrep.reachSize(1000)])
      .toEqual(['3 MiB', '1536 KiB', '1000 bytes']);
  });
});

describe('lib: a window of a longer text, redacted for display (W1-B2 task 12; coordinator rulings R-display-window and R-window2)', () => {
  /** A pair-only value: makePairIndex without belt units, so only the pair, shape and escape-reading layers can mask it. */
  const V = libGrepRandom(32).toString('hex');
  const idx = libGrep.makePairIndex(libGrep.secretPairs([V]).pairs);
  /** No value at all: only the shape and context layers can redact. */
  const none = libGrep.makePairIndex(libGrep.secretPairs([]).pairs);
  const M = libGrep.REDACTED_MARK;
  const NOTE = libGrep.DISPLAY_INEXACT_NOTE;
  // Built from code points, so nothing here is an escape in transit.
  const ESC = String.fromCharCode(27);
  const BS = String.fromCharCode(92);
  const Q = String.fromCharCode(34);
  const NL = String.fromCharCode(10);
  const alnum = (n: number): string => Array.from(libGrepRandom(n), (b) => 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789'[b % 62]!).join('');
  /** Each text holding 8 consecutive characters of `secret`, by index. */
  const pieces = (texts: readonly string[], secret: string): string[] => {
    const out: string[] = [];
    texts.forEach((t, i) => {
      for (let k = 0; k + 8 <= secret.length; k += 1) if (t.includes(secret.slice(k, k + 8))) { out.push(`#${i}: ${secret.slice(k, k + 8)}`); break; }
    });
    return out;
  };
  /** Whether a window was shown inexact: its first line is DISPLAY_INEXACT_NOTE. */
  const inexact = (s: string): boolean => s.startsWith(`${NOTE}${NL}`);
  /** The escaped-JSON command of findings V15 and V37: the key in quotes a decode removes, the value four words. */
  const CURL = `curl -d '{${BS}${Q}password${BS}${Q}: ${BS}${Q}correct horse battery staple${BS}${Q}}'`;

  it('redactDisplayWindow: text with nothing to redact comes back as its slice, and pages of it join to the text exactly', () => {
    const words = Array.from({ length: 30_000 }, (_, i) => `w${i % 97}`).join(' ');
    for (const [f, t] of [[0, 10], [5, 5], [1234, 1300], [40_000, 58_000], [words.length - 7, words.length + 9]] as const) {
      expect(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(words, f, t, idx), `[${f}, ${t})`).toBe(words.slice(f, t));
    }
    let joined = '';
    for (let f = 0; f < words.length; f += 18_000) joined += libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(words, f, f + 18_000, idx);
    expect(joined === words, 'pages cut inside words join exactly').toBe(true);
  });

  it('a value or a PEM block straddling either window edge leaves no piece on either side; the value\'s mark is shown whole, and the cut is exact', () => {
    const text = `${'p '.repeat(40_000)}${V} ${'q '.repeat(40_000)}`;
    const at = text.indexOf(V);
    for (let cut = at - 2; cut <= at + V.length + 2; cut += 1) {
      const before = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, cut - 500, cut, idx);
      const after = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, cut, cut + 500, idx);
      expect(pieces([before, after, before + after], V), `cut at ${cut - at}`).toEqual([]);
      expect(before + after, `cut at ${cut - at}: the mark is shown on one side`).toContain(M);
      expect(inexact(before) || inexact(after), `cut at ${cut - at}: both sides are cut exactly`).toBe(false);
    }
    // A PEM block is a shape, matched only with its BEGIN line: a window inside its body sees that line only in the margin.
    const LINES = [`MII${alnum(40)}`, alnum(43), alnum(43)];
    const PEM = ['-----BEGIN ', 'RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\n', LINES.join('\n'), '\n-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----'].join('');
    const pem = `${'p '.repeat(40_000)}${PEM}\n${'q '.repeat(40_000)}`;
    const p0 = pem.indexOf(PEM);
    const shown: string[] = [];
    for (let cut = p0; cut <= p0 + PEM.length; cut += 7) {
      shown.push(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(pem, cut - 500, cut, idx), libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(pem, cut, cut + 500, idx));
    }
    for (const l of LINES) expect(pieces(shown, l), l.slice(0, 6)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('a pair-only value behind a literal \\n is masked through the escape readings: inside the window, across either edge, and in a JSON key', () => {
    const glued = JSON.stringify({ text: `\n${V}` });
    const keyed = JSON.stringify({ headers: { [`\n${V}`]: 'x' } });
    const text = `${'r '.repeat(40_000)}x ${glued} y ${keyed} ${'s '.repeat(40_000)}`;
    const g = text.indexOf(V);
    expect(pieces([libGrep.redactField(text.slice(g - 10, g + 80), idx)], V), 'CONTROL: one reading cannot separate it').toHaveLength(1);
    for (let cut = g - 4; cut <= g + V.length + 2; cut += 1) {
      const sides = [libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, cut - 300, cut, idx), libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, cut, cut + 300, idx)];
      expect(pieces(sides, V), `cut at ${cut - g}`).toEqual([]);
    }
    const k = text.indexOf('headers');
    const key = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, k - 50, k + 120, idx);
    expect(key, 'CONTROL: the window holds the key').toContain('headers');
    expect(pieces([key], V)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('a [A-Za-z0-9_-] run longer than the margin that reaches the window is dropped, never shown in part; no slice splits a surrogate pair', () => {
    const text = `head ${'A'.repeat(3 * libGrep.ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN)} tail`;
    expect(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, 100_000, 100_050, idx)).toBe('');
    expect(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, 0, 20, idx)).toBe('head ');
    const P = String.fromCharCode(0xd83d, 0xde00);
    const astral = `${'a '.repeat(10)}${P.repeat(50)}${' b'.repeat(10)}`;
    /** Whether `s` holds half a surrogate pair, by code units (no regex escapes in transit). */
    const lone = (s: string): boolean => {
      for (let k = 0; k < s.length; k += 1) {
        const c = s.charCodeAt(k);
        if (c >= 0xd800 && c <= 0xdbff) {
          const n = s.charCodeAt(k + 1);
          if (!(n >= 0xdc00 && n <= 0xdfff)) return true;
          k += 1;
        } else if (c >= 0xdc00 && c <= 0xdfff) return true;
      }
      return false;
    };
    for (let f = 0; f < astral.length; f += 1) {
      for (const w of [1, 2, 3, 7]) expect(lone(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(astral, f, f + w, idx)), `[${f}, ${f + w})`).toBe(false);
    }
  });

  it('displaySnippet finds the hit in the raw text and redacts only the window around it: a value straddling the snippet\'s cut leaves no piece', () => {
    const far = `${'v '.repeat(100_000)}zqhit after ${V} end ${'w '.repeat(10)}`;
    expect(libGrep.snippetSpan(far, ['zqhit']).at).toBe(far.indexOf('zqhit'));
    expect(libGrep.displaySnippet(far, ['zqhit'], idx), 'what the whole text redacted would show').toBe(libGrep.snippetWindow(libGrep.redactField(far, idx), ['zqhit']));
    expect(libGrep.displaySnippet(far, ['zqhit'], idx)).toContain(`zqhit after ${M} end`);
    const outs: string[] = [];
    const raws: string[] = [];
    for (let pad = 20; pad <= 50; pad += 1) {
      const t = `zqhit ${'u'.repeat(pad)} ${V} tail ${'z '.repeat(200)}`;
      outs.push(libGrep.displaySnippet(t, ['zqhit'], idx));
      raws.push(libGrep.snippetWindow(t, ['zqhit']));
    }
    expect(pieces(raws, V).length, 'CONTROL: a cut of the raw text leaves pieces of the value').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(pieces(outs, V)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('displaySnippet costs the window, not the body: a 16 MiB escape-dense body\'s snippet stays under 5,000 ms and 512 MiB of RSS (a child process)', () => {
    // The body is built in the child from code points, so nothing here is an escape in transit. ESC and literal
    // backslash escapes on every run make each JSON-escape reading of the whole text a full rewrite. Each unit ends in
    // a space, so the margins' far ends find a token break (final-check W2's rule) and both margins are read whole:
    // without it the body is one token span, the margin's end moves back to the window, and nothing is measured.
    const SCRIPT = [
      'const L = await import(process.argv[1]);',
      "const { randomBytes } = await import('node:crypto');",
      "const idx = L.makePairIndex(L.secretPairs([randomBytes(32).toString('hex')]).pairs);",
      'const E = String.fromCharCode(27);',
      'const B = String.fromCharCode(92);',
      "const unit = E + '[31mzq' + B + 'nab' + E + '[0m' + B + 't ';",
      "const body = 'zqdense12 start ' + unit.repeat(Math.floor((16 * 1024 * 1024 - 64) / unit.length));",
      'const t0 = performance.now();',
      "const out = L.displaySnippet(body, ['zqdense12'], idx);",
      'process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ ms: Math.round(performance.now() - t0), rss: process.resourceUsage().maxRSS, chars: body.length, head: out.slice(0, 15) }));',
    ].join('\n');
    const lib = new URL('../../ccd/history/lib.mjs', import.meta.url).href;
    const r = libGrepSpawn(process.execPath, ['--no-warnings', '--input-type=module', '-e', SCRIPT, lib], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 240_000 });
    expect(r.status, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    const m = JSON.parse(r.stdout) as { ms: number; rss: number; chars: number; head: string };
    expect(m.chars, 'CONTROL: the body is 16 MiB').toBeGreaterThan(16 * 1024 * 1024 - 64);
    expect(m.head, 'CONTROL: the snippet shows the hit').toBe('zqdense12 start');
    expect(m.ms < 5_000, `displaySnippet took ${m.ms} ms`).toBe(true);
    expect(m.rss < 524_288, `peak RSS ${m.rss} KiB`).toBe(true);
  }, 300_000);

  it('a whole text\'s window is redactForDisplay\'s, and so is that text\'s window inside a longer one: every layer and reading at once, the bound\'s marked spans included', () => {
    let nested = `\n${V}`;
    for (let k = 0; k < 9; k += 1) nested = JSON.stringify(nested);
    const texts = [
      `plain ${V} text`, JSON.stringify({ a: `\n${V}`, b: 'x' }), nested,
      `x ${V.slice(0, 12)}${ESC}[31m${V.slice(12)}${ESC}[0m y`, `${ESC}[1mbold${ESC}[0m nothing`, CURL,
    ];
    texts.forEach((t, i) => expect(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(t, 0, t.length, idx), `text #${i}`).toBe(libGrep.redactForDisplay(t, idx)));
    // A whole text's window is redactForDisplay's by its first line (final-check W4); inside a longer text the same
    // window is cut from displayReading's reading, so this half pins that reading equal to redactForDisplay's.
    texts.forEach((t, i) => expect(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(`p ${t} q`, 2, 2 + t.length, idx), `text #${i} inside a longer text`).toBe(libGrep.redactForDisplay(t, idx)));
    expect(pieces([libGrep.redactForDisplay(nested, idx)], V), 'CONTROL: nine levels reach the bound, which marks V').toEqual([]);
  });

  it('a value only a decoded reading\'s context form sees, its key in the margin: no window starting at, inside or ending inside it prints it (findings V15, V37)', () => {
    const text = `${'p '.repeat(40_000)}${CURL} ${'q '.repeat(40_000)}`;
    const v = text.indexOf('correct');
    expect(libGrep.redactForDisplay(text, none), 'CONTROL: the whole text masks the value').not.toMatch(/correct|horse|battery|staple/);
    const outs: string[] = [];
    for (let k = -2; k <= 28; k += 1) {
      outs.push(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, v + k, v + k + 300, none), libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, v + k - 300, v + k, none));
    }
    expect(['correct', 'horse', 'battery', 'staple'].filter((w) => outs.some((o) => o.includes(w)))).toEqual([]);
    expect(outs.filter(inexact), 'every window is cut exactly').toEqual([]);
    const api = `zq${alnum(24)}`;
    for (const shape of [
      `{${BS}${Q}api_key${BS}${Q}:${BS}${Q}${api}${BS}${Q}}`,
      `payload: {${BS}${Q}api_key${BS}${Q}: ${BS}${Q}${api}${BS}${Q}, ${BS}${Q}n${BS}${Q}: 1}`,
    ]) {
      const t2 = `${'p '.repeat(40_000)}${shape} ${'q '.repeat(40_000)}`;
      const k0 = t2.indexOf('api_key');
      const at = t2.indexOf(api);
      expect(pieces([libGrep.redactForDisplay(t2, none)], api), 'CONTROL: the whole text masks the token').toEqual([]);
      const o2: string[] = [];
      for (let c = k0; c <= at + api.length + 3; c += 1) o2.push(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(t2, c, c + 300, none), libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(t2, c - 300, c, none));
      expect(pieces(o2, api), shape.slice(0, 12)).toEqual([]);
      expect(o2.filter(inexact), `${shape.slice(0, 12)}: every window is cut exactly`).toEqual([]);
    }
  });

  it('an escape-split value where a margin starts, another inside the window: the window is cut where it is, never from the margin (finding V18)', () => {
    const m = libGrep.ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN;
    const V2 = `QP${alnum(45)}7`;
    const W2 = `QP${alnum(45)}7`;
    const i2 = libGrep.makePairIndex(libGrep.secretPairs([V2, W2]).pairs);
    const fill = (n: number): string => 'f '.repeat(Math.ceil(n / 2)).slice(0, n);
    // Left: the margin starts on the ESC that splits V2, and W2 is split by another inside a 78-character window.
    const head = `${'h '.repeat(1000)}x ${V2.slice(0, 10)}`;
    const lo = head.length + m;
    const mid = `${ESC}[31m${V2.slice(10)} `;
    const win = ` w ${W2.slice(0, 20)}${ESC}[32m${W2.slice(20)} e `.padEnd(78, '.');
    const left = head + mid + fill(m - mid.length) + win + ` ${'t '.repeat(40_000)}`;
    expect(left.charCodeAt(lo - m), 'CONTROL: the margin starts on the ESC').toBe(27);
    expect(pieces([libGrep.redactForDisplay(left, i2)], V2), 'CONTROL: the whole text masks V2').toEqual([]);
    const outL = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(left, lo, lo + 78, i2);
    expect(pieces([outL], V2)).toEqual([]);
    expect(pieces([outL], W2)).toEqual([]);
    expect(outL.length, 'the window, never the margin').toBeLessThanOrEqual(78 + 2 * M.length);
    expect(inexact(outL), 'cut exactly').toBe(false);
    // Right: an 18,000-character window holding W2's split, the margin ending on the ESC that splits V2.
    const lo2 = 2000;
    const hi2 = lo2 + 18_000;
    const winR = `a ${W2.slice(0, 20)}${ESC}[32m${W2.slice(20)} b `.padEnd(18_000, '.');
    const right = `${'g '.repeat(lo2 / 2)}${winR} ${fill(m - 12)} ${V2.slice(0, 10)}${ESC}[31m${V2.slice(10)} ${'u '.repeat(40_000)}`;
    expect(right.charCodeAt(hi2 + m), 'CONTROL: the margin ends on the ESC').toBe(27);
    const outR = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(right, lo2, hi2, i2);
    expect(pieces([outR], V2)).toEqual([]);
    expect(pieces([outR], W2)).toEqual([]);
    expect(outR.length, 'the window, never the margin').toBeLessThanOrEqual(18_000 + 2 * M.length);
    expect(inexact(outR), 'cut exactly').toBe(false);
  });

  it('a page edge inside a word near an escape-glued value: the word prints whole across the two pages, the value on neither (finding V17)', () => {
    const text = `${JSON.stringify({ a: `\n${V}` })} ${'filler '.repeat(500)}importantword ${'tail '.repeat(500)}`;
    const mid = text.indexOf('importantword') + 6;
    const p1 = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, 0, mid, idx);
    const p2 = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, mid, text.length, idx);
    expect(p1 + p2).toContain('importantword');
    expect(pieces([p1, p2, p1 + p2], V)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('a page edge between a backslash and its escape letter is cut exactly, within DISPLAY_EDGE_SLACK, and shows no piece of the value', () => {
    const body = JSON.stringify({ k: `\n${V}`, lines: Array.from({ length: 400 }, (_, i) => `line ${i}`).join('\n') });
    const text = `${body} ${'z '.repeat(1000)}`;
    const all: string[] = [];
    for (let at = text.indexOf('line 1'), n = 0; n < 60; at = text.indexOf(`${BS}n`, at + 1), n += 1) {
      const cut = at + 1;
      all.push(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, cut - 400, cut, idx), libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, cut, cut + 400, idx));
    }
    expect(pieces(all, V)).toEqual([]);
    expect(all.filter(inexact).length, 'inexact windows').toBe(0);
  });

  it('a cut that cannot be shown exact fails closed: the window alone, every run of 8 or more masked, under one note line; never margin text', () => {
    const run = 'AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP';
    const text = `${'p '.repeat(40_000)}${run}QRSTUVWXYZ0123 rest of it longwordhere ${'q '.repeat(40_000)}`;
    const lo = text.indexOf('QRSTU');
    const out = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, lo, lo + 60, idx);
    expect(out.startsWith(`${NOTE}${NL}`), 'inexact, under its note line').toBe(true);
    expect(out, 'no margin text').not.toContain('AKIA');
    expect(out, 'the long word masked').not.toContain('longwordhere');
    expect(out).toContain(` rest of it ${M} q q`);
    expect(out.split(NL), 'one note line, then the window').toHaveLength(2);
    // grep's snippet over the same cut shows the note on its one line.
    const hit = `${'p '.repeat(40_000)}${run}QRSTUVWXYZ0123 ${'x'.repeat(184)} zqfb5 ${'q '.repeat(500)}`;
    expect(hit.indexOf('zqfb5') - libGrep.SNIPPET_MAX, 'CONTROL: the snippet window starts inside the run').toBe(hit.indexOf('QRSTU'));
    const snip = libGrep.displaySnippet(hit, ['zqfb5'], idx);
    expect(snip.startsWith(`${NOTE} `), 'the note leads the snippet').toBe(true);
    expect(snip).not.toContain('AKIA');
    expect(snip).not.toContain(NL);
    expect(snip).toContain('zqfb5');
  });

  it('a literal mark after a colour sequence where a margin starts does not move the cut into the margin', () => {
    const W = `QP${alnum(29)}8`;
    const i2 = libGrep.makePairIndex(libGrep.secretPairs([W]).pairs);
    const tok = `tk${alnum(30)}`;
    const m = libGrep.ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN;
    const head = `${'h '.repeat(1000)}Authorization: Bearer `;
    const left = `${tok} ${ESC}[0m${M} ${'f '.repeat(m)}`.slice(0, m);
    const lo = head.length + left.length;
    const win = ` w ${W.slice(0, 12)}${ESC}[32m${W.slice(12)} e `.padEnd(80, '.');
    const text = head + left + win + ` ${'t '.repeat(40_000)}`;
    expect(text.indexOf(tok), 'CONTROL: the margin starts on the token').toBe(lo - m);
    expect(pieces([libGrep.redactForDisplay(text, i2)], tok), 'CONTROL: the whole text masks the token').toEqual([]);
    const out = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, lo, lo + 80, i2);
    expect(pieces([out], tok)).toEqual([]);
    expect(pieces([out], W)).toEqual([]);
    expect(out.length, 'the window, never the margin').toBeLessThanOrEqual(80 + 2 * M.length);
    expect(inexact(out), 'cut exactly').toBe(false);
    // The same margin, now ending on the head of a value whose rest starts the window: of the margin's two readings, the
    // one with its sequences removed reaches the value, so it decides, and the value shows as its whole mark.
    const Z = `QP${alnum(29)}9`;
    const i3 = libGrep.makePairIndex(libGrep.secretPairs([W, Z]).pairs);
    const left3 = `${left.slice(0, m - 11)} ${Z.slice(0, 10)}`;
    const win3 = `${Z.slice(10)} w ${W.slice(0, 12)}${ESC}[32m${W.slice(12)} e `.padEnd(80, '.');
    const text3 = head + left3 + win3 + ` ${'t '.repeat(40_000)}`;
    expect(text3.indexOf(tok), 'CONTROL: the margin starts on the token').toBe(lo - m);
    const out3 = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text3, lo, lo + 80, i3);
    for (const s of [tok, W, Z]) expect(pieces([out3], s), s.slice(0, 4)).toEqual([]);
    expect(out3.length, 'the window, never the margin').toBeLessThanOrEqual(80 + 2 * M.length);
    expect(inexact(out3), 'cut exactly').toBe(false);
    expect(out3.startsWith(`${M} w `), 'the straddling value shows as its whole mark').toBe(true);
  });

  it('an inexact window reads an escape-split value as the readings do: a coloured or JSON-escaped value at its end leaves no 8-character stretch, and a coloured or escaped word inside it is masked whole (final check W1)', () => {
    const W = `QW${alnum(30)}`;
    /** V pair-only, W loaded in the belt: `ab_<W>_tail`, Task 7A's glue shape, makes a window starting in W inexact. */
    const i2 = libGrep.makePairIndex(libGrep.secretPairs([V, W]).pairs, libGrep.makeBelt(libGrep.beltUnits([W])));
    /** A colour sequence before every character, as lolcat prints. */
    const lolcat = (s: string): string[] => s.split('').map((c, k) => `${ESC}[38;5;${16 + k}m${c}`);
    /** Every character as a JSON unicode escape (a backslash, `u00`, two hex digits), built from code points. */
    const uesc = (s: string): string[] => s.split('').map((c) => `${BS}u00${c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')}`);
    const plain = (s: string): string => s.replace(new RegExp(`${ESC}${BS}[[0-9;]*m`, 'g'), '');
    const decoded = (s: string): string => s.replace(new RegExp(`${BS}${BS}u00([0-9a-f]{2})`, 'g'), (_m, h: string) => String.fromCharCode(parseInt(h, 16)));
    const word = `zq${alnum(14)}`;
    for (const [form, parts] of [['coloured', lolcat], ['escaped', uesc]] as const) {
      const build = (glued: string): { text: string; lo: number; hi: number } => {
        const head = `${'p '.repeat(40_000)}note ab_${glued}_tail and ${parts(word).join('')} rest of it `;
        const vp = parts(V);
        const text = `${head}${vp.join('')}${form === 'coloured' ? `${ESC}[0m` : ''} tail ${'q '.repeat(40_000)}`;
        return { text, lo: head.indexOf(`${glued}_tail`) + glued.length - 5, hi: head.length + vp.slice(0, 30).join('').length };
      };
      const hit = build(W);
      const whole = libGrep.redactForDisplay(hit.text, i2);
      expect(pieces([plain(whole), decoded(whole)], V), `${form}: CONTROL: the whole text masks V`).toEqual([]);
      const out = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(hit.text, hit.lo, hit.hi, i2);
      expect(inexact(out), `${form}: CONTROL: the glued belt unit at the start makes the window inexact`).toBe(true);
      expect(pieces([out, plain(out), decoded(out)], V), `${form}: V at the window's end`).toEqual([]);
      expect(pieces([out, plain(out), decoded(out)], word), `${form}: the word inside the window`).toEqual([]);
      const ctl = build('x'.repeat(W.length));
      const outC = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(ctl.text, ctl.lo, ctl.hi, i2);
      expect(inexact(outC), `${form}: CONTROL: without the glued unit the same window is exact`).toBe(false);
      expect(pieces([outC, plain(outC), decoded(outC)], V), `${form}: the exact window`).toEqual([]);
    }
  });

  it('an inexact window whose edge cuts a value leaves none of its characters, however few (final check W3)', () => {
    const run = 'AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP';
    const colour = (s: string): string => s.split('').map((c, k) => `${ESC}[38;5;${16 + k}m${c}`).join('');
    for (const [form, enc] of [['plain', (s: string): string => s], ['coloured', colour]] as const) {
      const head = `${'p '.repeat(40_000)}${run}QRSTUVWXYZ0123 rest of it `;
      const text = `${head}${enc(V)} tail ${'q '.repeat(40_000)}`;
      const lo = head.indexOf('QRSTU');
      for (let k = 1; k <= 7; k += 1) {
        const hi = head.length + enc(V.slice(0, k)).length;
        expect(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, lo, hi, idx), `${form}, ${k} of V's characters inside`).toBe(`${NOTE}${NL} rest of it `);
      }
    }
  });

  it('a match that is one token span and begins beyond the margin is dropped where it reaches the window; one that holds a space is the named residual (final check W2)', () => {
    const b64 = (n: number): string => Array.from(libGrepRandom(n), (b) => 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/'[b % 64]!).join('');
    const seg = (n: number): string => Array.from({ length: n }, () => alnum(9)).join('.');
    const closed: [string, string, string][] = [
      ['NAME= base64', 'SECRET_TOKEN=', b64(120_000)],
      ['Bearer, dotted', 'Authorization: Bearer ', seg(11_000)],
      ['JWT, first segment past the margin', 'jwt ', `eyJ${alnum(120_000)}.eyJzdWIiOiJ6cSJ9.${alnum(43)}`],
      ['?token=', 'GET https://h.example/cb?token=', b64(120_000)],
    ];
    for (const [form, key, value] of closed) {
      const text = `log start${NL}${key}${value}${NL}after ${'q '.repeat(1000)}`;
      const at = text.indexOf(value);
      const whole = libGrep.redactForDisplay(text, none);
      for (const lo of [at + 100_000, at + value.length - 20]) {
        const shown = value.slice(lo - at - 8, lo - at + 300);
        expect(pieces([whole], shown), `${form}: CONTROL: the whole text masks it`).toEqual([]);
        expect(pieces([libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(text, lo, lo + 300, none)], shown), `${form}: window at ${lo - at}`).toEqual([]);
      }
    }
    // The residual (spec §8.3): a match that holds a space, its key more than the margin before the window, is read
    // only from a break inside it, so the window shows what the whole text masks. Pinned so that a change is seen.
    const words = Array.from({ length: 20_000 }, (_, i) => `word${i}`).join(' ');
    const pw = `{${Q}password${Q}: ${Q}${words}${Q}}`;
    expect(libGrep.redactForDisplay(pw, none), 'residual: CONTROL: the whole text masks it').not.toContain('word11119');
    const lo = pw.indexOf('word11119');
    expect(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(pw, lo, lo + 40, none), 'residual: the window shows it').toContain('word11119');
  });

  it('a window longer than DISPLAY_WINDOW_MAX is shown inexact unless it is the whole text, which is redactForDisplay\'s (final check W4)', () => {
    const big = Array.from({ length: 85_000 }, (_, i) => `w${i % 997}xyzabcd`).join(' ');
    const out = libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(big, 1, big.length, idx);
    expect(big.length - 1, 'CONTROL: the window is longer than DISPLAY_WINDOW_MAX').toBeGreaterThan(libGrep.DISPLAY_WINDOW_MAX);
    expect(big.length, 'CONTROL: the text is within DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX').toBeLessThanOrEqual(libGrep.DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX);
    expect(inexact(out), 'a window past the bound that is not the whole text').toBe(true);
    expect(libGrep.redactDisplayWindow(big, 0, big.length, idx) === libGrep.redactForDisplay(big, idx), 'the whole text').toBe(true);
  });
});
```

```js
// ── grep: arguments and the index gate (W1-B2 Task 12; spec §8.4, §9.1) ──────────────────────────────

/** What the sweep indexes and grep may search: the searchable provenances plus recall-echo. Default grep
 *  filters to SEARCHABLE_PROVENANCE at query time; `--include-recall` widens it to this list (§8.4
 *  "Recall echoes … are stored, excluded from default search, and found with --include-recall").
 *  D-4712 (history-recall-echo-indexed) */
export const INDEXED_PROVENANCE = Object.freeze([...SEARCHABLE_PROVENANCE, 'recall-echo']);

/** derivation_state's FTS step (§9.1): the sweep creates and backfills the FTS tables under ('fts', 1), and
 *  grep's index gate reads the same row. Spelled once, here. */
export const FTS_STEP = 'fts';

/** A byte count as SEARCH_REACH spells it: whole MiB, else whole KiB, else bytes. */
export function reachSize(n) {
  if (n % 1048576 === 0) return `${n / 1048576} MiB`;
  if (n % 1024 === 0) return `${n / 1024} KiB`;
  return `${n} bytes`;
}

/** How far grep reaches. Grep's exit 3 prints these words on its hint line (recall.mjs `grepNotFound`), and the skill
 *  (section 9) and README's history section quote them verbatim (spec §6.2 and §8.4, rev 3.5). The index holds at
 *  most an entry's first ENTRY_FTS_BYTES and a sidecar's first SIDECAR_FTS_BYTES of redacted text (B1's
 *  history-entry-index-text-windowed and history-sidecar-redact-before-cut), and --regex scans that same text (Task 14,
 *  spec §8.4), so no grep form finds a word past it. The sentence is built from the two
 *  constants, so changing a window changes it, and the skill's and README's pins go red until their text follows.
 *  "At most": the cut can fall short of the window (cutIndexText's margin and trailing-run rules), and a read verb
 *  never decompresses a sidecar past SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX (D-4713 (history-read-skips-oversize-sidecar)). */
export const SEARCH_REACH = `grep reaches at most the first ${reachSize(ENTRY_FTS_BYTES)} of each message's redacted text and the first ${reachSize(SIDECAR_FTS_BYTES)} of each tool output Claude Code saved to its own file; text past that is stored but not searched`;

/** grep's index gate (§9.1, §8.3 exit 7), over what the reader measured:
 *  - a probe that THREW is 5 probe-failed, never folded into absent;
 *  - an absent module is 7 fts5-absent;
 *  - no blobs_fts yet, or a backfill ('fts', 1) that has not completed, is 7 fts-pending, so a partial index
 *    never answers 3 for text the store holds but has not indexed yet.
 *  D-4714 (history-grep-pending-until-backfilled) */
export function decideGrepIndex({ probe, table, completed }) {
  if (probe === 'threw') return { ok: false, exit: EXIT.DB, reason: 'probe-failed' };
  if (probe !== 'present') return { ok: false, exit: EXIT.FTS_UNAVAILABLE, reason: 'fts5-absent' };
  if (!table || !completed) return { ok: false, exit: EXIT.FTS_UNAVAILABLE, reason: 'fts-pending' };
  return { ok: true };
}

/** grep's option grammar (§8.4), over the argv after the verb word. Every value is checked here, before any
 *  identity or store read. The scope flags (--project, --workspace, --session <id>) are consumed and passed
 *  over: readContext decides them (Task 10). `--` ends the options, so a word that begins with `--` can be
 *  searched. With --regex there are no positional words and no rank to sort by (Task 14). */
export function parseGrepArgs(argv, nowMs) {
  const a = {
    words: [], regex: null, role: null, tool: null, sinceMs: null, beforeMs: null, node: null,
    sort: 'recency', limit: GREP_LIMIT_DEFAULT, cursor: null, includeRecall: false, json: false,
  };
  const bad = { ok: false, reason: 'bad-args' };
  const seen = new Set();
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i += 1) {
    const t = argv[i];
    if (t === '--') { a.words.push(...argv.slice(i + 1)); break; }
    if (!t.startsWith('--')) { a.words.push(t); continue; }
    if (seen.has(t)) return bad;
    seen.add(t);
    if (t === '--json') { a.json = true; continue; }
    if (t === '--include-recall') { a.includeRecall = true; continue; }
    if (t === '--project' || t === '--workspace') continue;
    if (i + 1 >= argv.length) return bad;
    i += 1;
    const v = argv[i];
    switch (t) {
      case '--session': break;
      case '--regex': a.regex = v; break;
      case '--role': if (!/^[a-z]{1,16}$/.test(v)) return bad; a.role = v; break;
      case '--tool': if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}$/.test(v)) return bad; a.tool = v; break;
      case '--since': a.sinceMs = parseTimeBound(v, nowMs); if (a.sinceMs === null) return bad; break;
      case '--before': a.beforeMs = parseTimeBound(v, nowMs); if (a.beforeMs === null) return bad; break;
      case '--node': a.node = v; break;
      case '--sort': if (!GREP_SORTS.includes(v)) return bad; a.sort = v; break;
      case '--limit': {
        if (!/^[1-9][0-9]{0,5}$/.test(v) || Number(v) > GREP_LIMIT_MAX) return bad;
        a.limit = Number(v);
        break;
      }
      case '--cursor': a.cursor = v; break;
      default: return bad;
    }
  }
  if (a.regex === null ? a.words.length === 0 : a.words.length > 0 || a.sort !== 'recency') return bad;
  return { ok: true, args: a };
}
```

Then append to the END of `ccd/history/lib.mjs`, below Step 3's section:

```js

// ── a window of a longer text, redacted for display (W1-B2 Task 12; coordinator rulings R-display-window, R-window2) ──
// A read verb that shows a window of a longer text (grep's snippet, describe's excerpt and --full page, expand's cut,
// page and outline input) redacts that window and ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN on each side of it, never the whole text, so
// one snippet's or one page's cost is bounded by the window, whatever the field's length: B1's D-4419
// (`history-entry-index-text-windowed`) bound, carried to display (spec §8.3 and §8.4, rev 3.5).

/** Where grep's snippet sits (§8.4, §11 P9): the earliest hit of any term, each also tried without a common ending
 *  (FTS5 matched through porter stems and prefixes), case-insensitive in place. `at` is -1 when no term is found.
 *  snippetWindow cuts around it; displaySnippet finds it in the RAW text and redacts only the window around it. */
export function snippetSpan(text, terms) {
  const content = String(text);
  let at = -1;
  let len = 0;
  for (const term of terms) {
    const needles = [term];
    for (const s of SNIPPET_STEM_SUFFIXES) if (term.endsWith(s) && term.length - s.length >= 3) needles.push(term.slice(0, -s.length));
    for (const needle of needles) {
      if (needle === '') continue;
      const idx = new RegExp(escapeRe(needle), 'i').exec(content)?.index ?? -1;
      if (idx !== -1 && (at === -1 || idx < at || (idx === at && needle.length > len))) {
        at = idx;
        len = needle.length;
      }
    }
  }
  return { at, len };
}

/** The longest window redactDisplayWindow cuts from its redacted context: with ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN on each side, the
 *  text read is at most DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX, where redactForDisplay IS redactForIndex (Task 7A). Every caller's
 *  window is far shorter (EXPLORE_READ_MAX, 256 KiB, is the longest); a longer one is shown inexact, unless it is the
 *  whole text (displayWindow's step 0). */
export const DISPLAY_WINDOW_MAX = DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX - 2 * ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN;

/** How many characters that are not a mark a window edge's cut may sit short of a margin's own reading and still
 *  count as exact (*chosen*). A JSON escape the edge splits (`\` on one side, `n` or `u0041` on the other, once per
 *  decode level) is decoded in the read text but stays as written in the margin read alone; measured on the
 *  prototype, 0 left 118 of 120 such page edges inexact and 32 left none. */
export const DISPLAY_EDGE_SLACK = 32;

/** The one line an inexact window is shown under (spec §8.3; coordinator ruling R-window2). It holds no `"`, `\`,
 *  `<`, `>` or `&`, as REDACTED_MARK holds none, so it prints as it is in every form. */
export const DISPLAY_INEXACT_NOTE = '[window redacted alone: every word of 8 or more characters masked]';

/** A mark, or a maximal span of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` characters, backslashes and ANSI sequences: the unit an inexact
 *  window masks (coordinator ruling on final-check W1). A mark is matched first and kept whole. Each arm opens on a
 *  character no other arm opens on, so the scan is linear (D-4306). */
const DISPLAY_SPAN_RE = new RegExp(`${MARK_RE_SRC}|(?:[A-Za-z0-9_\\\\-]|(?:${ANSI_ESCAPE_RE.source}))+`, 'g');

/** A run of 8 or more `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` characters: a word an inexact window masks. */
const DISPLAY_WORD_RE = /[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}/;

/** Whether a DISPLAY_SPAN_RE span holds a word of 8 or more characters in any of the readings redactForDisplay takes:
 *  the span with its ANSI sequences removed (B1's joined reading), then each JSON-escape decode of that, up to
 *  INDEX_UNESCAPE_PASSES, its sequences removed again. A value printed one coloured character at a time, or as one
 *  JSON unicode escape per character, is a word only in those readings (final-check W1: the raw text's runs were 5
 *  characters or fewer, and 30 of a value's 48 showed). Linear in the span, once per pass. */
function spanHoldsWord(span) {
  let s = span.replace(ANSI_ESCAPE_RE, '');
  if (DISPLAY_WORD_RE.test(s)) return true;
  for (let pass = 0; pass < INDEX_UNESCAPE_PASSES; pass += 1) {
    const u = unescapeJsonText(s);
    if (u === s) return false;
    s = u.replace(ANSI_ESCAPE_RE, '');
    if (DISPLAY_WORD_RE.test(s)) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

/** A break between token spans: whitespace, or one of `"`, `'`, `` ` ``, `,`, `;` and `&`, the characters that end
 *  a value in layer 2's `NAME=` form (coordinator ruling on final-check W2). */
const TOKEN_BREAK_RE = /[\s"'`,;&]/;

/** A code unit of a token span (`[^\s"'`,;&]`): a margin's far end moves off one, and a partial one that reaches the
 *  window is dropped. Every `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` run lies inside one, and so does a `NAME=` value with `+` or `/` in it,
 *  a dotted Bearer token or JWT, and a `?token=` value. */
function isTokenByte(c) {
  return !TOKEN_BREAK_RE.test(String.fromCharCode(c));
}

/** What ends an inexact window's edge drop: whitespace, or one of `"`, `'`, `` ` ``, `,` and `&`. */
const INEXACT_EDGE_BREAK_RE = /[\s"'`,&]/;

/** A code unit an inexact window's edge drop reads as part of a span: every run byte, the backslash, ESC and every
 *  other character a colour sequence holds (`;` among its parameters), so an edge that cuts a word a sequence or an
 *  escape split drops the window's part of it, however few of its characters are inside (final-check W1 and W3).
 *  A superset of the readings spanHoldsWord takes, so the drop fails closed. */
function isInexactEdgeByte(c) {
  return !INEXACT_EDGE_BREAK_RE.test(String.fromCharCode(c));
}

/** `s` without its leading run of `pred` code units, by a forward scan (linear; B1's dropTrailingRun, mirrored). */
function dropLeadingWhile(s, pred) {
  let k = 0;
  while (k < s.length && pred(s.charCodeAt(k))) k += 1;
  return k === 0 ? s : s.slice(k);
}

/** `s` without its trailing run of `pred` code units, by a backward scan (linear, as B1's dropTrailingRun). */
function dropTrailingWhile(s, pred) {
  let k = s.length;
  while (k > 0 && pred(s.charCodeAt(k - 1))) k -= 1;
  return k === s.length ? s : s.slice(0, k);
}

/** `k` moved back off the low half of a surrogate pair, so no slice at `k` splits the pair. */
function pairStart(t, k) {
  if (k <= 0 || k >= t.length) return k;
  const c = t.charCodeAt(k);
  const p = t.charCodeAt(k - 1);
  return c >= 0xdc00 && c <= 0xdfff && p >= 0xd800 && p <= 0xdbff ? k - 1 : k;
}

/** `s`'s length without its marks: the characters of `s` that came from text, not from a redaction. */
function unmarkedLength(s) {
  let n = s.length;
  for (let k = s.indexOf(REDACTED_MARK); k !== -1; k = s.indexOf(REDACTED_MARK, k + REDACTED_MARK.length)) n -= REDACTED_MARK.length;
  return n;
}

/** redactForDisplay's reading of `text` (at most DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX long, where redactForDisplay IS redactForIndex),
 *  with the reading it chose: `levels` JSON-escape decodes, and `bound` when it reached INDEX_UNESCAPE_PASSES and
 *  marked the escape-glued spans. redactForIndex's own loop, step for step, so the window knows which reading it is
 *  cut from; Step 1's case `a whole text's window is redactForDisplay's, …` pins the two equal on every reading, through
 *  each text's window inside a longer one (a whole text's window no longer reaches this function). */
function displayReading(text, idx) {
  let t = redactIndexReading(text, idx);
  let keep = t;
  let levels = 0;
  for (let pass = 0; pass < INDEX_UNESCAPE_PASSES; pass += 1) {
    const deeper = unescapeJsonText(t);
    if (deeper === t) return { text: keep, levels, bound: false };
    t = redactIndexReading(deeper, idx);
    if (t !== deeper) {
      keep = t;
      levels = pass + 1;
    }
  }
  return { text: markEscapeGluedSpans(t), levels: INDEX_UNESCAPE_PASSES, bound: true };
}

/** `text` read through exactly the reading displayReading chose for the text around it: the same decodes, each
 *  redacted, and the escape-glued spans marked when that reading marked them. A margin read so is comparable with the
 *  read text whichever reading the read text's content chose (finding V15: a margin read through its own choice stays
 *  raw while the read text is shown decoded). */
function readingAt(text, idx, levels, bound) {
  let t = redactIndexReading(text, idx);
  for (let pass = 0; pass < levels; pass += 1) t = redactIndexReading(unescapeJsonText(t), idx);
  return bound ? markEscapeGluedSpans(t) : t;
}

/** A margin's reading, and the same with its ANSI sequences removed when that differs. B1's redactField returns its
 *  joined reading, every sequence of the text removed, when that reading finds something anywhere in the text, so the
 *  read text can drop a margin's sequences that the margin read alone keeps (finding V18). ANSI_ESCAPE_RE never takes a
 *  mark's first character, so the removal leaves every mark whole. */
function marginReadings(m) {
  if (!ESCAPE_INTRODUCER_RE.test(m)) return [m];
  const plain = m.replace(ANSI_ESCAPE_RE, '');
  return plain === m ? [m] : [m, plain];
}

/** Where the window starts in `d`, the read text's reading, given the left margin's readings. Rank 1: the end of the
 *  longest prefix `d` shares with one of them, when that is the whole margin. Otherwise the reading whose shared prefix
 *  reaches furthest decides, when it is either of: rank 2, the start of the mark `d` holds where the two part, so a
 *  match straddling the edge shows as its whole mark; rank 3, the end of the shared prefix, when what the margin has
 *  left past it is at most DISPLAY_EDGE_SLACK characters and no mark (an escape the edge split). -1 when none holds:
 *  the cut cannot be shown exact. */
function windowStart(d, lefts) {
  let best = -1;
  let reach = -1;
  for (const l of lefts) {
    const n = Math.min(d.length, l.length);
    let s = 0;
    while (s < n && d.charCodeAt(s) === l.charCodeAt(s)) s += 1;
    if (s === l.length) return s;
    if (s <= reach) continue;
    const j = d.lastIndexOf(REDACTED_MARK, s);
    if (j !== -1 && j + REDACTED_MARK.length > s) {
      best = j;
      reach = s;
    } else if (l.length - s <= DISPLAY_EDGE_SLACK && l.indexOf(REDACTED_MARK, s) === -1) {
      best = s;
      reach = s;
    }
  }
  return best;
}

/** Where the window ends in `d`, at or past `s`, given the right margin's readings: windowStart's rule, mirrored, over
 *  the longest shared suffix. -1 when none holds. */
function windowEnd(d, rights, s) {
  let best = -1;
  let reach = -1;
  for (const r of rights) {
    const n = Math.min(d.length - s, r.length);
    let k = 0;
    while (k < n && d.charCodeAt(d.length - 1 - k) === r.charCodeAt(r.length - 1 - k)) k += 1;
    const e = d.length - k;
    if (k === r.length) return e;
    if (k <= reach) continue;
    const j = e > 0 ? d.lastIndexOf(REDACTED_MARK, e - 1) : -1;
    if (j !== -1 && j + REDACTED_MARK.length >= e && j + REDACTED_MARK.length > s) {
      best = j + REDACTED_MARK.length;
      reach = k;
    } else if (r.length - k <= DISPLAY_EDGE_SLACK && r.lastIndexOf(REDACTED_MARK, r.length - k - 1) === -1) {
      best = e;
      reach = k;
    }
  }
  return best;
}

/** An inexact window (coordinator ruling R-window2, the fail-closed display, and the ruling on final-check W1):
 *  `text[lo, hi)` alone, the span either window edge cuts dropped (isInexactEdgeByte, so a word joined across
 *  sequences or escapes at the edge goes with it), through redactForDisplay, then every span (DISPLAY_SPAN_RE) that
 *  holds a word of 8 or more characters in its own readings (spanHoldsWord) replaced by the mark. It reads the window
 *  and the one character beyond each edge, and nothing else. */
function inexactWindow(t, lo, hi, idx) {
  let w = t.slice(lo, hi);
  if (lo > 0 && isInexactEdgeByte(t.charCodeAt(lo - 1)) && isInexactEdgeByte(t.charCodeAt(lo))) w = dropLeadingWhile(w, isInexactEdgeByte);
  if (hi < t.length && hi > 0 && isInexactEdgeByte(t.charCodeAt(hi - 1)) && isInexactEdgeByte(t.charCodeAt(hi))) w = dropTrailingWhile(w, isInexactEdgeByte);
  return { text: redactForDisplay(w, idx).replace(DISPLAY_SPAN_RE, (s) => (s !== REDACTED_MARK && spanHoldsWord(s) ? REDACTED_MARK : s)), exact: false };
}

/** text[from, to) as a read verb shows it, and whether it was cut exactly (spec §8.3 and §8.4; coordinator rulings
 *  R-display-window and R-window2). In order:
 *  0. A window of the whole text (`from` at or before 0, `to` at or past its length) has no margin: it is
 *     redactForDisplay's reading of the text, exact, whatever its length (final-check W4). Any other window longer
 *     than DISPLAY_WINDOW_MAX is shown inexact.
 *  1. The margins. [a, b) is the window widened by ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN each way, each end moved off a token span
 *     (`[^\s"'`,;&]`, isTokenByte) before anything is redacted, so the text read never starts or ends inside one: B1's
 *     cut rule (D-4419's cutIndexText), widened from `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` runs to token spans (final-check W2), so a
 *     `NAME=` value with `+` or `/`, a dotted Bearer token or JWT and a `?token=` value are read whole or not at all.
 *     A token span longer than the margin stops the move at the window's edge, and that partial span is dropped from
 *     what is shown, as B1's cut drops a trailing run. A match that is not one token span (it holds whitespace or a
 *     break: a PEM body, a quoted value) and begins more than ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN before the window is read only from
 *     a break inside it: spec §8.3's residual.
 *  2. The read text's reading. [a, b) is read through redactForDisplay's reading (displayReading), so every layer and
 *     reading (the pairs, the belt, the context forms and their JSON-escaped form, the shapes, the escape readings,
 *     the joined reading) sees the margins with the window. What is shown is a slice of that reading and nothing
 *     else: a match straddling an edge was made whole there, so it shows only as its whole mark.
 *  3. The cut back. Each margin is read alone through the SAME reading (readingAt: the decodes the read text took),
 *     and also with its ANSI sequences removed (marginReadings). The window is what the read text leaves between the
 *     longest prefix it shares with a left reading and the longest suffix it shares with a right one (windowStart,
 *     windowEnd; of the readings, the one whose shared part reaches furthest). The cut is exact when that shared part
 *     is the whole margin, or ends at a mark the read text holds there, or leaves at most DISPLAY_EDGE_SLACK
 *     characters of an escape the edge split; and the slice then holds at
 *     most (to - from) + 2 × DISPLAY_EDGE_SLACK characters that are not a mark, since a redaction, a decode and a
 *     removed sequence each leave at most one character per character read.
 *  4. Otherwise the cut cannot be shown exact (B1's redactField is not local: its joined reading returns the whole
 *     text without its sequences), and the window is shown inexact (inexactWindow), never margin text.
 *  Each reading reads at most (to - from) + 2 × ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN characters, through at most
 *  INDEX_UNESCAPE_PASSES + 1 redactions; an inexact window reads the window once more. No slice splits a surrogate
 *  pair. `idx` is the read's pair index, with its belt (Task 7A). */
function displayWindow(text, from, to, idx) {
  const t = String(text);
  const lo = pairStart(t, Math.max(0, Math.min(from, t.length)));
  const hi = Math.max(lo, pairStart(t, Math.max(0, Math.min(to, t.length))));
  if (lo === 0 && hi === t.length) return { text: redactForDisplay(t, idx), exact: true };
  if (hi - lo > DISPLAY_WINDOW_MAX) return inexactWindow(t, lo, hi, idx);
  let a = pairStart(t, Math.max(0, lo - ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN));
  while (a > 0 && a < lo && isTokenByte(t.charCodeAt(a - 1)) && isTokenByte(t.charCodeAt(a))) a += 1;
  let b = pairStart(t, Math.min(t.length, hi + ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN));
  while (b < t.length && b > hi && isTokenByte(t.charCodeAt(b - 1)) && isTokenByte(t.charCodeAt(b))) b -= 1;
  const leadCut = a > 0 && isTokenByte(t.charCodeAt(a - 1)) && isTokenByte(t.charCodeAt(a));
  const tailCut = b < t.length && b > 0 && isTokenByte(t.charCodeAt(b - 1)) && isTokenByte(t.charCodeAt(b));
  const read = displayReading(t.slice(a, b), idx);
  const d = read.text;
  const lefts = lo > a ? marginReadings(readingAt(t.slice(a, lo), idx, read.levels, read.bound)) : [''];
  const rights = b > hi ? marginReadings(readingAt(t.slice(hi, b), idx, read.levels, read.bound)) : [''];
  const s0 = windowStart(d, lefts);
  const e0 = s0 === -1 ? -1 : windowEnd(d, rights, s0);
  if (s0 === -1 || e0 === -1) return inexactWindow(t, lo, hi, idx);
  const s = pairStart(d, s0);
  const e = Math.max(s, pairStart(d, e0));
  let out = d.slice(s, e);
  if (leadCut) out = dropLeadingWhile(out, isTokenByte);
  if (tailCut) out = dropTrailingWhile(out, isTokenByte);
  if (unmarkedLength(out) > (hi - lo) + 2 * DISPLAY_EDGE_SLACK) return inexactWindow(t, lo, hi, idx);
  return { text: out, exact: true };
}

/** text[from, to) as a read verb shows it (displayWindow): the exact cut of its redacted context, or an inexact window
 *  under DISPLAY_INEXACT_NOTE's one line. Describe's excerpt and --full pages (Task 15) and expand's cuts, pages and
 *  outline input (Task 16) call it; grep's snippet calls displayWindow itself. A window of the whole text
 *  (`from` at or before 0, `to` at or past its length) has no margin, so it is always exact and IS redactForDisplay's
 *  reading, whatever its length (displayWindow's step 0, ahead of the DISPLAY_WINDOW_MAX guard). */
export function redactDisplayWindow(text, from, to, idx) {
  const w = displayWindow(text, from, to, idx);
  return w.exact ? w.text : `${DISPLAY_INEXACT_NOTE}\n${w.text}`;
}

/** How far past the snippet's hit, each way, grep's snippet reads its RAW window (*chosen*): SNIPPET_MAX, more than
 *  snippetWindow's 24 before and 40 after, so a mark that shortens the text near the hit still leaves snippetWindow
 *  its whole window. */
const SNIPPET_READ = SNIPPET_MAX;

/** grep's snippet over a body or sidecar of any length (§8.4, §11 P9; §8.3, rev 3.5):
 *  the earliest hit is found in the RAW text (snippetSpan), the window around it is cut from its redacted context by
 *  displayWindow, and snippetWindow cuts that window, `...` marking a cut at either end of the text. With no hit the
 *  text's first 2 × SNIPPET_READ characters are read, and snippetWindow takes its first 80 of them. An inexact window
 *  is shown with DISPLAY_INEXACT_NOTE ahead of the snippet, on the snippet's one line. */
export function displaySnippet(text, terms, idx) {
  const content = String(text);
  const { at, len } = snippetSpan(content, terms);
  const from = at === -1 ? 0 : Math.max(0, at - SNIPPET_READ);
  const to = at === -1 ? Math.min(content.length, 2 * SNIPPET_READ) : Math.min(content.length, at + Math.max(len, 1) + SNIPPET_READ);
  const w = displayWindow(content, from, to, idx);
  const shown = snippetWindow(w.text, terms);
  const prefix = from > 0 && !shown.startsWith('...') ? '...' : '';
  const suffix = to < content.length && !shown.endsWith('...') ? '...' : '';
  return `${w.exact ? '' : `${DISPLAY_INEXACT_NOTE} `}${prefix}${shown}${suffix}`;
}
```

```ts
/** The ReadContext Task 10's readContext builds, as these tests build it in-process (cli.mjs is never imported
 *  here: it sets this worker's umask). */
interface GrepRc {
  db: RDatabaseSync; version: number; schema: unknown; storeId: string | null; nowMs: number; home: string; id: string;
  scope: {
    kind: 'family' | 'project' | 'workspace'; id: string; generation: string | null; project: string | null; workdir: string | null;
    sessionPks: number[]; transcriptPks: number[];
    families: Array<{ sessionPk: number; ccrcId: string; generation: string; firstSeenMs: number }>;
  };
  pairIdx: unknown;
}
interface GrepVerbResult {
  exit: number; reason?: string; header: string | null; blocks: string[]; items: Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
  shown: number; total: number; next: string[] | null; hint?: string;
}
interface GrepDeps { cap?: number; budgetMs?: number; spawn?: (...args: unknown[]) => unknown }
interface GrepMod {
  runGrep(rc: GrepRc, a: RGrepArgs, deps?: GrepDeps): GrepVerbResult;
  runDescribe?(rc: GrepRc, a: unknown, deps?: GrepDeps): GrepVerbResult;
}
type CliRun = rH.SpawnResult & { json: Record<string, unknown> | null };

const GRX = {
  idA: 'claude-a-demo',
  idB: 'claude-b-demo',
  idO: 'claude-b-other',
  /** The fixtures' default cwd (historyFixtures' envelope), used as the workdir of every family here. */
  W: '/home/u/worktrees/p/quiet-basin',
  t0: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 5, 10, 0, 0),
  ts(s: number): string { return new Date(GRX.t0 + s * 1000).toISOString(); },
  /** A row uuid: tag and ordinal in hex, the UUID grammar (lowercase). */
  uuid(tag: number, i: number): string {
    return `0189abcd-${tag.toString(16).padStart(4, '0')}-4000-8000-${i.toString(16).padStart(12, '0')}`;
  },
  /** A transcript's (cc session's) uuid for a tag. */
  file(tag: number): string { return `0189abcd-${tag.toString(16).padStart(4, '0')}-4fff-8fff-ffffffffffff`; },
  user(tag: number, i: number, text: string, extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}): rFx.Row {
    return { ...rFx.userRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(tag, i), ts: GRX.ts(i), sessionId: GRX.file(tag), text }), ...extra };
  },
  assistant(tag: number, i: number, text: string): rFx.Row {
    return rFx.assistantRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(tag, i), ts: GRX.ts(i), sessionId: GRX.file(tag), text,
      requestId: `req_g${tag}_${i}`, msgId: `msg_g${tag}_${i}` });
  },
  toolUse(tag: number, i: number, toolUseId: string, command: string): rFx.Row {
    return rFx.toolUseRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(tag, i), ts: GRX.ts(i), sessionId: GRX.file(tag), toolUseId, name: 'Bash',
      input: { command }, requestId: `req_g${tag}_${i}`, msgId: `msg_g${tag}_${i}` });
  },
  toolResult(tag: number, i: number, toolUseId: string, content: string): rFx.Row {
    return rFx.toolResultRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(tag, i), ts: GRX.ts(i), sessionId: GRX.file(tag), toolUseId, content });
  },
  /** A family: registry rows, the transcript, its startup line, swept to end of file (Task 10's seedFamily). */
  seed(box: rH.HistoryBox, tag: number, id: string, project: string, rows: rFx.Row[], accountId = 'claude-a'): string {
    return rH.seedFamily(box, { id, project, workdir: GRX.W, uuid: GRX.file(tag), rows, accountId }).transcript;
  },
  /** `ccrc history <args>` from `id`'s pane. */
  cli(box: rH.HistoryBox, id: string, args: string[], opts: rH.SpawnOpts = {}): CliRun {
    return rH.runCli(box, args, { ...opts, env: { ...rH.withPane(box, id), ...(opts.env ?? {}) } }) as CliRun;
  },
  items(r: CliRun): Array<Record<string, unknown>> {
    return ((r.json?.items ?? []) as Array<Record<string, unknown>>);
  },
  uuids(r: CliRun): unknown[] { return GRX.items(r).map((x) => x.entry_uuid); },
  async grepArgs(argv: string[]): Promise<RGrepArgs> {
    const lib = await import('../../ccd/history/lib.mjs');
    const p = lib.parseGrepArgs(argv, Date.now());
    if (!p.ok) throw new Error(`fixture argv refused: ${argv.join(' ')}`);
    return p.args;
  },
  async recall(): Promise<GrepMod> {
    return (await import('../../ccd/history/recall.mjs')) as unknown as GrepMod;
  },
  /** A family-scope ReadContext for `id`'s newest family, read off the fixture store the way Task 10 reads it: the
   *  family's confirmed epochs give its transcripts. The caller closes `db`. */
  async rc(box: rH.HistoryBox, id: string): Promise<GrepRc> {
    const store = await import('../../ccd/history/store.mjs');
    const lib = await import('../../ccd/history/lib.mjs');
    const db: RDatabaseSync = store.openReader(lib.historyPaths(box.home).dbFile);
    const fam = (db.prepare(`SELECT session_pk, ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms FROM sessions
      WHERE ccrc_id = ? AND merged_into IS NULL ORDER BY first_seen_ms DESC LIMIT 1`).all(id) as unknown as
      Array<{ session_pk: number; ccrc_id: string; generation: string; project: string; first_seen_ms: number }>);
    const sessionPks = fam.map((f) => f.session_pk);
    const transcriptPks = (db.prepare(`SELECT DISTINCT t.transcript_pk AS pk FROM epochs e
      JOIN transcripts t ON t.cc_session_uuid = e.cc_session_uuid
      WHERE e.confirmed_ms IS NOT NULL AND e.session_pk IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))`).all(JSON.stringify(sessionPks)) as unknown as
      Array<{ pk: number }>).map((r) => r.pk);
    const storeId = (db.prepare("SELECT v FROM meta WHERE k = 'store_id'").get() as { v: string } | undefined)?.v ?? null;
    return {
      db, version: store.userVersion(db), schema: lib.SCHEMA_ADDED, storeId, nowMs: Date.now(), home: box.home, id,
      scope: {
        kind: 'family', id, generation: fam[0]?.generation ?? null, project: fam[0]?.project ?? null, workdir: GRX.W,
        sessionPks, transcriptPks,
        families: fam.map((f) => ({ sessionPk: f.session_pk, ccrcId: f.ccrc_id, generation: f.generation, firstSeenMs: f.first_seen_ms })),
      },
      pairIdx: lib.makePairIndex([]),
    };
  },
  /** `db` with every prepare() recorded: the spy C7 reads. */
  spyDb(db: RDatabaseSync, calls: string[]): RDatabaseSync {
    return new Proxy(db, {
      get(t, k) {
        if (k === 'prepare') return (sql: string) => { calls.push(sql); return t.prepare(sql); };
        const v = Reflect.get(t, k, t) as unknown;
        return typeof v === 'function' ? (v as (...x: unknown[]) => unknown).bind(t) : v;
      },
    }) as RDatabaseSync;
  },
};

describe('grep, the FTS path: index gate, provenance, filters and everyday words (W1-B2 task 12)', () => {
  beforeEach((ctx) => { if (process.platform === 'darwin') ctx.skip(); });
  const T = 0x21;
  /** A deviation-number-shaped word, built in two pieces so this test's source holds no D-number token for the ledger's
   *  scanners to count (CLAUDE.md "Deviation ledger"). */
  const DNUM = ['D', '1234'].join('-');
  let box: rH.HistoryBox;
  beforeAll(() => {
    if (process.platform === 'darwin') return;
    box = rH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-grep-');
    GRX.seed(box, T, GRX.idA, 'demo', [
      GRX.user(T, 1, 'zqoperatorword plain operator words'),
      GRX.assistant(T, 2, 'zqmodelword the answer'),
      rFx.systemRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(T, 3), ts: GRX.ts(3), sessionId: GRX.file(T), subtype: 'informational', content: 'zqharnessword' }),
      GRX.user(T, 4, 'zqmetaword injected', { isMeta: true }),
      rFx.summaryRow({ uuid: GRX.uuid(T, 5), ts: GRX.ts(5), sessionId: GRX.file(T), text: 'zqsummaryword summary' }),
      GRX.toolUse(T, 6, 'toolu_g21echo', '"$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc" history grep zqasked'),
      GRX.toolResult(T, 7, 'toolu_g21echo', 'zqechoword earlier recall output'),
      GRX.toolUse(T, 8, 'toolu_g21cat', 'cat notes.md'),
      GRX.toolResult(T, 9, 'toolu_g21cat', 'zqcatword <ccrc-recall id="L0123456789abcdef0123"> page body'),
      GRX.user(T, 10, 'zqfirstline\nzqsecondword'),
      GRX.user(T, 11, 'edit server/src/coord/store.ts now'),
      GRX.user(T, 12, 'run it with --force please'),
      GRX.user(T, 13, `set history-off before ${DNUM} lands`),
      GRX.user(T, 14, 'fixes #123 finally'),
      GRX.user(T, 15, 'look at arr[0] closely'),
      GRX.user(T, 16, 'commit a0860d1f2e3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f70819 landed'),
      GRX.user(T, 17, 'a naïve café visit'),
      GRX.user(T, 18, 'please say zqinner words now'),
    ]);
  }, 120_000);
  const grep = (args: string[], opts: rH.SpawnOpts = {}): CliRun => GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', ...args], opts);

  it('C26: the CLI handle on an FTS-ready store answers 0 or 3, never 7, and every --json reason maps to its exit', () => {
    const hit = grep(['zqoperatorword', '--json']);
    expect(hit.code, hit.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(GRX.uuids(hit)).toEqual([GRX.uuid(T, 1)]);
    expect(hit.json?.total).toBe(1);
    const none = grep(['zqnowhereword', '--json']);
    expect(none.code, none.stderr).toBe(3);
    expect(none.json?.exit).toBe(3);
    expect(none.json).not.toHaveProperty('reason');
    expect(none.json?.coverage).toBe('this-box');
  }, 60_000);

  it("exit 3 states grep's reach on its one hint line, in lib's SEARCH_REACH words; a hit prints no reach line (spec §8.4, rev 3.5)", async () => {
    const lib = await import('../../ccd/history/lib.mjs');
    const none = grep(['zqnowhereword']);
    expect(none.code, none.stderr).toBe(3);
    expect(none.stdout.split('\n').filter((l) => l.startsWith('hint: '))).toEqual([`hint: ${lib.SEARCH_REACH}`]);
    const hit = grep(['zqoperatorword']);
    expect(hit.code, hit.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(hit.stdout).not.toContain(lib.SEARCH_REACH);
  }, 60_000);

  it('C26: a probe that throws is 5 probe-failed; one answering absent is 7 fts5-absent (the reader\'s own probe, never meta)', () => {
    const seam = (mode: string): CliRun => grep(['zqoperatorword', '--json'], { preloads: [rH.PRELOADS.faults], env: { HISTORY_TEST_FTS_PROBE: mode } });
    const threw = seam('throw');
    expect([threw.code, threw.json?.reason]).toEqual([5, 'probe-failed']);
    const absent = seam('absent');
    expect([absent.code, absent.json?.reason]).toEqual([7, 'fts5-absent']);
  }, 60_000);

  it('C7: regex syntax in plain search is exit 2 regex-syntax with a hint line, and no statement is ever prepared', async () => {
    const r = grep(['a|b', '--json']);
    expect([r.code, r.json?.reason]).toEqual([2, 'regex-syntax']);
    const human = grep(['zq.*word']);
    expect(human.code).toBe(2);
    expect(`${human.stdout}\n${human.stderr}`).toMatch(/^hint: .*--regex/m);
    const recall = await GRX.recall();
    const rc = await GRX.rc(box, GRX.idA);
    try {
      const calls: string[] = [];
      const spied = { ...rc, db: GRX.spyDb(rc.db, calls) };
      const refused = recall.runGrep(spied, await GRX.grepArgs(['a|b']));
      expect([refused.exit, refused.reason]).toEqual([2, 'regex-syntax']);
      expect(calls).toEqual([]);
      const answered = recall.runGrep(spied, await GRX.grepArgs(['zqoperatorword']));   // CONTROL: the spy sees a real query
      expect(answered.exit).toBe(0);
      expect(calls.some((s) => /blobs_fts MATCH/.test(s))).toBe(true);
    } finally { rc.db.close(); }
  }, 60_000);

  it('DM28 (CLI half): summary, harness and recall-echo text is not found by default grep; operator and model text is', () => {
    for (const w of ['zqharnessword', 'zqmetaword', 'zqsummaryword', 'zqechoword']) {
      const r = grep([w, '--json']);
      expect(r.code, w).toBe(3);
    }
    for (const w of ['zqoperatorword', 'zqmodelword']) expect(grep([w]).code, w).toBe(0);
  }, 60_000);

  it('C9: an earlier `ccrc history grep` tool_result is not matched by default, and is matched with --include-recall', () => {
    expect(grep(['zqechoword']).code).toBe(3);
    const r = grep(['zqechoword', '--include-recall', '--json']);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(GRX.uuids(r)).toEqual([GRX.uuid(T, 7)]);
    expect(GRX.items(r)[0]?.provenance).toBe('recall-echo');
  }, 60_000);

  it('DM32 (CLI half): a cat result holding <ccrc-recall stays in default search (provenance by structure)', () => {
    const r = grep(['zqcatword', '--json']);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(GRX.uuids(r)).toEqual([GRX.uuid(T, 9)]);
    expect(GRX.items(r)[0]?.provenance).toBe('tool');
  }, 60_000);

  it('DM30 (CLI half): a word after a newline in a text block is found; the JSON keys type and text are not', () => {
    expect(grep(['zqsecondword']).code).toBe(0);
    expect(grep(['type']).code).toBe(3);
    expect(grep(['text']).code).toBe(3);
  }, 60_000);

  it('filters: --role, --tool, --since and --before narrow inside the scope', () => {
    expect(grep(['zqmodelword', '--role', 'assistant']).code).toBe(0);
    expect(grep(['zqmodelword', '--role', 'user']).code).toBe(3);
    expect(grep(['zqasked', '--tool', 'Bash']).code).toBe(0);
    expect(grep(['zqasked', '--tool', 'Read']).code).toBe(3);
    expect(grep(['zqoperatorword', '--since', '2099-01-01T00:00:00Z']).code).toBe(3);
    expect(grep(['zqoperatorword', '--before', '2099-01-01T00:00:00Z']).code).toBe(0);
  }, 60_000);

  it('everyday words that are not plain words are quoted FTS terms, never an FTS syntax error or exit 1 (review focus 2)', () => {
    const found: Array<[string[], number]> = [
      [['server/src/coord/store.ts'], 11], [['--', '--force'], 12], [['history-off'], 13], [[DNUM], 13], [['#123'], 14],
      [['"arr[0]"'], 15], [['"a0860d1f"*'], 16], [['a0860d1f*'], 16], [['café'], 17], [['cafe'], 17],
      // A quoted phrase with an inner quote splits at the quotes into three quoted terms (AND); an unbalanced quote
      // is dropped from its word. Neither is an FTS syntax error.
      [['"say "zqinner" words"'], 18], [['"zqinner'], 18],
    ];
    for (const [words, row] of found) {
      const r = grep(['--json', ...words]);
      expect(r.code, `${words.join(' ')}: ${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
      expect(GRX.uuids(r), words.join(' ')).toContain(GRX.uuid(T, row));
    }
    for (const words of [['arr[0]'], ['a|b']]) {
      const r = grep(words);
      expect(r.code, words.join(' ')).toBe(2);
      expect(`${r.stdout}\n${r.stderr}`, words.join(' ')).toMatch(/^hint: /m);
    }
  }, 120_000);

  it('a statement that finds no blobs_fts (a repair racing the read) is 7 fts-pending, never exit 1 (review focus 5)', async () => {
    const recall = await GRX.recall();
    const rc = await GRX.rc(box, GRX.idA);
    try {
      const racing = new Proxy(rc.db, {
        get(t, k) {
          if (k === 'prepare') {
            return (sql: string) => {
              if (/blobs_fts MATCH/.test(sql)) throw new Error('no such table: blobs_fts');
              return t.prepare(sql);
            };
          }
          const v = Reflect.get(t, k, t) as unknown;
          return typeof v === 'function' ? (v as (...x: unknown[]) => unknown).bind(t) : v;
        },
      }) as RDatabaseSync;
      const r = recall.runGrep({ ...rc, db: racing }, await GRX.grepArgs(['zqoperatorword']));
      expect([r.exit, r.reason]).toEqual([7, 'fts-pending']);
    } finally { rc.db.close(); }
  });
});

describe('grep\'s index gate: no blobs_fts, or a backfill still running, is 7 fts-pending (W1-B2 task 12)', () => {
  beforeEach((ctx) => { if (process.platform === 'darwin') ctx.skip(); });

  it('a store whose sweep only ever saw FTS5 absent has no blobs_fts: grep is 7 fts-pending until a sweep with FTS makes it', () => {
    const T = 0x22;
    const box = rH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-grep-pend-');
    rH.plantSession(box, GRX.idA, { uuid: GRX.file(T), project: 'demo', workdir: GRX.W });
    rH.plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', '-home-u-worktrees-p-quiet-basin', GRX.file(T), [GRX.user(T, 1, 'zqpendingword here')]);
    rH.spoolLine(box, GRX.idA, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: GRX.idA, sid: GRX.file(T), src: 'startup', reg: GRX.file(T) });
    const absent = { preloads: [rH.PRELOADS.faults], env: { HISTORY_TEST_FTS_PROBE: 'absent' } };
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) { const s = rH.runSweep(box, [], absent); expect(s.code, s.stderr).toBe(0); }
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {   // CONTROL: the row is captured, and no FTS table exists
      expect((db.prepare("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM sqlite_master WHERE name = 'blobs_fts'").get() as { n: number }).n).toBe(0);
      expect((db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM entries WHERE uuid = ?').get(GRX.uuid(T, 1)) as { n: number }).n).toBe(1);
    } finally { db.close(); }
    const r = GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqpendingword', '--json']);
    expect([r.code, r.json?.reason]).toEqual([7, 'fts-pending']);
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) { const s = rH.runSweep(box); expect(s.code, s.stderr).toBe(0); }
    expect(GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqpendingword']).code).toBe(0);
  }, 120_000);

  it('a completed backfill re-opened by a tick that could not index answers 7 until a tick with FTS completes it', () => {
    const T = 0x23;
    const box = rH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-grep-reopen-');
    const file = GRX.seed(box, T, GRX.idA, 'demo', [GRX.user(T, 1, 'zqfirstword indexed at once')]);
    expect(GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqfirstword']).code).toBe(0);
    rFs.appendFileSync(file, rFx.jsonl([GRX.user(T, 2, 'zqlateword while the probe fails')]));
    rH.spoolLine(box, GRX.idA, { v: 1, ev: 'Stop', id: GRX.idA });
    const s = rH.runSweep(box, [], { preloads: [rH.PRELOADS.faults], env: { HISTORY_TEST_FTS_PROBE: 'throw' } });
    expect(s.code, s.stderr).toBe(0);
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {   // CONTROL: the table exists, the first word IS indexed, and the backfill row is open
      expect((db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM blobs_fts WHERE blobs_fts MATCH ?').get('zqfirstword') as { n: number }).n).toBe(1);
      expect((db.prepare("SELECT completed_ms AS c FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'fts' AND version = 1").get() as { c: number | null }).c).toBeNull();
    } finally { db.close(); }
    const pending = GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqfirstword', '--json']);
    expect([pending.code, pending.json?.reason]).toEqual([7, 'fts-pending']);
    expect(rH.runSweep(box).code).toBe(0);
    expect(GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqlateword']).code).toBe(0);
  }, 120_000);
});

describe('recall echoes are indexed by both paths, each pinned alone: inline at ingest, and by the backfill (W1-B2 task 12)', () => {
  beforeEach((ctx) => { if (process.platform === 'darwin') ctx.skip(); });
  /** An earlier recall and its output, appended in ONE write, so the tool_result meets its tool_use in one tick and is
   *  classed recall-echo by structure. */
  const echoPair = (tag: number, i: number): rFx.Row[] => [
    GRX.toolUse(tag, i, `toolu_g${tag.toString(16)}late`, '"$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc" history grep zq'),
    GRX.toolResult(tag, i + 1, `toolu_g${tag.toString(16)}late`, 'zqlateecho earlier recall output'),
  ];
  /** derivation ('fts', 1)'s completed_ms: null while the backfill is open. */
  const fts1 = (box: rH.HistoryBox): number | null => {
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      return (db.prepare("SELECT completed_ms AS c FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'fts' AND version = 1").get() as { c: number | null }).c;
    } finally { db.close(); }
  };
  /** A row's provenance and its first body's fts_indexed mark. */
  const echoRow = (box: rH.HistoryBox, uuid: string): { provenance: string; fts_indexed: number } | undefined => {
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      return db.prepare(`SELECT e.provenance AS provenance, b.fts_indexed AS fts_indexed FROM entries e
        JOIN blobs b ON b.blob_id = e.blob_id WHERE e.uuid = ?`).get(uuid) as { provenance: string; fts_indexed: number } | undefined;
    } finally { db.close(); }
  };

  it('inline: an echo appended after the backfill completed is indexed by the tick that ingests it', () => {
    const T = 0x24;
    const box = rH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-grep-echo-inline-');
    const file = GRX.seed(box, T, GRX.idA, 'demo', [GRX.user(T, 1, 'zqplainword before the echo')]);
    expect(fts1(box), 'CONTROL: the seed completed the backfill').not.toBeNull();
    rFs.appendFileSync(file, rFx.jsonl(echoPair(T, 2)));
    rH.spoolLine(box, GRX.idA, { v: 1, ev: 'Stop', id: GRX.idA });
    const s = rH.runSweep(box);
    expect(s.code, s.stderr).toBe(0);
    // CONTROL: captured as an echo, and the backfill never re-opened (resetFtsPending runs only on a tick that could not
    // index), so the inline index is the only writer that can have indexed it.
    expect(echoRow(box, GRX.uuid(T, 3))?.provenance).toBe('recall-echo');
    expect(fts1(box)).not.toBeNull();
    expect(GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqlateecho']).code).toBe(3);
    const r = GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqlateecho', '--include-recall', '--json']);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(GRX.uuids(r)).toEqual([GRX.uuid(T, 3)]);
  }, 120_000);

  it('backfill: an echo ingested by a tick that could not index is indexed by the next tick\'s backfill', () => {
    const T = 0x25;
    const box = rH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-grep-echo-backfill-');
    const file = GRX.seed(box, T, GRX.idA, 'demo', [GRX.user(T, 1, 'zqplainword before the echo')]);
    rFs.appendFileSync(file, rFx.jsonl(echoPair(T, 2)));
    rH.spoolLine(box, GRX.idA, { v: 1, ev: 'Stop', id: GRX.idA });
    const s = rH.runSweep(box, [], { preloads: [rH.PRELOADS.faults], env: { HISTORY_TEST_FTS_PROBE: 'throw' } });
    expect(s.code, s.stderr).toBe(0);
    // CONTROL: captured as an echo, NOT indexed (that tick could not), and the backfill re-opened: only the next tick's
    // backfill can index it, since its inline chance has passed.
    expect(echoRow(box, GRX.uuid(T, 3))).toEqual({ provenance: 'recall-echo', fts_indexed: 0 });
    expect(fts1(box)).toBeNull();
    const again = rH.runSweep(box);
    expect(again.code, again.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(fts1(box), 'CONTROL: the backfill completed').not.toBeNull();
    expect(GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqlateecho']).code).toBe(3);
    const r = GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqlateecho', '--include-recall', '--json']);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(GRX.uuids(r)).toEqual([GRX.uuid(T, 3)]);
  }, 120_000);
});

describe('C27 and DM46: the scope join runs before the LIMIT; another project\'s transcript is never in scope (W1-B2 task 12)', () => {
  beforeEach((ctx) => { if (process.platform === 'darwin') ctx.skip(); });
  const TA = 0x27; const TB = 0x28; const TO = 0x29;
  let box: rH.HistoryBox;
  beforeAll(() => {
    if (process.platform === 'darwin') return;
    box = rH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-grep-scope-');
    // A: one old hit in a long sentence. B (same project, another family): 3,000 newer short rows that each say the
    // word three times, so every one of them outranks A's hit on BM25 and on recency.
    GRX.seed(box, TA, GRX.idA, 'demo', [GRX.user(TA, 1, 'an older note with a single zqneedle among many other plain words here')]);
    GRX.seed(box, TB, GRX.idB, 'demo',
      Array.from({ length: 3000 }, (_, i) => GRX.user(TB, 100 + i, `zqneedle zqneedle zqneedle n${i}`)), 'claude-b');
    // O: another project's family, its own words.
    GRX.seed(box, TO, GRX.idO, 'other',
      [GRX.user(TO, 1, 'zqforeignword lives in the other project', { cwd: '/home/u/worktrees/other/x' })], 'claude-b');
    // A planted clear line in A's spool naming O's transcript (DM46): the first claim (O's, confirmed) stands.
    rH.spoolLine(box, GRX.idA, { v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id: GRX.idA, sid: GRX.file(TO), src: 'clear' });
    for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) { const s = rH.runSweep(box); expect(s.code, s.stderr).toBe(0); }
  }, 240_000);

  it('C27: 3,000 other-family blobs outrank one family hit, and the hit is still returned (exit 0, true count 1)', () => {
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {   // CONTROL: globally, A's blob is outside the top RANK_POOL on rank
      const aBlob = (db.prepare('SELECT blob_id AS b FROM entries WHERE uuid = ?').get(GRX.uuid(TA, 1)) as { b: number }).b;
      const top = (db.prepare('SELECT rowid AS r FROM blobs_fts WHERE blobs_fts MATCH ? ORDER BY rank LIMIT 2000').all('zqneedle') as unknown as
        Array<{ r: number }>).map((x) => x.r);
      expect(top).toHaveLength(2000);
      expect(top).not.toContain(aBlob);
    } finally { db.close(); }
    for (const sort of ['relevance', 'recency', 'hybrid']) {
      const r = GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqneedle', '--sort', sort, '--json']);
      expect(r.code, `${sort}: ${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
      expect(GRX.uuids(r), sort).toEqual([GRX.uuid(TA, 1)]);
      expect(r.json?.total, sort).toBe(1);
    }
  }, 120_000);

  it('DM46 (CLI half): a planted clear line naming another project\'s transcript leaves its text out of the family: default grep is 3', () => {
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {   // CONTROL: the text is stored and indexed; only the scope keeps it out
      expect((db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM blobs_fts WHERE blobs_fts MATCH ?').get('zqforeignword') as { n: number }).n).toBe(1);
    } finally { db.close(); }
    expect(GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqforeignword']).code).toBe(3);
    expect(GRX.cli(box, GRX.idO, ['grep', 'zqforeignword']).code).toBe(0);
  }, 60_000);

  it('DM46 (node half, review focus 4): the second claim chains no epoch, so none of that transcript\'s nodes can enter the family', () => {
    // A node's family is its epoch's (Tasks 8 and 9 take session_pk and epoch_seq from the epoch that holds the
    // transcript), so a uuid the first family keeps is never a node of the second.
    const db = rH.openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      const count = (sql: string): number => (db.prepare(sql).get(GRX.idA, GRX.file(TO)) as { n: number }).n;
      expect(count(`SELECT count(*) AS n FROM epochs e JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = e.session_pk
        WHERE s.ccrc_id = ? AND e.cc_session_uuid = ?`), 'no epoch of A names O\'s transcript').toBe(0);
      expect(count(`SELECT count(*) AS n FROM nodes n JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = n.session_pk
        JOIN transcripts t ON t.transcript_pk = n.transcript_pk WHERE s.ccrc_id = ? AND t.cc_session_uuid = ?`),
      'no node of A sits on O\'s transcript').toBe(0);
    } finally { db.close(); }
    const r = GRX.cli(box, GRX.idA, ['grep', 'zqneedle', '--json']);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect((r.json?.scope as { transcripts: number }).transcripts, 'A\'s scope holds its own transcript only').toBe(1);
  }, 60_000);
});
```
