- from `./store.mjs`: `childrenOf` and `parentOf`.

Append to the END of `ccd/history/recall.mjs`:

```js
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// describe (spec §8.4, §8.2, §8.3; W1-B2 Task 15). One node, resolved INSIDE the scope from a full id, a display
// prefix or a pasted card line (§11 P28, lib's extractNodeId). It prints:
//  - the node's kind, depth, status, time range, producing model family (§6.2) and parent;
//  - its gist, topics, refs and files;
//  - each child (a condensed node) or source (a leaf) as one line with chars= and fits=in|over (§11 P13: costs
//    in characters, against the output cap);
//  - for a leaf with a summary, the summary's first DESCRIBE_EXCERPT characters, with --full paging the rest by a
//    cursor bound to the node.
// Every recalled field is redacted first, then cut, then enveloped (history-redaction-before-cut). The summary is
// read RAW, and the excerpt and each --full page are redacted as windows with ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN each side (lib's
// redactDisplayWindow; spec §8.3 and §8.4), never the whole summary. A flagged gist is printed
// unchanged: the flag only marks it (§7.4 item 9).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** The nodes columns describe reads, named through selectColumns. */
const DESCRIBE_NODE_COLS = Object.freeze(['node_id', 'session_pk', 'transcript_pk', 'kind', 'depth', 'status', 'gist', 'topics',
  'summary_blob_id', 'boundary_entry_id', 'earliest_ms', 'latest_ms', 'src_chars', 'desc_count', 'desc_chars',
  'directive_flag', 'capped']);
/** Room a --full page keeps for its own label line and the envelope's tag. */
const PAGE_FRAME = 300;
/** The hint a refused describe cursor carries. */
const DESCRIBE_STALE_CURSOR = 'that --cursor pages another node, or ran past its summary; describe the node again with --full';

function nodeRow(rc, id) {
  return rc.db.prepare(`SELECT ${selectColumns(rc.version, 'nodes', DESCRIBE_NODE_COLS, rc.schema)} FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?`).get(id);
}

/** nodes.topics as a list: the JSON array derivation writes, or, for a value that is not one, its lines. */
function topicsOf(text) {
  if (text === null || text === undefined || text === '') return [];
  try {
    const v = JSON.parse(text);
    if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.filter((t) => typeof t === 'string');
  } catch { /* not JSON: one topic per line */ }
  return String(text).split('\n').filter((t) => t.trim() !== '');
}

function refsOf(rc, id) {
  return rc.db.prepare(`SELECT ${selectColumns(rc.version, 'node_refs', ['kind', 'value', 'origin'], rc.schema)} FROM node_refs
    WHERE node_id = ? ORDER BY kind, value`).all(id);
}

/** A leaf's sources in order, each with its blob's raw length. */
function sourcesOf(rc, id) {
  return rc.db.prepare(`SELECT e.uuid AS uuid, e.type AS type, e.role AS role, b.raw_len AS raw_len
      FROM ${versioned(rc, 'node_sources', 'ns', ['node_id', 'entry_id', 'ord'])}
        JOIN ${versioned(rc, 'entries', 'e', ['entry_id', 'uuid', 'type', 'role', 'blob_id'])} ON e.entry_id = ns.entry_id
        JOIN ${versioned(rc, 'blobs', 'b', ['blob_id', 'raw_len'])} ON b.blob_id = e.blob_id
      WHERE ns.node_id = ? ORDER BY ns.ord`).all(id);
}

/** A condensed node's children in order (Task 9's node_children, parent → children). */
function childRowsOf(rc, id) {
  const st = rc.db.prepare(`SELECT ${selectColumns(rc.version, 'nodes', DESCRIBE_NODE_COLS, rc.schema)} FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?`);
  return childrenOf(rc.db, id).slice().sort((x, y) => x.ord - y.ord).map((c) => st.get(c.childId)).filter((r) => r !== undefined);
}

/** The line of a leaf's summary row in its holding copy `at` ({ file_id, line: the boundary's }), picked as lib's
 *  summaryRowFor picks it for derivation (Task 8): the row the boundary's anchor_uuid names; when the anchor is the
 *  boundary itself, the first compact summary after the boundary. A `<local-command-stdout>` echo (a harness user row,
 *  summaryRowFor's isEcho) is never the pick. null for no pick: the producer is then counted after the boundary, as
 *  derivation counts it. Spelled in SQL so a describe never loads the whole copy. */
function summaryLine(rc, boundaryEntryId, at) {
  const bd = rc.db.prepare(`SELECT b.anchor_uuid AS anchor_uuid, e.uuid AS uuid
      FROM ${versioned(rc, 'boundaries', 'b', ['entry_id', 'anchor_uuid'])}
        JOIN ${versioned(rc, 'entries', 'e', ['entry_id', 'uuid'])} ON e.entry_id = b.entry_id
      WHERE b.entry_id = ?`).get(boundaryEntryId);
  if (bd === undefined || typeof bd.anchor_uuid !== 'string' || bd.anchor_uuid === '') return null;
  const inCopy = `FROM ${versioned(rc, 'memberships', 'mb', ['file_id', 'entry_id', 'line'])}
        JOIN ${versioned(rc, 'entries', 'e', ['entry_id', 'uuid', 'type', 'provenance', 'is_compact_summary'])} ON e.entry_id = mb.entry_id
      WHERE mb.file_id = ? AND NOT (e.type = 'user' AND e.provenance = 'harness')`;
  const hit = bd.anchor_uuid === bd.uuid
    ? rc.db.prepare(`SELECT mb.line AS line ${inCopy} AND mb.line > ? AND e.is_compact_summary = 1 ORDER BY mb.line LIMIT 1`)
      .get(at.file_id, at.line)
    : rc.db.prepare(`SELECT mb.line AS line ${inCopy} AND e.uuid = ?`).get(at.file_id, bd.anchor_uuid);
  return hit === undefined ? null : hit.line;
}

/** The producing model family of a leaf's span (§6.2, §8.3), derived as Task 8's leafFields derives it:
 *  - the copy: lib's pickHoldingCopy over the files of the node's transcript, the rule Task 8's holdingCopy decides
 *    by (among the files that hold the boundary, a live copy, source_key '', first, then the lowest file_id);
 *  - the witnesses: every assistant row after the summary pick (summaryLine), else after the boundary, to the end of
 *    the copy, in file order. B1's producerOf answers at the first whose backend is not `unknown`, so the lazy
 *    iterate() behind `models` reads only as far as that row. No row cap: a first real reply far past the summary
 *    still counts, as it does for derivation.
 *  memberships is reached by its primary key (file_id, entry_id) and its memberships_order (file_id, line) index; it
 *  has no entry_id index, deliberately. */
function producerOfLeaf(rc, n) {
  if (n.boundary_entry_id === null || n.transcript_pk === null) return 'unknown';
  const copies = rc.db.prepare(`SELECT f.file_id AS file_id, f.source_key AS source_key, mb.line AS line
      FROM ${versioned(rc, 'ingest_files', 'f', ['file_id', 'transcript_pk', 'source_key'])}
        LEFT JOIN ${versioned(rc, 'memberships', 'mb', ['file_id', 'entry_id', 'line'])} ON mb.file_id = f.file_id AND mb.entry_id = ?
      WHERE f.transcript_pk = ? ORDER BY f.file_id`)
    .all(n.boundary_entry_id, n.transcript_pk);
  const held = pickHoldingCopy(copies.map((c) => ({ fileId: Number(c.file_id), live: c.source_key === '', holds: c.line !== null })));
  if (held === null) return 'unknown';
  const at = copies.find((c) => Number(c.file_id) === held);
  const from = summaryLine(rc, n.boundary_entry_id, at) ?? at.line;
  const after = rc.db.prepare(`SELECT e.model AS model
      FROM ${versioned(rc, 'memberships', 'mb', ['file_id', 'entry_id', 'line'])}
        JOIN ${versioned(rc, 'entries', 'e', ['entry_id', 'type', 'model'])} ON e.entry_id = mb.entry_id
      WHERE mb.file_id = ? AND mb.line > ? AND e.type = 'assistant' ORDER BY mb.line`);
  function* models() {
    for (const r of after.iterate(at.file_id, from)) yield r.model;
  }
  return producerOf(models());
}

/** A condensed node's producer is its newest leaf's: down each level's last child. */
function producerOfNode(rc, n) {
  let cur = n;
  for (let hops = 0; cur !== undefined && cur.depth > 0 && hops < 16; hops += 1) {
    const kids = childrenOf(rc.db, cur.node_id);
    if (kids.length === 0) return 'unknown';
    cur = nodeRow(rc, kids.reduce((x, y) => (y.ord > x.ord ? y : x)).childId);
  }
  return cur === undefined || cur.depth > 0 ? 'unknown' : producerOfLeaf(rc, cur);
}

/** A node's native summary as RAW plain text, or null for a node with none (a raw leaf, a condensed node). It is
 *  never shown as it is: the excerpt and each --full page are redactDisplayWindow's windows of it, so describe's
 *  cost is a window's, whatever the summary's length (spec §8.3 and §8.4). */
function summaryOf(rc, n) {
  if (n.summary_blob_id === null) return null;
  const b = rc.db.prepare(`SELECT ${selectColumns(rc.version, 'blobs', ['z', 'raw_len'], rc.schema)} FROM blobs WHERE blob_id = ?`).get(n.summary_blob_id);
  if (b === undefined || b.z === null) return null;
  return blobPlainText(b.z, false, rc.pairIdx, Number(b.raw_len));
}

/** `end`, moved off the middle of a surrogate pair: when the character at `end` is a pair's low half, back one, or,
 *  when that would leave nothing after `start`, forward one. So a page or an excerpt never ends with half an astral
 *  character, which human output would print as U+FFFD. */
function pairSafeEnd(text, start, end) {
  if (end <= start || end >= text.length) return end;
  const c = text.charCodeAt(end);
  if (c < 0xdc00 || c > 0xdfff) return end;
  return end - 1 > start ? end - 1 : end + 1;
}

/** What `text[k]` prints at most, escaped for the envelope (escapeXmlText: `&` 5 characters, `<` and `>` 4) or
 *  JSON-encoded (JSON.stringify: `"` and `\` 2, a control character 2 or 6, a surrogate half without its pair 6). A
 *  redaction, a decode and a removed sequence never print longer than the raw characters they came from, except a
 *  mark longer than what it replaced. */
function describeCharCost(text, k, json) {
  const c = text.charCodeAt(k);
  if (!json) return c === 0x26 ? 5 : c === 0x3c || c === 0x3e ? 4 : 1;
  if (c === 0x22 || c === 0x5c) return 2;
  if (c < 0x20) return c === 0x08 || c === 0x09 || c === 0x0a || c === 0x0c || c === 0x0d ? 2 : 6;
  if (c >= 0xd800 && c <= 0xdbff) {
    const n = text.charCodeAt(k + 1);
    return n >= 0xdc00 && n <= 0xdfff ? 1 : 6;
  }
  if (c >= 0xdc00 && c <= 0xdfff) {
    const p = text.charCodeAt(k - 1);
    return p >= 0xd800 && p <= 0xdbff ? 1 : 6;
  }
  return 1;
}

/** The --full page that starts at `off`, and its shown window: as much of the RAW `text` as fits `room` once shown
 *  (`show(off, end)`, redactDisplayWindow's) and printed, either escaped for the envelope or JSON-encoded. The raw end
 *  is sized in one pass by what each raw character prints (describeCharCost), so ONE window is redacted per page
 *  (finding V19: a shrink step that redacted the window again each time cost a page 18 windows). Only a mark longer
 *  than what it replaced, a cut that keeps an edge's mark or slack, or an inexact window's note line prints past the
 *  room; the page then halves and is redacted again, as expand's page does. The end never splits a surrogate pair, and
 *  at least one character (or one pair) is always paged. Named apart from Task 16's lib pageEnd, which pages expand's
 *  text by its own cost rule. */
function describePageEnd(text, off, room, json, show) {
  const printed = (s) => (json ? JSON.stringify(s).length : escapeXmlText(s).length);
  const limit = Math.max(1, room - (json ? 2 : 0));
  let end = off;
  for (let used = 0; end < text.length; end += 1) {
    const c = describeCharCost(text, end, json);
    if (used + c > limit) break;
    used += c;
  }
  end = pairSafeEnd(text, off, Math.max(end, off + 1));
  let page = show(off, end);
  while (end > off + 1 && printed(page) > room) {
    const shorter = pairSafeEnd(text, off, off + Math.max(1, (end - off) >> 1));
    if (shorter >= end) break;
    end = shorter;
    page = show(off, end);
  }
  return { end, page };
}

/** `describe <id | prefix | pasted line>` (§8.4). */
export function runDescribe(rc, a, deps = {}) {
  const budget = (deps.cap ?? OUTPUT_CAP) - FRAME_RESERVE;
  const ex = extractNodeId(a.target);
  if (!ex.ok) return refusal('bad-args', hintLine(redactField(`${ex.error}${ex.hint ? ` ${ex.hint}` : ''}`, rc.pairIdx)));
  const found = resolveNodeInScope(rc, ex.id);
  if (!found.ok) return found.result;
  const id = found.id;
  const n = nodeRow(rc, id);
  if (n === undefined) return notFound();
  const pre = scopePrefixes(rc);
  const disp = (x) => pre.get(x) ?? x;
  const parent = parentOf(rc.db, id);
  const producer = producerOfNode(rc, n);
  const summary = summaryOf(rc, n);
  /** A window of the raw summary as shown: redacted with its margins, never the whole summary first. */
  const shownSummary = (from, to) => redactDisplayWindow(summary, from, to, rc.pairIdx);
  const env = (src, text) => recallEnvelope({ src, id: disp(id), ts: n.latest_ms, role: null, text });
  const nodeLine = `node ${disp(id)} ${n.kind} depth ${n.depth} status ${n.status} ${iso(n.earliest_ms)} → ${iso(n.latest_ms)} producer ${producer}`
    + `${n.directive_flag === 1 ? ' directive-flag' : ''}${n.capped === 1 ? ' capped' : ''}`;
  const base = {
    node_id: id, kind: n.kind, depth: n.depth, status: n.status, parent_id: parent,
    earliest_ms: n.earliest_ms, latest_ms: n.latest_ms, producer,
  };
  const tailArgs = [...scopeArgs(rc), ...(a.json ? ['--json'] : [])];

  if (a.full) {
    if (summary === null) return refusal('bad-args', `${disp(id)} has no summary to page; describe it without --full`);
    let off = 0;
    if (a.cursor !== null) {
      const c = decodeCursor(a.cursor, 'describe');
      if (c === null || c.node !== id || !Number.isSafeInteger(c.off) || c.off < 0 || c.off >= summary.length) {
        return refusal('bad-args', DESCRIBE_STALE_CURSOR);
      }
      off = c.off;
    }
    const { end, page } = describePageEnd(summary, off, budget - nodeLine.length - PAGE_FRAME, a.json, shownSummary);
    return {
      exit: EXIT.OK, header: null,
      blocks: [nodeLine, `summary, characters ${off + 1} to ${end} of ${summary.length}:`, env('summary', page)],
      items: [{ ...base, summary_chars: summary.length, summary_page: { offset: off, text: page }, trust: 'untrusted' }],
      shown: 1, total: 1,
      next: end < summary.length
        ? ['describe', id, '--full', ...tailArgs, '--cursor', encodeCursor({ v: 1, resource: 'describe', node: id, off: end })]
        : null,
    };
  }

  const gist = n.gist === null ? null : redactField(n.gist, rc.pairIdx);
  const topics = topicsOf(n.topics).map((t) => redactField(t, rc.pairIdx));
  const refs = refsOf(rc, id).map((r) => ({ kind: r.kind, value: redactField(r.value, rc.pairIdx), origin: r.origin }));
  const files = refs.filter((r) => r.kind === 'path').map((r) => r.value);
  const excerptEnd = summary === null ? 0 : Math.min(summary.length, pairSafeEnd(summary, 0, DESCRIBE_EXCERPT));
  const excerpt = summary === null ? null : shownSummary(0, excerptEnd);
  const head = [
    nodeLine,
    ...(parent === null ? [] : [`parent ${disp(parent)}`]),
    ...(gist === null ? [] : [`gist ${env('node', gist)}`]),
    ...(topics.length === 0 ? [] : [`topics ${env('node', topics.join(' · '))}`]),
    ...(refs.length === 0 ? [] : [`refs ${env('node', refs.map((r) => `${r.kind} ${r.value}`).join(' · '))}`]),
    ...(files.length === 0 ? [] : [`files ${env('node', files.join(' · '))}`]),
  ];
  const tail = excerpt === null ? [] : [`summary, the first ${excerptEnd} of ${summary.length} characters:`, env('summary', excerpt)];
  const label = n.depth > 0 ? 'children' : 'sources';
  const listed = n.depth > 0
    ? childRowsOf(rc, id).map((k) => {
      const c = costRow(Number((k.depth === 0 ? k.src_chars : k.desc_chars) ?? 0));
      return { line: `  ${disp(k.node_id)} ${k.kind} chars=${c.chars} fits=${c.fits}`, item: { id: k.node_id, kind: k.kind, chars: c.chars, fits: c.fits } };
    })
    : sourcesOf(rc, id).map((s) => {
      const c = costRow(Number(s.raw_len ?? 0));
      return { line: `  ${s.uuid} ${s.type} ${s.role ?? '-'} chars=${c.chars} fits=${c.fits}`, item: { uuid: s.uuid, type: s.type, role: s.role, chars: c.chars, fits: c.fits } };
    });
  const itemOf = (k) => ({
    ...base, gist, topics, refs, files, directive_flag: n.directive_flag, capped: n.capped,
    [label]: listed.slice(0, k).map((x) => x.item), [`${label}_total`]: listed.length,
    ...(excerpt === null ? {} : { summary_excerpt: excerpt, summary_chars: summary.length }),
    trust: 'untrusted',
  });
  const blocksOf = (k) => [...head, `${label} (${k} of ${listed.length} listed):`, ...listed.slice(0, k).map((x) => x.line), ...tail];
  // The fixed parts first, then as many child or source lines as still fit: a running total, so a leaf of thousands
  // of rows costs one pass.
  const each = listed.map((x) => (a.json ? JSON.stringify(x.item).length + 1 : x.line.length + 1));
  let used = a.json ? JSON.stringify(itemOf(0)).length : blocksOf(0).join('\n').length;
  let k = 0;
  while (k < listed.length && used + each[k] <= budget) { used += each[k]; k += 1; }
  return {
    exit: EXIT.OK, header: null, blocks: blocksOf(k), items: [itemOf(k)], shown: 1, total: 1,
    next: excerpt !== null && excerptEnd < summary.length ? ['describe', id, '--full', ...tailArgs] : null,
  };
}
```

  - `export function renderEntryText(body: unknown): string`: a row's RAW text as expand prints it. It redacts nothing; recall.mjs shows each window of it through `redactDisplayWindow`, whose escape readings separate a value JSON rendering glued an escape letter onto, in a string leaf or in an object KEY (review finding R38).
  - `export const EXPLORE_READ_MAX: number` (256 KiB of characters, *chosen*) and `export function exploreOutline(text: string, kind: ExploreKind, fileName: string | undefined, idx: PairIndex): string`: a cut item's outline, explored over `redactDisplayWindow`'s window of the whole text when the text is at most `EXPLORE_READ_MAX` long, and counts only (characters and lines, no content) past it.
- Produces, in recall.mjs:
  - `export function runExpand(rc: ReadContext, a: ExpandArgs & { json: boolean }): VerbResult`
  - `export function expandVerb(rc: ReadContext, parsed: { positional: readonly string[]; opts: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> }): VerbResult`. This is cli.mjs's `READ_RUNNERS.expand`. It takes `parseReadArgs`' answer.
  - The VerbResult's `shown` is the cumulative position of the last item reached. The `--json` item shape is `{ kind: 'entry' | 'sidecar', uuid, name?, type, role, ts_ms, provenance, text, from, to, of, cut, outline, outline_kind, variants: { cause }[], pruned_ms, undecodable?: true, sidecars?: { name }[], trust: 'untrusted' }`. `of` is the text's length in characters, except for a blob too large to expand, where it is the blob's recorded `raw_len` in bytes and `text` is empty. `undecodable: true` appears only on an item whose stored blob does not decode (its `text` is empty and `pruned_ms` null), so it is never read as a pruned one.

**Spec:**
- Sections: §8.4 `expand`; §6.1 (variants: "`expand` shows the unsanitised body"); §6.6 and §2 (pruned text); §8.2 ("Every verb resolves ids inside the scope"); §8.3 (Envelope, Redaction "on each field, before any cut or escape", Cap); §11 P17.
- Pins: C10, C11, C13, C29, DM2b (CLI half), DM29 (its `expand` half: expand pages reach past both windows, and a sidecar past `SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX` is never decompressed; Task 14 carries the grep half, both forms).
- Review focus 3 is owned here: multi-MiB items, a sidecar near SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX, timing, RSS, and a secret straddling a page.
- Departures:
  - B1's D-4240 (`history-sidecars-ingested`), B1's D-4200 (`history-variant-cause`), B1's D-4202 (`history-redaction-before-cut`), D-4678 (`history-scope-on-every-verb`).
  - D-4715 (`history-expand-message-id`) (NEW): a cut tool output needs a way to read the rest. A message uuid therefore expands that one row whole, with its sidecars, paged by cursor. DM29's text past the FTS window is read this way.
- Not a departure since spec rev 3.5: the windowed display (spec §8.3 and §8.4, as Task 12 implements it): an item's text is read raw, and every window of it expand shows is redacted with `ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN` each side, never the whole item first (review findings R36 and R38). An outline past `EXPLORE_READ_MAX` is counts only, since §11 P17's explorers would otherwise need the whole item redacted.

Choices this task makes (each listed in the PR's open questions):
- **Page cost.** A page is measured in `textCost`: each UTF-16 unit counts at its longest escaped form, XML or JSON. One page budget (`PAGE_TEXT_BUDGET` = 18,000) therefore fits the 20,000-character cap in the human form and in `--json` alike, and a cursor's offsets mean the same in both forms. The 2,000 left over covers the header, the shown, next and hint lines and the item lines, and the `--json` envelope's keys. That holds under `--project` too only because Task 11's `scopeJson` bounds its `families` list (`SCOPE_FAMILIES_JSON_MAX`, with `families_total`), so the envelope's scope object costs the same at 40 families as at one. The 40-family case below measures it on a full expand page and a full grep page.
- **What one call decompresses.** A blob whose `raw_len` passes `SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX` (64 MiB) is never decompressed by expand. Its item prints one fixed line, `content too large to expand here: <n> bytes …`, with `cut` true, an empty `text` and `of` = its byte size, and exit 0. B1 captures a larger sidecar by streaming it into one blob; decompressed whole, it would pass the 1 GiB RSS bound the scale case measures at 64 MiB, and past ~512 MiB Node's string limit would make the call exit 1. The decision is lib's `expandBlobFits`; the bound is read from `blobs.raw_len` before `z` is loaded. What keeps a 64 MiB item under that bound is that only the shown window is redacted (next bullet): redacted whole, one page of the scale case's sidecar peaked at 1,954 MiB (review finding R36, measured with Task 7A's belt on B1's lib). Windowed, the prototype (B1's `lib.mjs` with Tasks 7A's `redactForDisplay` and 12's `redactDisplayWindow` copied in, no belt layer, Node 24.14.1) measured one middle page of that sidecar at 201,720 KiB peak RSS and 438 ms with decoding, and of a 64 MiB ESC- and backslash-dense one at 372,756 KiB and 1,088 ms.
- **Every shown window is redacted, not the item** (spec §8.3 and §8.4; coordinator ruling R-display-window). `renderEntryText` renders a row's RAW text and `expandSidecarText` decodes a sidecar's; every offset (`from`, `to`, `of`, the cursor's `o`) counts characters of that raw text. A page is `redactDisplayWindow(raw, from, to)`: the window plus `ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN` each side read as one text through `redactForDisplay`'s reading, then the window cut from that reading, so a value straddling a page edge is matched whole and only its whole mark shows (a mark straddling a page edge may show on both pages). A cut Task 12 cannot show exact comes back inexact: `DISPLAY_INEXACT_NOTE`'s line, then the page alone with every run of 8 or more characters masked; its cost is still measured on what it prints, so the shrink loop below holds it too. An outline's input (a window of the whole item) has no margin and is always exact. A page's cost is still measured on what it prints: a window whose redacted text costs more than the budget (a mark longer than what it replaced) is shortened until it fits. A `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` run longer than the margin is dropped where a page edge cuts it, so such a run prints on no page (B1's cut rule; it is past what redaction can read whole).
- **An outline reads at most `EXPLORE_READ_MAX`** (256 KiB of characters, *chosen*). Up to it, the explorer reads `redactDisplayWindow`'s window of the whole item; past it, the outline is counts only (characters and lines, measured on the raw text, which carry no content). A JSON output past `EXPLORE_JSON_MAX` was counts only already. A message body holds B1's tighter body rules instead: one whose `raw_len` passes BLOB_DECODE_MAX (B1's `blobOverDecodeCap`; only a raw-only line-too-long blob can) prints the same too-large line and is not decompressed, a body is parsed only within B1's structure bound (`jsonWithinStructureBound`; past it the item shows the body's text as stored, never a parse), and every decode is bounded by its `raw_len` (`unbrotli(z, rawLen)`). A blob that does not decode prints its own fixed line, `content does not decode: …`, with `undecodable: true` on its `--json` item, never a throw and never the pruned placeholder: a damaged blob is not a pruned one.
- **Node ids resolve through Task 12's `resolveNodeInScope`.** It is the one spelling of §8.2's prefix-in-scope rule for grep `--node`, describe and expand alike; an ambiguous prefix's hint is that function's.
- **Cut items.** A cut item has two halves, its first `EXPLORE_CUT` characters and its outline. Each half is also held under `CUT_TEXT_BUDGET` (8,000), so a cut item always fits an empty page, even when a pathological `&`-only output escapes to five times its length. Both halves are cut after they are redacted: the first half is `redactDisplayWindow` of the raw window `cutText` picks, cut by `cutText` again; the outline is `exploreOutline`'s, cut by `cutText`.
- **Where a page breaks.** A whole item that does not fit starts as a partial when it is the page's first item, or when at least `EXPAND_MIN_PARTIAL` (4,000) of the page's budget is left. Otherwise it waits to be first on the next page. A message expansion's big sidecar therefore starts on the same page as its short row.
- **`--before`/`--after` without `--around` are ignored**, not refused. Task 10's `parseReadArgs` holds no record of which options were given, so a default cannot be told from an explicit value.
- **A bare `expand --cursor <c>` resumes the expansion its cursor names.** Task 10's grammar admits it, and the cursor carries its target key (`expandResumeOf`).
- **Which items are cut.** In a node or `--around` expansion, a tool output (provenance `tool` or `recall-echo`) or a sidecar over `EXPLORE_CUT` is cut. Every other row, and every item of a message expansion, is whole and paged.
- **`shown K of N`.** N counts items (entries plus their sidecars). K is the cumulative position of the last item the page reached, including a partial one.
- **The delegate hint** prints on the first page only. It estimates from `blobs.raw_len`, read by a statement that never loads `z`, with a cut item counted as at most twice `EXPLORE_CUT`, so no page decompresses or even reads the whole node to decide it.
- **Sidecars** are looked up by the linked entry's `transcript_pk` (a primary-key prefix) and filtered on `entry_id`. `sidecars` has no `entry_id` index, and a scan per item would grow with the store.
- **The scope's file rows are read in ONE statement** (`transcript_pk IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))`). `ingest_files` has no `transcript_pk` index, so a statement per in-scope transcript would scan the table once per transcript; one statement scans it once per call.
- **The tool_use pairing walk** stops at the first ancestor that holds the paired `tool_use`, whether or not it names a file (`toolUseInputPath`'s `found`), so a Bash result never decompresses the ancestors above its own call.

Append to the END of `ccd/history/lib.mjs`:

```js
// ── expand (W1-B2 Task 16) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// The decisions recall.mjs's expand delivers (spec §8.4 "expand", §8.3 "Redaction" and "Cap", §6.1 variants,
// §11 P17): what a page costs and where a page or a cut ends, which target an argument names, whether an
// entry is in scope, which items are cut, a cursor's validity, the delegate hint, a tool_result's paired path,
// the ONE rendering of a row's RAW text (every window of which recall.mjs shows through Task 12's
// redactDisplayWindow, before any cut or escape), and a cut item's outline over at most EXPLORE_READ_MAX of it.

/** What one page of expand text may cost (textCost): the cap less 2,000 for the header, the item lines, the
 *  shown and next lines and the hint (*chosen*). */
export const PAGE_TEXT_BUDGET = OUTPUT_CAP - 2000;
/** The cost ceiling of each half of a cut item (its first EXPLORE_CUT characters, its outline), so a cut item
 *  fits an empty page whatever it escapes to (*chosen*). */
export const CUT_TEXT_BUDGET = 8000;
/** The page budget left that lets a whole item which does not fit start here as a partial, when it is not the
 *  page's first item (*chosen*): below it the item waits to be first on the next page. */
export const EXPAND_MIN_PARTIAL = 4000;

/** One UTF-16 code unit's cost on a page: the longest form it escapes to. XML text turns `&` into `&amp;` and
 *  `<`/`>` into 4; JSON turns `"`, `\` and \b \f \n \r \t into 2, any other control character into 6, and a
 *  surrogate half is charged 6 too (a lone one is). So a page fits the cap in the human form and in --json
 *  alike, and a cursor's offsets mean the same in both. */
export function charCost(code) {
  if (code === 0x26) return 5;
  if (code === 0x3c || code === 0x3e) return 4;
  if (code === 0x22 || code === 0x5c) return 2;
  if (code < 0x20) return code === 0x08 || code === 0x09 || code === 0x0a || code === 0x0c || code === 0x0d ? 2 : 6;
  if (code >= 0xd800 && code <= 0xdfff) return 6;
  return 1;
}

/** The cost of text[start, end). */
export function textCost(text, start = 0, end = text.length) {
  let n = 0;
  for (let i = start; i < end; i += 1) n += charCost(text.charCodeAt(i));
  return n;
}

const isHighSurrogate = (text, k) => {
  const c = text.charCodeAt(k);
  return c >= 0xd800 && c <= 0xdbff;
};

/** Where a page of `text` that starts at `start` ends (exclusive) under `budget`. A page always moves (one
 *  character, or one surrogate pair, at least) and never splits a surrogate pair. */
export function pageEnd(text, start, budget) {
  if (start >= text.length) return text.length;
  let n = 0;
  let i = start;
  while (i < text.length) {
    const c = charCost(text.charCodeAt(i));
    if (n + c > budget) break;
    n += c;
    i += 1;
  }
  if (i === start) i = start + 1;
  if (i < text.length && isHighSurrogate(text, i - 1)) i = i - 1 > start ? i - 1 : i + 1;
  return i;
}

/** The first at most `maxChars` characters of `text` whose cost stays under `budget`, whole pairs only. */
export function cutText(text, maxChars, budget) {
  let n = Math.min(pageEnd(text, 0, budget), maxChars, text.length);
  if (n > 0 && n < text.length && isHighSurrogate(text, n - 1)) n -= 1;
  return text.slice(0, n);
}

/** A node id or its prefix (6 to 20 hex, §6.1's display minimum) — the grammar Task 12's resolveNodeInScope resolves. */
const EXPAND_NODE_RE = /^[LN][0-9a-f]{6,20}$/;
/** A raw-only row's key: B1's rawRowKey (`x` + 32 hex), the uuid an unparsable line is stored under. */
const EXPAND_RAW_RE = /^x[0-9a-f]{32}$/;

/** What an expand argument names. */
export function expandTargetOf(s) {
  if (typeof s !== 'string') return 'bad';
  if (EXPAND_NODE_RE.test(s)) return 'node';
  if (UUID_RE.test(s) || EXPAND_RAW_RE.test(s)) return 'entry';
  return 'bad';
}

/** expand's arguments from Task 10's parseReadArgs answer, whose `expand` row has checked every option's grammar:
 *  at most one target, and never a target with --around. --before/--after mean something only with --around and
 *  are ignored otherwise. Neither target nor --around leaves a bare --cursor, which names its own target. */
export function expandArgsOf(parsed) {
  const pos = parsed.positional;
  const o = parsed.opts;
  if (pos.length > 1) return { ok: false, reason: 'bad-args' };
  const target = pos.length === 1 ? pos[0] : null;
  const around = typeof o.around === 'string' ? o.around : null;
  if (target !== null && around !== null) return { ok: false, reason: 'bad-args' };
  return {
    ok: true,
    args: {
      target, around, before: Number.isSafeInteger(o.before) ? o.before : AROUND_DEFAULT,
      after: Number.isSafeInteger(o.after) ? o.after : AROUND_DEFAULT, cursor: typeof o.cursor === 'string' ? o.cursor : null,
    },
  };
}

/** What a decoded expand cursor names, for `expand --cursor <c>` given alone: its key is the target, or
 *  `around:<uuid>:<before>:<after>`. null when the key names nothing expand could resolve. */
export function expandResumeOf(cursor) {
  if (cursor === null || typeof cursor.t !== 'string') return null;
  const m = /^around:([^:]+):([0-9]{1,2}):([0-9]{1,2})$/.exec(cursor.t);
  if (m !== null) return { target: null, around: m[1], before: Number(m[2]), after: Number(m[3]) };
  return expandTargetOf(cursor.t) === 'bad' ? null : { target: cursor.t, around: null, before: AROUND_DEFAULT, after: AROUND_DEFAULT };
}

/** An entry named by uuid: outside the scope is out-of-scope, never not-found (§8.2). */
export function entryScopeVerdict({ found, inScope }) {
  if (!found) return 'not-found';
  return inScope ? 'ok' : 'out-of-scope';
}

/** Whether an item is cut to EXPLORE_CUT with an outline: a tool output or a sidecar, outside a message expansion
 *  (which shows its row whole, paged). */
export function expandCuts({ whole, kind, provenance }) {
  if (whole) return false;
  return kind === 'sidecar' || provenance === 'tool' || provenance === 'recall-echo';
}

/** A decoded expand cursor against this expansion: its key must be this target's, its item inside the list, its
 *  offset a non-negative integer. No cursor starts at the top. */
export function decideExpandCursor({ cursor, key, total }) {
  if (cursor === null) return { ok: true, i: 0, o: 0 };
  const { t, i, o } = cursor;
  if (t !== key || !Number.isSafeInteger(i) || !Number.isSafeInteger(o) || i < 0 || o < 0 || i >= total) return { ok: false };
  return { ok: true, i, o };
}

/** §8.4: more than DELEGATE_FACTOR times the cap is a `hint: delegate` line (cli.mjs prints `hint: ` before it). */
export function delegateHint(chars) {
  if (!(chars > DELEGATE_FACTOR * OUTPUT_CAP)) return null;
  return `delegate: this expansion holds about ${Math.ceil(chars / 1000)}k characters, more than ${DELEGATE_FACTOR} times `
    + `the ${OUTPUT_CAP / 1000}k cap; hand it to a subagent with the skill's delegation template`;
}

/** expand may decompress a blob of `rawLen` bytes in one call only up to SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX (*chosen*): the size the
 *  scale case measures the 1 GiB RSS bound at. B1 streams a larger sidecar into one blob; decompressed whole it
 *  would pass that bound, and past ~512 MiB Node's string limit. Such a blob prints one fixed line instead. */
export function expandBlobFits(rawLen) {
  return rawLen <= SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX;
}

/** The file a tool_use named, by its id, from an assistant row's content (P17 dispatches the outline on its
 *  extension): `file_path` (Read, Edit, Write), `notebook_path`, then `path` (Grep, Glob). `found` tells the
 *  paired tool_use that names no file (a Bash call: the walk up the chain stops there) from no paired tool_use in
 *  this content (the walk goes on): two conditions, two answers. */
export function toolUseInputPath(content, toolUseId) {
  if (!Array.isArray(content)) return { found: false };
  for (const b of content) {
    if (b === null || typeof b !== 'object' || b.type !== 'tool_use' || b.id !== toolUseId) continue;
    const input = b.input;
    if (input === null || typeof input !== 'object') return { found: true, path: null };
    for (const k of ['file_path', 'notebook_path', 'path']) if (typeof input[k] === 'string' && input[k] !== '') return { found: true, path: input[k] };
    return { found: true, path: null };
  }
  return { found: false };
}

/** A stored row's RAW text as expand prints it: text blocks, `[tool_use <name>] <input as JSON>`, a tool_result's
 *  content bare (so the outline reads the tool's own output), `[<type>]` for any other block. Nothing is redacted
 *  here (spec §8.3 and §8.4; coordinator ruling R-display-window): recall.mjs shows every window of
 *  this text through redactDisplayWindow, whose escape readings separate a value that JSON rendering glued an escape
 *  letter onto, in a string leaf or in an object KEY, which a replacer over leaves never sees (review finding R38).
 *  Redacting each leaf here instead would cost a whole 16 MiB leaf per page (R36, R37). */
export function renderEntryText(body) {
  const json = (v) => JSON.stringify(v === undefined ? null : v) ?? 'null';
  const block = (b) => {
    if (typeof b === 'string') return b;
    if (b === null || typeof b !== 'object') return String(b);
    switch (b.type) {
      case 'text': return typeof b.text === 'string' ? b.text : '';
      case 'tool_use': return `[tool_use ${typeof b.name === 'string' ? b.name : ''}] ${json(b.input)}`;
      case 'tool_result':
        if (typeof b.content === 'string') return b.content;
        return Array.isArray(b.content) ? b.content.map(block).join('\n') : json(b.content);
      default: return `[${typeof b.type === 'string' ? b.type : 'block'}]`;
    }
  };
  if (body === null || body === undefined) return '';
  if (typeof body === 'string') return body;
  if (Array.isArray(body)) return body.map(block).join('\n');
  if (typeof body === 'object') return json(body);
  return String(body);
}

/** How much of a cut item an outline reads (*chosen*: 256 Ki characters, under EXPLORE_JSON_MAX): up to it the
 *  explorer reads redactDisplayWindow's window of the whole item, past it the outline is counts only. An outline's
 *  explorers read the whole text they are given, so without the bound one cut 64 MiB sidecar would be redacted
 *  whole for its outline (spec §8.3 and §8.4). */
export const EXPLORE_READ_MAX = 256 * 1024;

/** A cut item's outline (§8.4, §11 P17): `explore` over the item's redacted window when the item is at most
 *  EXPLORE_READ_MAX characters, else Task 3's counts-only summary over the raw text (characters and lines: numbers,
 *  never content). The caller cuts the result to EXPLORE_CUT and CUT_TEXT_BUDGET. */
export function exploreOutline(text, kind, fileName, idx) {
  const t = String(text);
  if (t.length > EXPLORE_READ_MAX) return exploreCounts(stripReadPrefix(t));
  return explore(redactDisplayWindow(t, 0, t.length, idx), kind, fileName);
}
```

```ts
// ── W1-B2 Task 16: expand ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Pins C10, C11, C13, C29, DM2b (CLI half), DM29 (CLI half), and review focus 3 (scale), through the CLI as a
// session runs it: a fixture HOME, a functional fake tmux answering the family's cc- name (withPane), the statfs
// preload. Each family is seeded by real sweep ticks (seedFamily), and one more tick derives its leaf.
interface T16Item {
  kind: 'entry' | 'sidecar'; uuid: string; name?: string; type: string; role: string | null; ts_ms: number | null;
  provenance: string; text: string; from: number; to: number; of: number; cut: boolean; outline: string | null;
  outline_kind: string | null; variants: { cause: string }[]; pruned_ms: number | null; undecodable?: true; trust: string;
}
const t16items = (r: { json: Record<string, unknown> | null }): T16Item[] => (r.json?.['items'] ?? []) as T16Item[];
/** The resume cursor a page printed: its --json `next`, or the human form's last `next:` line that carries one. */
const t16cursor = (s: string): string | null => {
  const m = [...s.matchAll(/--cursor '?([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)'?/g)];
  return m.length === 0 ? null : m[m.length - 1]![1]!;
};
const t16ts = (i: number): string => new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 9, 1, 10, 0, i)).toISOString();
/** A fixture uuid: the family's 8-hex tag, then `i`. */
const t16uuid = (tag: string, i: number): string => `${tag}-0000-4000-8000-${String(i).padStart(12, '0')}`;
const t16summary = (tag: string): string => ['<summary>', '1. Primary Request and Intent:', `   ${tag} intent`,
  '8. Current Work:', `   ${tag} current work`, '9. Optional Next Step:', `   ${tag} next step`, '</summary>'].join('\n');
/** One leaf's rows: `sources`, then a manual boundary whose head is the last source and which keeps no row, then
 *  the summary row its anchor names (§6.1: leaf 1 claims every source). */
function t16leafRows(tag: string, sid: string, sources: object[]): object[] {
  const n = sources.length;
  const last = t16uuid(tag, n);
  return [
    ...sources,
    t16fx.boundaryRow({ uuid: t16uuid(tag, n + 1), ts: t16ts(n + 1), parentUuid: last, sessionId: sid, trigger: 'manual',
      headUuid: last, anchorUuid: t16uuid(tag, n + 2), tailUuid: last, allUuids: [] }),
    t16fx.summaryRow({ uuid: t16uuid(tag, n + 2), ts: t16ts(n + 2), parentUuid: t16uuid(tag, n + 1), sessionId: sid, text: t16summary(`zq${tag}`) }),
  ];
}
/** The leaf node of one family, read from the store. CONTROL: the fixture derived it. */
function t16leafOf(box: t16help.HistoryBox, id: string): string {
  const db = t16help.openStoreRO(box);
  try {
    const rows = db.prepare(`SELECT n.node_id AS node_id FROM nodes n JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = n.session_pk
      WHERE s.ccrc_id = ? AND n.kind <> 'condensed' ORDER BY n.created_ms`).all(id) as { node_id: string }[];
    expect(rows.length, `CONTROL: ${id}'s leaf was derived`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    return rows[0]!.node_id;
  } finally { db.close(); }
}
/** Seed one family, tick once more so its leaf is derived, and answer the transcript path. */
function t16seed(box: t16help.HistoryBox, f: { id: string; project: string; generation: string; uuid: string; rows: object[]; accountId?: string }): string {
  const seeded = t16help.seedFamily(box, f);
  const r = t16help.runSweep(box);
  expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
  return seeded.transcript;
}
const t16prefixed = (lines: string[]): string => lines.map((l, i) => `${String(i + 1).padStart(6)}→${l}`).join('\n');
/** A second copy of a known transcript, and a sidecar planted after its transcript was read, are found by the
 *  periodic discovery scan (SCAN_INTERVAL_MS). The run-pass driver's clock offset makes one due, as B1's DM35
 *  case does; two passes let the second ingest and link what the first found. */
function t16scan(box: t16help.HistoryBox): void {
  for (let k = 0; k < 2; k += 1) {
    const r = t16help.runDriver(box, { offsetMs: t16lib.SCAN_INTERVAL_MS + 60_000 });
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
  }
}

describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'darwin')('expand (Task 16): pages, cursors, variants, sidecars, redaction at rest', () => {
  const ID = 'claude-a-x16pg';
  const G = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-00000000c016';
  const T = 'a1600003';
  const U = t16uuid(T, 0);
  const e = (i: number): string => t16uuid(T, i);
  const BIG = `zqbig11 ${Array.from({ length: 18_000 }, (_, i) => `w${i % 97}`).join(' ')} zqbigend11`;
  let box: t16help.HistoryBox;
  let leaf = '';
  const cli = (args: string[], id = ID) => t16help.runCli(box, args, { env: t16help.withPane(box, id) });

  t16beforeAll(() => {
    box = t16help.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-x16pg-');
    t16seed(box, { id: ID, project: 'demo', generation: G, uuid: U, rows: t16leafRows(T, U, [
      t16fx.userRow({ uuid: e(1), ts: t16ts(1), sessionId: U, text: BIG }),
      t16fx.assistantRow({ uuid: e(2), ts: t16ts(2), parentUuid: e(1), sessionId: U, text: 'zqafter11 the small one after the big one' }),
    ]) });
    leaf = t16leafOf(box, ID);
  }, 240_000);

  it('C11: an oversized first item gives a partial page and a cursor; following it reads the rest exactly once; a page never passes the cap', () => {
    const human = cli(['expand', leaf]);
    expect(human.code, human.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(human.stdout.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(t16lib.OUTPUT_CAP);
    expect(human.stdout).toMatch(new RegExp(`${e(1)} \\S+ \\[chars 0-\\d+ of ${BIG.length}; continues\\]`));
    expect(human.stdout).toMatch(/^shown 1 of 2$/m);
    expect(human.stdout, 'more than 3x the cap: the first page says delegate').toMatch(/^hint: delegate: /m);
    expect(t16cursor(human.stdout)).not.toBeNull();
    const slices: string[] = [];
    let after = 0;
    let cursor: string | null = null;
    let pages = 0;
    do {
      const r = cli(['expand', leaf, ...(cursor === null ? [] : ['--cursor', cursor]), '--json']);
      expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
      expect(r.stdout.length, `page ${pages + 1}`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(t16lib.OUTPUT_CAP);
      for (const it of t16items(r)) {
        if (it.uuid === e(1)) { expect(it.from, 'each page resumes where the last one stopped').toBe(slices.join('').length); slices.push(it.text); }
        if (it.uuid === e(2)) after += 1;
      }
      cursor = t16cursor(String(r.json?.['next'] ?? ''));
      pages += 1;
    } while (cursor !== null && pages < 20);
    expect(pages, 'the big item took more than one page').toBeGreaterThan(1);
    expect(slices.join(''), 'the pages join to the text exactly').toBe(BIG);
    expect(after, 'the next item shows once, after the big one').toBe(1);
  });

  it('C11: a bare --cursor resumes the expansion it names; a cursor from another expansion, or one expand never printed, is bad-args', () => {
    const first = cli(['expand', leaf]);
    const c = t16cursor(first.stdout)!;
    const bare = cli(['expand', '--cursor', c, '--json']);
    expect(bare.code, bare.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(t16items(bare)[0]).toMatchObject({ uuid: e(1) });
    expect(t16items(bare)[0]!.from, 'it resumes past the first page').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    const wrong = cli(['expand', e(2), '--cursor', c, '--json']);
    expect([wrong.code, wrong.json?.['reason']]).toEqual([2, 'bad-args']);
    const junk = cli(['expand', leaf, '--cursor', 'zz', '--json']);
    expect([junk.code, junk.json?.['reason']]).toEqual([2, 'bad-args']);
  });

  it('DM2b: a ccd-sanitize variant pair prints the unsanitised body, and says it has a variant', () => {
    const VID = 'claude-a-x16var';
    const VT = 'a1600004';
    const VU = t16uuid(VT, 0);
    const v = (i: number): string => t16uuid(VT, i);
    const rows = (fill: string): object[] => {
      const a = t16fx.toolUseRow({ uuid: v(2), ts: t16ts(2), parentUuid: v(1), sessionId: VU, toolUseId: 'toolu_01X16VAR', name: 'Read', input: { file_path: '/home/u/tree/demo/a.md' } });
      const m = a['message'] as { content: unknown[] };
      m.content = [{ type: 'text', text: fill }, ...m.content];
      return [t16fx.userRow({ uuid: v(1), ts: t16ts(1), sessionId: VU, text: 'zqx16var question' }), a];
    };
    // The sanitised copy is ingested FIRST, so the entry's primary body is the "..." one: only pickExpandBody
    // can print the unsanitised body (the CONTROL mutant below prints the primary).
    const vbox = t16help.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-x16var-');
    const vcli = (args: string[]) => t16help.runCli(vbox, args, { env: t16help.withPane(vbox, VID) });
    const t = t16seed(vbox, { id: VID, project: 'demo', generation: '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-00000000d016', uuid: VU, rows: rows('...') });
    t16help.plantTranscript(vbox, 'claude-b', t16path.basename(t16path.dirname(t)), VU, rows(''));
    t16scan(vbox);
    const db = t16help.openStoreRO(vbox);
    try {
      const causes = (db.prepare(`SELECT v.cause AS cause FROM entry_variants v JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = v.entry_id WHERE e.uuid = ?`)
        .all(v(2)) as { cause: string }[]).map((r) => r.cause);
      expect(causes, 'CONTROL: B1 stored the pair as a ccd-sanitize variant').toEqual(['ccd-sanitize', 'ccd-sanitize']);
    } finally { db.close(); }
    const j = vcli(['expand', v(2), '--json']);
    expect(j.code, j.stderr).toBe(0);
    const item = t16items(j)[0]!;
    expect(item.text).toBe('\n[tool_use Read] {"file_path":"/home/u/tree/demo/a.md"}');
    expect(item.variants).toEqual([{ cause: 'ccd-sanitize' }]);
    expect(vcli(['expand', v(2)]).stdout).toMatch(/^variant cause=ccd-sanitize$/m);
  });

  it('C13: a token and a PEM block are redacted on output and kept verbatim at rest', () => {
    const SID = 'claude-a-x16sec';
    const ST = 'a1600005';
    const SU = t16uuid(ST, 0);
    const GHO = ['gh', 'o_', 'Zq9fixture0not0a0real0token0abcdefgh'].join('');
    const PEM = ['-----BEGIN ', 'RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\n', 'MIIZQfixture0body0line0one0abcdefghijklmnop', '\n',
      'ZQfixture0body0line0two0qrstuvwxyz0123456', '\n-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----'].join('');
    const text = `zqx16sec deploy with ${GHO} and\n${PEM}\nend`;
    t16seed(box, { id: SID, project: 'demo', generation: '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-00000000e016', uuid: SU, rows: [
      t16fx.userRow({ uuid: t16uuid(ST, 1), ts: t16ts(1), sessionId: SU, text }),
    ] });
    for (const form of [[], ['--json']]) {
      const r = cli(['expand', t16uuid(ST, 1), ...form], SID);
      expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
      expect(r.stdout).toContain('zqx16sec deploy with');
      for (const frag of ['Zq9fixture0not', 'MIIZQfixture0body', 'ZQfixture0body0line0two']) expect(r.stdout, `${frag} ${form.join('')}`).not.toContain(frag);
    }
    const db = t16help.openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      const row = db.prepare('SELECT b.z AS z FROM entries e JOIN blobs b ON b.blob_id = e.blob_id WHERE e.uuid = ?').get(t16uuid(ST, 1)) as { z: Uint8Array };
      const atRest = t16zlib.brotliDecompressSync(row.z).toString('utf8');
      expect(atRest).toContain(GHO);
      expect(atRest).toContain('ZQfixture0body0line0two');
    } finally { db.close(); }
  });

  it('DM29: a sidecar past its 512 KB FTS window is not found by grep, and expand pages reach its tail; one past SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX is never decompressed', () => {
    const DID = 'claude-a-x16side';
    const DT = 'a1600006';
    const DU = t16uuid(DT, 0);
    const d = (i: number): string => t16uuid(DT, i);
    const dbox = t16help.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-x16side-');
    const dcli = (args: string[]) => t16help.runCli(dbox, args, { env: t16help.withPane(dbox, DID) });
    const t = t16seed(dbox, { id: DID, project: 'demo', generation: '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-00000000f016', uuid: DU, rows: [
      t16fx.userRow({ uuid: d(1), ts: t16ts(1), sessionId: DU, text: 'zqx16side build it' }),
      t16fx.toolUseRow({ uuid: d(2), ts: t16ts(2), parentUuid: d(1), sessionId: DU, toolUseId: 'toolu_01X16SIDE', name: 'Bash', input: { command: 'cat build.log' } }),
      t16fx.toolResultRow({ uuid: d(3), ts: t16ts(3), parentUuid: d(2), sessionId: DU, toolUseId: 'toolu_01X16SIDE', content: 'Output too large. Full output saved to: tool-results/big29.txt' }),
    ] });
    const dir = t16path.join(t16path.dirname(t), DU, 'tool-results');
    t16fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
    const body = `zqhead29 ${'x '.repeat(270_000)}zqtail29\n`;
    expect(body.indexOf('zqtail29'), 'CONTROL: the tail sits past the FTS window').toBeGreaterThan(t16lib.SIDECAR_FTS_BYTES);
    t16fs.writeFileSync(t16path.join(dir, 'big29.txt'), body);
    t16scan(dbox);
    const db = t16help.openStoreRO(dbox);
    try {
      const linked = db.prepare(`SELECT e.uuid AS uuid FROM sidecars s JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = s.entry_id WHERE s.name = 'big29.txt'`).get() as { uuid: string } | undefined;
      expect(linked?.uuid, 'CONTROL: the sidecar is stored and linked to its tool_result').toBe(d(3));
    } finally { db.close(); }
    expect(dcli(['grep', 'zqtail29']).code, 'past the window: no index term').toBe(3);
    expect(dcli(['grep', 'zqhead29']).code, 'CONTROL: inside the window').toBe(0);
    const first = dcli(['expand', d(3), '--json']);
    expect(first.code, first.stderr).toBe(0);
    const [entry, side] = t16items(first);
    expect(entry!.uuid).toBe(d(3));
    expect(side).toMatchObject({ kind: 'sidecar', name: 'big29.txt', from: 0, of: body.length });
    expect(side!.text.startsWith('zqhead29')).toBe(true);
    // A cursor is ids and offsets only: one aimed near the end reads the tail without 30 page calls.
    let cursor: string | null = t16lib.encodeCursor({ v: 1, resource: 'expand', t: d(3), i: 1, o: body.length - 40_000 });
    const tail: string[] = [];
    for (let pages = 0; cursor !== null && pages < 10; pages += 1) {
      const r = dcli(['expand', d(3), '--cursor', cursor, '--json']);
      expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
      for (const it of t16items(r)) if (it.kind === 'sidecar') tail.push(it.text);
      cursor = t16cursor(String(r.json?.['next'] ?? ''));
    }
    expect(tail.join('')).toContain('zqtail29');
    // lib's expandBlobFits: a blob whose recorded size passes SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX is never decompressed. Its raw_len
    // is raised in place, so the bound is measured without a second 64 MiB fixture; z still holds the small body,
    // which is exactly what a mutant that decompresses anyway would print.
    const w = new t16sqlite.DatabaseSync(t16lib.historyPaths(dbox.home).dbFile);
    try {
      w.prepare("UPDATE blobs SET raw_len = ? WHERE blob_id = (SELECT blob_id FROM sidecars WHERE name = 'big29.txt')").run(t16lib.SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX + 1);
    } finally { w.close(); }
    const huge = dcli(['expand', d(3), '--json']);
    expect(huge.code, huge.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(huge.stdout.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(t16lib.OUTPUT_CAP);
    expect(t16items(huge)[1]).toMatchObject({ kind: 'sidecar', name: 'big29.txt', text: '', cut: true, of: t16lib.SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX + 1 });
    const hugeHuman = dcli(['expand', d(3)]);
    expect(hugeHuman.stdout).toMatch(/^content too large to expand here: \d+ bytes/m);
    expect(hugeHuman.stdout, 'nothing of the body is printed').not.toContain('zqhead29');
  });

  it('DM29: a message past its 1 MiB index window and its redaction margin is not found by grep past the window, and expand pages reach its tail', () => {
    const LID = 'claude-a-x16long';
    const LT = 'a1600009';
    const LU = t16uuid(LT, 0);
    const l = (i: number): string => t16uuid(LT, i);
    const lbox = t16help.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-x16long-');
    const lcli = (args: string[]) => t16help.runCli(lbox, args, { env: t16help.withPane(lbox, LID) });
    // As Task 14's reach describe builds it: the head inside the window, the tail after 1,190,000 bytes of plain words.
    const LONG = `zqlonghead29 ${'plain words here '.repeat(70_000)}zqlongtail29 end`;
    expect(Buffer.byteLength(LONG.slice(0, LONG.indexOf('zqlongtail29')), 'utf8'), 'CONTROL: the tail sits past the window and its margin')
      .toBeGreaterThan(t16lib.ENTRY_FTS_BYTES + t16lib.ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN);
    t16seed(lbox, { id: LID, project: 'demo', generation: '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-00000001c016', uuid: LU, rows: [
      t16fx.userRow({ uuid: l(1), ts: t16ts(1), sessionId: LU, text: LONG }),
    ] });
    expect(lcli(['grep', 'zqlonghead29']).code, 'CONTROL: inside the window').toBe(0);
    expect(lcli(['grep', 'zqlongtail29']).code, 'past the window: no index term').toBe(3);
    // A cursor is ids and offsets only: one aimed near the end reads the tail without 60 page calls.
    let cursor: string | null = t16lib.encodeCursor({ v: 1, resource: 'expand', t: l(1), i: 0, o: LONG.length - 40_000 });
    const tail: string[] = [];
    for (let pages = 0; cursor !== null && pages < 10; pages += 1) {
      const r = lcli(['expand', l(1), '--cursor', cursor, '--json']);
      expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
      for (const it of t16items(r)) if (it.kind === 'entry' && it.uuid === l(1)) tail.push(it.text);
      cursor = t16cursor(String(r.json?.['next'] ?? ''));
    }
    expect(tail.join(''), 'the stored row holds the tail, and expand reads it').toContain('zqlongtail29');
  }, 300_000);

  it("a message body past B1's BLOB_DECODE_MAX prints the too-large line and is not decompressed; a blob that does not decode prints its own line, never a throw or a pruned one", () => {
    const CID = 'claude-a-x16cap';
    const CT = 'a1600008';
    const CU = t16uuid(CT, 0);
    const c = (i: number): string => t16uuid(CT, i);
    const cbox = t16help.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-x16cap-');
    const ccli = (args: string[]) => t16help.runCli(cbox, args, { env: t16help.withPane(cbox, CID) });
    t16seed(cbox, { id: CID, project: 'demo', generation: '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-00000001b016', uuid: CU, rows: [
      t16fx.userRow({ uuid: c(1), ts: t16ts(1), sessionId: CU, text: 'zqx16cap the body under the cap test' }),
      t16fx.userRow({ uuid: c(2), ts: t16ts(2), sessionId: CU, text: 'zqx16bad the body whose bytes are damaged' }),
    ] });
    expect(ccli(['expand', c(1)]).stdout, 'CONTROL: the body prints before its raw_len is raised').toContain('zqx16cap');
    expect(ccli(['expand', c(2)]).stdout, 'CONTROL: the body prints before its bytes are damaged').toContain('zqx16bad');
    // raw_len is raised in place past BLOB_DECODE_MAX but kept under SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX, so only B1's body cap refuses it;
    // z still holds the small body, which is exactly what a mutant that decompresses anyway would print. The second
    // row's z is replaced by bytes that are not Brotli.
    expect(t16lib.BLOB_DECODE_MAX + 1, 'CONTROL: expandBlobFits alone would admit it').toBeLessThanOrEqual(t16lib.SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX);
    const w = new t16sqlite.DatabaseSync(t16lib.historyPaths(cbox.home).dbFile);
    try {
      w.prepare('UPDATE blobs SET raw_len = ? WHERE blob_id = (SELECT blob_id FROM entries WHERE uuid = ?)').run(t16lib.BLOB_DECODE_MAX + 1, c(1));
      w.prepare('UPDATE blobs SET z = ? WHERE blob_id = (SELECT blob_id FROM entries WHERE uuid = ?)').run(Buffer.from('zq not brotli at all, damaged'), c(2));
    } finally { w.close(); }
    const capJ = ccli(['expand', c(1), '--json']);
    expect(capJ.code, capJ.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(t16items(capJ)[0]).toMatchObject({ kind: 'entry', uuid: c(1), text: '', cut: true, of: t16lib.BLOB_DECODE_MAX + 1 });
    const capH = ccli(['expand', c(1)]);
    expect(capH.stdout).toContain(`content too large to expand here: ${t16lib.BLOB_DECODE_MAX + 1} bytes, over the ${t16lib.BLOB_DECODE_MAX}-byte bound`);
    expect(capH.stdout, 'nothing of the body is printed').not.toContain('zqx16cap');
    const badJ = ccli(['expand', c(2), '--json']);
    expect(badJ.code, badJ.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(t16items(badJ)[0]).toMatchObject({ kind: 'entry', uuid: c(2), text: '', pruned_ms: null, undecodable: true });
    const badH = ccli(['expand', c(2)]);
    expect(badH.code, badH.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(badH.stdout).toMatch(/^content does not decode: the stored blob is damaged/m);
    expect(badH.stdout).not.toMatch(/^content pruned/m);
  });
});

describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'darwin')('expand at scale (Task 16, review focus 3): multi-MiB items, a sidecar near SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX', () => {
  const ID = 'claude-a-x16big';
  const G = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-00000001a016';
  const T = 'a1600007';
  const U = t16uuid(T, 0);
  const e = (i: number): string => t16uuid(T, i);
  /** The per-call wall clock this measures against (*chosen*: "a few seconds" on a quiet box, with room for CI
   *  load; the worker records the measured values in the PR). */
  const SCALE_MS = 20_000;
  /** Peak RSS for one page of a ~64 MiB blob (*chosen*): one blob decompressed, only the page's window redacted
   *  (Task 12's redactDisplayWindow), never the store. Redacting the whole blob instead peaked at 1,954 MiB (review
   *  finding R36), which Step 13's mutant (b) shows red here; windowed, a prototype page peaked at 201,720 KiB. */
  const RSS_KIB = 1_048_576;
  const RSS_PRELOAD = t16path.join(t16help.REPO, 'server', 'test', 'fixtures', 'history', 'preload-rss.mjs');
  const S = t16crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex');
  const items = Math.ceil((t16lib.EXPLORE_JSON_MAX * 1.25) / 48);
  const BULK = JSON.stringify(Array.from({ length: items }, (_, i) => ({ id: i, name: `zqbulk item ${i}`, tags: ['a', 'b'] })));
  const DENSE = `zqx16dense ${Array.from({ length: 2000 }, () => S).join(' ')}`;
  const HUGE = t16lib.SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX - 4096;
  let box: t16help.HistoryBox;
  let leaf = '';
  const cli = (args: string[], preloads?: string[]) => t16help.runCli(box, args, { env: t16help.withPane(box, ID), ...(preloads === undefined ? {} : { preloads }) });

  t16beforeAll(() => {
    expect(BULK.length, 'CONTROL: the bulk output is past the explorer\'s JSON bound').toBeGreaterThan(t16lib.EXPLORE_JSON_MAX);
    expect(Math.ceil(BULK.length * 1.3), 'CONTROL: its transcript line, quotes escaped, stays under LINE_MAX (a parsed row)').toBeLessThan(t16lib.LINE_MAX);
    box = t16help.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-x16big-');
    t16fs.mkdirSync(t16path.join(box.home, '.cc-secrets'), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    t16fs.writeFileSync(t16path.join(box.home, '.cc-secrets', 'x16.env'), `ZQ_X16_KEY=${S}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    const t = t16seed(box, { id: ID, project: 'demo', generation: G, uuid: U, rows: t16leafRows(T, U, [
      t16fx.userRow({ uuid: e(1), ts: t16ts(1), sessionId: U, text: 'zqx16big load the data' }),
      t16fx.toolUseRow({ uuid: e(2), ts: t16ts(2), parentUuid: e(1), sessionId: U, toolUseId: 'toolu_01X16BULK', name: 'Read', input: { file_path: '/home/u/tree/demo/big.json' } }),
      t16fx.toolResultRow({ uuid: e(3), ts: t16ts(3), parentUuid: e(2), sessionId: U, toolUseId: 'toolu_01X16BULK', content: BULK }),
      t16fx.toolUseRow({ uuid: e(4), ts: t16ts(4), parentUuid: e(3), sessionId: U, toolUseId: 'toolu_01X16HUGE', name: 'Bash', input: { command: 'cat huge16.log' } }),
      t16fx.toolResultRow({ uuid: e(5), ts: t16ts(5), parentUuid: e(4), sessionId: U, toolUseId: 'toolu_01X16HUGE', content: 'Output too large. Full output saved to: tool-results/huge16.log' }),
      t16fx.userRow({ uuid: e(6), ts: t16ts(6), sessionId: U, parentUuid: e(5), text: DENSE }),
      t16fx.assistantRow({ uuid: e(7), ts: t16ts(7), parentUuid: e(6), sessionId: U, text: 'zqx16big done' }),
    ]) });
    const dir = t16path.join(t16path.dirname(t), U, 'tool-results');
    t16fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
    t16fs.writeFileSync(t16path.join(dir, 'huge16.log'), Buffer.alloc(HUGE, '2026-10-05T12:00:00Z INFO worker 17 processed batch 4242 in 31ms ok\n'));
    t16scan(box);
    leaf = t16leafOf(box, ID);
  }, 600_000);

  it('a node holding a multi-MiB tool output and a ~64 MiB sidecar: one page, cut and outlined, within the cap and the clock; the JSON outline is skipped past its bound', () => {
    const r = cli(['expand', leaf]);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(r.ms, `expand of the node took ${r.ms} ms`).toBeLessThan(SCALE_MS);
    expect(r.stdout.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(t16lib.OUTPUT_CAP);
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(new RegExp(`${e(3)} \\S+ \\[cut 2000 of ${BULK.length} chars; outline: json\\]`));
    expect(r.stdout, 'JSON.parse is skipped above EXPLORE_JSON_MAX').not.toContain('Structured summary (JSON)');
    expect(r.stdout).toMatch(new RegExp(`sidecar huge16\\.log of ${e(5)} \\[cut 2000 of ${HUGE} chars; outline: code\\]`));
  }, 120_000);

  it('the multi-MiB row whole, and the sidecar paged at its start and in its middle: each page within the cap, the clock and the RSS bound', () => {
    const bulk = cli(['expand', e(3), '--json']);
    expect(bulk.code, bulk.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(bulk.ms).toBeLessThan(SCALE_MS);
    expect(bulk.stdout.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(t16lib.OUTPUT_CAP);
    expect(t16items(bulk)[0]!.to).toBeLessThan(t16items(bulk)[0]!.of);
    const first = cli(['expand', e(5)], [RSS_PRELOAD]);
    expect(first.code, first.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(first.ms).toBeLessThan(SCALE_MS);
    expect(first.stdout.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(t16lib.OUTPUT_CAP);
    const rss = Number(/history-test-maxrss-kib=(\d+)/.exec(first.stderr)?.[1] ?? 'NaN');
    expect(rss, 'the RSS preload reported').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(rss, `peak RSS ${rss} KiB for one page of a ${HUGE}-byte blob`).toBeLessThan(RSS_KIB);
    const mid = cli(['expand', e(5), '--cursor', t16lib.encodeCursor({ v: 1, resource: 'expand', t: e(5), i: 1, o: HUGE >> 1 })]);
    expect(mid.code, mid.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(mid.ms).toBeLessThan(SCALE_MS);
    expect(mid.stdout.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(t16lib.OUTPUT_CAP);
    const grep = cli(['grep', 'zqbulk']);
    expect(grep.code, grep.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(grep.ms).toBeLessThan(SCALE_MS);
    expect(grep.stdout.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(t16lib.OUTPUT_CAP);
  }, 300_000);

  it('a secret straddling a page boundary: no page, and no two pages joined, print 8 consecutive characters of it', () => {
    const windows = Array.from({ length: S.length - 7 }, (_, i) => S.slice(i, i + 8));
    const outs: string[] = [];
    const slices: string[] = [];
    let cursor: string | null = null;
    let pages = 0;
    do {
      const r = cli(['expand', e(6), ...(cursor === null ? [] : ['--cursor', cursor]), '--json']);
      expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
      outs.push(r.stdout);
      for (const it of t16items(r)) slices.push(it.text);
      cursor = t16cursor(String(r.json?.['next'] ?? ''));
      pages += 1;
    } while (cursor !== null && pages < 20);
    expect(pages, 'CONTROL: even redacted, the region spans more than one page').toBeGreaterThan(1);
    for (const text of [...outs, slices.join('')]) {
      expect(windows.filter((w) => text.includes(w)), 'a window of the secret printed').toEqual([]);
    }
  }, 120_000);
});

describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'darwin')('expand and grep under --project with 40 families: a full --json page stays within the cap (Task 16)', () => {
  // The page budgets (expand's PAGE_TEXT_BUDGET, grep's FRAME_RESERVE) count the items, not the envelope. They fit
  // only while Task 11's scopeJson bounds its families list (lib's SCOPE_FAMILIES_JSON_MAX, with families_total):
  // listed whole, 40 families add ~4.5k characters to every --json envelope. One family is captured with all the
```
