Append at the end of `ccd/history/recall.mjs`:

```js
// ── expand (W1-B2 Task 16) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// `ccrc history expand` (spec §8.4 "expand", §6.1 variants, §6.6 pruned text, §8.2 "Every verb resolves ids
// inside the scope", §8.3 "Redaction" and "Cap", §11 P17). Three targets, from Task 10's parseReadArgs through lib's expandArgsOf:
//   - a node id or prefix: the node's real text in order. A leaf's sources come by node_sources.ord. A condensed
//     node's leaves come in child order, their sources through P7's range CTE (store.mjs's lineageEntries, which
//     walks DOWN). Each source is followed by the sidecars linked to it. A tool output or sidecar over
//     EXPLORE_CUT is cut, with a deterministic outline (P17) and a `next:` line naming `expand <uuid>`;
//   - a message uuid: that one row WHOLE, with its sidecars, paged by cursor (slug
//     history-expand-message-id, NEW: a cut tool output needs a way to read the rest);
//   - --around <uuid> [--before N --after N]: the rows around one row in its holding copy's file order, cut as a
//     node's are.
// Every id resolves inside the scope: outside it is exit 2 out-of-scope, never 3.
// THE ORDER EVERY FIELD TAKES (slug history-redaction-before-cut; spec §8.3 and §8.4): its FULL
// raw text leaves the blob (lib's renderEntryText for a row, the decoded bytes for a sidecar); the window to show is
// picked on that raw text (the cut's first EXPLORE_CUT characters, or a page); lib's redactDisplayWindow redacts that
// window with ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN each side and cuts it back (the outline's input likewise, through exploreOutline);
// then recallEnvelope's escape, then cli.mjs's serialisation and redactFinal. Nothing redacts a whole item: one page
// costs its window (coordinator ruling R-display-window). One blob is decompressed at a time, and only one lib's
// expandBlobFits admits (at most SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX bytes); nothing holds a whole node in memory.
// A PAGE is measured in lib's textCost on what it prints, so it fits the cap in the human form and in --json alike.
// A cursor's offsets count characters of the item's raw text, the same in both forms.

/** How far a tool_result's paired tool_use is looked for up its parentUuid chain (B1's sweep walks 16). */
const EXPAND_PAIR_WALK = 16;
const EXPAND_ENTRY_COLS = Object.freeze(['entry_id', 'uuid', 'transcript_pk', 'type', 'role', 'ts_ms', 'provenance', 'parent_uuid', 'blob_id']);
/** cli.mjs prints a VerbResult's hint after `hint: `. */
const EXPAND_TARGET_HINT = 'expand <node id | message uuid> [--cursor <c>], or expand --around <uuid> [--before N] [--after N]';
/** Prepared once per read handle. Every select names its columns through selectColumns at the STORE's version
 *  (§6.11, DM44), so a column an older store lacks reads as NULL, never "no such column". */
const EXPAND_STMTS = new WeakMap();

function expandStmts(rc) {
  const hit = EXPAND_STMTS.get(rc.db);
  if (hit !== undefined) return hit;
  const cols = (table, list) => xlib.selectColumns(rc.version, table, list, rc.schema);
  const q = (sql) => rc.db.prepare(sql);
  const s = {
    node: q(`SELECT ${cols('nodes', ['node_id', 'kind', 'session_pk'])} FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?`),
    entryById: q(`SELECT ${cols('entries', EXPAND_ENTRY_COLS)} FROM entries WHERE entry_id = ?`),
    entryByUuid: q(`SELECT ${cols('entries', EXPAND_ENTRY_COLS)} FROM entries WHERE uuid = ?`),
    hop: q(`SELECT ${cols('entries', ['parent_uuid', 'blob_id'])} FROM entries WHERE uuid = ?`),
    // A blob's size and tombstone, read WITHOUT its z: the delegate estimate and the decompression bound need no body.
    blobLen: q(`SELECT ${cols('blobs', ['raw_len', 'pruned_ms'])} FROM blobs WHERE blob_id = ?`),
    blob: q(`SELECT ${cols('blobs', ['z'])} FROM blobs WHERE blob_id = ?`),
    variants: q(`SELECT ${cols('entry_variants', ['blob_id', 'cause'])} FROM entry_variants WHERE entry_id = ? ORDER BY first_seen_ms, blob_id`),
    sidecars: q(`SELECT ${cols('sidecars', ['entry_id', 'name', 'blob_id'])} FROM sidecars WHERE transcript_pk = ? ORDER BY name, blob_id`),
    // ingest_files has no transcript_pk index: every in-scope transcript's rows in ONE statement, one scan per call.
    files: q(`SELECT ${cols('ingest_files', ['file_id', 'status', 'source_key'])} FROM ingest_files WHERE transcript_pk IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?)) ORDER BY file_id`),
    member: q(`SELECT ${cols('memberships', ['line'])} FROM memberships WHERE file_id = ? AND entry_id = ?`),
    before: q(`SELECT ${cols('memberships', ['entry_id', 'line'])} FROM memberships WHERE file_id = ? AND line < ? ORDER BY line DESC LIMIT ?`),
    after: q(`SELECT ${cols('memberships', ['entry_id', 'line'])} FROM memberships WHERE file_id = ? AND line > ? ORDER BY line LIMIT ?`),
  };
  EXPAND_STMTS.set(rc.db, s);
  return s;
}

function expandRefusal(exit, reason, hint) {
  return {
    exit, ...(reason === undefined ? {} : { reason }), header: null, blocks: [], items: [], total: 0, shown: 0, next: null,
    ...(hint === undefined ? {} : { hint }),
  };
}

/** The in-scope transcripts' file rows, the live copy first: where a row's holding copy is looked for. The live copy is
 *  the row whose `source_key` is '' WHATEVER its status: B1 marks a deleted-from-disk live copy `gone` and keeps its
 *  `source_key` '' (sweep's markGone), and only a `retired` copy carries a non-empty key. That is lib's
 *  pickHoldingCopy rule (Task 8; §6.1 "The copy": a live copy, then the smallest file_id), which describe and the
 *  derivation use, so expand picks the same copy's memberships for --around and orders the lineage the same way. */
function expandScopedFiles(s, rc) {
  const out = s.files.all(JSON.stringify(rc.scope.transcriptPks));
  return out.sort((a, b) => (a.source_key === '' ? 0 : 1) - (b.source_key === '' ? 0 : 1) || a.file_id - b.file_id);
}

/** The first in-scope file holding an entry, by primary-key probes: memberships has no entry_id index. */
function expandHolding(s, files, entryId) {
  for (const f of files) {
    const m = s.member.get(f.file_id, entryId);
    if (m !== undefined) return { fileId: f.file_id, line: m.line };
  }
  return null;
}

/** A condensed node's source entries in leaf order (its children's ord, depth first), then node_sources.ord. */
function expandLineage(rc, s, nodeId, kind) {
  const leaves = [];
  if (kind !== 'condensed') leaves.push(nodeId);
  else {
    const stack = [nodeId];
    const seen = new Set();
    while (stack.length > 0) {
      const id = stack.pop();
      if (seen.has(id)) continue;
      seen.add(id);
      const n = s.node.get(id);
      if (n === undefined) continue;
      if (n.kind !== 'condensed') { leaves.push(id); continue; }
      const kids = [...xstore.childrenOf(rc.db, id)].sort((a, b) => a.ord - b.ord);
      for (let i = kids.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) stack.push(kids[i].childId);
    }
  }
  const rank = new Map(leaves.map((id, i) => [id, i]));
  const rows = xstore.lineageEntries(rc.db, nodeId).filter((r) => rank.has(r.nodeId));
  rows.sort((a, b) => rank.get(a.nodeId) - rank.get(b.nodeId) || a.ord - b.ord);
  const out = [];
  const seenEntry = new Set();
  for (const r of rows) if (!seenEntry.has(r.entryId)) { seenEntry.add(r.entryId); out.push(r.entryId); }
  return out;
}

/** What the arguments name, resolved inside the scope: {refuse} or {key, args, entryIds, whole}. */
function expandResolve(rc, s, a) {
  const files = expandScopedFiles(s, rc);
  const scopeTranscripts = new Set(rc.scope.transcriptPks);
  const entryNamed = (uuid) => {
    const e = s.entryByUuid.get(uuid);
    const hold = e === undefined ? null : expandHolding(s, files, e.entry_id);
    const verdict = xlib.entryScopeVerdict({ found: e !== undefined, inScope: e !== undefined && (scopeTranscripts.has(e.transcript_pk) || hold !== null) });
    return { verdict, e, hold };
  };
  const refuseEntry = (verdict) => (verdict === 'not-found' ? expandRefusal(xlib.EXIT.NOT_FOUND) : expandRefusal(xlib.EXIT.REFUSED, 'out-of-scope'));
  if (a.around !== null) {
    if (xlib.expandTargetOf(a.around) !== 'entry') return { refuse: expandRefusal(xlib.EXIT.REFUSED, 'bad-args', EXPAND_TARGET_HINT) };
    const { verdict, e, hold } = entryNamed(a.around);
    if (verdict !== 'ok') return { refuse: refuseEntry(verdict) };
    const ids = [];
    if (hold !== null) {
      for (const r of s.before.all(hold.fileId, hold.line, a.before).reverse()) ids.push(r.entry_id);
      ids.push(e.entry_id);
      for (const r of s.after.all(hold.fileId, hold.line, a.after)) ids.push(r.entry_id);
    } else ids.push(e.entry_id);
    return {
      key: `around:${e.uuid}:${a.before}:${a.after}`, entryIds: ids, whole: false,
      args: ['--around', e.uuid, '--before', String(a.before), '--after', String(a.after)],
    };
  }
  const kind = xlib.expandTargetOf(a.target);
  if (kind === 'bad') return { refuse: expandRefusal(xlib.EXIT.REFUSED, 'bad-args', EXPAND_TARGET_HINT) };
  if (kind === 'entry') {
    const { verdict, e } = entryNamed(a.target);
    if (verdict !== 'ok') return { refuse: refuseEntry(verdict) };
    return { key: e.uuid, args: [e.uuid], entryIds: [e.entry_id], whole: true };
  }
  // A node id or prefix: Task 12's resolveNodeInScope is the ONE spelling of §8.2's rule (out-of-scope is 2, never 3;
  // prefix uniqueness among the scope's nodes), shared with grep --node and describe.
  const found = resolveNodeInScope(rc, a.target);
  if (!found.ok) return { refuse: found.result };
  const node = s.node.get(found.id);
  return { key: found.id, args: [found.id], entryIds: expandLineage(rc, s, found.id, node.kind), whole: false };
}

/** The expansion's items: each entry, then the sidecars linked to it. Sidecars are read by their transcript (the
 *  primary key's prefix) once per transcript; sidecars has no entry_id index. */
function expandItems(s, entryIds) {
  const byTranscript = new Map();
  const sidecarsOf = (e) => {
    let m = byTranscript.get(e.transcript_pk);
    if (m === undefined) {
      m = new Map();
      for (const r of s.sidecars.all(e.transcript_pk)) {
        if (r.entry_id === null) continue;
        const list = m.get(r.entry_id) ?? [];
        list.push(r);
        m.set(r.entry_id, list);
      }
      byTranscript.set(e.transcript_pk, m);
    }
    return m.get(e.entry_id) ?? [];
  };
  const items = [];
  for (const id of entryIds) {
    const e = s.entryById.get(id);
    if (e === undefined) continue;
    const sidecars = sidecarsOf(e);
    items.push({ kind: 'entry', e, sidecars });
    for (const sc of sidecars) items.push({ kind: 'sidecar', e, name: sc.name, blobId: sc.blob_id });
  }
  return items;
}

/** The delegate hint's measure: stored sizes, read without any z, a cut item counted as at most twice EXPLORE_CUT. */
function expandEstimate(s, items, whole) {
  let chars = 0;
  for (const it of items) {
    const m = s.blobLen.get(it.kind === 'entry' ? it.e.blob_id : it.blobId);
    const len = m === undefined ? 0 : Number(m.raw_len);
    chars += xlib.expandCuts({ whole, kind: it.kind, provenance: it.e.provenance }) ? Math.min(len, 2 * xlib.EXPLORE_CUT) : len;
  }
  return chars;
}

/** One blob, decompressed only when lib's expandBlobFits lets one call hold it whole: a tombstone answers `pruned`
 *  (with its date, when recorded), a blob past SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX answers `too-large` with its byte size, and
 *  neither is decompressed. A message body (`isSidecar` false) also holds B1's body cap: past BLOB_DECODE_MAX
 *  (blobOverDecodeCap, B1's history-permanent-failures-classified; only a raw-only line-too-long blob gets there) it
 *  is `too-large` too, against that bound. Its size is read before its z is. The decode is bounded by the stored
 *  raw_len (B1's unbrotli(z, maxLen), FPM10), and a blob that does not decode answers `undecodable`, never a throw
 *  and never `pruned`: a damaged blob is not a pruned one (no overloaded value at a seam). */
function expandBlob(s, blobId, isSidecar) {
  const m = s.blobLen.get(blobId);
  if (m === undefined) return { state: 'pruned', prunedMs: null };
  if (m.pruned_ms !== null) return { state: 'pruned', prunedMs: Number(m.pruned_ms) };
  const rawLen = Number(m.raw_len);
  if (!xlib.expandBlobFits(rawLen)) return { state: 'too-large', rawLen };
  if (!isSidecar && xlib.blobOverDecodeCap(rawLen)) return { state: 'too-large', rawLen, bound: xlib.BLOB_DECODE_MAX };
  const b = s.blob.get(blobId);
  if (b === undefined || b.z === null) return { state: 'pruned', prunedMs: null };
  let bytes;
  try { bytes = xstore.unbrotli(b.z, rawLen); } catch { return { state: 'undecodable', rawLen }; }
  return { state: 'bytes', bytes };
}

/** A stored body: JSON for a parsed row, the line's text for a raw-only one. A body past B1's structure bound
 *  (jsonWithinStructureBound, B1's history-json-structure-bound: a raw-only blob can nest millions of levels) is
 *  never parsed: its text is shown as stored. */
function expandParse(bytes) {
  const text = bytes.toString('utf8');
  if (!xlib.jsonWithinStructureBound(bytes)) return text;
  try { return JSON.parse(text); } catch { return text; }
}

/** An entry's RAW text (lib's renderEntryText; every shown window of it is redacted by expandRenderItem): the
 *  unsanitised variant when the pair is ccd's own (DM2b), a tombstone as `pruned`. */
function expandEntryText(rc, s, e) {
  const p = expandBlob(s, e.blob_id, false);
  if (p.state !== 'bytes') return p;
  const primary = expandParse(p.bytes);
  const rows = s.variants.all(e.entry_id).filter((v) => v.blob_id !== e.blob_id);
  const others = [];
  for (const v of rows) {
    const vb = expandBlob(s, v.blob_id, false);
    if (vb.state === 'bytes') others.push({ body: expandParse(vb.bytes), cause: v.cause });
  }
  const body = others.length === 0 ? primary : xlib.pickExpandBody({ primary, variants: others });
  return { state: 'text', text: xlib.renderEntryText(body), causes: rows.map((v) => v.cause), primary };
}

/** A sidecar's bytes as RAW text. It is never redacted whole: a 64 MiB sidecar redacted whole peaked at 1,954 MiB
 *  for one page (review finding R36), so expandRenderItem redacts only the window it shows. */
function expandSidecarText(rc, s, blobId) {
  const p = expandBlob(s, blobId, true);
  if (p.state !== 'bytes') return p;
  return { state: 'text', text: p.bytes.toString('utf8'), causes: [], primary: null };
}

/** The file a tool_result's tool_use named (P17 dispatches the outline on its extension), redacted. The walk stops
 *  at the first ancestor holding the paired tool_use, whether or not it names a file. */
function expandPairedPath(rc, s, e, body) {
  const ids = xlib.toolResultIdsOf(body);
  if (ids.length === 0) return null;
  let uuid = e.parent_uuid;
  for (let hop = 0; hop < EXPAND_PAIR_WALK && typeof uuid === 'string'; hop += 1) {
    const r = s.hop.get(uuid);
    if (r === undefined) return null;
    const b = expandBlob(s, r.blob_id, false);
    if (b.state === 'bytes') {
      const p = xlib.toolUseInputPath(expandParse(b.bytes), ids[0]);
      if (p.found) return p.path === null ? null : xlib.redactField(p.path, rc.pairIdx);
    }
    uuid = r.parent_uuid;
  }
  return null;
}

/** The primary body of an entry, for a sidecar's pairing (small: a tool_result row). */
function expandPrimaryBody(s, e) {
  const b = expandBlob(s, e.blob_id, false);
  return b.state === 'bytes' ? expandParse(b.bytes) : null;
}

/** One item rendered for this page: {block, json, cost, partial, to}, or null when it may not start here. A cut or
 *  pruned item that does not fit waits for the next page unless it is the page's first. A whole item that does not
 *  fit starts as a partial when it is the first, or while EXPAND_MIN_PARTIAL of the budget is left.
 *  o = {whole, from, budget, first, scope}. */
function expandRenderItem(rc, s, it, pos, total, o) {
  const isEntry = it.kind === 'entry';
  const e = it.e;
  const src = isEntry ? (e.provenance ?? 'harness') : 'sidecar';
  const id = isEntry ? e.uuid : `${e.uuid}/${it.name}`;
  const t = isEntry ? expandEntryText(rc, s, e) : expandSidecarText(rc, s, it.blobId);
  const ts = e.ts_ms === null ? '-' : new Date(Number(e.ts_ms)).toISOString();
  const lead = isEntry
    ? `── ${pos}/${total} ${e.type === '' ? 'raw' : e.type}${e.role ? `/${e.role}` : ''} ${src} ${e.uuid} ${ts}`
    : `── ${pos}/${total} sidecar ${it.name} of ${e.uuid}`;
  const causes = t.state === 'text' ? t.causes : [];
  const tail = causes.map((c) => `variant cause=${c}`);
  const base = {
    kind: it.kind, uuid: e.uuid, ...(isEntry ? {} : { name: it.name }), type: e.type, role: e.role,
    ts_ms: e.ts_ms === null ? null : Number(e.ts_ms), provenance: src, trust: 'untrusted',
  };
  const extra = { variants: causes.map((cause) => ({ cause })), ...(isEntry ? { sidecars: it.sidecars.map((sc) => ({ name: sc.name })) } : {}) };
  const env = (text, suffix = '') => xlib.recallEnvelope({
    src, id: `${id}${suffix}`, ts: e.ts_ms === null ? null : Number(e.ts_ms), role: isEntry ? e.role : null, text,
  });
  const measure = (block, json) => Math.max(block.length, JSON.stringify(json).length);

  if (t.state === 'pruned') {
    const when = t.prunedMs === null ? 'on an unrecorded date' : `on ${new Date(t.prunedMs).toISOString().slice(0, 10)}`;
    const block = [lead, `content pruned ${when}`].join('\n');
    const json = { ...base, text: '', from: 0, to: 0, of: 0, cut: false, outline: null, outline_kind: null, pruned_ms: t.prunedMs, ...extra };
    const cost = measure(block, json);
    return cost <= o.budget || o.first ? { block, json, cost, partial: false, to: 0 } : null;
  }

  if (t.state === 'too-large') {
    // lib's expandBlobFits said no (or, for a message body, B1's blobOverDecodeCap: `bound` names BLOB_DECODE_MAX):
    // one fixed line, nothing decompressed. `of` is the recorded size, in bytes.
    const block = [lead, `content too large to expand here: ${t.rawLen} bytes, over the ${t.bound ?? xlib.SIDECAR_WHOLE_MAX}-byte bound one call decompresses`].join('\n');
    const json = { ...base, text: '', from: 0, to: 0, of: t.rawLen, cut: true, outline: null, outline_kind: null, pruned_ms: null, ...extra };
    const cost = measure(block, json);
    return cost <= o.budget || o.first ? { block, json, cost, partial: false, to: 0 } : null;
  }

  if (t.state === 'undecodable') {
    // The stored bytes do not decode within their recorded raw_len (B1's blob-undecodable; doctor counts it). Not a
    // pruned blob, and never a throw: one fixed line, with `undecodable: true` on the --json item.
    const block = [lead, `content does not decode: the stored blob is damaged (recorded ${t.rawLen} bytes)`].join('\n');
    const json = { ...base, text: '', from: 0, to: 0, of: 0, cut: false, outline: null, outline_kind: null, pruned_ms: null, undecodable: true, ...extra };
    const cost = measure(block, json);
    return cost <= o.budget || o.first ? { block, json, cost, partial: false, to: 0 } : null;
  }

  // R is the item's RAW text. Every window shown of it goes through shownOf, which redacts the window plus
  // ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN each side and cuts it back (Task 12's redactDisplayWindow): never the whole item first.
  const R = t.text;
  const shownOf = (from, to) => xlib.redactDisplayWindow(R, from, to, rc.pairIdx);
  if (xlib.expandCuts({ whole: o.whole, kind: it.kind, provenance: e.provenance }) && R.length > xlib.EXPLORE_CUT) {
    const path = expandPairedPath(rc, s, e, isEntry ? t.primary : expandPrimaryBody(s, e));
    const kind = xlib.exploreKindOf(path) ?? (isEntry ? null : xlib.exploreKindOf(it.name)) ?? 'code';
    const cutEnd = xlib.cutText(R, xlib.EXPLORE_CUT, xlib.CUT_TEXT_BUDGET).length;
    const shown = xlib.cutText(shownOf(0, cutEnd), xlib.EXPLORE_CUT, xlib.CUT_TEXT_BUDGET);
    const outline = xlib.cutText(xlib.exploreOutline(R, kind, path === null ? undefined : xbasename(path), rc.pairIdx),
      xlib.EXPLORE_CUT, xlib.CUT_TEXT_BUDGET);
    const block = [`${lead} [cut ${cutEnd} of ${R.length} chars; outline: ${kind}]`, env(shown), env(outline, '#outline'),
      xlib.nextLine(['expand', e.uuid, ...o.scope]), ...tail].join('\n');
    const json = { ...base, text: shown, from: 0, to: cutEnd, of: R.length, cut: true, outline, outline_kind: kind, pruned_ms: null, ...extra };
    const cost = measure(block, json);
    return cost <= o.budget || o.first ? { block, json, cost, partial: false, to: 0 } : null;
  }

  const from = Math.min(o.from, R.length);
  const frame = [`${lead} [chars ${from}-${R.length} of ${R.length}; continues]`, env(''), ...tail].join('\n');
  const frameJson = { ...base, text: '', from, to: R.length, of: R.length, cut: false, outline: null, outline_kind: null, pruned_ms: null, ...extra };
  const fixed = measure(frame, frameJson);
  let to = R.length;
  if (fixed + xlib.textCost(R, from) > o.budget) {
    if (!o.first && o.budget - fixed < xlib.EXPAND_MIN_PARTIAL) return null;
    to = xlib.pageEnd(R, from, Math.max(1, o.budget - fixed));
  }
  let text = shownOf(from, to);
  // A mark can print longer than what it replaced: the page shrinks until what it prints fits, keeping one
  // character (or one pair) at least, as pageEnd does.
  while (fixed + xlib.textCost(text) > o.budget) {
    const shorter = xlib.pageEnd(R, from, Math.max(1, xlib.textCost(R, from, to) >> 1));
    if (shorter >= to) break;
    to = shorter;
    text = shownOf(from, to);
  }
  const partial = to < R.length;
  const note = from === 0 && !partial ? '' : ` [chars ${from}-${to} of ${R.length}${partial ? '; continues' : ''}]`;
  const block = [`${lead}${note}`, env(text), ...tail].join('\n');
  const json = { ...base, text, from, to, of: R.length, cut: false, outline: null, outline_kind: null, pruned_ms: null, ...extra };
  return { block, json, cost: fixed + xlib.textCost(text), partial, to };
}

/** `expand` over a ReadContext. Returns a VerbResult whose `shown` is the position of the last item reached. */
export function runExpand(rc, a) {
  const s = expandStmts(rc);
  const decoded = a.cursor === null ? null : xlib.decodeCursor(a.cursor, 'expand');
  if (a.cursor !== null && decoded === null) return expandRefusal(xlib.EXIT.REFUSED, 'bad-args', 'that --cursor is not one expand printed');
  // A bare `expand --cursor <c>` resumes the expansion its cursor names.
  let want = a;
  if (a.target === null && a.around === null) {
    const resume = xlib.expandResumeOf(decoded);
    if (resume === null) return expandRefusal(xlib.EXIT.REFUSED, 'bad-args', EXPAND_TARGET_HINT);
    want = { ...a, ...resume };
  }
  const r = expandResolve(rc, s, want);
  if (r.refuse !== undefined) return r.refuse;
  const items = expandItems(s, r.entryIds);
  const at = xlib.decideExpandCursor({ cursor: decoded, key: r.key, total: items.length });
  if (!at.ok) return expandRefusal(xlib.EXIT.REFUSED, 'bad-args', 'that --cursor belongs to another expansion');
  const scope = rc.scopeArgs ?? [];
  const blocks = [];
  const out = [];
  let budget = xlib.PAGE_TEXT_BUDGET;
  let next = null;
  let shown = at.i;
  for (let i = at.i; i < items.length; i += 1) {
    const item = expandRenderItem(rc, s, items[i], i + 1, items.length, { whole: r.whole, from: i === at.i ? at.o : 0, budget, first: blocks.length === 0, scope });
    if (item === null) { next = { i, o: 0 }; break; }
    blocks.push(item.block);
    out.push(item.json);
    budget -= item.cost;
    shown = i + 1;
    if (item.partial) { next = { i, o: item.to }; break; }
  }
  const nextArgs = next === null ? null
    : ['expand', ...r.args, ...scope, '--cursor', xlib.encodeCursor({ v: 1, resource: 'expand', t: r.key, i: next.i, o: next.o })];
  const hint = a.cursor === null ? xlib.delegateHint(expandEstimate(s, items, r.whole)) : null;
  return { exit: xlib.EXIT.OK, header: null, blocks, items: out, total: items.length, shown, next: nextArgs, ...(hint === null ? {} : { hint }) };
}

/** cli.mjs's READ_RUNNERS.expand: Task 10's parseReadArgs answer, through lib's expandArgsOf. */
export function expandVerb(rc, parsed) {
  const p = xlib.expandArgsOf(parsed);
  if (!p.ok) return expandRefusal(xlib.EXIT.REFUSED, 'bad-args', EXPAND_TARGET_HINT);
  return runExpand(rc, { ...p.args, json: parsed.opts.json === true });
}
```

  - `export function schemaAdditive(schema: Readonly<Record<number, SchemaVersionAdded>>, measured?: Readonly<Record<number, Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>>>): { ok: true } | { ok: false; lost: string[] }`

  - The ReadContext gains an optional `verbTables`. Only tests set it. Its default is `VERB_TABLES`.

**Spec:**
- Sections:
  - §6.11 "The CLI keeps answering": named-column queries built from `SCHEMA_ADDED` at the STORE's version, NULL for a column it lacks, exit 5 `migration-pending` for a missing table, additive-only migrations.
  - §6.2 (the CLI's connection names its columns).
  - §6.9 (coverage and `store_id`).
  - §8.3 ("Every envelope carries top-level `store_id` and `coverage`"; full node ids in `--json`).
- Pins: DM44, DM17 (CLI half), C43, C45.
- Departures:
  - B1's D-4212 (`history-cli-reads-store-version`), B1's D-4216 (`history-newer-schema-readable`), B1's D-4167 (`history-coverage-this-box`).
  - D-4716 (`history-schema-additive-measured`) (NEW): §6.11 asks for "a test over SCHEMA_ADDED" that refuses a drop or a rename. SCHEMA_ADDED's shape can only add, so the check compares it with what the migrations actually build (B1's `schemaOf` after each one), as well as with its own shape.

Choices this task makes:
- **The DM44 seam is in-process.** The test imports `recall.mjs`, which sets no umask, and passes a ReadContext whose `schema` (and, for the table case, `verbTables`) is a test-only v2. The fixture store is real: its v1 tables have had two columns dropped, so a select built for the code's version genuinely fails "no such column".
- **DM44's `status` clause is pinned on the same older store, through the CLI.** `status --json` answers it exit 0 with the store's own `user_version` (1) and its `migration` word (`none`), never exit 1 over the dropped columns. A spawned `status` reads lib's own `SCHEMA_VERSION`, and the code-side v2 seam exists only in-process, so `status`'s word for a migration the code is AHEAD of is not reachable here: that word is B1's pin (its `migration` health rows), and DM17's CLI half below pins `status` for a store AHEAD of the code.
- **The columns the seam pretends are new** are `entries.role` (expand and grep render it) and `nodes.directive_flag` (describe's `--json` names it). Neither column is in an index, a key or a CHECK, so SQLite's `DROP COLUMN` takes them.
- **The tables `VERB_TABLES` names** are every table each verb's executor reads. They are all v1 tables today, so a v1 store misses none. A later version that adds a table one verb needs adds it here in the same PR.
- **A join names its columns through Task 10's `selectColumns` with its `alias` argument**, so the rule "which columns does this store version have" is spelled once.

```ts
    expect(t17lib.schemaAdditive(t17lib.SCHEMA_ADDED, measure(store.MIGRATIONS))).toEqual({ ok: true });
    const lostOf = (r: { ok: boolean; lost?: string[] }): string[] => (r.ok ? [] : r.lost!);
    const renamed: Schema = { ...t17lib.SCHEMA_ADDED, 2: { heavy: false, tables: { nodes: ['gist2'] } } };
    expect(lostOf(t17lib.schemaAdditive(renamed, measure([...store.MIGRATIONS, 'ALTER TABLE nodes RENAME COLUMN gist TO gist2']))))
      .toContain('nodes.gist lost at v2');
    const dropped: Schema = { ...t17lib.SCHEMA_ADDED, 2: { heavy: false, tables: {} } };
    expect(lostOf(t17lib.schemaAdditive(dropped, measure([...store.MIGRATIONS, 'ALTER TABLE nodes DROP COLUMN topics']))))
      .toContain('nodes.topics lost at v2');
    expect(lostOf(t17lib.schemaAdditive({ ...t17lib.SCHEMA_ADDED, 2: { heavy: false, tables: { nodes: ['gist'] } } })))
      .toContain('nodes.gist re-listed at v2');
    const unknownKey = { ...t17lib.SCHEMA_ADDED, 2: { heavy: false, tables: {}, drops: { nodes: ['gist'] } } } as unknown as Schema;
    expect(lostOf(t17lib.schemaAdditive(unknownKey))).toContain('v2 has keys drops,heavy,tables');
    expect(lostOf(t17lib.schemaAdditive({ ...t17lib.SCHEMA_ADDED, 3: { heavy: false, tables: { seam: ['x'] } } }))).toContain('versions are not 1..N');
    const undeclared = measure([...store.MIGRATIONS, 'CREATE TABLE seam_extra (x INTEGER)']);
    expect(lostOf(t17lib.schemaAdditive({ ...t17lib.SCHEMA_ADDED, 2: { heavy: false, tables: {} } }, undeclared))).toContain('seam_extra.x undeclared at v2');
  });
});

describe('C43: no ccd/history module prepares SELECT * (W1-B2 Task 17; the server/src/coord/db.ts rule)', () => {
  /** Star selects in code, with comments removed: a block comment, and a line comment not preceded by `:` (a
   *  URL) or a quote. */
  const starSelects = (src: string): string[] => {
    const code = src.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '').replace(/(^|[^:'"`\\])\/\/.*$/gm, '$1');
    return [...code.matchAll(/\bSELECT\s+(?:DISTINCT\s+)?(?:[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\.)?\*/gi)].map((m) => m[0]);
  };

  it('CONTROL: the scan sees a star select on one line and across a line break, and none inside a comment', () => {
    expect(starSelects('db.prepare("SELECT * FROM x")')).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(starSelects('db.prepare(`SELECT\n  e.* FROM entries e`)')).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(starSelects('db.prepare("select distinct * from x")')).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(starSelects('// queries never SELECT * here\n/** nor SELECT * here */\nconst u = "https://x/y";')).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('every ccd/history/*.mjs names its columns', () => {
    const dir = t17path.join(REPO, 'ccd', 'history');
    const files = t17fs.readdirSync(dir).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.mjs')).sort();
    expect(files).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(['cli.mjs', 'derive.mjs', 'lib.mjs', 'recall.mjs', 'regex-worker.mjs', 'store.mjs', 'sweep.mjs']));
    for (const f of files) expect(starSelects(t17fs.readFileSync(t17path.join(dir, f), 'utf8')), f).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

```js
// ── version-aware reads (W1-B2 Task 17) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Spec §6.11 "The CLI keeps answering" (slug history-cli-reads-store-version): the CLI reads user_version first
// and builds its named-column queries for THAT version from SCHEMA_ADDED. A column the store lacks is selected
// as NULL (Task 10's selectColumns, with its alias argument for a join), and a verb that cannot answer without a
// newer table answers exit 5 migration-pending. Migrations are additive only, so an older store's columns are
// always a subset (DM44); schemaAdditive is the test that refuses one that is not.

/** Every table each read verb's executor reads (recall.mjs). All are v1 tables today; a version that adds a
 *  table a verb needs adds it here, in the same PR. */
export const VERB_TABLES = Object.freeze({
  grep: Object.freeze(['blobs', 'entries', 'entry_variants', 'sidecars', 'transcripts', 'epochs', 'sessions', 'ingest_files', 'memberships', 'nodes', 'node_sources']),
  describe: Object.freeze(['nodes', 'node_children', 'node_sources', 'node_refs', 'entries', 'blobs', 'boundaries', 'ingest_files', 'memberships', 'sessions', 'epochs', 'transcripts']),
  expand: Object.freeze(['nodes', 'node_children', 'node_sources', 'entries', 'blobs', 'entry_variants', 'sidecars', 'ingest_files', 'memberships']),
  tree: Object.freeze(['sessions', 'epochs', 'nodes', 'node_children']),
});

/** The tables a store at `version` has: every SCHEMA_ADDED entry at or below it. A newer store has all this
 *  build knows. */
function tablesThrough(version, schema) {
  const have = new Set();
  for (const [v, entry] of Object.entries(schema)) if (Number(v) <= version) for (const t of Object.keys(entry.tables)) have.add(t);
  return have;
}

/** The tables `verb` needs that a store at `version` lacks; [] when it can answer. */
export function missingTablesAt(version, verb, schema = SCHEMA_ADDED, verbTables = VERB_TABLES) {
  if (!Object.hasOwn(verbTables, verb)) throw new TypeError(`missingTablesAt: ${JSON.stringify(verb)} is not a read verb`);
  const have = tablesThrough(version, schema);
  return verbTables[verb].filter((t) => !have.has(t));
}

/** Whether a SCHEMA_ADDED is additive only (slug history-schema-additive-measured, NEW). Its shape: versions
 *  1..N, each exactly {heavy, tables}, no column listed twice. Given `measured` (B1's schemaOf after each
 *  migration, by version), each version must build exactly what SCHEMA_ADDED declares up to it: a rename or a
 *  drop shows as a column `lost`, a column nothing declared as `undeclared`. */
export function schemaAdditive(schema, measured) {
  const lost = [];
  const versions = Object.keys(schema).map(Number).sort((a, b) => a - b);
  if (versions.some((v, i) => v !== i + 1)) lost.push('versions are not 1..N');
  const cum = new Map();
  const cumAt = new Map();
  for (const v of versions) {
    const entry = schema[v];
    const keys = Object.keys(entry).sort();
    if (keys.join(',') !== 'heavy,tables' || typeof entry.heavy !== 'boolean') lost.push(`v${v} has keys ${keys.join(',')}`);
    for (const [t, cols] of Object.entries(entry.tables ?? {})) {
      const have = cum.get(t) ?? new Set();
      for (const c of cols) {
        if (have.has(c)) lost.push(`${t}.${c} re-listed at v${v}`);
        have.add(c);
      }
      cum.set(t, have);
    }
    cumAt.set(v, new Map([...cum].map(([t, set]) => [t, new Set(set)])));
  }
  for (const [vs, tables] of Object.entries(measured ?? {})) {
    const v = Number(vs);
    const want = cumAt.get(v);
    if (want === undefined) { lost.push(`v${v} measured but not declared`); continue; }
    for (const [t, cols] of want) for (const c of cols) if (!(tables[t] ?? []).includes(c)) lost.push(`${t}.${c} lost at v${v}`);
    for (const [t, cols] of Object.entries(tables)) for (const c of cols) if (!(want.get(t)?.has(c) ?? false)) lost.push(`${t}.${c} undeclared at v${v}`);
  }
  return lost.length === 0 ? { ok: true } : { ok: false, lost };
}
```

```js
// ── version-aware reads (W1-B2 Task 17) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Spec §6.11 "The CLI keeps answering" (slug history-cli-reads-store-version): every select above names its
// columns through selectColumns (with its alias argument, for a join) at the STORE's version, so a column an
// older store lacks reads as NULL. A verb that needs a TABLE the store lacks answers exit 5 migration-pending
// here, before any statement is prepared — never exit 1, never "no such table".

/** null when `verb` can answer a store at rc.version; otherwise the migration-pending VerbResult. rc.schema and
 *  rc.verbTables default to the build's own; only a test sets them (the DM44 seam). */
export function pendingFor(rc, verb) {
  const missing = xlib.missingTablesAt(rc.version, verb, rc.schema ?? xlib.SCHEMA_ADDED, rc.verbTables ?? xlib.VERB_TABLES);
  if (missing.length === 0) return null;
  return {
    exit: xlib.EXIT.DB, reason: 'migration-pending', header: null, blocks: [], items: [], total: 0, shown: 0, next: null,
    hint: `this store is at schema v${rc.version} and has no ${missing.join(', ')}: the next scheduled tick migrates it, `
      + 'or run "$HOME/.local/bin/ccrc" history doctor --migrate',
  };
}
```

Then make these two lines the FIRST statement of each verb executor's body, with the verb named in quotes:

```js
  const pending = pendingFor(rc, 'expand');
  if (pending !== null) return pending;
```

The executors are:
- `runExpand`: `'expand'`.
- `runTree`: `'tree'`.
- `runGrep`: `'grep'`.
- `runRegex`: `'grep'`, because the regex path is grep's.
- `runDescribe`: `'describe'`.

Each function's first parameter is the ReadContext. Where an executor names it other than `rc`, use its name in place of `rc`. A function declaration is hoisted, so `pendingFor` sitting at the file's end is in scope for the earlier executors.

- **A single-table select** builds its column list with `xlib.selectColumns(rc.version, '<table>', [...], rc.schema)`.
- **A join** builds each table's columns with `xlib.selectColumns(rc.version, '<table>', [...], rc.schema, '<alias>')`, which answers `<alias>.<col>` or `NULL AS <col>`.
- **A column read only in WHERE, ORDER BY or a JOIN condition** must be a v1 column, which every store has. If it is not, the verb's VERB_TABLES row and its logic are wrong, not the select.
- **A red at `toBeNull()`** (describe's `directive_flag`, expand's `role`) means the executor coerced the value it read, for example with `Boolean(...)` or `?? 0`. A field the store's version lacks must reach `--json` as null, so pass the column's value through unchanged.

**Spec:**
- Sections: §8.3 "Redaction" (four layers since spec rev 3.5, layer 1 with its glue windows and layer 4 the substring belt; "on each field, before any cut or escape"; the second belt); §9.8; §6.2 (the index sees redacted text; "The belt"); §8.4 `--regex` (over redacted text).
- Pins: C32, C33, C49, C59, C60, C69, DM31 (CLI half).
- Departures:
  - B1's D-4202 (`history-redaction-before-cut`), B1's D-4203 (`history-redaction-by-value`), B1's D-4205 (`history-redaction-from-roster`), B1's D-4201 (`history-redaction-agent-env`), B1's D-4206 (`history-secret-value-grammar`), B1's D-4243 (`history-fts-indexes-redacted-text`).
  - Not a departure: every recalled field shown through `redactForDisplay` (the index's escape readings), and every nodes_fts row through `nodeIndexTexts`, are spec rev 3.5's rule (§8.3 "Where it runs", §6.2 `nodes_fts`). Both reuse B1's D-4343 (`history-index-escape-readings-to-fixpoint`) unchanged.
  - D-4702 (`history-loader-values-in-tick-memory`) (NEW; confirmed by coordinator ruling RB16 for the tick and the CLI's pairs; widened by spec rev 3.5 to the CLI's values and the `--regex` child, which the coordinator confirmed). C32 says "the loader returns only `{len, sha}`", but B1's `loadSecrets` also returns the loaded values. Two things need them: the tick's re-index of already-indexed text, and §8.3 layer 4, which cannot find a substring from a pair.
    - They are held only in the memory of the processes that redact: the tick; the CLI, inside its belt, read from the frozen list and the declared paths in meta `redact_sources`; and the `--regex` child, on its stdin.
    - Nothing persisted, journaled or printed carries a value: meta `fts_belt` holds rowids, and `redact_sources` holds paths.
    - All three run as the same UNIX user, which can already read the files the values come from.
    - The C32 loader case and Task 7B's O59 case pin that, and no B2 task changes B1's loader.

Choices this task makes:
- **Fixture secrets are minted at runtime** (B1's rule: the public repo holds no key-shaped literal). Shape-matched ones (`sk-`, `gho_`, the PEM header) are joined from parts, so no scanner sees one in source.
- **A "leak" is any 8 consecutive characters of a secret** in any stdout, or in the joined text slices one item printed across pages. A secret split over two pages leaves at least half of itself on one of them, so the per-page check catches every two-way split. The joined check is a second net.
- **C59's 300-character steer cap is vacuous in B2.** Steering ships in W3, so no B2 output has a steer cap. Its clause is noted in the case and passes by construction.
- **C60's "doctor WARN"** is asserted on `status --json`'s `health.warn`. That is the measured source doctor's `history` check relays (B1 Task 32); running `ccrc doctor` itself here would add nothing but time.
- **C49's codex lane** is declared in the fixture roster, so "the roster's `exec.authDir`" is a real roster field. Its directory holds a value that the loader must never open.
- **C69's leak is a belt-width stretch, case folded, read as written and decoded.** §8.3 layer 4 promises no K consecutive characters, so C69 asks exactly that. C59's 8-character rule stays for the field-first cases, where a cut, not the belt, is under test.
- **C49 gains an index-bytes line.** The CLI now reads the declared secretsFile itself (Task 10), so its output stays clean even when the sweep never read the file. Output alone can no longer see C49's mutant (b), so the case also asserts the sweep indexed the key redacted.
- **Mutant (c) moves.** Since Task 7A the final pass carries the belt, so a token glued behind `\n` is masked there too. Mutant (c) reds instead where a cut, taken on unredacted text, leaves a piece of a secret shorter than its belt width on one page.
- **The escape-readings case uses pair-only values** (the same pair-only pattern as Task 8's redaction-order describe, review R30: that describe pins the derive side's order, redaction before `parseBlocks` and `minedRefs`; this one pins the display side). The belt (Task 7A) holds only the values loaded now, and it masks a loaded value glued to a literal `\n` in every reading, so a loaded value could not show what `redactForDisplay` adds. The case records both values' pairs on a first tick, rewrites the secret file without them, and only then seeds the session: a value no source still holds keeps its pair (redact_hashes only grows) but is no belt unit, so only the escape readings find it behind `\n` (redactField's one reading sees the run `n<value>`, which no pair matches, and layer 1's glue windows take only a run end, `_` or `-` as a bound). That is the rotated-value shape, and the hash-only one (sessions.json) behaves the same.

```ts
import * as t18fs from 'node:fs';
import * as t18path from 'node:path';
import * as t18crypto from 'node:crypto';
import * as t18lib from '../../ccd/history/lib.mjs';
import * as t18help from './historyHelpers.js';
```

Append at the end of the file:

```ts
// ── W1-B2 Task 18: output redaction across every verb ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Pins C32, C33, C49, C59, C60 and DM31's CLI half. Every fixture secret is minted at runtime; a shape-matched one
// is joined from parts. A "leak" is any 8 consecutive characters of a secret in any stdout, or in the text one
// item printed across pages, joined.
const t18hex = (bytes: number): string => t18crypto.randomBytes(bytes).toString('hex');
const t18alnum = (n: number): string => {
  const a = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789';
  return Array.from(t18crypto.randomBytes(n), (b) => a[b % a.length]!).join('');
};
const t18ts = (i: number): string => new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 9, 3, 10, 0, i)).toISOString();
const t18uuid = (tag: string, i: number): string => `${tag}-0000-4000-8000-${String(i).padStart(12, '0')}`;
/** A secret file under the fixture HOME, 0600 in a 0700 directory, as ccrc keeps them. */
function t18secret(box: t18help.HistoryBox, rel: string, body: string): string {
  const p = t18path.join(box.home, rel);
  t18fs.mkdirSync(t18path.dirname(p), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  t18fs.writeFileSync(p, body, { mode: 0o600 });
  return p;
}
/** Every 8-character window of `secret` found in any of `texts`, with the text's index. */
function t18leaks(texts: readonly string[], secret: string): string[] {
  const windows = Array.from({ length: secret.length - 7 }, (_, i) => secret.slice(i, i + 8));
  const out: string[] = [];
  texts.forEach((t, i) => { for (const w of windows) if (t.includes(w)) { out.push(`#${i}: ${w}`); break; } });
  return out;
}
/** The FTS index's own bytes, as latin1 (B1 Task 23's measure). */
function t18ftsBytes(box: t18help.HistoryBox): string {
  const db = t18help.openStoreRO(box);
  try {
    return (db.prepare('SELECT block FROM blobs_fts_data').all() as { block: Uint8Array }[]).map((r) => Buffer.from(r.block).toString('latin1')).join('');
  } finally { db.close(); }
}
/** One leaf over `sources`: a manual boundary whose head is the last source, keeping no row, and its summary. */
function t18leafRows(tag: string, sid: string, sources: object[], summary: string): object[] {
  const n = sources.length;
  const last = t18uuid(tag, n);
  return [
    ...sources,
    t18fx.boundaryRow({ uuid: t18uuid(tag, n + 1), ts: t18ts(n + 1), parentUuid: last, sessionId: sid, trigger: 'manual',
      headUuid: last, anchorUuid: t18uuid(tag, n + 2), tailUuid: last, allUuids: [] }),
    t18fx.summaryRow({ uuid: t18uuid(tag, n + 2), ts: t18ts(n + 2), parentUuid: t18uuid(tag, n + 1), sessionId: sid, text: summary }),
  ];
}
function t18leafOf(box: t18help.HistoryBox, id: string): string {
  const db = t18help.openStoreRO(box);
  try {
    const row = db.prepare(`SELECT n.node_id AS node_id FROM nodes n JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = n.session_pk
      WHERE s.ccrc_id = ? AND n.kind <> 'condensed'`).get(id) as { node_id: string } | undefined;
    expect(row?.node_id, `CONTROL: ${id}'s leaf was derived`).toMatch(/^L[0-9a-f]{20}$/);
    return row!.node_id;
  } finally { db.close(); }
}
const t18cursor = (s: string): string | null => {
  const m = [...s.matchAll(/--cursor '?([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)'?/g)];
  return m.length === 0 ? null : m[m.length - 1]![1]!;
};
type T18Run = { code: number | null; stdout: string; json: Record<string, unknown> | null };
/** Every page of a paged verb, human or --json, following its cursors. */
function t18pages(run: (args: string[]) => T18Run, args: string[]): T18Run[] {
  const out: T18Run[] = [];
  let cursor: string | null = null;
  do {
    const r = run([...args, ...(cursor === null ? [] : ['--cursor', cursor])]);
    expect(r.code, args.join(' ')).toBe(0);
    out.push(r);
    cursor = t18cursor(r.json === null ? r.stdout : String(r.json['next'] ?? ''));
  } while (cursor !== null && out.length < 30);
  return out;
}

    // B1's loadSecrets also returns the values, for the tick's re-index; they live in that process's memory only.
    // This case pins what leaves it: the pairs, the redact_hashes table, and every journal byte.
    const sweep = await import('../../ccd/history/sweep.mjs');
    const loaded = sweep.loadSecrets(box.home, []) as { pairs: Array<Record<string, unknown>> };
    expect(loaded.pairs.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const p of loaded.pairs) expect(Object.keys(p).sort()).toEqual(['len', 'sha256']);
    const text = JSON.stringify(loaded.pairs);
    for (const s of [V, A, TOK, K, P]) expect(text.includes(s)).toBe(false);
    const db = t18help.openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      const cols = (db.prepare('PRAGMA table_info(redact_hashes)').all() as { name: string }[]).map((c) => c.name);
      expect(cols, 'redact_hashes has no column a value could sit in').toEqual(['len', 'sha256', 'first_seen_ms']);
    } finally { db.close(); }
    const files: string[] = [];
    const walk = (d: string): void => {
      for (const e of t18fs.readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true })) {
        const p = t18path.join(d, e.name);
        if (e.isDirectory()) walk(p);
        else if (e.isFile()) files.push(p);
      }
    };
    walk(t18lib.historyPaths(box.home).journalDir);
    expect(files.length, 'CONTROL: the ticks journaled').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    const bytes = files.map((f) => t18fs.readFileSync(f).toString('latin1')).join('\n');
    for (const s of [V, A, TOK, K, P]) expect(bytes.includes(s), 'no journal byte holds a loaded value').toBe(false);
  });

  it('C33: a token in a describe gist, a tree gist and a next: echo of the query is redacted', () => {
    const d = [cli(['describe', leaf]).stdout, cli(['describe', leaf, '--json']).stdout];
    expect(d[0], 'CONTROL: the gist is shown').toContain('zqc33 rotating');
    const t = [cli(['tree']).stdout, cli(['tree', '--json']).stdout];
    const g = [cli(['grep', 'zqc33tool', '--tool', K, '--limit', '1']).stdout, cli(['grep', 'zqc33tool', '--tool', K, '--limit', '1', '--json']).stdout];
    expect(g[0], 'CONTROL: two hits over a limit of one print a next: line echoing the query').toMatch(/^next: /m);
    expect(t18leaks([...d, ...t, ...g], K)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('DM31 (CLI half): a planted token is no FTS prefix and no --regex match: both exit 3', () => {
    expect(cli(['grep', 'zqdm31']).code, 'CONTROL: the row itself is indexed').toBe(0);
    expect(cli(['grep', `"${P.slice(0, 6)}"*`]).code).toBe(3);
    expect(cli(['grep', '--regex', P.slice(0, 10)]).code).toBe(3);
  });
});

    const summary = `${PRE}${S.excerpt}\n8. Current Work:\n   zqc59 current work\n9. Optional Next Step:\n   zqc59 next step\n`

      t18fx.toolUseRow({ uuid: e(2), ts: t18ts(2), parentUuid: e(1), sessionId: U, toolUseId: 'toolu_01C59BASH', name: 'Bash', input: { command: `deploy --key\n${S.tool}` } }),
      t18fx.toolResultRow({ uuid: e(3), ts: t18ts(3), parentUuid: e(2), sessionId: U, toolUseId: 'toolu_01C59BASH', content: `${'p '.repeat(995)}${S.cut} ${'q '.repeat(1500)}` }),
      t18fx.toolUseRow({ uuid: e(4), ts: t18ts(4), parentUuid: e(3), sessionId: U, toolUseId: 'toolu_01C59PEM', name: 'Read', input: { file_path: '/home/u/tree/demo/key.pem' } }),
      t18fx.toolResultRow({ uuid: e(5), ts: t18ts(5), parentUuid: e(4), sessionId: U, toolUseId: 'toolu_01C59PEM', content: `${'r '.repeat(950)}${PEM}\n${'s '.repeat(1500)}` }),
      t18fx.userRow({ uuid: e(6), ts: t18ts(6), parentUuid: e(5), sessionId: U, text: `zqc59snip ${'u '.repeat(10)}${S.snip} tail words` }),
      t18fx.userRow({ uuid: e(7), ts: t18ts(7), parentUuid: e(6), sessionId: U, text: `zqc59shape x\n${SK}\ny\n${GHO}` }),
      t18fx.userRow({ uuid: e(8), ts: t18ts(8), parentUuid: e(7), sessionId: U, text: `zqc59sgr \x1b[32m${S.sgr}\x1b[0m done` }),
      t18fx.userRow({ uuid: e(9), ts: t18ts(9), parentUuid: e(8), sessionId: U, text: `zqc59page ${Array.from({ length: 2000 }, () => S.page).join(' ')}` }),

describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'darwin')('the index\'s escape readings at display: no output shows a value the index masked (Task 18; B1\'s D-4343; spec §8.3)', () => {
  const ID = 'claude-a-x18esc';

  const V = t18hex(32);   // in a row, glued to a literal escape twice
  const W = t18hex(32);   // in the summary, so in the leaf's gist
  /** What a tool printing JSON leaves in text: a literal backslash and `n` glued onto the value (B1's review 316 F2). */
  const glued = (v: string): string => JSON.stringify({ text: `\n${v}` });
  let box: t18help.HistoryBox;
  let leaf = '';
  const cli = (args: string[]): T18Run => t18help.runCli(box, args, { env: t18help.withPane(box, ID) });
  /** Every nodes_fts row's stored text (nodes_fts keeps its content, unlike the contentless blobs_fts). */
  const nodeRows = (): string[] => {
    const db = t18help.openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      return (db.prepare('SELECT gist, topics, refs FROM nodes_fts').all() as Array<Record<string, string | null>>)
        .map((r) => `${r['gist'] ?? ''}\n${r['topics'] ?? ''}\n${r['refs'] ?? ''}`);
    } finally { db.close(); }
  };

  t18beforeAll(() => {
    box = t18help.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-x18esc-');
    // Both values are PAIRS ONLY by the time the leaf is derived and the CLI runs. A first tick records their pairs
    // from the secret file, which is then rewritten without them: a value no source still holds keeps its pair
    // (redact_hashes only grows) but is no belt unit (Task 7A's belt holds the values loaded now). So only the escape
    // readings find either value behind a literal `\n`: redactField's one reading sees the run `n<value>`, which no pair
    // matches, and layer 1's glue windows bound a window only at a run end, `_` or `-`.
    const file = t18secret(box, '.cc-secrets/x18esc.env', `ZQ_ESC_ROW=${V}\nZQ_ESC_GIST=${W}\n`);
    expect(t18help.runSweep(box).code).toBe(0);
    t18fs.writeFileSync(file, `ZQ_ESC_OTHER=${t18hex(32)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    const summary = ['<summary>', '1. Primary Request and Intent:', '   zqesc intent', '8. Current Work:',
      `   zqescgist printed ${glued(W)} here`, '9. Optional Next Step:', '   zqesc next step', '</summary>'].join('\n');
    t18help.seedFamily(box, { id: ID, project: 'demo', generation: '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-00000000f018', uuid: U, rows: t18leafRows(T, U, [
      // The value starts 20 characters after the hit word, inside grep's snippet window (24 before, 40 after).
      t18fx.userRow({ uuid: e(1), ts: t18ts(1), sessionId: U, text: `zqescrow ${glued(V)} then \\u005cn${V} done` }),
      t18fx.assistantRow({ uuid: e(2), ts: t18ts(2), parentUuid: e(1), sessionId: U, text: 'zqesc done' }),
    ], summary) });
    expect(t18help.runSweep(box).code).toBe(0);
    leaf = t18leafOf(box, ID);
    const db = t18help.openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      const pairs = db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM redact_hashes WHERE len = ? AND sha256 = ?');
      for (const v of [V, W]) {
        expect((pairs.get(v.length, t18crypto.createHash('sha256').update(v).digest()) as { n: number }).n,
          'CONTROL: the first tick recorded the value\'s pair').toBe(1);
      }
    } finally { db.close(); }
  }, 240_000);

  it('grep and its snippet, expand, describe and tree, human and --json, and grep --regex show no 8 characters of either value', () => {
    const runs = [cli(['grep', 'zqescrow']), cli(['grep', 'zqescrow', '--json']), cli(['expand', e(1)]), cli(['expand', e(1), '--json']),

    for (const r of runs) expect(r.code, r.stdout).toBe(0);

    expect(texts[2], 'CONTROL: the row is printed').toContain('zqescrow');
    expect(texts[4], 'CONTROL: the gist is printed').toContain('zqescgist');
    expect(t18leaks(texts, V)).toEqual([]);
    expect(t18leaks(texts, W)).toEqual([]);

  it('nodes_fts holds neither value, as Task 8 derives the row and as Task 9\'s backfill re-inserts it (lib\'s nodeIndexTexts)', () => {
    expect(nodeRows().join('\n'), 'CONTROL: the leaf is indexed').toContain('zqescgist');
    expect(t18leaks(nodeRows(), W), 'as derived (Task 8 indexNode)').toEqual([]);
    const w = new T18Db(t18lib.historyPaths(box.home).dbFile);
```

```ts
describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'darwin')('C69: the substring belt on every verb, the index and --regex (Tasks 7A, 7B, 10, 14, 18; spec §8.3 layer 4)', () => {
  const ID = 'claude-a-x18c69';
  const T = 'a1800005';
  const U = t18uuid(T, 0);
  const e = (i: number): string => t18uuid(T, i);
  const ESC = String.fromCharCode(27);
  const BS = String.fromCharCode(92);
  /** Review 351's shape: `Q`, a CSI final byte (`P`), 29 letters and digits, a digit. */
  const V = `QP${t18alnum(29)}7`;
  /** A declared secretsFile's key, which only the shim names: the CLI reads its file through meta redact_sources. */
  const G = `${t18alnum(39)}7`;
  /** A 64-hex value, printed upper-cased in the summary a leaf's gist is taken from. */
  const H = t18hex(32);
  /** V with every eighth character a JSON escape: no literal piece reaches V's belt width. */
  const SPLIT = [...V].map((c, i) => (i % 8 === 7 ? `${BS}u00${c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16)}` : c)).join('');
  let box: t18help.HistoryBox;
  let leaf = '';
  const cli = (args: string[]): T18Run => t18help.runCli(box, args, { env: t18help.withPane(box, ID) });
  /** Each text holding beltWidth(secret) consecutive characters of `secret`, case folded. */
  const beltLeaks = (texts: readonly string[], secret: string): string[] => {
    const w = t18lib.beltWidth(secret);
    const out: string[] = [];
    texts.forEach((t, i) => {
      const low = t.toLowerCase();
      for (let k = 0; k + w <= secret.length; k += 1) {
        if (low.includes(secret.slice(k, k + w).toLowerCase())) { out.push(`#${i}: ${secret.slice(k, k + w)}`); break; }
      }
    });
    return out;
  };
  /** `s` as a reader decodes it: JSON escapes undone, three levels deep. */
  const decoded = (s: string): string => {
    let t = s;
    for (let k = 0; k < 3; k += 1) t = t.split(`${BS}${BS}`).join(BS).replace(/\\u([0-9a-fA-F]{4})/g, (_m, h: string) => String.fromCharCode(parseInt(h, 16)));
    return t;
  };
  /** Every term of an FTS table (fts5vocab, so a value inside a longer term is seen and no prefix compression hides it):
   *  blobs_fts for the rows, nodes_fts for the leaf whose gist is taken from the summary that holds H. */
  const termsOf = (table: 'blobs_fts' | 'nodes_fts'): string[] => {
    const db = t18help.openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      db.exec(`CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS temp.c69_${table} USING fts5vocab(main, ${table}, 'row')`);
      return (db.prepare(`SELECT term FROM temp.c69_${table}`).all() as { term: string }[]).map((r) => r.term);
    } finally { db.close(); }
  };
  const terms = (): string[] => termsOf('blobs_fts');

  t18beforeAll(() => {
    const roster = structuredClone(t18roster) as { version: number; accounts: Record<string, unknown>[] };
    roster.accounts.find((a) => a['id'] === 'gpt')!['exec'] = { kind: 'external', secretsFile: '.config/x18c69-gw/gw.env' };
    box = t18help.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-x18c69-', { roster });
    t18secret(box, '.cc-secrets/x18c69.env', `ZQ_C69_V=${V}\nZQ_C69_H=${H}\n`);
    t18secret(box, '.config/x18c69-gw/gw.env', `GW_C69_KEY=${G}\n`);
    const summary = ['<summary>', '1. Primary Request and Intent:', '   zqc69 intent', '8. Current Work:', `   zqc69 work ${H.toUpperCase()} now`,
      '9. Optional Next Step:', '   zqc69 next step', '</summary>'].join('\n');
    t18help.seedFamily(box, { id: ID, project: 'demo', generation: '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-00000000e018', uuid: U, rows: t18leafRows(T, U, [
      t18fx.userRow({ uuid: e(1), ts: t18ts(1), sessionId: U, text: `zqc69 csi w ${V[0]}${ESC}[0m${ESC}[${V.slice(1)} y` }),
      t18fx.userRow({ uuid: e(2), ts: t18ts(2), parentUuid: e(1), sessionId: U, text: `zqc69 glued ab_${V}_tail and ab${V}cd end` }),
      t18fx.userRow({ uuid: e(3), ts: t18ts(3), parentUuid: e(2), sessionId: U, text: `zqc69 split cfg "${SPLIT}" end` }),
      t18fx.userRow({ uuid: e(4), ts: t18ts(4), parentUuid: e(3), sessionId: U, text: `zqc69 gateway xq${G}zz end` }),
      t18fx.assistantRow({ uuid: e(5), ts: t18ts(5), parentUuid: e(4), sessionId: U, text: 'zqc69 done' }),
    ], summary) });
    // The shim passes the declared secretsFile to the sweep, which records its path in meta redact_sources.
    const r = t18help.runShim(box);
    expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    leaf = t18leafOf(box, ID);
  }, 240_000);

  it('grep, expand, describe and tree, human and --json, print no belt-width stretch of any value, read as written or decoded', () => {
    const runs: T18Run[] = [cli(['grep', 'zqc69']), cli(['grep', 'zqc69', '--json'])];
    for (let i = 1; i <= 4; i += 1) runs.push(cli(['expand', e(i)]), cli(['expand', e(i), '--json']));
    runs.push(cli(['describe', leaf]), cli(['describe', leaf, '--json']), cli(['tree']), cli(['tree', '--json']));
    for (const r of runs) expect(r.code, r.stdout).toBe(0);
    const outs = runs.map((r) => r.stdout);
    expect(outs.join('\n'), 'CONTROL: the rows are printed').toContain('zqc69 glued');
    for (const s of [V, G, H]) {
      expect(beltLeaks(outs, s), s.slice(0, 6)).toEqual([]);
      expect(beltLeaks(outs.map(decoded), s), `${s.slice(0, 6)} decoded as a reader would`).toEqual([]);
    }
  });

  it('no index term holds a belt-width stretch; the stray-CSI remnant is no MATCH, and a stretch is no --regex hit (exit 3)', () => {
    const t = terms();
    expect(t, 'CONTROL: the rows are indexed').toContain('zqc69');
    for (const s of [V, G, H]) expect(beltLeaks(t, s), s.slice(0, 6)).toEqual([]);
    // H is in the summary only, and summary provenance is no blobs_fts term (INDEXED_PROVENANCE), so the loop above
    // cannot see H's index half: nodes_fts, which indexes the leaf's gist (Current Work, the line holding H), can.
    const nt = termsOf('nodes_fts');
    expect(nt, 'CONTROL: H\'s leaf has a nodes_fts row, from the gist line that holds H').toContain('now');
    expect(beltLeaks(nt, H), 'nodes_fts holds no belt-width stretch of H').toEqual([]);
    expect(cli(['grep', V.slice(1)]).code, 'the 31 characters a stray CSI left').toBe(3);
    // An unanchored literal is no whole word, so regexPrefilter answers null and the child scans every in-scope blob.
    expect(cli(['grep', '--regex', V.slice(2, 16)]).code).toBe(3);
    expect(cli(['grep', '--regex', G.slice(3, 17)]).code).toBe(3);
  });

  it('the --regex child names a malformed job in fixed words, never echoing the units it was handed', async () => {
    const { spawnSync } = await import('node:child_process');
    const worker = new URL('../../ccd/history/regex-worker.mjs', import.meta.url).pathname;
    const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--no-warnings', worker], { input: `{"belt":["${V}"`, encoding: 'utf8' });
    expect(r.status).toBe(1);
    expect(r.stderr).toContain('the job on stdin is not JSON');
    expect(r.stderr).not.toContain(V.slice(2, 16));
  });
});
```

`T18Run` carries no `stderr` (Step 1's type), so a CLI run's assertion message is its `stdout`; `runShim`'s result carries `stderr`.

- [ ] **Step 2A: Show every recalled field through `redactForDisplay` (Task 7A; spec §8.3 "Where it runs").** From the repository root:


The rename covers recall.mjs's named import from `./lib.mjs` (it becomes Task 7A's `redactForDisplay`), its `xlib.` namespace calls, every call and the comments that name the call: grep's query echo (Tasks 12, 13) and its group headings' gists (13), describe's gist, topics and refs (15), tree's gists (10), and expand's tool path (16). The windowed displays are not renamed and need no rename: grep's snippet (lib's `displaySnippet`), describe's excerpt and pages, and expand's cuts, pages and outline input all go through Task 12's `redactDisplayWindow`, which reads through `redactForDisplay` itself. `redactDisplayWindow` is matched by neither `\bredactField\b` nor `\bredactForIndex\b`, so the `sed` leaves it alone; the count of 2 reads its two call sites (an import line holds no `(` after the name). A display site Task 12 or 16 already moved to `redactForIndex` is renamed too: `redactForDisplay` IS `redactForIndex` up to `DISPLAY_READINGS_MAX`, and past it reads span by span where `redactForIndex` would read the whole text. If recall.mjs's named import held both names, the clause now names `redactForDisplay` twice and `node --check` reports the duplicate binding: delete the second. The `--regex` child is not edited: it matches the index's own text (`entryIndexText`, Task 14), so its readings are the index's already. `cli.mjs` keeps `redactFinal`, the second belt over the whole output, and the derivation (Tasks 4, 8, 9) keeps `redactField` for the stored fields. - [ ] **Step 3: Fix any red at its site.**

For every recalled field, the order is: the FULL raw text, then `redactForDisplay` (Task 7A: `redactField`'s layers, the belt included, over B1's escape readings), then any cut, snippet, excerpt, page, outline or cursor boundary, then the escape (`recallEnvelope`, or `JSON.stringify` of the envelope), then `redactFinal` over the whole rendered string. A display that shows a window of a longer text (a snippet, an excerpt, a page, a cut, an outline's input) redacts that window with `ENTRY_REDACT_MARGIN` each side through Task 12's `redactDisplayWindow`, never the whole text, and the cut follows that redaction (spec §8.3 and §8.4). Locate each verb's cut sites with:
`grep -nE 'displaySnippet\(|redactDisplayWindow\(|exploreOutline\(|nextLine\(|cutText\(|pageEnd\(|DESCRIBE_EXCERPT|\.slice\(0, |explore\(|regexSyntaxHint\(' ccd/history/recall.mjs ccd/history/cli.mjs ccd/history/regex-worker.mjs`

Each site's input must already be `redactForDisplay`'s output, or `redactDisplayWindow`'s for a window (the `--regex` child's, `entryIndexText`'s). The sites, by verb:

| Verb (task) | Field | Its cut or escape site | Redacted before it by |
|---|---|---|---|
| grep (12, 13) | the hit's text | lib's `displaySnippet`: `snippetWindow` over the redacted window, then the single-line cut to `SNIPPET_MAX` | Task 12's `displayWindow` (the one `redactDisplayWindow` wraps) on the window around the hit in `blobPlainText`'s RAW body: the window and its margins read through `redactForDisplay`'s reading, escape readings included, never the whole body |
| grep (13) | the covering leaf's gist in each group heading | `snippetLine`, the envelope | `redactForDisplay` on the stored gist |
| grep (12, 13) | the query echoed in `next:` and in a `hint:` | `nextLine(args)`, `regexSyntaxHint` | `redactForDisplay` on each argument |
| grep `--regex` (14) | the text the worker matches | the regex match itself | `entryIndexText` inside `regex-worker.mjs`, per blob: the index's own text and readings, with the parent's belt units from the job. The worker prints nothing of it but the match, which seeds the parent's snippet; the printed snippet is the grep (13) row's |
| describe (15) | gist, topics, refs, files | the envelope | `redactForDisplay` on each stored field (gists are derived redacted, Task 8; the late-pair re-derivation is Task 29's) |
| describe (15) | the summary's 4k excerpt, and each `--full` page | `DESCRIBE_EXCERPT`, the page boundary | `redactDisplayWindow` (`shownSummary`) on that window of the RAW summary |
| tree (10) | each gist | the envelope | `redactForDisplay` on the stored gist |
| expand (16) | a row's text | the 2k cut, the outline, the page | `redactDisplayWindow` (`shownOf`) on that window of `renderEntryText`'s RAW rendering, whose escape readings separate a value JSON glued onto a leaf or a key; the outline through `exploreOutline` |
| expand (16) | a sidecar's text | the 2k cut, the outline, the page | `redactDisplayWindow` (`shownOf`) on that window of the RAW decoded sidecar; the outline through `exploreOutline` (counts only past `EXPLORE_READ_MAX`) |
| every verb (10) | the whole stdout, stderr and `--json` | none, it is the last pass | `redactFinal` over the final string (B1's `redactField`, so the belt with its decoded readings) |

Choices this task makes:
- **Under `--json`, stdout carries only the envelope.** The sweep's relayed lines (an import's `mapped`/`unmapped` listing, a migration's line) go to stderr, through `redactFinal`.
- **A relayed line is redacted with the read verbs' index** (coordinator ruling, theme T2). `runOpVerb` builds it once the gate has passed and before the shim starts (`relayIndexOf`: Task 10's `pairIndexOf`, the recorded pairs plus the frozen list and meta `redact_sources`' files read now, with their belt), so a refused form reads no secret file, and the handle it read through is closed before the op runs. Where the store cannot be read (an unsettled stat, no DB before a rebuild or a restore, a StoreError or SQLite error on the open or a select), the index is the files read now with their belt. Step 2's relay-redaction case pins it through the CLI door (a declared secretsFile's value and a stray-CSI split of a frozen value, both redacted on stdout and, under `--json`, on stderr), and Step 7's mutants (i) (no `redactFinal`) and (j) (the frozen list's index alone, no belt) each turn it red.
- **The relay is a streaming one.** Each stdout line is printed as soon as the next one arrives. The last line is held back: when it is the sweep's `{"rc"…}`, it goes to `decideRelay`; anything else is printed, and the relay answers exit 1.
- **The `--op` pass is split into tables.**

  - `BINDING_PASSES` is the place adopt, restore and rebuild run, BEFORE `openStore`. It is empty here, so they answer `bad-args`. Task 26 replaces the table and its branch with one call to `bindingPass(home, P, op, args, deps, out)`, which Tasks 26–28 fill. That call keeps this branch's `released` answer, with the writer ids re-read from the files after the bind and a journal failure the arm already counted passed as `counted`, and answers a throw out of it through `opThrowResult(e, (rc, reason) => released(rc, reason))`, as B1's `openStore` catch does, so the half at release runs on that path too (Task 26's Choices).

B1's `history-op.test.ts` describes `Task 26F item 2`, `Task 26F items 3 and 4`, `Task 26F item 5`, `FR2-c`, `RF5a F19: the half at release runs on every --op outcome` and `the op marker (§9.6)` are the guard: Step 6 runs them, and they must stay green.

The store's presence is decided by Task 6's `decideOpDoor` over those facts (`store.id` and the DB, through B1's `decideCliStore`), never from whether the history root exists. No third copy of either is written. So a shim-less box with a store answers `writer-absent`, and one whose store root dangles or whose stat does not settle answers exit 5 `store-root-dangling` or `store-unreachable` at the door, as `status` would.
- **RB6 is measured in both halves; the sweep's is authoritative.**
  - The sweep half: after the role check, the lock-take journal half and the statfs probe, `opPass` reads `recoverStepAt(P.dbFile)` and, on `open`, runs `decideOpGate` again with `recovering: true` and the three facts RB13 and RB14 read (`storedVersion`, `codeVersion`, `storeId`), before the binding branch and `openStore`. adopt on a bound store is therefore refused before `bindingPass`, and no refused form writes the op marker, flushes the outbox or opens the writer.

Its facts are `storedVersionAt` on the same file, lib's `SCHEMA_VERSION`, and the `store.id` presence `measureReach` already read, so it never refuses a form the sweep would let through.
  - A dry run (null form) is never measured and never refused; `restore` and `rebuild` pass Task 6's row and replace the step.
- **`doctor --migrate` while recovering (coordinator ruling RB13).** `--migrate` is refused `recovering` only when the store's stored `user_version` already equals the code's. A restored backup older than the code (a `pre-v<N>.db`), whose migration may answer `snapshot-needs-op`, therefore migrates through the door while its recovery step stays registered, and the step runs at the code's version on a later pass: it never waits for an op that waits on it. A store newer than the code passes the row too and meets `openStore`'s own `schema-newer`, which `--migrate` answers `migrate-refused` (C63).
- **`doctor --adopt` while recovering (coordinator ruling RB14)** is measured here and pinned in Task 26: the gate's `storeId` fact is `store.id`'s presence, and only `absent` exempts.
- **One pane rule for both doors.** B1's `paneNameFor` (sweep) and this task's `opPaneName` (cli) each keep their own bounded tmux call, but whether a form reads a pane at all is lib's `paneReadWanted`, so the two doors cannot drift apart on it.

```ts
import { spawn as spawnHolder } from 'node:child_process';
```

Append at the end of the file:

```ts
// ── W1-B2 Task 19: the operator door's stand-ins ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
/** Replace the box's placed shim with a stand-in: it appends its argv, one line per run, to
 *  `<home>/stub-shim-argv`, prints `stdout` verbatim and exits `exit`. The CLI's relay is then measured against an
 *  answer the case chose; a case that must spawn nothing reads the argv file as absent. A box keeps its stand-in;
 *  a case that needs the real shim builds its own box. */
export function stubShim(box: HistoryBox, script: { stdout: string; exit: number }): void {
  const quote = (s: string): string => `'${s.replace(/'/g, `'\\''`)}'`;
  const p = path.join(box.home, '.local', 'bin', 'ccd-history-sweep');
  fs.writeFileSync(p, [
    '#!/usr/bin/env bash',
    'printf \'%s\\n\' "$*" >> "$HOME/stub-shim-argv"',
    `printf '%s' ${quote(script.stdout)}`,
    `exit ${script.exit}`,
    '',
  ].join('\n'));
  fs.chmodSync(p, 0o755);
}

/** Hold the shim's lock from outside, as a first concurrent pass holds it: a `flock` holder that sleeps, in its own
 *  process group, until the returned release kills it. Returns only once the lock is really taken. */
export function holdLock(box: HistoryBox): () => void {
  const lock = historyPaths(box.home).lock;
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(lock), { recursive: true });
  const holder = spawnHolder('flock', [lock, 'sleep', '120'], { stdio: 'ignore', detached: true });
  const release = (): void => {
    try { process.kill(-holder.pid!, 'SIGKILL'); } catch { /* already gone */ }
  };
  for (let i = 0; i < 200; i += 1) {
    if (spawnSync('flock', ['-n', lock, 'true']).status !== 0) return release;
    Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, 25);
  }
  release();
  throw new Error('holdLock: the holder never took the lock');
}
```
