```ts
const G1 = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-00000000a019';
const U1 = '19000001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001';
const SLUG = '-home-u-tree-maint';
const V2 = 'CREATE TABLE seam_v2 (x INTEGER)';
const TS = new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 9, 4, 10, 0, 0)).toISOString();

interface Run { code: number | null; stdout: string; stderr: string; json: Record<string, unknown> | null }
const op = (box: HistoryBox, args: string[], env: Record<string, string> = {}): Run => runCli(box, args, { env });
function boundBox(prefix: string): HistoryBox {
  const box = makeHistoryBox(prefix, { role: 'fleet', shim: true });
  const r = runSweep(box);
  expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
  return box;
}
/** What the stand-in shim was asked, one argv per run; null when it never ran. */
const stubArgv = (box: HistoryBox): string[] | null => {
  const p = path.join(box.home, 'stub-shim-argv');
  return fs.existsSync(p) ? fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8').trim().split('\n') : null;
};
const dbFile = (box: HistoryBox): string => path.join(box.root, 'db', 'history.db');
const storeIdOf = (box: HistoryBox): string => fs.readFileSync(path.join(box.root, 'store.id'), 'utf8').trim();
const sha = (p: string): string => createHash('sha256').update(fs.readFileSync(p)).digest('hex');
const versionOf = (p: string): number => {
  const db = new DatabaseSync(p, { readOnly: true });
  try { return (db.prepare('PRAGMA user_version').get() as { user_version: number }).user_version; } finally { db.close(); }
};
const snapshotsIn = (box: HistoryBox): string[] => {
  try { return fs.readdirSync(path.join(box.root, 'db', 'backups')).filter((n) => n.startsWith('pre-v')); } catch { return []; }
};
/** The --op pass's one JSON result, its LAST stdout line. */
const lastResult = (stdout: string): Record<string, unknown> => {
  const lines = stdout.split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l.startsWith('{"rc"'));
  expect(lines.length, `no {"rc":…} line in:\n${stdout}`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  return JSON.parse(lines[lines.length - 1]!) as Record<string, unknown>;
};
/** Every entry under ~/.ccrc with each file's size and mtime: "writes nothing", measured. The lock and SQLite's
 *  WAL sidecars are excluded (a read-only open may create the sidecars, §8.1). */
function snapshot(box: HistoryBox): string[] {
  const root = path.join(box.home, '.ccrc');
  const out: string[] = [];
  const visit = (d: string): void => {
    for (const e of fs.readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      if (e.name === 'history-sweep.lock' || /-(wal|shm)$/.test(e.name)) continue;
      const p = path.join(d, e.name);
      if (e.isDirectory()) { out.push(`${path.relative(root, p)}/`); visit(p); continue; }
      const st = fs.lstatSync(p);
      out.push(`${path.relative(root, p)} ${st.size} ${Math.trunc(st.mtimeMs)}`);
    }
  };
  visit(root);
  return out.sort();
}
/** The real shim, exec'ing B1's run-pass driver in place of sweep.mjs: the driver's HISTORY_TEST_DEPS (its only
 *  seam) can then stage a v2 migration behind the CLI's own door, lock and roster included. */
function driverShim(box: HistoryBox): void {
  const text = fs.readFileSync(SHIM, 'utf8');
  const from = '"$HOME/ccrc/ccd/history/sweep.mjs"';
  expect(text, 'CONTROL: the shim execs sweep.mjs through the ~/ccrc link').toContain(from);
  const p = path.join(box.home, '.local', 'bin', 'ccd-history-sweep');
  fs.writeFileSync(p, text.replace(from, JSON.stringify(PASS_DRIVER)));
  fs.chmodSync(p, 0o755);
}
const PENDING = { HISTORY_TEST_DEPS: JSON.stringify({ extraMigrations: [V2] }) };

describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'darwin')('O54 (relay half): the CLI and the shim agree (Task 19)', () => {
  it('a refusal decided under the lock reaches the operator: {"rc":2,"reason":"adopt-refused"} is exit 2 with that reason', () => {
    const box = boundBox('ccrc-hist-o54a-');
    stubShim(box, { stdout: '{"rc":2,"reason":"adopt-refused"}\n', exit: 2 });
    const r = op(box, ['doctor', '--backup', '--json']);
    expect(r.code).toBe(2);
    expect(r.json).toMatchObject({ exit: 2, reason: 'adopt-refused', coverage: 'this-box' });
    expect(r.json?.['store_id']).toBe(storeIdOf(box));
    expect(stubArgv(box), 'the CLI ran the shim with the --op form, and nothing else').toEqual(['--op backup']);
  });

  it('75 from the shim (its lock held) is exit 4 writer-busy, in both forms', () => {
    const box = boundBox('ccrc-hist-o54b-');
    stubShim(box, { stdout: '', exit: 75 });
    const j = op(box, ['doctor', '--backup', '--json']);
    expect([j.code, j.json?.['reason']]).toEqual([4, 'writer-busy']);
    const h = op(box, ['doctor', '--backup']);
    expect(h.code).toBe(4);
    expect(h.stderr).toMatch(/^ccrc history doctor: writer-busy: /m);
  });

  it('the real shim with its lock held: exit 4, and nothing written', () => {
    const box = boundBox('ccrc-hist-o54c-');
    const before = snapshot(box);
    const release = holdLock(box);
    try {
      const r = op(box, ['import', '--apply', '--json']);
      expect([r.code, r.json?.['reason']]).toEqual([4, 'writer-busy']);
    } finally { release(); }
    expect(snapshot(box)).toEqual(before);
  });

  it('a result the relay cannot trust is exit 1: a reason off its exit, no result, a result the exit contradicts, no JSON', () => {
    const box = boundBox('ccrc-hist-o54d-');
    for (const [stdout, exit] of [['{"rc":2,"reason":"store-missing"}\n', 2], ['', 0], ['{"rc":5,"reason":"store-missing"}\n', 0], ['not json\n', 0]] as const) {
      stubShim(box, { stdout, exit });
      const r = op(box, ['doctor', '--backup', '--json']);
      expect([r.code, r.json?.['exit']], JSON.stringify(stdout)).toEqual([1, 1]);
    }
  });

  it('the sweep\'s lines before its result are relayed in order and the result line is not; under --json they go to stderr', () => {
    const box = boundBox('ccrc-hist-o54e-');
    stubShim(box, { stdout: 'line one\nline two\n{"rc":0}\n', exit: 0 });
    const h = op(box, ['doctor', '--backup']);
    expect(h.code, h.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(h.stdout).toBe('line one\nline two\n');
    const j = op(box, ['doctor', '--backup', '--json']);
    expect(j.code).toBe(0);
    expect(j.stdout.trim().split('\n'), 'stdout is the envelope alone').toHaveLength(1);
    expect(j.json).toMatchObject({ exit: 0, coverage: 'this-box' });
    expect(j.stderr).toContain('line one\nline two\n');
  });
});

describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'darwin')('the relay redaction: every line the relay passes on goes through redactFinal with the read verbs\' index, belt included (Task 19; spec §8.3 layers 1 and 4)', () => {
  it('a declared secretsFile value and a stray-CSI split of a frozen value come out redacted, human and --json', () => {
    const AL = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789';
    const alnum = (n: number): string => Array.from(randomBytes(n), (b) => AL[b % AL.length]!).join('');
    const ESC = String.fromCharCode(27);
    /** A frozen-list value of review 351's shape (C69's V): `Q`, a CSI final byte (`P`), 29 letters and digits, a digit. */
    const V = `QP${alnum(29)}7`;
    /** A declared secretsFile's key (C69's G): only the shim names its file, so the CLI reads it through meta redact_sources
     *  and finds its pair in redact_hashes. No shape matches it (C49's shape), so only those layers mask it. */
    const G = `${alnum(39)}7`;
    /** Each beltWidth(s) stretch of the value `s` found in `text`, case folded (C69's measure: §8.3 layer 4's promise). */
    const leaks = (text: string, s: string): string[] => {
      const w = beltWidth(s);
      const low = text.toLowerCase();
      const out: string[] = [];
      for (let k = 0; k + w <= s.length; k += 1) if (low.includes(s.slice(k, k + w).toLowerCase())) out.push(s.slice(k, k + w));
      return out;
    };
    const roster = structuredClone(DEFAULT_TEST_ROSTER) as { version: number; accounts: Record<string, unknown>[] };
    roster.accounts.find((a) => a['id'] === 'gpt')!['exec'] = { kind: 'external', secretsFile: '.config/x19-gw/gw.env' };
    const box = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-relay-red-', { role: 'fleet', shim: true, roster });
    const secret = (rel: string, body: string): void => {
      const p = path.join(box.home, rel);
      fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(p), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
      fs.writeFileSync(p, body, { mode: 0o600 });
    };
    secret('.cc-secrets/x19relay.env', `ZQ_X19_V=${V}\n`);
    secret('.config/x19-gw/gw.env', `GW_X19_KEY=${G}\n`);
    // The real shim's pass creates the store, records both values' pairs and the declared file's path (meta
    // redact_sources, Task 7B): the shim reads the roster's secretsFile from accounts.sh and passes it to the sweep.
    const bound = runShim(box);
    expect(bound.code, bound.stderr).toBe(0);
    // The stand-in then prints both shapes on lines the relay passes on: G whole, and V behind a stray CSI that took its
    // second character, so the 31 characters after it are one run that no pair matches and only the belt masks.
    stubShim(box, { stdout: `zqx19 gateway ${G} end\nzqx19 csi w ${V[0]}${ESC}[0m${ESC}[${V.slice(1)} y\n{"rc":0}\n`, exit: 0 });
    const h = op(box, ['doctor', '--backup']);
    expect(h.code, h.stderr).toBe(0);
    const j = op(box, ['doctor', '--backup', '--json']);
    expect(j.code, j.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(stubArgv(box), 'CONTROL: both runs reached the stand-in').toEqual(['--op backup', '--op backup']);
    expect(h.stdout, 'CONTROL: the lines are relayed to stdout').toContain('zqx19 gateway');
    expect(h.stdout, 'CONTROL: both of them').toContain('zqx19 csi w');
    expect(j.stderr, 'CONTROL: under --json, to stderr').toContain('zqx19 gateway');
    // One assertion per stream over both values, so a red names every leak at once: G (the declared secretsFile's value)
    // and V (the stray-CSI split of a frozen value).
    for (const [where, text] of [['human stdout', h.stdout], ['--json stderr', j.stderr]] as const) {
      expect({ G: leaks(text, G), V: leaks(text, V) }, `${where}: no belt-width stretch of either value`).toEqual({ G: [], V: [] });
    }
  }, 120_000);
});

describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'darwin')('the no-store table and the speed bumps: decided by the CLI before any spawn (Task 19)', () => {
  it('a server role, and a box that never installed, answer 9; a store with no shim answers 2 writer-absent', () => {
    const server = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-door-srv-', { role: 'server', shim: true });
    stubShim(server, { stdout: '{"rc":0}\n', exit: 0 });
    expect(op(server, ['doctor', '--backup', '--json']).code).toBe(9);
    expect(stubArgv(server), 'never spawned').toBeNull();
    const never = makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-door-none-', { role: 'fleet', shim: false });
    const n = op(never, ['import', '--json']);
    expect([n.code, n.json?.['reason']]).toEqual([9, undefined]);
    const absent = boundBox('ccrc-hist-door-abs-');
    fs.rmSync(path.join(absent.home, '.local', 'bin', 'ccd-history-sweep'));
    const a = op(absent, ['import', '--apply', '--json']);
    expect([a.code, a.json?.['reason']]).toEqual([2, 'writer-absent']);
  });

  it('arguments are refused by lib\'s one grammar before any spawn, each with its word', () => {
    const box = boundBox('ccrc-hist-door-args-');
    stubShim(box, { stdout: '{"rc":0}\n', exit: 0 });
    const cases: Array<[string[], string]> = [
      [['prune', '--older-than', '7d'], 'older-than-floor'],
      [['doctor', '--restore', 'a/b.db'], 'restore-refused'],
      [['doctor', '--repair', '--backup'], 'bad-args'],
      [['doctor', '--bogus'], 'bad-args'],
      [['import', '--session', '../x', '--file', `/home/u/x/${U1}.jsonl`], 'bad-id'],
      [['import', '--bogus'], 'bad-args'],
    ];
    for (const [args, reason] of cases) {
      const r = op(box, [...args, '--json']);
      expect([r.code, r.json?.['reason']], args.join(' ')).toEqual([2, reason]);
    }
    expect(stubArgv(box), 'no refused form reached the shim').toBeNull();
  });

  it('the speed bumps: CLAUDECODE refuses a writing form, history-off refuses a non-binding one, an irreversible one needs a TTY; a dry run passes', () => {
    const box = boundBox('ccrc-hist-door-gate-');
    stubShim(box, { stdout: '{"rc":0}\n', exit: 0 });
    const cc = op(box, ['doctor', '--backup', '--json'], { CLAUDECODE: '1' });
    expect([cc.code, cc.json?.['reason']]).toEqual([2, 'apply-in-session']);
    expect(op(box, ['doctor', '--adopt', '--json']).json?.['reason'], 'adopt is irreversible: no TTY here').toBe('needs-tty');
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(box.home, '.ccrc', 'history-off'), '');
    try {
      const off = op(box, ['doctor', '--migrate', '--json']);
      expect([off.code, off.json?.['reason']]).toEqual([2, 'history-off']);
    } finally { fs.rmSync(path.join(box.home, '.ccrc', 'history-off')); }
    expect(stubArgv(box), 'no refused form reached the shim').toBeNull();
    const dry = op(box, ['import'], { CLAUDECODE: '1' });
    expect(dry.code, 'a dry run is no writing form: it passes CLAUDECODE').toBe(0);
    expect(stubArgv(box)).toEqual(['--op import']);
  });

  it('bare doctor prints the status health lines and spawns nothing; with --json it is the status envelope', () => {
    const box = boundBox('ccrc-hist-door-doc-');
    stubShim(box, { stdout: '{"rc":0}\n', exit: 0 });
    const h = op(box, ['doctor']);
    expect(h.code, h.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(h.stdout).toMatch(/^health: (PASS|WARN|FAIL) /m);
    const j = op(box, ['doctor', '--json']);
    expect(j.json?.['health']).toBeDefined();
    expect(j.json?.['store_id']).toBe(storeIdOf(box));
    expect(stubArgv(box)).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'darwin')('C42 (CLI half): import maps from evidence only (Task 19)', () => {
  it('the dry run lists every mapped and unmapped file and writes nothing; --apply ingests the mapped only', () => {
    const box = boundBox('ccrc-hist-c42cli-');
    plantSession(box, ID, { uuid: U1, generation: G1, project: 'maint' });
    const mapped = plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', SLUG, U1, [userRow({ uuid: '19000001-0000-4000-8000-0000000000a1', ts: TS, sessionId: U1, text: 'mapped words' })]);
    const unmapped: string[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 120; i += 1) {
      const u = `19000003-0000-4000-8000-${String(i).padStart(12, '0')}`;
      unmapped.push(plantTranscript(box, 'claude-b', SLUG, u, [userRow({ uuid: `19000004-0000-4000-8000-${String(i).padStart(12, '0')}`, ts: TS, sessionId: u, text: 'no evidence names me' })]));
    }
    const before = snapshot(box);
    const dry = op(box, ['import']);
    expect(dry.code, dry.stderr).toBe(0);
    const lines = dry.stdout.split('\n').filter(Boolean);
    expect(lines).toContain(`mapped ${ID} ${G1} ${mapped}`);
    expect(lines.filter((l) => l.startsWith('unmapped ')).sort()).toEqual(unmapped.map((p) => `unmapped ${p}`).sort());
    expect(lines.some((l) => l.startsWith('{"rc"')), 'the result line is the relay\'s, never printed').toBe(false);
    expect(snapshot(box), 'a dry run writes nothing').toEqual(before);
    const apply = op(box, ['import', '--apply', '--json']);
    expect(apply.code, apply.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(apply.json).toMatchObject({ exit: 0, coverage: 'this-box' });
    expect(apply.stderr, 'under --json the sweep\'s listing goes to stderr').toContain('unmapped ');
    const db = openStoreRO(box);
    try {
      const uuids = (db.prepare('SELECT cc_session_uuid FROM transcripts').all() as { cc_session_uuid: string }[]).map((r) => r.cc_session_uuid);
      expect(uuids).toContain(U1);
      expect(uuids.filter((u) => u.startsWith('19000003')), 'an unmapped file is never ingested').toEqual([]);
    } finally { db.close(); }
  });
});

describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'darwin')('RB6: while a recovery step is registered, a writing form is refused recovering at both doors (Task 19)', () => {
  /** A bound store holding an open ('recover', <ms>) step, as restore and rebuild leave one (Tasks 27, 28), planted
   *  by SQL. Only import and migrate are --op verbs at this task, and no case here has a TTY: Task 25's RB6 case
   *  runs every writing form on a terminal, and Tasks 27 and 28 show restore and rebuild are never refused. */
  function recoveringBox(prefix: string): HistoryBox {
    const box = boundBox(prefix);
    const w = new DatabaseSync(dbFile(box));
    try {
      w.prepare("INSERT INTO derivation_state (step, version, cursor, completed_ms) VALUES ('recover', ?, NULL, NULL)").run(Date.UTC(2026, 9, 4));
      w.exec('PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)');
    } finally { w.close(); }
    return box;
  }

  it('the direct door: import --apply and migrate answer {rc:2, reason:"recovering"} and write nothing; the import dry run answers 0', () => {
    const box = recoveringBox('ccrc-hist-rb6a-');
    const before = snapshot(box);
    expect(lastResult(runShim(box, ['--op', 'import', '--apply']).stdout)).toEqual({ rc: 2, reason: 'recovering' });
    expect(lastResult(runShim(box, ['--op', 'migrate']).stdout)).toEqual({ rc: 2, reason: 'recovering' });
    // No op marker, no outbox flush, no writer open. No spool line is pending here, so the lock-take journal half,
    // which runs before the measure, and the half at release, which B1's `released` runs on the refusal, write nothing
    // either.
    expect(snapshot(box), 'a refused form writes nothing').toEqual(before);
    expect(lastResult(runShim(box, ['--op', 'import']).stdout), 'a dry run is no writing form').toEqual({ rc: 0 });
  });

  it('the CLI door: import --apply, doctor --backup and doctor --migrate answer 2 recovering before any spawn; the import dry run reaches the shim', () => {
    const box = recoveringBox('ccrc-hist-rb6b-');
    stubShim(box, { stdout: '{"rc":0}\n', exit: 0 });
    for (const args of [['import', '--apply'], ['doctor', '--backup'], ['doctor', '--migrate']]) {
      const r = op(box, [...args, '--json']);
      expect([r.code, r.json?.['reason']], args.join(' ')).toEqual([2, 'recovering']);
    }
    expect(stubArgv(box), 'the CLI refused each before it spawned').toBeNull();
    expect(op(box, ['import']).code, 'a dry run passes').toBe(0);
    expect(stubArgv(box)).toEqual(['--op import']);
  });

  it('RB13, the direct door: migrate is refused while the stored user_version equals the code\'s; a store older than the code migrates, and its step stays for a later pass', () => {
    const box = recoveringBox('ccrc-hist-rb13a-');
    driverShim(box);
    const openStep = (): number => {
      const db = new DatabaseSync(dbFile(box), { readOnly: true });
      try {
        return (db.prepare("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'recover' AND completed_ms IS NULL").get() as { n: number }).n;
      } finally { db.close(); }
    };
    // Stored 1, code 1: the refusal stands.
    expect(lastResult(runShim(box, ['--op', 'migrate']).stdout), 'stored = code').toEqual({ rc: 2, reason: 'recovering' });
    expect(versionOf(dbFile(box))).toBe(1);
    // Stored 1, code 2 (a v2 migration staged): a restored older backup migrates rather than wait on its own step.
    const m = runShim(box, ['--op', 'migrate'], { env: PENDING });
    expect(lastResult(m.stdout), `${m.stdout}\n${m.stderr}`).toEqual({ rc: 0 });
    expect(versionOf(dbFile(box))).toBe(2);
    expect(snapshotsIn(box)).toEqual(['pre-v2.db']);
```

```js
// ── W1-B2 Task 19: a registered recovery step and the stored version, measured read-only (RB6, RB13) ──────────
/** An open ('recover', <bind ms>) step: what restore and rebuild register (§9.14), and what refuses every writing
 *  --op form lib's recoveryExempt does not exempt meanwhile (RB6 with RB12-RB14, slug
 *  history-ops-refused-while-recovering; lib's decideOpGate decides). */
const RECOVER_OPEN_SQL = "SELECT 1 AS x FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'recover' AND completed_ms IS NULL LIMIT 1";

/** Whether db/history.db holds an open recovery step, on its OWN read-only handle, closed before it returns, so it
 *  can run before any writer opens the store. Four answers, kept apart: 'absent' (no file), 'unmeasured' (the
 *  file would not open read-only, or has no derivation_state), 'none' and 'open'. A caller refuses on 'open' only
 *  and leaves every other answer to the store's own refusal words further on (openStore, decideBind). */
export function recoverStepAt(dbFile) {
  if (dbFileState(dbFile) === 'absent') return 'absent';
  let db;
  try { db = openReader(dbFile); } catch { return 'unmeasured'; }
  try {
    return db.prepare(RECOVER_OPEN_SQL).get() === undefined ? 'none' : 'open';
  } catch {
    return 'unmeasured';
  } finally {
    db.close();
  }
}

/** history.db's own user_version, on its OWN read-only handle, closed before it returns: the stored-version fact
 *  decideOpGate's RB13 exemption reads while a recovery step is open (both halves), and the one decideBind's adopt
 *  arm decides a newer store by (RB17, through sweep.mjs's bindFactsOf). A Presence, never a bare number: 'absent'
 *  (no file) and 'unreadable' (the file would not open read-only, or the pragma would not read) stay apart from a
 *  value, so an unmeasured version is never read as one (IV5). B1's peekVersion stays openStore's throwing peek. */
export function storedVersionAt(dbFile) {
  if (dbFileState(dbFile) === 'absent') return { state: 'absent' };
  let db;
  try { db = openReader(dbFile); } catch { return { state: 'unreadable' }; }
  try {
    const v = userVersion(db);
    return Number.isSafeInteger(v) && v >= 0 ? { state: 'value', value: v } : { state: 'unreadable' };
  } catch {
    return { state: 'unreadable' };
  } finally {
    db.close();
  }
}
```

(e) Replace the `OP_VERBS` declaration and `parseOpArgs` (each with its doc comment, from `/** The --op verbs B1 runs` through `parseOpArgs`'s closing brace) with:

```js
/** The --op verbs this build runs (§8.4). Each B2 verb joins in the task that ships its path (Tasks 20–28): a verb
 *  named here has an entry in OP_HANDLERS or BINDING_PASSES, and one in OP_DRY_RUNS when it has a dry run. */
const OP_VERBS = new Set(['import', 'migrate']);

/** adopt, restore and rebuild (§8.4): they run BEFORE openStore, which refuses exactly the states they exist to
 *  repair (store-unbound, store-missing, store-recoverable, store-zero-byte, store-schema-missing, …). */
const BINDING_OPS = new Set(BIND_KINDS);

/** The verbs whose rows the code's schema version shapes: a store awaiting its migration refuses them
 *  (migration-pending). backup and migrate run at any stored version; the binding verbs never reach openStore. */
const OP_NEEDS_CODE_VERSION = new Set(['import', 'prune', 'reparse', 'repair']);

/** Each verb's dry run, its null form (§8.4 "dry run by default"): READ-ONLY, after the bounded reachability probe,
 *  with no journal half, no op marker and no flush. c = {home, P, parsed, args, deps, out, now}; answers
 *  {rc, reason?}. */
const OP_DRY_RUNS = Object.freeze({
  import: async (c) => {
    importDryRun(c.P, c.parsed.homes, c.args, c.out);
    return { rc: EXIT.OK };
  },
});

/** Each writing verb's body, on the store openStore opened, under the lock, after the lock-take journal half, the
 *  op marker and the first outbox flush. c = {db, ctx, P, args, opened, free}; answers {rc, reason?}. An rc of 0 is
 *  followed by the release flush and journal half (§8.4: every writing form flushes before it exits 0). */
const OP_HANDLERS = Object.freeze({
  import: (c) => importApply(c.db, c.ctx, c.P, c.args),
  migrate: (c) => migrateOp(c.db, c.ctx, c.opened, c.free),
});

/** The binding verbs' place, run in place of openStore and a handler. Empty in this task, so adopt, restore and
 *  rebuild answer bad-args; W1-B2 Task 26 replaces this table and its branch in opPass with one call to
 *  bindingPass, which Tasks 26–28 fill. */
const BINDING_PASSES = Object.freeze({});

/** B1's name, kept: a verb's arguments by lib's one grammar (parseOpVerbArgs), or null when refused. opPass
 *  reads parseOpVerbArgs itself, for the refusal's word. */
export function parseOpArgs(op, args) {
  if (!OP_VERBS.has(op)) return null;
  const p = parseOpVerbArgs(op, args);
  return p.ok ? p.args : null;
}
```

```js
// `ccrc history import|prune|reparse …` and `ccrc history doctor --repair|--backup|--migrate|--adopt|
// --restore <file>|--rebuild [--store-id <uuid>]` (spec §8.4 "Operator verbs" and "Speed bumps", §8.3's no-store

//   2. the door, by decideOpDoor over cliFactsOf(reach) (§8.3's one no-store table, decideCliStore, from store.id
//      and the DB). macOS, a recorded server role and a box that never installed answer 9; a store with no shim
//      answers 2 writer-absent (a plain uninstall kept the data); an unreachable or dangling store answers its 5;
//   3. THE GATE, decideOpGate, from this process's CLAUDECODE, isatty(0), a registered recovery step with the facts

//      the sweep's own isatty(0) is the operator's terminal. stdout is piped and relayed line by line as it arrives
//      (an import's dry run can list thousands of files). Its LAST line, the sweep's `{"rc":…}`, is held back for
//      decideRelay: 75 (the shim found the lock held) is exit 4 writer-busy, a well-formed result is its rc and
//      reason, and anything else is exit 1.

// this process's, so the env allow-list holds.
// Bare `doctor` is the status health, read-only (slug history-bare-doctor-is-status-health, NEW: §8.4 lists the
// bare form without saying what it does; those lines are what doctor's history check relays).

/** A CLI operator verb, or a doctor flag, → the --op verb the sweep runs. */
export const OP_OF_VERB = Object.freeze({
  import: 'import', prune: 'prune', reparse: 'reparse',
  '--repair': 'repair', '--backup': 'backup', '--migrate': 'migrate', '--adopt': 'adopt', '--restore': 'restore', '--rebuild': 'rebuild',
});

/** What a human reads for an operator verb's non-zero exit without a word of its own (§8.3). */
const OP_EXIT_WORDS = Object.freeze({
  [EXIT.INTERNAL]: 'internal error: the history writer gave no result this CLI could relay',
  [EXIT.WRITER_BUSY]: 'writer-busy: another history pass holds the lock; run it again when that pass ends',
  [EXIT.NO_STORE]: 'no store on this box (macOS, a server role, or never installed): stop, do not retry',
});

/** {op, opArgs} for `<verb> <rest…>`, or null. A doctor flag comes first and alone names the op; what follows it
 *  is that op's arguments, which parseOpVerbArgs judges. */
function opFormOf(verb, rest) {
  if (verb === 'doctor') {
    const flag = rest[0];
    if (typeof flag !== 'string' || !flag.startsWith('--') || !Object.hasOwn(OP_OF_VERB, flag)) return null;
    return { op: OP_OF_VERB[flag], opArgs: rest.slice(1) };
  }
  if (verb.startsWith('--') || !Object.hasOwn(OP_OF_VERB, verb)) return null;
  return { op: OP_OF_VERB[verb], opArgs: [...rest] };
}

/** The pane an irreversible form runs in, read as the sweep reads it (§8.2, §8.4): whether to read it at all is
 *  lib's paneReadWanted, the one rule the sweep's paneNameFor asks too; the read is Task 10's bounded tmuxSession,
 *  always with -t. Anything else is null, and the TTY requirement still stands then. */
function opPaneName(form) {
  const pane = process.env.TMUX_PANE ?? '';
  if (!healthLib.paneReadWanted(form, pane)) return null;
  const t = tmuxSession(pane);
  return t.settled && t.status === 0 ? t.stdout.trim() : null;
}

/** The shim as a child: its stdout relayed line by line as it arrives, its LAST line held back for the relay. */
function opRelay(P, op, opArgs, emit) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    let done = false;
    const finish = (r) => { if (!done) { done = true; resolve(r); } };
    let child;
    try {
      child = spawnOp(P.shim, ['--op', op, ...opArgs], { stdio: ['inherit', 'pipe', 'inherit'] });
    } catch {
      finish({ exit: EXIT.INTERNAL });
      return;
    }
    let buf = '';
    let held = null;
    const take = (line) => {
      if (held !== null) emit(held);
      held = line;
    };
    child.stdout.setEncoding('utf8');
    child.stdout.on('data', (d) => {
      buf += d;
      for (let i = buf.indexOf('\n'); i !== -1; i = buf.indexOf('\n')) {
        take(buf.slice(0, i));
        buf = buf.slice(i + 1);
      }
    });
    child.on('error', () => finish({ exit: EXIT.INTERNAL }));
    child.on('close', (status, signal) => {
      if (buf !== '') take(buf);
      let lastLine = null;
      if (held !== null && held.startsWith('{"rc"')) lastLine = held;
      else if (held !== null) emit(held);
      finish(healthLib.decideRelay({ status, signal, lastLine }));
    });
  });
}

/** The relay's redaction index (§8.3, layers 1 and 4): Task 10's pairIndexOf, the read verbs' own index, so a relayed
 *  sweep line is redacted as a recalled field is: the pairs the sweep recorded in redact_hashes, the frozen list's and
 *  the declared secretsFiles' pairs read now (the paths from meta redact_sources), and the belt of those values. It
 *  reads the store only where a read verb would (decideCliStore's `read`, so behind measureReach's settled stat), on
 *  a read-only handle closed before it returns, so the shim's op never runs beside this process's reader. Where the
 *  store cannot be read (no settled stat, no DB yet before a rebuild or a restore, or an open or a select that failed
 *  as a StoreError or SQLite's own error), the index is the files read now with their belt, never no index; any
 *  other throw is a defect and propagates (exit 1). */
function relayIndexOf(home, P, reach) {
  if (decideCliStore(cliFactsOf(reach)).read) {
    let db = null;
    try {
      db = openReader(P.dbFile);
      return pairIndexOf(db, home);
    } catch (e) {
      if (!(e instanceof StoreError) && !(e !== null && typeof e === 'object' && e.code === 'ERR_SQLITE_ERROR')) throw e;
    } finally {
      if (db !== null) db.close();
    }
  }
  const files = loadSecrets(home, []);
  return makePairIndex(files.pairs, makeBelt(beltUnits(files.values)));
}

/** One operator verb through the door. `emit` gets each line the sweep printed before its result, already through
 *  redactFinal with relayIndexOf's index, which is built only once the gate has passed, before the shim starts. */
export async function runOpVerb(home, verb, rest, emit) {
  const P = healthLib.historyPaths(home);
  const map = opFormOf(verb, rest);
  if (map === null) return { exit: EXIT.REFUSED, reason: 'bad-args' };
  const parsed = healthLib.parseOpVerbArgs(map.op, map.opArgs);
  if (!parsed.ok) return { exit: EXIT.REFUSED, reason: parsed.reason };
  const reach = await measureReach(home);
  const door = healthLib.decideOpDoor(cliFactsOf(reach));
  if (!door.ok) return door.reason === undefined ? { exit: door.exit } : { exit: door.exit, reason: door.reason };
  const form = healthLib.formOf(map.op, map.opArgs);
  // RB6 (slug history-ops-refused-while-recovering): the CLI's pre-check, so a refused form spawns nothing. It opens
  // the store read-only only behind measureReach's settled 2 s stat; an unsettled stat, or any answer but `open`,
  // leaves the call to the sweep's half, which is authoritative. While a step is open it also carries the facts lib's
  // recoveryExempt reads (RB13: the stored user_version against this build's; RB14: store.id's presence, as
  // measureReach read it), so it never refuses a form the sweep would let through.
  const recovering = form !== null && reach.statSettled && opRecoverStepAt(P.dbFile) === 'open';
  const recovery = recovering
    ? { storedVersion: opStoredVersionAt(P.dbFile), codeVersion: healthLib.SCHEMA_VERSION, storeId: reach.facts.storeId }
    : {};
  const gate = healthLib.decideOpGate(form, { claudecode: (process.env.CLAUDECODE ?? '') !== '', historyOff: healthFs.existsSync(P.off), recovering, ...recovery },
    isattyOp(0), opPaneName(form));
  if (!gate.ok) return { exit: gate.rc, reason: gate.reason };
  const idx = relayIndexOf(home, P, reach);
  return opRelay(P, map.op, map.opArgs, (line) => emit(redactFinal(line, idx)));
}

/** main's arm for `import`, `prune`, `reparse` and `doctor`: argv is main's own, the verb first, `--json` anywhere.
 *  Under --json, stdout is the envelope alone and the sweep's lines go to stderr; every relayed line arrives here
 *  already through redactFinal (runOpVerb's relayIndexOf). */
export async function operatorMain(home, argv) {
  const json = argv.includes('--json');
  const rest = argv.filter((a) => a !== '--json');
  const verb = rest[0] ?? '';
  if (verb === 'doctor' && rest.length === 1) {
    const env = await statusWithHealth(home, Date.now());
    process.stdout.write(json ? `${JSON.stringify(env)}\n` : formatHealth(env.health).map((l) => `${l}\n`).join(''));
    return env.exit;
  }
  const P = healthLib.historyPaths(home);
  const emit = (line) => {
    const text = `${line}\n`;
    if (json) process.stderr.write(text);
    else process.stdout.write(text);
  };
  const r = await runOpVerb(home, verb, rest.slice(1), emit);
  if (json) {
    const id = readTrimmed(P.storeId);
    const env = healthLib.readEnvelope({
      exit: r.exit, ...(r.reason === undefined ? {} : { reason: r.reason }),
      storeId: id !== null && healthLib.UUID_RE.test(id) ? id : null,
      scope: null, header: null, items: [], shown: 0, total: 0, next: null,
    });
    process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify(env)}\n`);
  } else if (r.exit !== EXIT.OK) {
    const words = OP_EXIT_WORDS[r.exit] ?? `${r.exit === EXIT.REFUSED ? 'refused' : 'store error'}: ${r.reason ?? ''}`;
    process.stderr.write(`ccrc history ${verb}: ${words}\n`);
  }
  return r.exit;
}
```

Tasks 21–23 use them.

**Spec:** §6.6 (prune: dry run by default, the 30-day floor, bounded `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` batches, every-referrer age, NULL time never old, structure blobs never pruned, FTS rows deleted, `PRAGMA incremental_vacuum(N)`, never by a source file's absence, never the journal or the export, the dry run's export count), §8.4 (operator verbs through the shim, the speed bumps), §9.3 ("prune frees space"), §9.14 (a registered recovery step), §11 P15. Pins: DM14, DM15, DM22, DM27, O12, C25, C34; DM49 (spec rev 3.4: prune below the free-space floor; it is RB3's two halves, reachability only and the WAL truncated per batch, pinned by Step 1's `walSizes` and Step 6's `RB3: below the free-space floor …` case, with Step 5's mutant (f) and Step 10's RB3 mutant as its two CONTROLs); RB6's prune row. Departures: D-4718 (`history-prune-referrers`), B1's D-4221 (`history-apply-via-shim`), B1's D-4179 (`history-free-space-floor`), D-4719 (`history-prune-not-floor-gated`) (RULED by the operator on 2026-10-07, spec rev 3.4, no longer provisional; first raised by this plan as coordinator ruling RB3: §9.3 said `prune --apply` "runs the same preflight", but a store below the floor is exactly the one prune exists to shrink, so the pass probes reachability only, never refuses for room, and truncates the WAL after each batch; §9.3 is amended to say so, §6.6 and DM49 pin it), D-4720 (`history-prune-needs-a-referrer`) (NEW: "every referrer is older than the cutoff" is vacuously true for a blob nothing names; a blob with no `entries`, `entry_variants` or `sidecars` referrer is never pruned), D-4698 (`history-ops-refused-while-recovering`) (NEW, RB6; defined by Task 6; Task 19 places the refusal).

Not a departure (spec §6.2 "The belt", "Passes that do not stamp"; the coordinator's ruling on the pass-6 cross-file items): `--op prune --apply` neither checks nor stamps the belt witness. Its batches delete blobs and `blobs_fts` rows, which move the witness, and it runs no secrets step and writes no `ticks` row, so the next tick reads its writes as a moved witness and records the belt due: one whole belt generation per apply, never a missed row. Add no `stampBeltWitness` here: a stamp without the check before the batches would hide an interleaved write by a build without the belt.

Choices this task makes (each is in the PR body's open issues):
- **Reachability, not room** (RB3; ruled by the operator on 2026-10-07, DM49). The `--op` pass's own statfs probe (Task 19's runOpPass, under `STATFS_DEADLINE_MS`) is prune's whole preflight: unsettled answers 5 `store-unreachable`; low disk never refuses. Step 6's below-the-floor case pins both halves.
- **The WAL is truncated after every batch** (RB3; part of the same operator ruling, DM49). Each batch's tombstones, FTS deletes and incremental vacuum land in the WAL, and the store prune serves is the one with no room for a WAL that grows across a long pass. So `pruneApply` runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` after each batch's vacuum, outside any transaction, as upstream does after its VACUUM (src/prune.ts:382). A reader holding an older snapshot makes it wait up to the writer's busy timeout and answer `busy` = 1; that is not an error, and the next batch's checkpoint tries again.
- **A tombstone clears `fts_indexed`.** The blob holds no text, so it holds no index row; B1's backfill already skips `z IS NULL`.
- **The deleted index bytes are merged by the ticks.** In the same transaction as a batch's FTS deletes, the pass registers `('fts-merge', 1)` through B1's `derivStmts(db).pending` (pruneBatch's `onDeleted`), so a pass that stops between batches (a failed journal append, a kill) never leaves deleted index bytes with no merge step to purge them; the scheduled ticks' bounded merge steps purge them from `blobs_fts_data` (§6.2's merge rule).
- **Batch 500, vacuum at most 65 536 pages per batch** (*chosen*).
- **Measured on Node 24.14.1** (re-measure on the 22.16.0 floor in Step 13): `DELETE FROM blobs_fts WHERE rowid = ?` for a rowid the contentless table never held is a no-op (no `_data` growth, integrity-check ok); `PRAGMA incremental_vacuum(64)` on an `auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL` WAL store returned 64 pages and a large N returned the whole freelist; on a WAL store with no other connection, `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` after each of three small batches left the `-wal` file at 0 bytes each time (`{ busy: 0, log: 0, checkpointed: 0 }`), and without it the file read 8 272, 16 512 and 24 752 bytes.

```ts
// ── W1-B2 Task 20: prune by referrer age (spec 2026-10-05 §6.6; DM14 store half, DM15) ────────────
describe('store.mjs: prune tombstones by referrer age (W1-B2 Task 20)', () => {
  const DAY = 86_400_000;
  const NOW = Date.UTC(2026, 9, 6, 12, 0, 0);
  const CUTOFF = NOW - 90 * DAY;
  const OLD = NOW - 200 * DAY;
  const NEW = NOW - DAY;

  /** A bound store holding one referrer arrangement per DM15 clause, planted by SQL on the writer handle.
   *  Blob ids are assigned in this order: old-only 1, shared 2, young 3, summary 4, kept 5, boundary 6,
   *  null-ts 7, variant-host-old 8, variant-of-old 9, variant-host-new 10, variant-of-new 11,
   *  sidecar-unlinked 12, orphan 13. */
  function planted(): { home: string; db: DatabaseSync; blob: Record<string, number>; close: () => void } {
    const home = mkTmp('ccrc-history-prune-');
    createStore(home);
    const db = openWriter(historyPaths(home).dbFile);
    const blob: Record<string, number> = {};
    const mkBlob = (tag: string): number => {
      const r = db.prepare("INSERT INTO blobs (sha256, codec, z, raw_len) VALUES (?, 'br5', ?, ?)")
        .run(createHash('sha256').update(tag).digest(), brotli(Buffer.from(tag)), tag.length);
      blob[tag] = Number(r.lastInsertRowid);
      return blob[tag]!;
    };
    const tp = Number(db.prepare('INSERT INTO transcripts (cc_session_uuid) VALUES (?)')
      .run('11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111').lastInsertRowid);
    let n = 0;
    const entry = (blobId: number, tsMs: number | null): number => {
      n += 1;
      return Number(db.prepare(`INSERT INTO entries (uuid, transcript_pk, type, provenance, prov_version, struct_rank_ns,
          struct_file_id, blob_id, ts_ms) VALUES (?, ?, 'user', 'operator', 1, ?, 1, ?, ?)`)
        .run(`e${String(n).padStart(4, '0')}`, tp, n, blobId, tsMs).lastInsertRowid);
    };
    entry(mkBlob('old-only'), OLD);
    const shared = mkBlob('shared');
    entry(shared, OLD);
    const young = entry(mkBlob('young'), NEW);
    db.prepare('INSERT INTO sidecars (transcript_pk, name, blob_id, entry_id, first_seen_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')
      .run(tp, 'toolu_01shared.txt', shared, young, NEW);
    const summary = mkBlob('summary');
    entry(summary, OLD);
    const sp = Number(db.prepare("INSERT INTO sessions (ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms) VALUES ('claude-a-demo', '', 'demo', 1)")
      .run().lastInsertRowid);
    db.prepare(`INSERT INTO nodes (node_id, session_pk, epoch_seq, transcript_pk, kind, depth, status, summary_blob_id,
        parser_version, created_ms) VALUES ('L00000000000000000001', ?, 1, ?, 'native_leaf', 0, 'not-requested', ?, 1, 1)`)
      .run(sp, tp, summary);
    const kept = mkBlob('kept');
    entry(kept, OLD);   // a kept list some old row also names: only the structure rule protects it
    const boundaryEntry = entry(mkBlob('boundary'), OLD);
    db.prepare('INSERT INTO boundaries (entry_id, transcript_pk, ord, kept_blob_id) VALUES (?, ?, 1, ?)').run(boundaryEntry, tp, kept);
    entry(mkBlob('null-ts'), null);
    const oldHost = entry(mkBlob('variant-host-old'), OLD);
    db.prepare('INSERT INTO entry_variants (entry_id, blob_id, first_file_id, first_seen_ms) VALUES (?, ?, 1, ?)')
      .run(oldHost, mkBlob('variant-of-old'), OLD);
    const newHost = entry(mkBlob('variant-host-new'), NEW);
    db.prepare('INSERT INTO entry_variants (entry_id, blob_id, first_file_id, first_seen_ms) VALUES (?, ?, 1, ?)')
      .run(newHost, mkBlob('variant-of-new'), NEW);
    db.prepare('INSERT INTO sidecars (transcript_pk, name, blob_id, entry_id, first_seen_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?, NULL, ?)')
      .run(tp, 'toolu_01unlinked.txt', mkBlob('sidecar-unlinked'), OLD);
    mkBlob('orphan');
    return { home, db, blob, close: () => closeWriter(db) };
  }
  const PRUNED = ['boundary', 'old-only', 'variant-host-old', 'variant-of-old'];
  const KEPT = ['shared', 'young', 'summary', 'kept', 'null-ts', 'variant-host-new', 'variant-of-new', 'sidecar-unlinked', 'orphan'];

  it('DM15: a blob is a candidate only when every referrer is older than the cutoff; shared, NULL-time, unlinked-sidecar, unreferenced and structure blobs stay', () => {
    const { db, blob, close } = planted();
    try {
      const protectedIds = pruneProtected(db);
      expect([...protectedIds].sort((a, b) => a - b), 'structure: the native summary and the kept list')
        .toEqual([blob['summary']!, blob['kept']!].sort((a, b) => a - b));
      const c = pruneCandidates(db, { cutoffMs: CUTOFF, afterBlobId: 0, limit: 100, protectedIds });
      const name = (id: number): string => Object.keys(blob).find((k) => blob[k] === id)!;
      expect(c.blobIds.map(name).sort()).toEqual(PRUNED);
      expect(c.more).toBe(false);
      expect(c.exported, 'nothing is exported before W1-B4').toBe(0);
      expect(pruneDryRun(db, CUTOFF)).toEqual({ blobs: 4, bytes: c.bytes, exported: 0 });
    } finally { close(); }
  });

  it('DM14 (store half): pruneApply tombstones in bounded batches — z NULL, pruned_ms stamped, the FTS row gone, the merge step registered inside the batch — keeps every row, truncates the WAL after each batch, and calls back between batches', (ctx) => {
    const { home, db, blob, close } = planted();
    try {
      if (probeFts5(db) === 'absent') ctx.skip();
      withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
        createFtsTables(db);
        db.prepare('INSERT INTO blobs_fts (rowid, body) VALUES (?, ?)').run(blob['old-only']!, 'oldonlyword');
        db.prepare('INSERT INTO blobs_fts (rowid, body) VALUES (?, ?)').run(blob['shared']!, 'sharedword');
        db.prepare('UPDATE blobs SET fts_indexed = 1 WHERE blob_id IN (?, ?)').run(blob['old-only']!, blob['shared']!);
      });
      const count = (t: string): number => (db.prepare(`SELECT count(*) AS n FROM ${t}`).get() as { n: number }).n;
      const TABLES = ['entries', 'entry_variants', 'sidecars', 'nodes', 'boundaries', 'blobs'];
      const before = TABLES.map(count);
      // RB3: the -wal file's size at each between() call, after that batch's vacuum and checkpoint. This test holds
      // no other connection, so a TRUNCATE checkpoint always completes and leaves the file empty.
      const wal = `${historyPaths(home).dbFile}-wal`;
      const walSizes: number[] = [];
      let registered = 0;
      // batch 2: SQL pages [1,4] [5,6] [8,9] [] — the protected 4 and 5 dropped — so three batches tombstone.
      const r = pruneApply(db, {
        cutoffMs: CUTOFF, nowMs: NOW, batch: 2, vacuumPages: 64,
        between: () => { walSizes.push(fs.statSync(wal).size); },
        onDeleted: () => { expect(db.isTransaction, 'registered inside the batch\'s own transaction').toBe(true); registered += 1; },
      });
      expect(r).toEqual({ blobs: 4, bytes: expect.any(Number), fts: true });
      expect(walSizes, 'one call after each batch that tombstoned something, the WAL truncated before each').toEqual([0, 0, 0]);
      expect(registered, 'every batch that deleted index rows registers the merge step with them').toBe(3);
      const state = (tag: string): { z: Uint8Array | null; pruned_ms: number | null; fts_indexed: number } =>
        db.prepare('SELECT z, pruned_ms, fts_indexed FROM blobs WHERE blob_id = ?').get(blob[tag]!) as never;
      for (const tag of PRUNED) expect(state(tag), tag).toEqual({ z: null, pruned_ms: NOW, fts_indexed: 0 });
      for (const tag of KEPT) expect(state(tag).z, tag).not.toBeNull();
      const match = (w: string): number =>
        (db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM blobs_fts WHERE blobs_fts MATCH ?').get(w) as { n: number }).n;
      expect(match('oldonlyword'), 'the tombstoned blob left the index').toBe(0);
      expect(match('sharedword'), 'a kept blob keeps its row').toBe(1);
      expect(TABLES.map(count), 'tombstones content, never rows').toEqual(before);
      expect(pruneApply(db, { cutoffMs: CUTOFF, nowMs: NOW, batch: 2, vacuumPages: 64, between: () => {} }).blobs,
        'a second pass finds nothing left').toBe(0);
    } finally { close(); }
  });

  it('incrementalVacuum returns what it freed and refuses a page count that is not a positive integer', () => {
    const { db, close } = planted();
    try {
      expect(incrementalVacuum(db, 64)).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
      expect(() => incrementalVacuum(db, 0)).toThrow(TypeError);
    } finally { close(); }
  });
});
```

Append to the end of `ccd/history/store.mjs`:

```js
// ── prune: tombstones by referrer age (§6.6; W1-B2 Task 20) ──────────────────────────────────────

/** The blob ids that are structure, never content (§6.6): every native summary a node names
 *  (nodes.summary_blob_id) and every kept list (boundaries.kept_blob_id). Read once per pass: nodes has no
 *  index on summary_blob_id, so a probe per candidate would scan it once per blob. */
export function pruneProtected(db) {
  const ids = new Set();
  for (const r of db.prepare('SELECT summary_blob_id AS id FROM nodes WHERE summary_blob_id IS NOT NULL').all()) ids.add(Number(r.id));
  for (const r of db.prepare('SELECT kept_blob_id AS id FROM boundaries WHERE kept_blob_id IS NOT NULL').all()) ids.add(Number(r.id));
  return ids;
}

const PRUNE_STMTS = new WeakMap();
/** The candidate page, prepared once per connection (a reader's too: it writes nothing). One row per blob past
 *  the cursor that still holds text, has at least one content referrer
 *  (history-prune-needs-a-referrer), and has no referrer at or after the cutoff: a referrer with no time is
 *  never old, a variant ages by its entry, a sidecar ages by its entry, and a sidecar no entry names is
 *  never old. Each clause is ONE line: the mutation steps edit them line by line. The referrer probes are
 *  index searches (entries_blob, entry_variants_blob, sidecars_blob). */
function pruneStmts(db) {
  let s = PRUNE_STMTS.get(db);
  if (s !== undefined) return s;
  s = {
    candidates: db.prepare(`SELECT b.blob_id AS blob_id, length(b.z) AS zlen, b.exported_ms IS NOT NULL AS exported
      FROM blobs b
      WHERE b.blob_id > ? AND b.z IS NOT NULL
        AND (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM entries e WHERE e.blob_id = b.blob_id) OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM entry_variants v WHERE v.blob_id = b.blob_id) OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sidecars s WHERE s.blob_id = b.blob_id))
        AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM entries e WHERE e.blob_id = b.blob_id AND (e.ts_ms IS NULL OR e.ts_ms >= ?))
        AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM entry_variants v JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = v.entry_id WHERE v.blob_id = b.blob_id AND (e.ts_ms IS NULL OR e.ts_ms >= ?))
        AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sidecars s LEFT JOIN entries e ON e.entry_id = s.entry_id WHERE s.blob_id = b.blob_id AND (e.entry_id IS NULL OR e.ts_ms IS NULL OR e.ts_ms >= ?))
      ORDER BY b.blob_id LIMIT ?`),
  };
  PRUNE_STMTS.set(db, s);
  return s;
}

/** One page of prune candidates past `afterBlobId` (§6.6): `limit` rows read, the protected ones dropped.
 *  `more` says the page was full, so the caller reads the next one from `lastBlobId`; `exported` counts the
 *  candidates the sole-copy export already holds (exported_ms, set from W1-B4). */
export function pruneCandidates(db, i) {
  const rows = pruneStmts(db).candidates.all(i.afterBlobId, i.cutoffMs, i.cutoffMs, i.cutoffMs, i.limit);
  const blobIds = [];
  let bytes = 0;
  let exported = 0;
  for (const r of rows) {
    const id = Number(r.blob_id);
    if (i.protectedIds.has(id)) continue;
    blobIds.push(id);
    bytes += Number(r.zlen);
    if (Number(r.exported) === 1) exported += 1;
  }
  const lastBlobId = rows.length > 0 ? Number(rows[rows.length - 1].blob_id) : i.afterBlobId;
  return { blobIds, bytes, exported, lastBlobId, more: rows.length === i.limit };
}

/** One batch in its own BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction (§6.6): each blob's z set NULL, pruned_ms stamped and
 *  fts_indexed cleared — a tombstone; the blob row and every row naming it stay — and its blobs_fts row
 *  deleted when the index exists. Deleting a rowid the contentless index never held is a no-op (measured,
 *  24.14.1). When it deleted index rows it calls `onDeleted` INSIDE the same transaction, so the caller's merge
 *  step commits with the deletes it exists to purge (§6.2) and no stop between batches can separate them.
 *  Answers how many blobs this batch tombstoned. */
export function pruneBatch(db, i) {
  const tombstone = db.prepare('UPDATE blobs SET z = NULL, pruned_ms = ?, fts_indexed = 0 WHERE blob_id = ? AND z IS NOT NULL');
  const del = i.fts ? db.prepare('DELETE FROM blobs_fts WHERE rowid = ?') : null;
  let n = 0;
  withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
    for (const id of i.blobIds) {
      if (Number(tombstone.run(i.nowMs, id).changes) !== 1) continue;
      n += 1;
      if (del !== null) del.run(id);
    }
    if (del !== null && n > 0 && i.onDeleted !== undefined) i.onDeleted();
  });
  return n;
}

/** What `prune` without --apply reports (§6.6): how many blobs, and their compressed bytes, --apply would
 *  tombstone at this cutoff, and how many of those the export already holds. It runs on a reader. */
export function pruneDryRun(db, cutoffMs) {
  const protectedIds = pruneProtected(db);
  let after = 0;
  let blobs = 0;
  let bytes = 0;
  let exported = 0;
  for (;;) {
    const c = pruneCandidates(db, { cutoffMs, afterBlobId: after, limit: 500, protectedIds });
    blobs += c.blobIds.length;
    bytes += c.bytes;
    exported += c.exported;
    after = c.lastBlobId;
    if (!c.more) return { blobs, bytes, exported };
  }
}

/** §6.6's PRAGMA incremental_vacuum(N): returns at most `pages` free pages to the filesystem (the store is
 *  auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL from creation, §6.2). A full VACUUM is never run: it needs about the store's size
 *  free, which the floor (§9.3) forbids. Answers the pages it freed. */
export function incrementalVacuum(db, pages) {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(pages) || pages < 1) {
    throw new TypeError(`incrementalVacuum: pages must be a positive integer, not ${String(pages)}`);
  }
  const free = Number(db.prepare('PRAGMA freelist_count').get().freelist_count);
  const n = Math.min(free, pages);
  if (n > 0) db.exec(`PRAGMA incremental_vacuum(${n})`);
  return n;
}

/** `prune --apply`'s loop (§6.6): pages of candidates from a blob-id cursor; each non-empty page tombstoned
 *  in one batch (with `onDeleted`, the caller's merge-step registration, inside it), the freed pages vacuumed,
 *  the WAL checkpointed and truncated (RB3: the batch's frames never accumulate across a long pass on the very
 *  store that has no room for them; a reader on an older snapshot makes the checkpoint answer busy, which is not
 *  an error and is retried after the next batch), then `between()` — the caller's journal half, which may throw
 *  to end the pass. It stops when a page comes back short. Answers what it tombstoned and whether the FTS table
 *  exists.
 *  derived from lossless-claw src/prune.ts @ e05d8d3, MIT, see LICENSE.lossless-claw */
export function pruneApply(db, i) {
  const protectedIds = pruneProtected(db);
  const fts = db.prepare("SELECT 1 AS x FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'blobs_fts'").get() !== undefined;
  let after = 0;
  let blobs = 0;
  let bytes = 0;
  for (;;) {
    const c = pruneCandidates(db, { cutoffMs: i.cutoffMs, afterBlobId: after, limit: i.batch, protectedIds });
    if (c.blobIds.length > 0) {
      blobs += pruneBatch(db, { blobIds: c.blobIds, nowMs: i.nowMs, fts, onDeleted: i.onDeleted });
      bytes += c.bytes;
      incrementalVacuum(db, i.vacuumPages);
      db.prepare('PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)').get();
      i.between();
    }
    after = c.lastBlobId;
    if (!c.more) return { blobs, bytes, fts };
  }
}
```

Append to `ccd/history/store.d.mts`:

```ts
export function pruneProtected(db: DatabaseSync): Set<number>;
export function pruneCandidates(db: DatabaseSync, i: {
  cutoffMs: number; afterBlobId: number; limit: number; protectedIds: ReadonlySet<number>;
}): { blobIds: number[]; bytes: number; exported: number; lastBlobId: number; more: boolean };
export function pruneBatch(db: DatabaseSync, i: {
  blobIds: readonly number[]; nowMs: number; fts: boolean; onDeleted?: () => void;
}): number;
export function pruneDryRun(db: DatabaseSync, cutoffMs: number): { blobs: number; bytes: number; exported: number };
export function incrementalVacuum(db: DatabaseSync, pages: number): number;
export function pruneApply(db: DatabaseSync, i: {
```

```ts
// ── W1-B2 Tasks 20-23: prune, reparse, backup and repair (spec 2026-10-05 §6.6, §8.4) ──────────────
// Shared by those four tasks' describes. Every name carries a `maint`/`MAINT_` prefix so nothing collides with
// Task 19's block above. The TTY gate has no seam (§10.1): an irreversible form runs under a real node-pty
// terminal, through either door — the CLI (`node cli.mjs …`, which spawns the shim) or the shim itself.
const MAINT_ID = 'claude-a-maint';
const MAINT_U1 = '11111111-1111-4111-8111-1111111111a1';
const MAINT_QUOKKA = 'c0000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000a1';
const MAINT_DAY = 86_400_000;
function maintIso(msAgo: number): string { return new Date(Date.now() - msAgo).toISOString(); }

interface MaintOp { rc: number; reason?: string }
/** The --op pass's one JSON result, its LAST `{"rc"…}` stdout line (§8.4); a pty's \r stripped. */
function maintResult(stdout: string): MaintOp {
  const lines = stdout.replace(/\r/g, '').split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l.startsWith('{"rc"'));
  expect(lines.length, `no {"rc":…} line in:\n${stdout}`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  return JSON.parse(lines[lines.length - 1]!) as MaintOp;
}
/** The CLI's --json envelope read off a pty: the last line that parses as a JSON object. */
function maintJson(out: string): Record<string, unknown> | null {
  const lines = out.replace(/\r/g, '').split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l.startsWith('{'));
  for (let i = lines.length - 1; i >= 0; i -= 1) {
    try { return JSON.parse(lines[i]!) as Record<string, unknown>; } catch { /* a partial line */ }
  }
  return null;
}
/** Every entry under ~/.ccrc with each file's size and mtime — "writes nothing", measured. The shim's lock
 *  and SQLite's -wal/-shm (a read-only open may create them, §8.1) are left out; directories by name only. */
function maintSnapshot(box: HistoryBox): string[] {
  const root = path.join(box.home, '.ccrc');
  const out: string[] = [];
  const visit = (d: string): void => {
    for (const e of fs.readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      if (e.name === 'history-sweep.lock' || /-(wal|shm)$/.test(e.name)) continue;
      const p = path.join(d, e.name);
      if (e.isDirectory()) { out.push(`${path.relative(root, p)}/`); visit(p); continue; }
      const st = fs.lstatSync(p);
      out.push(`${path.relative(root, p)} ${st.size} ${Math.trunc(st.mtimeMs)}`);
    }
  };
  visit(root);
  return out.sort();
}
function maintQ<T>(box: HistoryBox, sql: string, ...args: Array<string | number>): T[] {
  const db = openStoreRO(box);
  try { return db.prepare(sql).all(...args) as T[]; } finally { db.close(); }
}
function maintMatch(box: HistoryBox, word: string): number {
  return maintQ<{ n: number }>(box, 'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM blobs_fts WHERE blobs_fts MATCH ?', word)[0]!.n;
}
function maintMeta(box: HistoryBox, k: string): string | null {
  return maintQ<{ v: string }>(box, 'SELECT v FROM meta WHERE k = ?', k)[0]?.v ?? null;
}
function maintNames(dir: string): string[] { try { return fs.readdirSync(dir).sort(); } catch { return []; } }
function maintTombstones(box: HistoryBox): number {
  return maintQ<{ n: number }>(box, 'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM blobs WHERE z IS NULL')[0]!.n;
}
/** A fleet box whose first scheduled pass created and bound its store. */
function maintBound(prefix: string): HistoryBox {
  const box = makeHistoryBox(prefix, { role: 'fleet', shim: true });
  const r = runSweep(box);
  expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
  return box;
}
/** RB6's state: a `('recover', <ms>)` step registered as restore and rebuild register it (§9.14), planted by SQL
 *  with no sweep running. No scheduled pass may run on the box afterwards: it would start replaying. */
function maintRecovering(box: HistoryBox): void {
  const db = new DatabaseSync(historyPaths(box.home).dbFile);
  try {
    db.prepare("INSERT INTO derivation_state (step, version, cursor, completed_ms) VALUES ('recover', ?, NULL, NULL)").run(Date.now());
  } finally { db.close(); }
}
/** A door on a REAL terminal (node-pty), so stdin is a TTY and only the pane, the switches or the lock can
 *  refuse. `cli` is `node --no-warnings cli.mjs <args>` (which spawns the shim with stdin inherited); `shim` is
 *  the placed `~/.local/bin/ccd-history-sweep <args>`. Every spawn carries the statfs preload. A pty merges
 *  stdout and stderr; `signal` is set when the child died of one. The guard timer is a safety net, never the
 *  assertion. */
function maintPty(box: HistoryBox, door: 'cli' | 'shim', args: string[],
  o: { env?: Record<string, string>; preloads?: string[] } = {}): Promise<{ code: number; signal: number | undefined; out: string }> {
  const file = door === 'cli' ? process.execPath : 'bash';
  const argv = door === 'cli' ? ['--no-warnings', CLI, ...args] : [path.join(box.home, '.local', 'bin', 'ccd-history-sweep'), ...args];
  const merged: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {
    ...box.env, HISTORY_TEST_STATFS: 'plenty', NODE_OPTIONS: preloadOptions(o.preloads ?? [PRELOADS.statfs]), ...(o.env ?? {}),
  };
  const env: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(merged)) if (v !== undefined) env[k] = v;
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const p = pty.spawn(file, argv, { name: 'xterm-color', cols: 200, rows: 40, cwd: box.home, env });
    let out = '';
    let done = false;
    const finish = (code: number, signal: number | undefined): void => {
      if (done) return;
      done = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve({ code, signal, out });
    };
    const timer = setTimeout(() => { p.kill(); finish(-1, undefined); }, 80_000);
    p.onData((d) => { out += d; });
    p.onExit(({ exitCode, signal }) => finish(exitCode, signal));
  });
}
```

```js
// ── prune (W1-B2 Task 20) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// §6.6 "prune --older-than <dur>", §8.4. A dry run by default: the store read through a read-only handle,
// nothing written. `--apply` (irreversible: a TTY and no cc- pane, both decided by the gate before this
// runs) tombstones every blob whose every referrer is older than the cutoff, in bounded BEGIN IMMEDIATE
// batches with the journal half between them (store.mjs's pruneApply). It never deletes a row, never
// touches the journal or the export, and never decides by a source file's absence (lossless-claw #610,
// DM27). Free space is probed for reachability only, by runOpPass: prune frees space, so a store below the
// floor is exactly the one it must not refuse (history-prune-not-floor-gated).

/** Blobs per prune batch (§6.6 "bounded BEGIN IMMEDIATE batches"). Chosen. */
const PRUNE_BATCH = 500;
/** The most free pages one batch's PRAGMA incremental_vacuum returns: 256 MiB at 4 KiB pages. Chosen. */
const PRUNE_VACUUM_PAGES = 65_536;

/** A dry run's store (§8.4 "dry run by default"): measured as a scheduled pass would find it and opened
 *  READ-ONLY only when decideStoreOpen would open it. No store yet answers rc 0 with a line; a refusal word
 *  answers its own exit; nothing is written — no journal half, no marker, no flush. Returns `{ ro }` or
 *  `{ result }`; the caller closes `ro`. */
function dryRunReader(home, P, out) {
  const verdict = decideStoreOpen(measureStoreFacts(home, readRole(P)));
  if (verdict.act === 'create' || verdict.act === 'drop-pending-create') {
    out('history-sweep: no store on this box yet; nothing to do');
    return { result: { rc: EXIT.OK } };
  }
  if (verdict.act === 'refuse') {
    return { result: REASONS[verdict.word] === EXIT.DB ? { rc: EXIT.DB, reason: verdict.word } : { rc: EXIT.INTERNAL } };
  }
  return { ro: openReader(P.dbFile) };
}

/** `prune --older-than <dur>` without --apply (§6.6): what --apply would tombstone, and how much of it the
 *  export already holds. */
export function pruneDryRunOp(home, P, args, out, nowMs) {
  const r = dryRunReader(home, P, out);
  if (r.result !== undefined) return r.result;
  try {
    const t = pruneDryRun(r.ro, nowMs - args.days * DAY_MS);
    out(`history-sweep: prune --older-than ${args.days}d would tombstone ${t.blobs} blob(s), ${t.bytes} bytes compressed; the export holds ${t.exported} of them`);
    out('history-sweep: a dry run writes nothing; rows, nodes, the journal and the export are never touched; add --apply to tombstone');
    return { rc: EXIT.OK };
  } finally {
    r.ro.close();
  }
}

/** `prune --older-than <dur> --apply` (§6.6): the batched tombstone, the WAL truncated after each batch, the
 *  journal half between batches (a failed append ends the pass through runOpPass's JournalError arm), and the
 *  merge step registered INSIDE each batch that deleted index rows (store.mjs's onDeleted), so the bytes those
 *  deletes left are purged by the scheduled ticks' bounded merges (§6.2) even when the pass stops between
 *  batches. */
export function pruneApplyOp(db, ctx, args) {
  const nowMs = ctx.now();
  const r = pruneApply(db, {
    cutoffMs: nowMs - args.days * DAY_MS,
    nowMs,
    batch: PRUNE_BATCH,
    vacuumPages: PRUNE_VACUUM_PAGES,
    between: () => { if (runJournalHalf(ctx.home, ctx.ids, ctx.now)) throw new JournalError('append-failed'); },
    onDeleted: () => { derivStmts(db).pending.run(MERGE_STEP, 1); },
  });
  ctx.out(`history-sweep: pruned ${r.blobs} blob(s), ${r.bytes} bytes compressed, older than ${args.days} days; every row and node stays, and expand says "content pruned on <date>"`);
  return { rc: EXIT.OK };
}
```

Not a departure since spec rev 3.5: the operator passes' belt-state rule (§6.2 "The belt": only the tick's `rederiveFts` moves meta `fts_belt`, through lib's `decideBelt`, and no operator pass runs it; so an operator pass that writes index rows or stored node fields with a belt lacking a unit the state records as covered, or while an open generation is at another `gv`, applies the tick's belt-state rule itself and records the belt due, or that unit's letter-glued and stray-CSI remnants stay terms with no generation ever owed for them). Departures: D-4687 (`history-span-exact-partition`), D-4697 (`history-reparse-targets`) (NEW, Task 6's slug: §8.4 sets the limit, not the target grammar — `--node` a leaf or every leaf under a condensed node, `--session` every leaf of that id's families, neither every leaf), D-4706 (`history-parser-crash-recorded`) (NEW, Task 8's slug, RB5: a parser crash is recorded on the leaf, or as a boundary marker, counted once, and retried only by reparse), D-4698 (`history-ops-refused-while-recovering`) (NEW, RB6; defined by Task 6; Task 19 places the refusal).

Choices this task makes (each is in the PR body's open issues):
- **One refusal refuses the whole run.** Any pruned target answers `span-pruned` and nothing is re-derived, so `node_sources` (and every other row) stay byte-identical.
- **A dry run predicts the refusal.** `reparse` without `--apply` answers the same `reparse-too-many` or `span-pruned` exit 2 the `--apply` would, so the operator sees it before applying; otherwise exit 0 with the target count.
- **An unknown `--node` is exit 3** (not found, no reason word, §8.3) in both forms.
- **A tombstoned summary blob is a pruned span too.** prune never tombstones one (it is structure, Task 20), but a restored or hand-edited store can hold one.
- **Over the limit, `pruned` is not measured**: the refusal is `reparse-too-many` whatever the spans hold, and a per-leaf probe over every leaf of a large store buys nothing.
- **reparse is RB5's one retry.** A `parse-failed` leaf is an ordinary target (it is a node row), so any reparse that names it re-derives it. A leaf whose derivation still throws is recorded `parse-failed` again, counted, and reported in the line (`F failed`); the run still exits 0, and the others are re-derived. An all-leaves or `--session` run also clears the matching `leaf-crashed` markers and lowers the leaves cursor, so the next tick derives those boundaries; a `--node` run names no boundary without a leaf, so it clears none.
- **Parents are re-rolled over every target, whatever changed.** `rerollParents` is idempotent, so a rerun after a run that stopped between a leaf's commit and the re-roll heals the parents even when every leaf now reads `unchanged`.
- **One pass cache per run.** The targets share deriveLeaves' `{ copy, epochs, files }` cache, so a 500-leaf reparse over one transcript plans that copy once, not once per leaf.
- **The reparse applies the tick's belt-state rule before it rewrites a leaf (spec §6.2 "The belt").** A reparse redacts gists, topics, refs and `nodes_fts` rows with its own pass's belt. A unit whose file is unreadable during the pass is missing from that belt, while meta `fts_belt` may record it as covered, so no tick would ever open the generation that re-redacts those rows (spec §6.2 "The belt"). `recordBeltDueIfUncovered` runs in its own transaction after `secretsStep` and before the first leaf: a kill after any leaf's commit then finds the belt already due. The rule is the plain inequality (the state's version, its `rids` against the pass's live units, an open `gen` against them and its `gv` against `BELT_VERSION`), so a pass with a unit the state does not name yet also records the belt due; that costs at most one extra belt generation per operator pass, which is rare, and buys a rule that needs no mark.

```js
    const protoR21 = DatabaseSyncR21.prototype;
    const realPrepareR21 = protoR21.prepare;
    protoR21.prepare = function prepareR21(sql) {
      const st = realPrepareR21.call(this, sql);
      if (String(sql) === 'SELECT z FROM blobs WHERE blob_id = ?') {
        const realGetR21 = st.get.bind(st);
        st.get = (...args) => {
          if (String(args[0]) === throwBlobR21 && String(new Error().stack).includes('/ccd/history/derive.mjs')) {
            throw new Error(`preload-faults: HISTORY_TEST_THROW_BLOB ${throwBlobR21}`);
          }
          return realGetR21(...args);
        };
      }
      return st;
    };
  }
}
```

`fs` and `path` are history-maint.test.ts's own imports (Task 19), and `maintMeta` is Task 20's helper. The O59 case reads the belt state through `maintMeta` and `JSON.parse`, not lib's `parseBeltState`, so it holds whatever extra fields a later state grammar adds beside `v`, `rids` and `gen`; its last assertions are the exact due record `recordBeltDueIfUncovered` writes, read as `v`, `rids` and `gen` apart from the witness `w` that the pass's closing `stampBeltWitness` adds, and that `w` itself. Its first comparison, `toBe(covered)` after a reparse with every unit loaded, holds byte for byte: that pass records no pair and moves no witnessed value, so its stamp writes nothing. The node rewrite that this due record buys (the next tick's belt generation reopens `('nodes-belt', 1)`, whose step re-redacts every stored node field) is Task 29's, which pins it end to end.
