```ts
// ── W1-B2 Task 24: the binding verbs' store sequences (spec §8.4 adopt, restore, rebuild; §6.2) ────────────────
describe('store.mjs: the binding verbs\' sequences (W1-B2 Task 24)', () => {
  const STORE_MJS = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../ccd/history/store.mjs');
  const FAULTS_MJS = path.resolve(__dirname, 'fixtures/history/preload-faults.mjs');
  /** One fixed bind time, so every `bound:<ms>`, recover step and `bind` record below is named exactly. */
  const T = 1_791_000_000_000;
  const RESTORE_BODY = 'const s = S.stageRestore(process.argv[1], process.argv[2]); '
    + 'S.commitRestore(process.argv[1], s, { nowMs: Number(process.argv[3]) });';
  const ADOPT_BODY = 'S.adoptStore(process.argv[1], { nowMs: Number(process.argv[2]) });';
  const REBUILD_BODY = "S.createStore(process.argv[1], { storeId: process.argv[2], bind: { kind: 'rebuild', nowMs: Number(process.argv[3]) } });";
  const home = (): string => mkTmp('ccrc-history-bindverb-');

  /** `body` in a child that imports store.mjs as `S`, SIGKILLed by the fault preload at `kill`. The `timeout`
   *  ends a child that hangs instead, with SIGTERM, so a hang is never read as the planned SIGKILL. */
  const killedAt = (h: string, kill: string, body: string, args: string[]): ReturnType<typeof spawnSync> => spawnSync(
    process.execPath,
    ['--no-warnings', '--import', pathToFileURL(FAULTS_MJS).href, '--input-type=module', '-e',
      `import * as S from ${JSON.stringify(pathToFileURL(STORE_MJS).href)}; ${body}`, ...args],
    { encoding: 'utf8', env: { PATH: process.env['PATH'] ?? '', HOME: h, HISTORY_TEST_KILL: kill }, timeout: 60_000, killSignal: 'SIGTERM' },
  );

  /** A store, a `VACUUM INTO` backup of it under its own db/backups/, then the box as a loss leaves it. The DB,
   *  its sidecars and store.writer are gone, and store.id is gone too unless `keepStoreId`. */
  const backedUp = (h: string, name: string, keepStoreId: boolean): { storeId: string; oldWriter: string } => {
    const { storeId, writer } = createStore(h);
    const P = historyPaths(h);
    const db = openWriter(P.dbFile);
    bump(db, 'fixture_rows', 3);
    fs.mkdirSync(P.backups, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    db.prepare('VACUUM INTO ?').run(path.join(P.backups, name));
    closeWriter(db);
    for (const f of [P.dbFile, P.wal, P.shm, P.writer, ...(keepStoreId ? [] : [P.storeId])]) fs.rmSync(f, { force: true });
    return { storeId, oldWriter: writer };
  };

  /** A backup whose middle page is overwritten. integrity_check reports such damage as rows, it does not throw
   *  (measured, 22.16.0 and 24.14.1), and meta.store_id still reads. So only the integrity check can refuse it. */
  const corruptBackup = (h: string, name: string): void => {
    const P = historyPaths(h);
    const db = openWriter(P.dbFile);
    const ins = db.prepare('INSERT INTO counters (name, n) VALUES (?, ?)');
    withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
      for (let i = 0; i < 4000; i += 1) ins.run(`fixture_counter_${String(i).padStart(5, '0')}_${'x'.repeat(60)}`, i);
    });
    fs.mkdirSync(P.backups, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    const out = path.join(P.backups, name);
    db.prepare('VACUUM INTO ?').run(out);
    closeWriter(db);
    const pages = Math.floor(fs.statSync(out).size / 4096);
    const fd = fs.openSync(out, 'r+');
    try { fs.writeSync(fd, Buffer.alloc(200, 0xff), 0, 200, Math.floor(pages / 2) * 4096 + 8); } finally { fs.closeSync(fd); }
  };

  /** What a binding left INSIDE a DB file, read through a read-only handle. */
  const inside = (dbFile: string): {
    storeId: string | null; writer: string | null; journalMode: string;
    bound: Array<Record<string, unknown>>; recover: Array<Record<string, unknown>>; binds: Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
  } => {
    const db = new DatabaseSync(dbFile, { readOnly: true });
    try {
      return {
        storeId: getMeta(db, 'store_id'),
        writer: getMeta(db, 'writer'),
        journalMode: String(pragma(db, 'journal_mode')),
        bound: db.prepare("SELECT k, v FROM meta WHERE k LIKE 'bound:%' ORDER BY k").all().map((r) => ({ ...r })),
        recover: db.prepare("SELECT version, cursor, completed_ms FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'recover' ORDER BY version")
          .all().map((r) => ({ ...r })),
        binds: db.prepare('SELECT rec FROM journal_outbox ORDER BY seq').all().flatMap((r) => {
          const p = parseJournalRecord(String(r['rec']));
          return p.kind === 'record' ? [{ ...p.rec }] : [];
        }),
      };
    } finally {
      db.close();
    }
  };
  const bindRecord = (kind: string, writer: string, t = T): Record<string, unknown> =>
    ({ v: 1, k: 'verdict', t, event_key: 'none', kind: 'bind', bind: kind, writer });

  it('adoptStore: the bind commits inside the DB, then store.writer, then store.id; a fresh token and no recovery step', () => {
    const h = home();
    const P = historyPaths(h);
    const { storeId, writer: oldWriter } = createStore(h);
    fs.rmSync(P.storeId);
    fs.rmSync(P.writer);
    expect(decideStoreOpen(measureStoreFacts(h, 'fleet'))).toEqual({ act: 'refuse', word: 'store-unbound' });
    const got = adoptStore(h, { nowMs: T });
    expect(got.storeId).toBe(storeId);
    expect(got.writer).toMatch(WRITER_RE);
    expect(got.writer).not.toBe(oldWriter);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(P.storeId, 'utf8').trim()).toBe(storeId);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(P.writer, 'utf8').trim()).toBe(got.writer);
    expect(mode(P.storeId)).toBe(0o600);
    const f = inside(P.dbFile);
    expect(f.writer).toBe(got.writer);
    expect(f.bound).toEqual([{ k: `bound:${T}`, v: 'adopt' }]);
    expect(f.recover, 'adopt registers no recovery step (RC16)').toEqual([]);
    expect(f.binds).toEqual([bindRecord('adopt', got.writer)]);
    expect(decideStoreOpen(measureStoreFacts(h, 'fleet'))).toEqual({ act: 'open' });
  });

  it('adoptStore killed right after store.id lands finds the bind already committed; killed before it, the store stays unbound and a second adopt binds it', () => {
    const h = home();
    const P = historyPaths(h);
    createStore(h);
    fs.rmSync(P.storeId);
    fs.rmSync(P.writer);
    // writeFileAtomic(store.id) renames `store.id.tmp.<pid>`: the first rename naming `store.id.tmp`.
    const r = killedAt(h, 'renameSync:store.id.tmp:1:after', ADOPT_BODY, [h, String(T)]);
    expect(r.signal, String(r.stderr)).toBe('SIGKILL');
    expect(fs.existsSync(P.storeId)).toBe(true);
    const f = inside(P.dbFile);
    expect(f.bound, 'the bind committed before store.id named the store').toEqual([{ k: `bound:${T}`, v: 'adopt' }]);
    expect(f.binds).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(f.writer).toBe(fs.readFileSync(P.writer, 'utf8').trim());

    const h2 = home();
    const P2 = historyPaths(h2);
    createStore(h2);
    fs.rmSync(P2.storeId);
    fs.rmSync(P2.writer);
    const r2 = killedAt(h2, 'renameSync:store.id.tmp:1', ADOPT_BODY, [h2, String(T)]);
    expect(r2.signal, String(r2.stderr)).toBe('SIGKILL');
    expect(fs.existsSync(P2.storeId)).toBe(false);
    expect(decideStoreOpen(measureStoreFacts(h2, 'fleet'))).toEqual({ act: 'refuse', word: 'store-unbound' });
    const again = adoptStore(h2, { nowMs: T + 1 });
    expect(fs.readFileSync(P2.storeId, 'utf8').trim()).toBe(again.storeId);
    const f2 = inside(P2.dbFile);
    expect(f2.binds).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(f2.writer).toBe(again.writer);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(P2.writer, 'utf8').trim()).toBe(again.writer);
    expect(decideStoreOpen(measureStoreFacts(h2, 'fleet'))).toEqual({ act: 'open' });
  });

  it('restore onto a fresh box: a 0600 copy measured, then made WAL with every binding fact inside it, linked, and bound through the pending marker', () => {
    const h = home();
    const P = historyPaths(h);
    const name = '20261001T000000Z.db';

    const prev = process.umask(0o002);
    let staged: ReturnType<typeof stageRestore> | null = null;
    let tempMode = 0;
    let got: { storeId: string; writer: string } | null = null;

      tempMode = mode(staged.tempPath);

    expect(tempMode, 'the copy is 0600 under any umask').toBe(0o600);
    expect(path.basename(staged!.tempPath)).toMatch(/^\.history\.db\.restore\.[0-9]+$/);
    expect(staged).toMatchObject({ storeId: { state: 'value', value: storeId }, userVersion: SCHEMA_VERSION, integrityOk: true });
    expect(staged!.sizeBytes).toBe(fs.statSync(path.join(P.backups, name)).size);
    const bound = got!;
    expect(bound.storeId).toBe(storeId);
    expect(bound.writer).toMatch(WRITER_RE);
    expect(bound.writer).not.toBe(oldWriter);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(P.storeId, 'utf8').trim()).toBe(storeId);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(P.writer, 'utf8').trim()).toBe(bound.writer);
    expect(fs.existsSync(P.pending)).toBe(false);
    expect(fs.readdirSync(P.dbDir).filter((n) => n.startsWith('.history.db.restore.'))).toEqual([]);
    expect(mode(P.dbFile)).toBe(0o600);

    expect(f).toMatchObject({

    expect(f.binds).toEqual([bindRecord('restore', bound.writer)]);
    expect(decideStoreOpen(measureStoreFacts(h, 'fleet'))).toEqual({ act: 'open' });

  it('restore with store.id already naming the backup\'s store writes no pending marker, and a kill right after the link finds the binding and the recovery step inside history.db', () => {
    const h = home();

  it('restore puts every journal-known redact pair into the copy before the link and starts the step +pairs; a pair the backup already holds adds nothing (spec §8.4 and §9.14)', () => {
    const shaA = 'a1'.repeat(32);   // recorded before the backup was taken: the backup holds it
    const shaB = 'b2'.repeat(32);   // learned after it: only the journal holds it
    /** A store holding pair A, its VACUUM INTO backup under db/backups/, then the box as a loss leaves it. */
    const withPairA = (h: string, name: string): void => {

      try {
        db.prepare('INSERT INTO redact_hashes (len, sha256, first_seen_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?)').run(32, Buffer.from(shaA, 'hex'), T - 10);
        fs.mkdirSync(P.backups, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
        db.prepare('VACUUM INTO ?').run(path.join(P.backups, name));
      } finally { closeWriter(db); }
      for (const f of [P.dbFile, P.wal, P.shm, P.writer, P.storeId]) fs.rmSync(f, { force: true });
    };
    const pairsIn = (dbFile: string): Array<Record<string, unknown>> => {
      const db = new DatabaseSync(dbFile, { readOnly: true });
      try {
        return db.prepare('SELECT len, lower(hex(sha256)) AS sha FROM redact_hashes ORDER BY len').all().map((r) => ({ ...r }));
      } finally { db.close(); }
    };
    const PAIRS_BODY = 'const s = S.stageRestore(process.argv[1], process.argv[2]); '
      + 'S.commitRestore(process.argv[1], s, { nowMs: Number(process.argv[3]), pairs: JSON.parse(process.argv[4]) });';

    // Killed right before the link: the copy the kill leaves already holds both pairs and the +pairs cursor.
    const h = home();
    const P = historyPaths(h);
    const name = '20261005T000000Z.db';
    withPairA(h, name);
    const both = JSON.stringify([{ len: 32, sha256: shaA, t: T - 10 }, { len: 40, sha256: shaB, t: T - 5 }]);
    const r = killedAt(h, 'linkSync:.history.db.restore.:1', PAIRS_BODY, [h, name, String(T), both]);
    expect(r.signal, String(r.stderr)).toBe('SIGKILL');
    expect(fs.existsSync(P.dbFile), 'CONTROL: killed before the link').toBe(false);
    const temps = fs.readdirSync(P.dbDir).filter((n) => /^\.history\.db\.restore\.[0-9]+$/.test(n));
    expect(temps.length, 'CONTROL: the kill left the copy').toBe(1);
    const copy = path.join(P.dbDir, temps[0]!);
    expect(pairsIn(copy), 'both pairs are inside the copy before it is linked').toEqual([{ len: 32, sha: shaA }, { len: 40, sha: shaB }]);
    expect(inside(copy).recover, 'the journal-only pair starts the step +pairs, so the reindex phase still runs')
      .toEqual([{ version: T, cursor: 'index+pairs', completed_ms: null }]);

    // Every pair the journal knows already in the backup: nothing added, and the step starts at NULL as before.
    const h2 = home();
    const P2 = historyPaths(h2);
    withPairA(h2, name);
    commitRestore(h2, stageRestore(h2, name), { nowMs: T, pairs: [{ len: 32, sha256: shaA, t: T - 10 }] });
    expect(pairsIn(P2.dbFile)).toEqual([{ len: 32, sha: shaA }]);
    expect(inside(P2.dbFile).recover).toEqual([{ version: T, cursor: null, completed_ms: null }]);
    // A malformed pair is a caller's bug, refused before anything is written.
    const h3 = home();
    withPairA(h3, name);
    const s3 = stageRestore(h3, name);
    expect(() => commitRestore(h3, s3, { nowMs: T, pairs: [{ len: 40, sha256: 'not hex', t: T }] })).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(fs.existsSync(historyPaths(h3).dbFile), 'nothing linked').toBe(false);
    abortRestore(s3);
  });

  it('restore runs the caller\'s belt hooks inside the FULL bind transaction: the check before any binding fact or pair, the stamp after the pairs; a throw links nothing (ruling R-witness-restore)', () => {
    const shaB = 'b2'.repeat(32);   // a journal-only pair: the backup lacks it
    const name = '20261006T000000Z.db';
    const h = home();
    const P = historyPaths(h);
    backedUp(h, name, false);
    const seen: Array<{ hook: string; pairs: number; recover: number; inTx: boolean }> = [];
    const look = (hook: string) => (db: DatabaseSync): void => {
      seen.push({
        hook,
        pairs: Number((db.prepare('SELECT count(*) AS n FROM redact_hashes').get() as { n: number }).n),
        recover: Number((db.prepare("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'recover'").get() as { n: number }).n),
        inTx: db.isTransaction,
      });
    };
    commitRestore(h, stageRestore(h, name), { nowMs: T, pairs: [{ len: 40, sha256: shaB, t: T - 5 }], belt: { check: look('check'), stamp: look('stamp') } });
    expect(seen, 'the check sees the copy as the backup left it, the stamp sees every write, both inside the transaction').toEqual([
      { hook: 'check', pairs: 0, recover: 0, inTx: true },
      { hook: 'stamp', pairs: 1, recover: 1, inTx: true },
    ]);
    expect(inside(P.dbFile).recover, 'CONTROL: the restore committed').toEqual([{ version: T, cursor: 'index+pairs', completed_ms: null }]);

    // A throw from the stamp rolls the whole bind back: nothing is linked, and the copy holds none of it.
    const h2 = home();
    backedUp(h2, name, false);
    const s2 = stageRestore(h2, name);
    expect(() => commitRestore(h2, s2, { nowMs: T, pairs: [{ len: 40, sha256: shaB, t: T - 5 }], belt: {
      check: () => {}, stamp: () => { throw new Error('fixture: the stamp failed'); },
    } })).toThrow('fixture: the stamp failed');
    expect(fs.existsSync(historyPaths(h2).dbFile), 'nothing linked').toBe(false);
    expect(inside(s2.tempPath).recover, 'the bind rolled back with the stamp').toEqual([]);
    abortRestore(s2);
    // A belt without both hooks is a caller's bug, refused before anything is written.
    const h3 = home();
    backedUp(h3, name, false);
    const s3 = stageRestore(h3, name);
    expect(() => commitRestore(h3, s3, { nowMs: T, belt: { check: () => {} } as never })).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(inside(s3.tempPath).bound, 'nothing written').toEqual([]);
    abortRestore(s3);
  });

  it('stageRestore measures the copy and never trusts it: damage reads integrityOk false, a file that is no store reads its store_id unreadable, a link or a path is refused, and abortRestore takes the temp', () => {
    const h = home();
    const P = historyPaths(h);
    const { storeId } = createStore(h);
    corruptBackup(h, 'corrupt.db');
    const s = stageRestore(h, 'corrupt.db');
    expect(s.storeId, 'meta still reads: only the integrity check can refuse this copy').toEqual({ state: 'value', value: storeId });
    expect(s.integrityOk).toBe(false);
    abortRestore(s);
    expect(fs.existsSync(s.tempPath)).toBe(false);

    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(P.backups, 'text.db'), 'this is not a database file at all, it is text\n'.repeat(400));
    const t = stageRestore(h, 'text.db');
    expect(t).toMatchObject({ storeId: { state: 'unreadable' }, userVersion: null, integrityOk: false });
    abortRestore(t);

    fs.symlinkSync(path.join(P.backups, 'corrupt.db'), path.join(P.backups, 'link.db'));
    expect(wordOf(() => stageRestore(h, 'link.db')), 'a symlink is never followed (O_NOFOLLOW)').toBe('restore-refused');
    expect(wordOf(() => stageRestore(h, '../store.id'))).toBe('restore-refused');
    expect(fs.readdirSync(P.dbDir).filter((n) => n.startsWith('.history.db.restore.'))).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('createStore with a store_id and a rebuild bind: that id, the binding and the recovery step inside, store.id through the pending marker; none when store.id already names it; B1\'s plain creation unchanged', () => {
    const S1 = mintStoreId();
    const h = home();
    const P = historyPaths(h);
    const got = createStore(h, { storeId: S1, bind: { kind: 'rebuild', nowMs: T } });
    expect(got.storeId).toBe(S1);
    expect(fs.readFileSync(P.storeId, 'utf8').trim()).toBe(S1);
    expect(fs.existsSync(P.pending)).toBe(false);
    const f = inside(P.dbFile);
    expect(f).toMatchObject({
      storeId: S1, writer: got.writer, journalMode: 'wal',

      recover: [{ version: T, cursor: null, completed_ms: null }],

    expect(f.binds).toEqual([bindRecord('rebuild', got.writer)]);

    // store.id already names the store: a kill right after the link leaves no marker, and the store opens.

    const r = killedAt(h2, 'linkSync:history.db.new.:1:after', REBUILD_BODY, [h2, S1, String(T)]);
    expect(r.signal, String(r.stderr)).toBe('SIGKILL');

    expect(inside(P2.dbFile).recover).toEqual([{ version: T, cursor: null, completed_ms: null }]);

    // B1's first install: no bound row, no recovery step, an empty outbox.
    const h3 = home();
    createStore(h3);
    expect(inside(historyPaths(h3).dbFile)).toMatchObject({ bound: [], recover: [], binds: [] });
  });

  it('createStore with a rebuild bind killed between the link and the pending rename: finish-pending, the recovery step already inside', () => {
    const S1 = mintStoreId();
    const h = home();
    const P = historyPaths(h);
    const r = killedAt(h, 'renameSync:store.id.pending:2', REBUILD_BODY, [h, S1, String(T)]);

    expect(f.bound).toEqual([{ k: `bound:${T}`, v: 'rebuild' }]);
```

```js
/** First creation (§6.2), run only on `decideStoreOpen`'s `create` (or after
 *  `dropPending` on `drop-pending-create`), under the shim's lock. Since
 *  W1-B2 it is also run by `doctor --rebuild` (§8.4), which passes the
 *  journal's store_id as `opts.storeId` and a `bind` (D-4694 (history-rebuild-verb)):
 *
 *   1. root and db/ exist, 0700;
 *   2. the store_id (`opts.storeId`, else minted) and a fresh writer token.
 *      `store.writer` is written first, then `store.id.pending`. The marker is
 *      skipped when `store.id` already names the store, as a rebuild's may.
 *      Each is written temp-then-rename and fsynced (§9.14: the token is on
 *      disk before any marker names the store);
 *   3. `history.db.new.<pid>` created O_CREAT|O_EXCL 0600 — a temp whose name
 *      exists, or whose sidecars exist, is never opened;
 *   4. auto_vacuum, WAL, the v1 DDL, meta store_id and writer, user_version 1,
 *      and with `opts.bind` every DB-side fact of the binding (`bound:<ms>`,
 *      the ('recover', <ms>) step, the `bind` outbox row), all in ONE
 *      transaction; then close (the WAL is checkpointed away);
 *   5. fsync the temp, `link()` it to history.db (fails if one appeared), unlink
 *      the temp, fsync db/;
 *   6. when step 2 wrote the marker, rename `store.id.pending` to `store.id`
 *      and fsync the root.
 *
 *  A kill at any step leaves a state `decideStoreOpen` decides:
 *  - before step 5, no history.db exists. The pending marker is dropped
 *    (`drop-pending-create`, DM33). For a rebuild, its journal makes the box
 *    `store-recoverable`, and the operator runs the verb again;
 *  - between 5 and 6, the DB carries the marker's id, and the next pass
 *    finishes the rename (`finish-pending`, DM33b). A rebuild's binding and
 *    recovery step are already inside it (D-4724 (history-binding-facts-before-link)). */
export function createStore(home, opts = {}) {
  const P = historyPaths(home);
  mkdirDurable(P.dbDir);
  chmodSync(P.root, 0o700);
  if (lstatSync(P.dbDir).isDirectory()) chmodSync(P.dbDir, 0o700);

  const storeId = opts.storeId ?? mintStoreId();
  const writer = mintWriter();
  const viaPending = readBindingFile(P.storeId, UUID_RE).state === 'absent';
  writeFileAtomic(P.writer, `${writer}\n`);
  if (viaPending) writeFileAtomic(P.pending, `${storeId}\n`);

  const tmp = `${P.dbDir}/history.db.new.${process.pid}`;
  for (const s of ['-wal', '-shm', '-journal']) {
    if (existsSync(`${tmp}${s}`)) throw new Error(`${tmp}${s} exists; a temp with sidecars is never opened`);
  }
  closeSync(openSync(tmp, FS.O_CREAT | FS.O_EXCL | FS.O_WRONLY, 0o600));
  const db = new DatabaseSync(tmp);
  try {
    db.exec('PRAGMA auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL');
    db.exec('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL');
    db.exec('BEGIN IMMEDIATE');
    try {
      db.exec(MIGRATIONS[0]);
      const put = db.prepare('INSERT INTO meta (k, v) VALUES (?, ?)');
      put.run('store_id', storeId);
      put.run('writer', writer);
      if (opts.bind !== undefined) insertBindFacts(db, { kind: opts.bind.kind, nowMs: opts.bind.nowMs, writer, recover: true });
      db.exec(`PRAGMA user_version = ${SCHEMA_VERSION}`);
      db.exec('COMMIT');
    } catch (err) {
      try { db.exec('ROLLBACK'); } catch { /* the transaction is already gone */ }
      throw err;
    }
  } finally {
    db.close();
  }
  const fd = openSync(tmp, FS.O_RDONLY);
  try { fsyncSync(fd); } finally { closeSync(fd); }
  linkSync(tmp, P.dbFile);
  unlinkSync(tmp);
  fsyncDir(P.dbDir);
  if (viaPending) {
    renameSync(P.pending, P.storeId);
    fsyncDir(P.root);
  }
  return { storeId, writer };
}
```

On the first-install path `store.id` is absent, so `viaPending` is true. B1's sequence and its tests (DM33, DM33b, "§9.14: store.writer is on disk before any marker") are therefore unchanged.

- [ ] **Step 5: Append the binding section to the end of `ccd/history/store.mjs`:**

```js
// ── The binding verbs' sequences: adopt, restore, rebuild (spec §8.4, §6.2, §9.14; W1-B2) ───────────────────
// lib's decideBind decides each verb's preconditions from measureStoreFacts' facts (L1). These functions only
// execute the sequence §8.4 names, in its order (L3).
//
// The rule all three share (rev 3.2 review, DI3; D-4724 (history-binding-facts-before-link)): every DB-side fact of a
// binding is committed INSIDE the database before any binding file names it. The facts are:
//   - `bound:<ms>` = the verb, so a later merger can see that the store moved;
//   - a new writer token as meta.writer, the mirror of store.writer (D-4226,
//     D-4220);
//   - for a restore or a rebuild, the ('recover', <ms>) derivation step the following ticks run (§9.14);
//   - the `bind` verdict in journal_outbox, which the first pass to open the store flushes into
//     journal/<store_id>/ under the new token.
// So a kill leaves one of two states (D-4184):
//   - an unbound store, which a second run binds;
//   - a store whose binding and recovery are already inside it, which the pending-marker path finishes (§6.2).
// It never leaves a bound store under a departed box's token, and never a restore whose replay is skipped.

/** The size of one read and one write while a restore copies its backup. */
const RESTORE_PIECE = 1 << 20;
/** A journal-known redact pair into the staged copy (spec §8.4 and §9.14): the same row the
 *  recovery step's index phase inserts, so that phase finds it present. */
const RESTORE_PAIR_INSERT = 'INSERT INTO redact_hashes (len, sha256, first_seen_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT (len, sha256) DO NOTHING';
const PAIR_SHA_RE = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/;

/** Every DB-side fact of one binding, inside the CALLER's transaction. A second call for the same verb and
 *  millisecond rewrites meta.writer and adds its `bind` row; the `bound:<ms>` row and the recover row stay single. */
function insertBindFacts(db, b) {
  setMeta(db, `bound:${b.nowMs}`, b.kind);
  setMeta(db, 'writer', b.writer);
  if (b.recover) {
    db.prepare("INSERT INTO derivation_state (step, version, cursor, completed_ms) VALUES ('recover', ?, NULL, NULL) ON CONFLICT (step, version) DO NOTHING")
      .run(b.nowMs);
  }
  db.prepare('INSERT INTO journal_outbox (rec) VALUES (?)')
    .run(journalRecord('verdict', b.nowMs, { event_key: 'none', kind: 'bind', bind: b.kind, writer: b.writer }));
}

/** `doctor --adopt` (§8.4; D-4692 (history-adopt-verb)), once decideBind admitted it: the present DB's own
 *  meta.store_id becomes this box's store. In order:
 *  1. the bind commits FULL: `bound:<ms>` = adopt, the new token, the `bind` row. No recovery step: the store is
 *     whole, it only moved (RC16);
 *  2. store.writer;
 *  3. store.id.
 *  A kill between 1 and 3 leaves the store unbound, and a second adopt binds it. Never a bound store under the
 *  departed box's token. */
export function adoptStore(home, { nowMs }) {
  const P = historyPaths(home);
  const writer = mintWriter();
  const db = openWriter(P.dbFile);
  try {
    const storeId = getMeta(db, 'store_id');
    if (storeId === null || !UUID_RE.test(storeId)) {
      throw new StoreError('adopt-refused', `${P.dbFile} carries no readable meta.store_id`);
    }
    withTx(db, 'FULL', () => { insertBindFacts(db, { kind: 'adopt', nowMs, writer, recover: false }); });
    writeFileAtomic(P.writer, `${writer}\n`);
    writeFileAtomic(P.storeId, `${storeId}\n`);
    return { storeId, writer };
  } finally {
    closeWriter(db);
  }
}

/** What a staged restore copy says about itself, measured on the COPY, never on the backup: its user_version, its
 *  meta.store_id (a value, absent, or unreadable for a file that is no store) and whether PRAGMA integrity_check
 *  answers exactly one row, `ok`. A file that will not open as a database reads as unreadable and not ok. */
function measureStaged(tempPath) {
  const out = { storeId: { state: 'unreadable' }, userVersion: null, integrityOk: false };
  let db;
  try {
    db = openReader(tempPath);
    out.userVersion = userVersion(db);
    const row = db.prepare("SELECT v FROM meta WHERE k = 'store_id'").get();
    if (row === undefined) out.storeId = { state: 'absent' };
    else if (UUID_RE.test(String(row.v))) out.storeId = { state: 'value', value: String(row.v) };
    const rows = db.prepare('PRAGMA integrity_check').all();
    out.integrityOk = rows.length === 1 && String(Object.values(rows[0])[0]) === 'ok';
  } catch {
    // A file that is no database, or whose meta cannot be read: what was measured stands, the rest stays unread.
  } finally {
    try { db?.close(); } catch { /* read-only: nothing to lose */ }
  }
  return out;
}

/** `doctor --restore <name>`, first half (§8.4; D-4693 (history-restore-verb)). Copy db/backups/<name> to
 *  db/.history.db.restore.<pid>:
 *  - the backup is opened O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and must be a regular file;
 *  - the temp is created O_EXCL and fchmodded 0600, so it is 0600 from its first byte under any umask;
 *  - the copy is fsynced, then measured (measureStaged) for decideBind's second look.
 *  A bare name only: anything with a `/` is refused here as in lib's restoreNameOk. The caller removes the temp on
 *  any refusal (abortRestore), and the next lock-holding pass's removeStaleTemps catches a kill. */
export function stageRestore(home, name) {
  const P = historyPaths(home);
  if (typeof name !== 'string' || name === '' || name === '.' || name === '..' || name.includes('/')) {
    throw new StoreError('restore-refused', `${JSON.stringify(name)} is not a bare file name under db/backups`);
  }
  const src = `${P.backups}/${name}`;
  const tempPath = `${P.dbDir}/.history.db.restore.${process.pid}`;
  for (const s of ['', '-wal', '-shm', '-journal']) {
    if (existsSync(`${tempPath}${s}`)) throw new Error(`${tempPath}${s} exists; a temp is never reopened`);
  }
  let from;
  try {
    from = openSync(src, FS.O_RDONLY | FS.O_NOFOLLOW | FS.O_NONBLOCK);
  } catch (e) {
    throw new StoreError('restore-refused', `${src} cannot be opened as a regular file without following a link (${e && e.code ? e.code : 'error'})`);
  }
  let sizeBytes = 0;
  try {
    if (!fstatSync(from).isFile()) throw new StoreError('restore-refused', `${src} is not a regular file`);
    const to = openSync(tempPath, FS.O_CREAT | FS.O_EXCL | FS.O_WRONLY, 0o600);
    try {
      fchmodSync(to, 0o600);
      const buf = Buffer.allocUnsafe(RESTORE_PIECE);
      for (;;) {
        const n = readSync(from, buf, 0, buf.length, null);
        if (n === 0) break;
        for (let off = 0; off < n;) off += writeSync(to, buf, off, n - off);
        sizeBytes += n;
      }
      fsyncSync(to);
    } finally {
      closeSync(to);
    }
  } finally {
    closeSync(from);
  }
  return { tempPath, ...measureStaged(tempPath), sizeBytes };
}

/** `doctor --restore`, second half, once decideBind admitted the staged copy (D-4218,
 *  D-4724 (history-binding-facts-before-link)). In order:
 *  1. on the COPY: `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, because a VACUUM INTO output is a rollback-journal database (M,
 *     22.16.0);
 *  2. still on the copy, ONE FULL transaction: `bound:<ms>` = restore, a new writer token, the ('recover', <ms>)
 *     step and the `bind` outbox row, and every journal-known redact pair `i.pairs` carries (W1-B2 Task 25's
 *     journalRedactPairs, which Task 27's restore reads under its lock) into redact_hashes. A pair the copy lacked
 *     starts the step's cursor `+pairs` (lib's formatRecoverCursor), so the reindex phase still re-derives what the
 *     pair masks, although the index phase will find every pair already present
 *     (spec §8.4 and §9.14). So no read verb ever serves the restored store without a pair the
 *     journal knows: they answer while the step is registered, and their pair index is the store's redact_hashes.
 *     The pair insert raises a value the belt's witness reads, so with `i.belt` that transaction opens with
 *     `belt.check(db)` and closes with `belt.stamp(db)` (spec §6.2 "The belt"; coordinator ruling R-witness-restore:
 *     a belt-aware writer that changes witnessed values checks the witness first, then writes, then stamps). Task 27
 *     passes sweep.mjs's check and Task 7B's stampBeltWitness; store.mjs owns the order only;
 *  3. close it, which checkpoints its own -wal away, and fsync it;
 *  4. store.writer, then store.id.pending when store.id is absent (decideBind refused a store.id naming another
 *     store);
 *  5. `link()` the copy to history.db, which fails if one appeared; unlink the temp;
 *  6. rename the marker to store.id.
 *  A kill anywhere leaves either no history.db, or one whose binding and recovery step are already inside it. */
export function commitRestore(home, staged, { nowMs, pairs = [], belt = null }) {
  const P = historyPaths(home);
  if (staged.storeId.state !== 'value') {
    throw new StoreError('restore-refused', `${staged.tempPath} carries no readable meta.store_id`);
  }
  for (const pr of pairs) {
    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(pr.len) || pr.len <= 0 || !PAIR_SHA_RE.test(String(pr.sha256)) || !Number.isSafeInteger(pr.t)) {
      throw new TypeError(`commitRestore: a redact pair is { len, sha256 (64 hex), t }: ${JSON.stringify(pr)}`);
    }
  }
  if (belt !== null && (typeof belt?.check !== 'function' || typeof belt?.stamp !== 'function')) {
    throw new TypeError('commitRestore: a belt is null or { check(db), stamp(db) }');
  }
  const storeId = staged.storeId.value;
  const writer = mintWriter();
  const db = new DatabaseSync(staged.tempPath);
  try {
    db.exec(`PRAGMA busy_timeout = ${BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS}`);
    db.exec('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL');
    if (journalModeOf(db) !== 'wal') {
      throw new StoreError('store-not-wal', `${staged.tempPath} would not change to WAL mode`);
    }
    withTx(db, 'FULL', () => {
      // spec §6.2 "The belt" (R-witness-restore): the witness checked before this transaction writes anything.
      if (belt !== null) belt.check(db);
      insertBindFacts(db, { kind: 'restore', nowMs, writer, recover: true });
      // spec §8.4 and §9.14 (R-restore-pairs): every journal-known pair, inside the copy, before the link.
      const ins = db.prepare(RESTORE_PAIR_INSERT);
      let added = 0;
      for (const pr of pairs) added += Number(ins.run(pr.len, Buffer.from(pr.sha256, 'hex'), pr.t).changes);
      if (added > 0) {
        db.prepare("UPDATE derivation_state SET cursor = ? WHERE step = 'recover' AND version = ?")
          .run(formatRecoverCursor({ phase: RECOVER_PHASES[0], file: null, offset: 0, blobId: null, pairsAdded: true }), nowMs);
      }
      // ... and stamped after its last write, so the first recovery pass never reads the pairs as another build's.
      if (belt !== null) belt.stamp(db);
    });
  } finally {
    db.close();
  }
  const fd = openSync(staged.tempPath, FS.O_RDONLY);
  try { fsyncSync(fd); } finally { closeSync(fd); }
  writeFileAtomic(P.writer, `${writer}\n`);
  const needsPending = readBindingFile(P.storeId, UUID_RE).state === 'absent';
  if (needsPending) writeFileAtomic(P.pending, `${storeId}\n`);
  linkSync(staged.tempPath, P.dbFile);
  unlinkSync(staged.tempPath);
  fsyncDir(P.dbDir);
  if (needsPending) {
    renameSync(P.pending, P.storeId);
    fsyncDir(P.root);
  }
  return { storeId, writer };
}

/** A refused restore's copy, removed with its sidecars: SQLite pairs a WAL with its file by name (DI13). */
export function abortRestore(staged) {
  for (const s of ['', '-wal', '-shm', '-journal']) rmSync(`${staged.tempPath}${s}`, { force: true });
}
```

```bash
git commit -m "feat(history): binding sequences for adopt, restore and rebuild in store.mjs

adoptStore commits bound:<ms>, a new writer token and the bind outbox row
before store.writer and store.id. stageRestore copies a backup O_NOFOLLOW into
an O_EXCL 0600 temp and measures the copy. commitRestore sets WAL on the copy
and commits the binding facts with the ('recover', <ms>) step inside it, then
links it through store.id.pending. Every redact pair the journal knows goes
into the copy in that same transaction, before the link, and starts the step
+pairs when one was new, so a restored store is never readable without a
journal-known pair. A caller's belt hooks open and close that transaction:
the witness check first, the stamp last. createStore takes the journal's store_id and a rebuild
bind, all inside its creation transaction. Each order is pinned by a kill
seam."
```

  - `export function journalRedactPairs(P, storeId: string): { pairs: Array<{ len: number; sha256: string; t: number }>; skipped: string[] }` (spec §8.4 and §9.14): every `redact` record of the files the index phase reads (journalListing, lib's `indexRecord`), `sha256` in hex as the record carries it, and the name of every file it did not read (a foreign head, a name it cannot open, a read that failed part-way). W1-B2 Task 27's restore reads it under its lock and hands `pairs` to Task 24's `commitRestore`.
  - `export const RECOVER_EXECUTORS`, a frozen map from phase to executor. **The executor contract, which Task 29 and W1-B4 implement:**
    - the signature is `(db, run, cursor: RecoverCursor) => { cursor: RecoverCursor; moved: boolean; phaseDone: boolean }`, or a Promise of it;
    - it does ONE bounded chunk;
    - it commits its own cursor, at its own phase, in the same transaction as the records it applies;
    - when it answers `phaseDone`, `recoveryStep` commits the move to the next phase. On the last phase, `recoveryStep` completes the step;
    - an answer of `{ moved: false, phaseDone: false }` ends the step for this pass: the pass counts toward recovery-stalled instead of calling the executor again until the budget runs out;
    - `run` carries `version`, `P`, `storeId`, `budget`, `now`, `ectx` (with `replay: true`, and `belt`: the pass's substring belt from `ctx.belt`, or null), `pairsAdded` and the replay state.
  - A stored cursor that `parseRecoverCursor` refuses is a failed chunk (counted `recover_chunk_failed`, the step ends for the pass), never a silent restart.
  - Scratch tables, made by the step and dropped when it completes (D-4725 (`history-recovery-scratch-tables`), NEW):
    - `recover_verdicts (seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_key TEXT NOT NULL, rec TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE (event_key, rec))`;
    - `recover_drained (file TEXT PRIMARY KEY)`.
  - New counters: `recover_chunk_failed`, `journal_spool_undrained_gone`, `journal_head_mismatch`. `replayStep` names `journal_line_malformed` and `journal_record_unknown`; this task bumps them.
  - `scheduledPass` passes `recovering: isRecovering(db)`, and gains a `run.arm === 'recover'` branch.
  - `passCtx` builds its budget from `deps.budget`, an in-process `{ maxMs?, maxBytes?, chunkBytes? }` (B1's D-4247 (`history-test-seams-not-env`)).

Choices this task makes:
- **The recover arm runs B1's tick prefix, all of it.** `recoverPass` runs items 1-6 of B1's `tick` doc comment, in B1's order and B1's forms:
  - `flushOutbox(db, ctx.home, ctx.ids, ctx.now())`, inside its own `try`, with a `JournalError` counted `journal_write_failed` as `tick` counts it. B1's `scheduledPass` has already flushed once before `planRun` (`flushFirst`), as it does before `tick`, so this flush usually finds nothing;
  - `makeIngestCtx`, then `secretsStep`, whose `pairIdx` goes on the ingest context and whose belt is kept as `ctx.belt`, which `recoveryStep` hands to the executors as `run.ectx.belt` (Task 29);
  - `ftsPrepare`;
  - `reindexForValues(db, ictx, secrets.values, secrets.newValues, ctx.budget, slice)`, then `rederiveFts(db, ictx, ctx.budget, slice)`, sharing one `rederiveSlice(ctx.budget)` slice (review 344 F2). `reindexForValues` searches each value by unit, as B1's tick has it search (B1's D-4311 (`history-reindex-by-units-and-complete-loads`)); B1's D-4344 (`history-reindex-mark-by-rederivation`) removed the `complete` argument D-4311 first gave it, so the recover arm passes none, and only `rederiveFts` moves the mark.
  The prefix stops there. `beltNodesStep`, which Task 29 adds to `tick` as item 7, is left out. When a replay learned a pair, the reindex phase's `recoverNodesBatch` rewrites every node with the full pair index and the belt. A `('nodes-belt', 1)` step that a generation reopened stays open, and the first tick after the step completes runs it. Output stays masked meanwhile (§6.2 states the window).
- **Ruling: the two re-index steps run while the step's `reindex` phase is pending or part-done; nothing gates them.** That phase is Task 29's `recoverReindex` over Task 23's `ftsRebuildJob`. Each way the two steps could harm that rebuild was checked against the code:
  - **Doubled rows.** `blobs_fts` is contentless with `contentless_delete=1` (B1's `store.mjs`), and FTS5 merges a second insert of one rowid instead of refusing it (measured, Task 23). The rebuild's blobs chunk deletes each blob's row before it inserts it (`f.del.run(last);` above `indexBlob`, Task 23 Step 8). So a row the two steps wrote for a blob the rebuild has not reached yet is replaced, never doubled. Both B1 steps also delete before they insert, so a row the rebuild already wrote is replaced the same way. `rederiveFts` writes no `nodes_fts` row. `reindexForValues` does from Task 29 on, through `rederiveGistsFor`, but each of its writers (`refreshLeaf`, `redactNodeFields`) deletes a node's row before inserting one. The rebuild's nodes phase (`indexNodesFts`) skips any node that already has a row. So no node row is doubled either.
  - **Dropped rows.** The rebuild drops and recreates both tables in its first chunk's transaction. It runs only inside `recoveryStep`, after both steps have returned in that pass (`doctor --repair`, its other caller, is refused `recovering` by RB6). What the steps wrote before that chunk is dropped, and the rebuild then re-indexes every blob from 0. What they write in later passes lands in the new tables and is replaced as above.
  - **The mark.** Only `rederiveFts` moves `fts_reindex_rid`, and only to its generation's target, which is at most the highest `redact_hashes` rowid when the generation opened. Each rebuild call indexes with `recoverPairIdx`, which holds every `redact_hashes` row at that call (Task 29), and pairs are only ever added. So every row the rebuild writes after the mark moves carries every pair up to the mark. A blob the rebuild has not reached has either no row in the new tables, or a row one of the two steps wrote with this pass's full pair index. Task 29's `recoverReindex` moves neither `fts_reindex_rid` nor `fts_rederive`.
  - **The belt-due record.** The rebuild's first chunk writes meta `fts_belt` `{ v: 0, rids: [], gen: null }`. An open belt generation reads that record through `decideBelt`, which answers `due: true` and `restart: true` (the record holds no `gen`, so the open generation covers nothing this version can stamp; ruling R-version, Task 7A), and `rederivePlan(mark, top, maxBlobId, state, belt.due, belt.restart)` restarts it as a belt generation from cursor 0 at once: it is never finished and then reopened. Within one pass, both steps finish before the recovery step starts, so a stale belt state never overwrites the record that pass writes. `secretsStep` measures the pass's live units (`pairIdx.beltLive`), and writes belt state in one case only: when lib's `beltWitnessMoved(parseBeltState(fts_belt), beltWitness(db))` is true (a build without the belt wrote since the state was last stamped, ruling R-rollback, Task 7B), it first writes the due record. What takes a unit that stopped being live out of `rids` is `rederiveFts`'s `decideBelt`, which this pass runs before the step, as `tick` runs it before any row is written; and the rebuild itself opens every call with Task 21's `recordBeltDueIfUncovered`, which records the belt due whenever the stored state names a unit the pass has not loaded (spec §6.2 "The belt"). So a rebuild chunk never writes rows without a unit's belt while the state records that unit as covered, whether or not `rederiveFts` wrote a state this pass.
  - **Counters.** Each step bumps `blob_undecodable` only when it removed a row. The rebuild writes no row for an undecodable blob, so nothing is counted twice. The rebuild's completion writes the count it measured, through `applyCounterResets`.
  - **Reads.** grep answers exit 7 `fts-pending` while any `FTS_REBUILD_STEP` row is open (Task 23's `indexGate` term), so no reader sees a half-rebuilt index.
  Gating the two steps would delay a re-index owed by a pair learned during the recovery. It would also leave `fts_rederive` and the belt-due record idle until the step completes. Task 29's restore case and its M1 and M4 predictions assume the steps run. No case pins this choice, because it adds no guard. The guard the ruling rests on is Task 23's delete-before-insert line.

Append to the end of `server/test/fixtures/history/preload-faults.mjs`. Its binding names carry the `Rcv` suffix, because several tasks append to this file:

```js
// ── W1-B2 Task 25: a statement that throws (the recovery chunk's rollback; recovery-stalled) ─────────────────
// HISTORY_TEST_THROW_SQL=<substring>: every prepared statement whose SQL contains <substring> throws, from run, get,
//   all and iterate, an Error coded ERR_SQLITE_ERROR, instead of executing. Not a kill: the pass lives on, so what
//   it does with a failed chunk (roll back, count recover_chunk_failed, keep its cursor) is observable.
import { DatabaseSync as DatabaseSyncRcv } from 'node:sqlite';
{
  const throwSqlRcv = process.env.HISTORY_TEST_THROW_SQL ?? '';
  if (throwSqlRcv !== '') {
    const protoRcv = DatabaseSyncRcv.prototype;
    const prepareRcv = protoRcv.prepare;
    protoRcv.prepare = function prepareThrowRcv(sql) {
      const st = prepareRcv.call(this, sql);
      if (!String(sql).includes(throwSqlRcv)) return st;
      for (const m of ['run', 'get', 'all', 'iterate']) {
        st[m] = () => {
          throw Object.assign(new Error(`preload-faults: injected failure in ${m} of ${throwSqlRcv}`), { code: 'ERR_SQLITE_ERROR' });
        };
      }
      return st;
    };
  }
}
```

```ts
// ── W1-B2 Task 25: recovery fixtures ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
/** Merged with Task 24's DriverDeps: the run budget's limits, which run-pass.mjs hands to sweep.mjs as deps.budget
 *  (an injected dependency, never an environment read; slug history-test-seams-not-env). */
export interface DriverDeps { budgetMs?: number; budgetBytes?: number; chunkBytes?: number }

/** The box's journal directory for its bound store: `~/.ccrc/history/journal/<store.id>`. */
export function journalDirOf(box: HistoryBox): string {
  return path.join(box.root, 'journal', fs.readFileSync(path.join(box.root, 'store.id'), 'utf8').trim());
}

/** The newest recovery step registered in the box's store (what status reads), or undefined. */
export function recoverRow(box: HistoryBox): { version: number; cursor: string | null; completed_ms: number | null } | undefined {
  const db = openStoreRO(box);
  try {
    const r = db.prepare("SELECT version, cursor, completed_ms FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'recover' ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 1")
      .get() as { version: number; cursor: string | null; completed_ms: number | null } | undefined;
    if (r === undefined) return undefined;
    return {
      version: Number(r.version),
      cursor: r.cursor === null ? null : String(r.cursor),
      completed_ms: r.completed_ms === null ? null : Number(r.completed_ms),
    };
  } finally {
    db.close();
  }
}

/** What `doctor --rebuild` leaves before its first recovery tick, made in-process: a fresh history.db with `storeId`
 *  and a new writer token, and inside it the ('recover', version) step, the `bind` outbox row and `bound:<version>`
 *  (store.mjs createStore with a rebuild bind, W1-B2 Task 24). The caller has already removed the lost DB. */
export function boundEmptyStore(box: HistoryBox, storeId: string, version = Date.now()): { storeId: string; writer: string; version: number } {
  const got = createStore(box.home, { storeId, bind: { kind: 'rebuild', nowMs: version } });
  return { ...got, version };
}
```

```ts
// server/test/history-recover.test.ts — the history store's recovery step, and the binding verbs that register it
// (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-ccrc-history-lossless-dag-design.md §9.14 "Recovery", §9.2, §8.4). W1-B2.

removeTmpFixturesEachTest();

const ID2 = 'claude-b-demo';

const MIN = 60_000;

/** A lowercase uuid from a small number: the UUID_RE grammar, readable in a failure. */
const u = (n: number): string => `${n.toString(16).padStart(8, '0')}-0000-4000-8000-${n.toString(16).padStart(12, '0')}`;

interface SweepRecover {
  RECOVER_EXECUTORS: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  recoveryStep(db: DatabaseSync, ctx: Record<string, unknown>, executors?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>):
    Promise<{ moved: boolean; done: boolean; held: boolean }>;
  newBudget(now?: () => number, limits?: { maxMs?: number; maxBytes?: number; chunkBytes?: number }): Record<string, unknown>;
  recoverPass(db: DatabaseSync, ctx: Record<string, unknown>, failedAtStart: number): Promise<number>;
  journalRedactPairs(P: ReturnType<typeof historyPaths>, storeId: string):
    { pairs: Array<{ len: number; sha256: string; t: number }>; skipped: string[] };
}
let SW: SweepRecover;
beforeAll(async () => { SW = (await import('../../ccd/history/sweep.mjs')) as unknown as SweepRecover; });

/** What recoveryStep reads of a TickCtx, in-process: a statfs stub with room to spare (so no case reads the free
 *  space of the box running it) and a run budget, lib's unless `limits` makes it smaller. */
const stepCtx = (box: HistoryBox, ids: { storeId: string; writer: string },
  limits: { maxMs?: number; maxBytes?: number; chunkBytes?: number } = {}): Record<string, unknown> => ({
  home: box.home, paths: historyPaths(box.home), ids, now: () => Date.now(), homes: box.homes, out: () => {},
  deps: { statfs: async () => ({ bsize: 1, bavail: 4 * 2 ** 40, blocks: 8 * 2 ** 40 }) },
  budget: SW.newBudget(() => Date.now(), limits), parsed: { secrets: [] },
});
/** The registered recovery step's cursor, read on the caller's own handle. */
const cursorOn = (db: DatabaseSync): string | null => {
  const r = db.prepare("SELECT cursor FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'recover'").get() as { cursor: string | null } | undefined;
  return r === undefined || r.cursor === null ? null : String(r.cursor);
};
/** Named counters, read on the caller's own handle (0 when never bumped). */
const countersOn = (db: DatabaseSync, ...names: string[]): Record<string, number> =>
  Object.fromEntries(names.map((n) => {
    const r = db.prepare('SELECT n FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get(n) as { n: number } | undefined;
    return [n, r === undefined ? 0 : Number(r.n)];
  }));

/** One scheduled pass that must exit 0. */
const pass = (box: HistoryBox, env: Record<string, string> = {}, preloads: string[] = []): void => {
  const r = runSweep(box, [], { env, preloads });
  expect(r.code, `${r.stdout}\n${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
};
/** One query on the box's store, as plain objects. */
const rows = (box: HistoryBox, sql: string, ...args: (string | number)[]): Array<Record<string, unknown>> => {
  const db = openStoreRO(box);
  try { return db.prepare(sql).all(...args).map((r) => ({ ...r })); } finally { db.close(); }
};
const countOf = (box: HistoryBox, table: string): number => Number(rows(box, `SELECT count(*) AS n FROM ${table}`)[0]!['n']);
const metaOf = (box: HistoryBox, k: string): string | null => {
```
