  - The file's `vitest` import must name `describe`, `it`, `expect` and `beforeEach`. Add any of the four that is missing to that import line.
  - Then append at the end of the file:

```ts
// ── W1-B2 Tasks 27–29: doctor --restore, doctor --rebuild, and redaction through recovery ──────────────────────
// Spec 2026-10-05 §8.4 ("doctor --restore <file>", "doctor --rebuild [--store-id <uuid>]"), §9.14 (recovery,
// journal replay, redaction first), §6.2 (a pair learned late). Pins: C57 (Task 27); C58, O35, O36's replay
// half, C67 (Task 28); O47 (Task 29). Every name here is prefixed rr/Rr, so nothing collides with the cases of
// Tasks 25 and 26 above. The binding verbs are irreversible, so their runs go through a REAL terminal (node-pty).
// The TTY gate has no seam (§10.1). Every spawn carries the statfs preload (historyHelpers), and every HOME is a
// fixture.
type RrBox = rrH.HistoryBox;
type RrRow = Record<string, unknown>;

const RR_ID = 'claude-a-demo';
const RR_SLUG = '-home-u-tree-demo';
const RR_CWD = '/home/u/tree/demo';
const RR_G1 = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000a1';
const RR_U1 = 'a1a1a1a1-0000-4000-8000-000000000001';
/** The migration seam history-op.test.ts uses (B1 Task 25): an additive v2 through the run-pass driver. */
const RR_V2 = 'CREATE TABLE seam_v2 (x INTEGER)';

const rrU = (n: number): string => `00000000-0000-4000-8000-${String(n).padStart(12, '0')}`;
const rrIso = (minutesAgo: number): string => new Date(Date.now() - minutesAgo * 60_000).toISOString();
const rrRoot = (box: RrBox): rrLib.HistoryPaths => rrLib.historyPaths(box.home);
const rrNames = (dir: string): string[] => { try { return rrFs.readdirSync(dir).sort(); } catch { return []; } };

/** A read of the box's store through a read-only handle, closed after. */
function rrQ<T>(box: RrBox, sql: string, ...args: (string | number)[]): T[] {
  const db = rrH.openStoreRO(box);
  try { return db.prepare(sql).all(...args) as T[]; } finally { db.close(); }
}
const rrCount = (box: RrBox, table: string): number => rrQ<{ n: number }>(box, `SELECT count(*) AS n FROM ${table}`)[0]!.n;
const rrMeta = (box: RrBox, k: string): string | null =>
  rrQ<{ v: string }>(box, 'SELECT v FROM meta WHERE k = ?', k)[0]?.v ?? null;

/** Any SQLite file (a backup, the store), read-only. */
function rrFileDb<T>(file: string, f: (db: RrDb) => T): T {
  const db = new RrDb(file, { readOnly: true });
  try { return f(db); } finally { db.close(); }
}
const rrDbMeta = (file: string, k: string): string | null =>
  rrFileDb(file, (db) => (db.prepare('SELECT v FROM meta WHERE k = ?').get(k) as { v: string } | undefined)?.v ?? null);
const rrJournalMode = (file: string): string =>
  rrFileDb(file, (db) => String((db.prepare('PRAGMA journal_mode').get() as { journal_mode: string }).journal_mode));
const rrUserVersion = (file: string): number =>
  rrFileDb(file, (db) => Number((db.prepare('PRAGMA user_version').get() as { user_version: number }).user_version));

interface RrRecoverRow { version: number; cursor: string | null; completed_ms: number | null }
/** The newest ('recover', <bind ms>) row: what a restore or a rebuild registers, and what status reads. */
const rrRecover = (box: RrBox): RrRecoverRow | undefined =>
  rrQ<RrRecoverRow>(box, "SELECT version, cursor, completed_ms FROM derivation_state WHERE step = 'recover' ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 1")[0];
const rrRecovered = (box: RrBox): boolean => {
  const r = rrRecover(box);
  return r !== undefined && r.completed_ms !== null;
};
const rrStepDone = (box: RrBox, step: string, version: number): boolean =>
  rrQ<{ c: number | null }>(box, 'SELECT completed_ms AS c FROM derivation_state WHERE step = ? AND version = ?', step, version)[0]?.c != null;

/** Every entry under ~/.ccrc with each file's size and mtime: "writes nothing", measured. The shim's lock (opened
 *  on every run) and SQLite's WAL sidecars (a read-only open may create them) are excluded. Directories are listed
 *  by name only, because a temp that is created and then removed moves its directory's mtime. */
function rrSnapshot(box: RrBox): string[] {
  const root = rrPath.join(box.home, '.ccrc');
  const out: string[] = [];
  const visit = (d: string): void => {
    for (const e of rrFs.readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      if (e.name === 'history-sweep.lock' || /-(wal|shm)$/.test(e.name)) continue;
      const p = rrPath.join(d, e.name);
      if (e.isDirectory()) { out.push(`${rrPath.relative(root, p)}/`); visit(p); continue; }
      const st = rrFs.lstatSync(p);
      out.push(`${rrPath.relative(root, p)} ${st.size} ${Math.trunc(st.mtimeMs)}`);
    }
  };
  visit(root);
  return out.sort();
}

interface RrOp { rc: number; reason?: string }
/** The --op pass's one JSON result, its LAST `{"rc"…}` line (§8.4), with a pty's \r stripped. */
function rrLast(stdout: string): RrOp {
  const lines = stdout.replace(/\r/g, '').split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l.startsWith('{"rc"'));
  expect(lines.length, `no {"rc":…} line in:\n${stdout}`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  return JSON.parse(lines[lines.length - 1]!) as RrOp;
}

interface RrPty { code: number; out: string }
/** A child on a REAL terminal (node-pty), so stdin is a TTY. The pty merges stdout and stderr. The guard timer is a
 *  safety net, never the assertion. */
function rrPtyRun(box: RrBox, file: string, argv: string[], env: Record<string, string>): Promise<RrPty> {
  const full: Record<string, string> = {};
  const merged: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {
    ...box.env, HISTORY_TEST_STATFS: 'plenty', NODE_OPTIONS: rrH.preloadOptions([rrH.PRELOADS.statfs]), ...env,
  };
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(merged)) if (v !== undefined) full[k] = v;
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const p = rrPty.spawn(file, argv, { name: 'xterm-color', cols: 200, rows: 40, cwd: box.home, env: full });
    let out = '';
    let done = false;
    const finish = (code: number): void => {
      if (done) return;
      done = true;
      clearTimeout(timer);
      resolve({ code, out });
    };
    const timer = setTimeout(() => { p.kill(); finish(-1); }, 60_000);
    p.onData((d) => { out += d; });
    p.onExit(({ exitCode }) => finish(exitCode));
  });
}
/** The direct door: the box's placed shim, `--op …`, on a terminal. */
const rrShimPty = (box: RrBox, args: string[], env: Record<string, string> = {}): Promise<RrPty> =>
  rrPtyRun(box, 'bash', [rrPath.join(box.home, '.local', 'bin', 'ccd-history-sweep'), ...args], env);
/** The CLI door: `ccrc history …` as the dispatch line runs it, on a terminal. */
const rrCliPty = (box: RrBox, args: string[], env: Record<string, string> = {}): Promise<RrPty> =>
  rrPtyRun(box, process.execPath, ['--no-warnings', rrH.CLI, ...args], env);
/** The env of a run that B1's faults preload SIGKILLs at one fs call (HISTORY_TEST_KILL). */
const rrKill = (spec: string): Record<string, string> => ({
  NODE_OPTIONS: rrH.preloadOptions([rrH.PRELOADS.statfs, rrH.PRELOADS.faults]), HISTORY_TEST_KILL: spec,
});

/** Scheduled passes through the shim until `done()` holds, at most `max`. Every one must exit 0. No pass may answer
 *  store-unbound, which is what a restored or rebuilt store must never become (DI3). */
function rrTickUntil(box: RrBox, done: () => boolean, max = 8, opts: rrH.SpawnOpts = {}): void {
  for (let i = 0; i < max; i += 1) {
    const r = rrH.runShim(box, [], opts);
    expect(r.code, `pass ${i + 1}:\n${r.stdout}\n${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
    expect(r.stdout, 'a restored or rebuilt store is never refused unbound').not.toMatch(/store-unbound/);
    if (done()) return;
  }
  throw new Error(`rrTickUntil: not done after ${max} passes`);
}

const rrStart = (id: string, sid: string, src: 'startup' | 'resume' | 'clear', extra: RrRow = {}): RrRow =>
  ({ v: 1, ev: 'SessionStart', id, sid, src, ...extra });

/** `n` alternating user and assistant rows of transcript `sid`, uuids rrU(base)… */
function rrTalk(sid: string, base: number, n: number): object[] {
  const rows: object[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i += 1) {
    const at = { uuid: rrU(base + i), ts: rrIso(n - i), parentUuid: i === 0 ? null : rrU(base + i - 1), sessionId: sid, cwd: RR_CWD };
    rows.push(i % 2 === 0 ? rrFx.userRow({ ...at, text: `zqrecover ask ${i}` }) : rrFx.assistantRow({ ...at, text: `zqrecover answer ${i}` }));
  }
  return rows;
}

/** A transcript with one manual compaction (§7.4). It has a user and an assistant row, then the boundary, then the
 *  summary right after it (the manual +1 position, which the boundary's anchor names), then one more row. The
 *  first row and the summary's Current Work section both carry `work`. Row uuids are rrU(base)…rrU(base + 4).
 *  One native leaf derives from it. */
function rrCompacted(sid: string, base: number, work: string): object[] {
  const at = (k: number) => ({
    uuid: rrU(base + k), ts: rrIso(10 - k), parentUuid: k === 0 ? null : rrU(base + k - 1), sessionId: sid, cwd: RR_CWD,
  });
  const anchor = rrU(base + 3);
  const summary = [
    '<summary>',
    '1. Primary Request and Intent:',
    '   Keep the fixture repository healthy.',
    '8. Current Work:',
    `   ${work}`,
    '9. Optional Next Step:',
    '   Run the suite again.',
    '</summary>',
  ].join('\n');
  return [
    rrFx.userRow({ ...at(0), text: `zqrecover ask about ${work}` }),
    rrFx.assistantRow({ ...at(1), text: 'zqrecover answer' }),
    rrFx.boundaryRow({ ...at(2), trigger: 'manual', headUuid: anchor, anchorUuid: anchor, tailUuid: anchor, allUuids: [] }),
    rrFx.summaryRow({ ...at(3), text: summary }),
    rrFx.userRow({ ...at(4), text: 'zqrecover after the compaction' }),
  ];
}

interface RrBuilt { box: RrBox; storeId: string; transcript: string }
/** A bound box whose store holds one confirmed family (RR_ID, RR_G1) and its three-row transcript, ingested. Its
 *  journal holds the file, spool, verdict (`drained` included) and tick records of that work. */
function rrBuilt(prefix: string): RrBuilt {
  const box = rrH.makeHistoryBox(prefix, { role: 'fleet' });
  rrH.plantSession(box, RR_ID, { uuid: RR_U1, generation: RR_G1, project: 'demo' });
  const transcript = rrH.plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', RR_SLUG, RR_U1, rrTalk(RR_U1, 1, 3));
  rrH.spoolLine(box, RR_ID, rrStart(RR_ID, RR_U1, 'startup', { reg: RR_U1, gen: RR_G1 }));
  rrTickUntil(box, () => rrCount(box, 'entries') === 3);
  return { box, storeId: rrFs.readFileSync(rrRoot(box).storeId, 'utf8').trim(), transcript };
}

/** `doctor --backup` through the direct door (Task 22; not irreversible, so no terminal). Returns the new name. */
function rrBackup(box: RrBox): string {
  const dir = rrRoot(box).backups;
  const before = new Set(rrNames(dir));
  const r = rrH.runShim(box, ['--op', 'backup']);
  expect(r.code, `${r.stdout}\n${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
  const made = rrNames(dir).filter((n) => /^[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z\.db$/.test(n) && !before.has(n));
  expect(made, 'one new <ts>.db').toHaveLength(1);
  return made[0]!;
}

/** The loss. The DB always goes, with its -wal and -shm (§8.4's remedy moves the three together). With
 *  `binding`, store.id, store.writer and any pending marker go too. With `journal`, so does journal/. A box that
 *  loses all three holds only what a fresh box with a planted backup holds (C57). */
function rrLose(box: RrBox, o: { binding: boolean; journal: boolean }): void {
  const P = rrRoot(box);
  for (const f of [P.dbFile, P.wal, P.shm]) rrFs.rmSync(f, { force: true });
  if (o.binding) for (const f of [P.storeId, P.writer, P.pending]) rrFs.rmSync(f, { force: true });
  if (o.journal) rrFs.rmSync(P.journalDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
}

/** Every `bind` verdict in every journal directory. */
const rrBinds = (box: RrBox): { bind: unknown; writer: unknown }[] =>
  rrH.journalRecords(box).filter((r) => r['k'] === 'verdict' && r['kind'] === 'bind').map((r) => ({ bind: r['bind'], writer: r['writer'] }));

/** What a restore or a rebuild must leave (§8.4):
 *  - store.id and meta.store_id name `storeId`;
 *  - a new writer token is in store.writer and mirrored in meta.writer;
 *  - one `bound:<ms>` row names the verb;
 *  - the store is in WAL mode;
 *  - its `bind` record sits in journal/<storeId>/ under the new token. */
function rrExpectBound(box: RrBox, storeId: string, kind: 'restore' | 'rebuild', oldWriter: string | null): void {
  const P = rrRoot(box);
  expect(rrFs.readFileSync(P.storeId, 'utf8').trim(), 'store.id').toBe(storeId);
  expect(rrMeta(box, 'store_id'), 'meta.store_id').toBe(storeId);
  const writer = rrFs.readFileSync(P.writer, 'utf8').trim();
  expect(writer).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{8}$/);
  expect(rrMeta(box, 'writer'), 'meta.writer mirrors store.writer').toBe(writer);
  if (oldWriter !== null) expect(writer, 'a binding mints a new writer token').not.toBe(oldWriter);
  expect(rrQ<{ v: string }>(box, "SELECT v FROM meta WHERE k LIKE 'bound:%'").map((x) => x.v)).toEqual([kind]);
  expect(rrJournalMode(P.dbFile), 'journal_mode').toBe('wal');
  expect(rrBinds(box).filter((b) => b.writer === writer)).toEqual([{ bind: kind, writer }]);
  expect(rrNames(rrPath.join(P.journalDir, storeId)).some((n) => n.endsWith(`.${writer}.jsonl`)),
    'the bind record went to journal/<store_id>/ under the new writer').toBe(true);
}

const rrFamilies = (box: RrBox, id: string): { generation: string; merged_into: number | null }[] =>
  rrQ(box, 'SELECT generation, merged_into FROM sessions WHERE ccrc_id = ? ORDER BY generation', id);
const rrEpochs = (box: RrBox, id: string): { generation: string; seq: number; cc_session_uuid: string; cause: string }[] =>
  rrQ(box, `SELECT s.generation, e.seq, e.cc_session_uuid, e.cause FROM epochs e JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = e.session_pk
    WHERE s.ccrc_id = ? ORDER BY s.generation, e.seq`, id);

/** A copy of a backup that claims a newer schema than this build knows. */
function rrSetUserVersion(file: string, v: number): void {
  const db = new RrDb(file);
  try { db.exec(`PRAGMA user_version = ${v}`); } finally { db.close(); }
}
/** A copy of a backup whose integrity_check fails while every table still reads. The entries_ts index's
 *  definition is rewritten so its stored keys no longer match its table (integrity_check then answers "row N
 *  missing from index entries_ts" rows rather than throwing, and meta still reads). The handle is opened with
 *  `defensive: false`: node:sqlite's defensive flag defaults to true on Node 24, where even writable_schema ON
 *  refuses the sqlite_master UPDATE ("table sqlite_master may not be modified", measured on 24.14.1, the workers'
 *  Node); 22.16.0 has no such option and is not defensive, so the flag changes nothing there. */
function rrCorruptIndex(file: string): void {
  const db = new RrDb(file, { defensive: false });
  try {
    db.exec('PRAGMA writable_schema = ON');
    db.prepare("UPDATE sqlite_master SET sql = ? WHERE name = 'entries_ts'").run('CREATE INDEX entries_ts ON entries(ts_ms, transcript_pk)');
    db.exec('PRAGMA writable_schema = OFF');
  } finally { db.close(); }
  const rows = rrFileDb(file, (d) => (d.prepare('PRAGMA integrity_check').all() as { integrity_check: string }[]).map((r) => r.integrity_check));
  expect(rows, 'CONTROL: the fixture really fails integrity_check').not.toEqual(['ok']);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2A: Append the failing redaction-first describe** at the end of `server/test/history-recover.test.ts`, after Step 2's (the coordinator's ruling R-restore-pairs; spec §9.14 "Redaction first"). A restore links a backup whose blobs are readable at once, and read verbs answer while the recovery step is registered, so a pair only the journal holds (a value rotated out of its file after the backup was taken) must be in the staged copy before `link()`, not only after the step's index phase. A rebuild does not share this window: it links an empty store, and its replay applies every pair before any blob is replayed or indexed (§9.14), so Task 28 needs no such case. The describe's third case pins the coordinator's ruling R-witness-restore (spec §6.2 "The belt"): the pair insert raises a witnessed value, so the restore checks the witness before it and stamps after it. Every operand that could be large is asserted as a boolean, so a red never prints a whole output.

```ts
describe('Redaction first at the link: a restore applies the journal\'s redact records before history.db exists (W1-B2 Task 27)', () => {
  beforeEach((ctx) => { if (process.platform === 'darwin') ctx.skip(); });

  it('a backup that lacks a pair only the journal holds: read verbs run right after the commit, before any pass, print no stretch of the value', async () => {
    const box = rrH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-c57r-', { role: 'fleet' });
    const P = rrRoot(box);
    const value = rrRandomBytes(32).toString('hex');
    const sha = rrCreateHash('sha256').update(value).digest('hex').toUpperCase();
    const tokenFile = rrPath.join(box.home, '.ccrc', 'fixture.token');
    rrH.plantSession(box, RR_ID, { uuid: RR_U1, generation: RR_G1, project: 'demo' });
    rrH.plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', RR_SLUG, RR_U1, [
      rrFx.userRow({ uuid: rrU(1), ts: rrIso(3), parentUuid: null, sessionId: RR_U1, cwd: RR_CWD, text: `zqatlink the key ${value} here` }),
      rrFx.assistantRow({ uuid: rrU(2), ts: rrIso(2), parentUuid: rrU(1), sessionId: RR_U1, cwd: RR_CWD, text: 'zqatlink noted' }),
    ]);
    rrH.spoolLine(box, RR_ID, rrStart(RR_ID, RR_U1, 'startup', { reg: RR_U1, gen: RR_G1 }));
    rrTickUntil(box, () => rrCount(box, 'entries') === 2);
    const name = rrBackup(box);                                // taken before the pair is known
    rrFs.writeFileSync(tokenFile, `${value}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    expect(rrH.runShim(box).code).toBe(0);                     // learned now, and journaled as a redact record
    rrFs.rmSync(tokenFile);                                    // then rotated out of every file: only the journal knows it
    const pairSql = 'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM redact_hashes WHERE len = ? AND hex(sha256) = ?';
    expect(rrFileDb(rrPath.join(P.backups, name), (db) => Number((db.prepare(pairSql).get(value.length, sha) as { n: number }).n)),
      'CONTROL: the backup lacks the pair').toBe(0);
    expect(rrH.journalRecords(box).some((r) => r['k'] === 'redact' && String(r['sha256']).toUpperCase() === sha),
      'CONTROL: the journal holds it').toBe(true);
    rrLose(box, { binding: false, journal: false });
    expect(rrLast((await rrShimPty(box, ['--op', 'restore', name])).out)).toEqual({ rc: 0 });
    expect(rrRecover(box), 'CONTROL: no pass has run the recovery step yet').toMatchObject({ completed_ms: null });
    expect(rrQ<{ n: number }>(box, pairSql, value.length, sha)[0]!.n, 'the linked store already holds the journal\'s pair').toBe(1);
    const pane = rrH.withPane(box, RR_ID);
    for (const args of [['grep', 'zqatlink'], ['grep', 'zqatlink', '--json'], ['expand', rrU(1)], ['expand', rrU(1), '--json']]) {
      const o = rrH.runCli(box, args, { env: pane });
      expect(o.code, `${args.join(' ')}: rc`).toBe(0);
      const said = o.stdout + o.stderr;
      for (let i = 0; i + 14 <= value.length; i += 10) {
        expect(said.includes(value.slice(i, i + 14)), `${args.join(' ')}: a stretch of the value at ${i}`).toBe(false);
      }
      expect(o.stdout.includes(rrLib.REDACTED_MARK), `${args.join(' ')}: masked`).toBe(true);
    }
    expect(rrRecover(box), 'the read verbs ran before any pass: the step is still open').toMatchObject({ completed_ms: null });
  }, 180_000);

  it('a journal file the pair read cannot open is named on the restore\'s output, and the restore proceeds', async (ctx) => {
    if (process.getuid?.() === 0) ctx.skip();                       // root reads a 0000 file regardless of its mode
    const { box, storeId } = rrBuilt('ccrc-hist-c57s-');
    const P = rrRoot(box);
    const name = rrBackup(box);
    rrLose(box, { binding: false, journal: false });
    const files = rrNames(rrPath.join(P.journalDir, storeId)).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.jsonl'));
    expect(files.length > 0, 'CONTROL: the journal holds a file').toBe(true);
    const shut = rrPath.join(P.journalDir, storeId, files[0]!);
    rrFs.chmodSync(shut, 0o000);
    try {
      const r = await rrShimPty(box, ['--op', 'restore', name]);
      expect(rrLast(r.out)).toEqual({ rc: 0 });
      const line = r.out.replace(/\r/g, '').split('\n').find((l) => l.includes('journal file(s) not read for redact pairs:'));
      expect(line !== undefined && line.includes(files[0]!), 'the unread file is named, never skipped silently').toBe(true);
    } finally { rrFs.chmodSync(shut, 0o600); }
  }, 180_000);

  it('the restore checks the belt witness before its pair insert and stamps it after: a backup stale against its own content records the belt due, a stamped one keeps its state (ruling R-witness-restore)', async () => {
    const belt = (box: RrBox): rrLib.BeltState | null => rrLib.parseBeltState(rrMeta(box, 'fts_belt'));
    /** A completed belt generation, stamped by the tick that wrote it (Task 7B's recordTick). */
    const stamped = (box: RrBox): boolean => {
      const s = belt(box);
      return s !== null && s.v === rrLib.BELT_VERSION && s.gen === null && s.w !== undefined;
    };
    const vrg = (s: rrLib.BeltState | null): unknown => (s === null ? null : { v: s.v, rids: s.rids, gen: s.gen });

    // A: after the last stamped tick, a B1-shaped write (a pair recorded straight into redact_hashes: the top rowid, a
    // witnessed value, rises and fts_belt is not touched, as a build without the belt records one), then the backup.
    // Its fts_belt witness is stale against its own content, so the restore must record the belt due, never stamp the
    // stale state clean.
    const a = rrBuilt('ccrc-hist-c57w-');
    rrTickUntil(a.box, () => stamped(a.box), 12);
    const before = rrMeta(a.box, 'fts_belt');
    const db = new RrDb(rrRoot(a.box).dbFile);
    try {
      db.prepare('INSERT INTO redact_hashes (len, sha256, first_seen_ms) VALUES (?, ?, ?)').run(40, rrRandomBytes(32), Date.now());
    } finally { db.close(); }
    const nameA = rrBackup(a.box);
    expect(rrMeta(a.box, 'fts_belt'), 'CONTROL: neither the B1-shaped write nor the backup pass wrote the belt state').toBe(before);
    rrLose(a.box, { binding: false, journal: false });
    expect(rrLast((await rrShimPty(a.box, ['--op', 'restore', nameA])).out)).toEqual({ rc: 0 });
    expect(rrRecover(a.box), 'CONTROL: no pass has run since the restore').toMatchObject({ cursor: null, completed_ms: null });
    expect(vrg(belt(a.box)), 'the restore recorded the belt due: the copy\'s witness had moved').toEqual({ v: 0, rids: [], gen: null });

    // B: a backup right after a stamped tick, then a pair only the journal holds. The check finds the witness unmoved
    // and keeps the backup's state; the stamp records the pair insert, so `w` moves with the top rowid and the first
    // recovery pass does not read the restore's own write as another build's.
    const b = rrBuilt('ccrc-hist-c57x-');
    rrTickUntil(b.box, () => stamped(b.box), 12);
    const atBackup = belt(b.box)!;
    const nameB = rrBackup(b.box);
    const value = rrRandomBytes(32).toString('hex');
    rrFs.writeFileSync(rrPath.join(b.box.home, '.ccrc', 'fixture.token'), `${value}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    expect(rrH.runShim(b.box).code).toBe(0);                       // learned and journaled after the backup
    rrLose(b.box, { binding: false, journal: false });
    expect(rrLast((await rrShimPty(b.box, ['--op', 'restore', nameB])).out)).toEqual({ rc: 0 });
    expect(rrRecover(b.box), 'CONTROL: the journal-only pair went in, so the step starts +pairs').toMatchObject({ cursor: 'index+pairs', completed_ms: null });
    const kept = belt(b.box);
    expect(vrg(kept), 'the restore kept the backup\'s belt state: its witness had not moved').toEqual(vrg(atBackup));
    expect(kept?.w !== undefined && kept.w !== atBackup.w, 'the restore stamped its own pair insert: w moved with the top redact_hashes rowid').toBe(true);
  }, 240_000);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write `restoreArm`.** It declares no helper of its own: it reuses Task 26's `bindFactsOf` and `finishBind`. In `ccd/history/sweep.mjs`, insert this block directly above the entry guard line:

```js
// ── W1-B2 Task 27: doctor --restore (§8.4 "doctor --restore <file>"; slugs history-restore-verb,
// history-restore-wal-mode, history-binding-facts-before-link). It reuses Task 26's bindFactsOf and finishBind. ─────

/** The restore's belt-witness hooks (spec §6.2 "The belt"; coordinator ruling R-witness-restore), which store.mjs's
 *  commitRestore runs on the staged copy inside its FULL bind transaction: `check` before any write, `stamp` after the
 *  journal's pairs. The pair insert raises the top redact_hashes rowid, a value beltWitness reads, and a belt-aware
 *  writer that changes witnessed values checks first, then writes, then stamps:
 *  - check: Task 7B's recordBeltDueIfWitnessMoved, the one function secretsStep calls at a pass's start (ruling
 *    R-rollback), which opens no withTx of its own. A copy whose witness moved since its fts_belt was stamped (a backup
 *    taken after a build without the belt wrote) has its belt recorded due, which also clears an open generation's
 *    record so that it restarts;
 *  - stamp: Task 7B's stampBeltWitness, so the first recovery pass does not read the restore's own pairs as another
 *    build's writes. The check ran first in the same transaction, so the stamp hides nothing. */
const RESTORE_BELT = {
  check(db) { recordBeltDueIfWitnessMoved(db); },   // the restore's witness check (R-witness-restore)
  stamp(db) { stampBeltWitness(db); },
};

/** `doctor --restore <name>` (§8.4): put a backup under db/backups/ back as this box's store.
 *  It first removes the writer temps a killed pass left in db/ (a killed restore's full-size copy among them): the
 *  lock is held, so every temp is stale (§9.4), and free space is then measured without the dead copy. Task 26's
 *  binding section names this as each verb's first step.
 *  Refusals come next, and none of them writes anything:
 *  - the name (restoreNameOk: a <ts>.db or a pre-v<N>.db, never a path or a temp);
 *  - the file, by lstat, so a symlink is never followed;
 *  - the binding table on the facts as they stand (decideBind, Task 6): a DB present, an orphaned WAL, a store.id
 *    naming another store, an unreadable binding input (exit 5);
 *  - room for the copy (planCopy, the one copy preflight, §6.11; a statfs that throws reads low-disk, R3).
 *  Then the copy is staged and judged again on what only the copy can tell: its store_id, its user_version and its
 *  integrity_check. It is committed with every binding fact inside it before it becomes history.db (Task 24's
 *  commitRestore: WAL set, bound:<ms>, a new writer, the ('recover', <ms>) step, the bind outbox row, then the
 *  pending marker and link()), and with every redact pair the store's journal holds (Task 25's journalRedactPairs;
 *  R-restore-pairs), so §9.14's "redaction first" holds from the moment the store is visible. A StoreError from that commit (a copy with no store_id, or one that will not take
 *  WAL: store-not-wal, exit 5) answers its own word and exit, as adoptArm answers one; the finally removes the
 *  temp. It runs before openStore, because a missing store is the state it exists to repair. It runs under
 *  history-off too, since it is a binding verb (§8.4); its recovery step waits for the switch. */
export async function restoreArm(home, P, args, deps, out) {
  const now = deps.now ?? Date.now;
  const role = readRole(P);
  removeStaleTemps(home);
  const refuse = (detail) => {
    out(`history-sweep: restore-refused: ${detail}`);
    return { rc: EXIT.REFUSED, reason: 'restore-refused' };
  };
  if (typeof args.name !== 'string' || !restoreNameOk(args.name)) {
    return refuse(`${JSON.stringify(args.name)} is not a <ts>.db or pre-v<N>.db name under db/backups/`);
  }
  const file = `${P.backups}/${args.name}`;
  let st;
  try { st = lstatSync(file); } catch { return refuse(`db/backups/${args.name} cannot be read`); }
  if (!st.isFile()) return refuse(`db/backups/${args.name} is not a regular file; a symlink is never followed`);
  const facts = bindFactsOf(home, role, deps, {});
  const restorePre = decideBind('restore', {
    ...facts, backup: { regular: true, storeId: peekStoreId(file), userVersion: null, integrityOk: null },
  });
  if (!restorePre.ok) {
    out(`history-sweep: ${restorePre.reason}: ${restorePre.detail}`);
    return { rc: restorePre.rc, reason: restorePre.reason };
  }
  const free = await statfsWithDeadline(probePath(P, home), STATFS_DEADLINE_MS, deps.statfs);
  if (free.state === 'unsettled') return { rc: EXIT.DB, reason: 'store-unreachable' };
  const restoreRoom = free.state === 'ok'
    ? planCopy({ freeBytes: free.bytes, thresholdBytes: floorThreshold(free.fsSize), sizeBytes: st.size })
    : { admit: false, needBytes: null };
  if (!restoreRoom.admit) {
    return refuse(restoreRoom.needBytes === null
      ? 'free space on the store\'s filesystem could not be measured, so no copy is admitted'
      : `a copy of ${st.size} bytes needs more than ${restoreRoom.needBytes} bytes free, and ${free.bytes} are`);
  }
  writeOpMarker(P, 'restore', now());
  let staged = null;
  try {
    try {
      staged = stageRestore(home, args.name);
    } catch (e) {
      removeStaleTemps(home);
      return refuse(`db/backups/${args.name} could not be copied and opened (${e && e.code ? e.code : 'error'})`);
    }
    const restorePost = decideBind('restore', {
      ...facts,
      backup: { regular: true, storeId: staged.storeId, userVersion: staged.userVersion, integrityOk: staged.integrityOk },
    });
    if (!restorePost.ok) {
      out(`history-sweep: ${restorePost.reason}: ${restorePost.detail}`);
      return { rc: restorePost.rc, reason: restorePost.reason };
    }
    // Redaction first, at the link (R-restore-pairs; spec §8.4 and §9.14): every redact record of
    // this store's journal goes into the copy inside commitRestore's bind transaction, before link(), so no read verb
    // ever serves the restored store without a pair the journal knows. A file it could not read is named, never skipped
    // silently; the recovery's index phase reads the same files again. The witness is checked before those pairs go
    // in and stamped after them, in the same transaction (RESTORE_BELT; R-witness-restore).
    const journalPairs = journalRedactPairs(P, restorePost.storeId);
    if (journalPairs.skipped.length > 0) {
      out(`history-sweep: restore: ${journalPairs.skipped.length} journal file(s) not read for redact pairs: ${journalPairs.skipped.join(', ')}`);
    }
    try {
      commitRestore(home, staged, { nowMs: now(), pairs: journalPairs.pairs, belt: RESTORE_BELT });
    } catch (e) {
      if (!(e instanceof StoreError)) throw e;
      out(`history-sweep: restore stopped: ${e.message}`);
      return REASONS[e.word] === undefined ? { rc: EXIT.INTERNAL } : { rc: REASONS[e.word], reason: e.word };
    }
    staged = null;
    return finishBind(home, P, role, deps, out, now);
  } finally {
    if (staged !== null) abortRestore(staged);
    removeEntry(P.op);   // B1's type-aware removal (history-planted-entries-never-wedge), as adoptArm's
  }
}
```

```ts
// ── Task 28's helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
/** A journal directory journal/<dir>/ whose one month file holds only a head record naming `headStoreId`. */
function rrPlantJournalDir(box: RrBox, dir: string, headStoreId: string = dir): void {
  const at = rrPath.join(rrRoot(box).journalDir, dir);
  rrFs.mkdirSync(at, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  const month = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 7);
  const writer = rrRandomBytes(4).toString('hex');
  const head = rrLib.journalRecord('head', Date.now(), { store_id: headStoreId, month, writer });
  rrFs.writeFileSync(rrPath.join(at, `${month}.${writer}.jsonl`), `${head}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
}
const rrLeafIds = (box: RrBox): string[] =>
  rrQ<{ node_id: string }>(box, "SELECT node_id FROM nodes WHERE kind <> 'condensed' ORDER BY node_id").map((r) => r.node_id);

/** What O35 compares, each by its natural key and journaled times (§8.4 "What comes back equal"). Surrogate keys,
 *  cwd_real, leaf_id_forked and uuid_two_sessions are not compared. */
interface RrState {
  storeId: string | null; sessions: unknown[]; epochs: unknown[]; receipts: unknown[]; redact: unknown[];
  recall: unknown[]; leaves: string[];
}
function rrState(box: RrBox): RrState {
  return {
    storeId: rrMeta(box, 'store_id'),
    sessions: rrQ(box, 'SELECT ccrc_id, generation, project, first_seen_ms FROM sessions ORDER BY ccrc_id, generation'),
    epochs: rrQ(box, `SELECT s.ccrc_id, s.generation, e.seq, e.cc_session_uuid, e.cause, e.declared_by
      FROM epochs e JOIN sessions s ON s.session_pk = e.session_pk ORDER BY s.ccrc_id, s.generation, e.seq`),
    receipts: rrQ(box, 'SELECT event_key, hex(payload_sha) AS sha, received_ms FROM spool_receipts ORDER BY event_key'),
    redact: rrQ(box, 'SELECT len, hex(sha256) AS sha FROM redact_hashes ORDER BY len, sha'),
    recall: rrQ(box, 'SELECT event_key, ccrc_id, generation, ts_ms, verb, rc, ms, arm FROM recall_calls ORDER BY event_key'),
    leaves: rrLeafIds(box),
  };
}
/** The journal's records by kind, every store directory. `head` and `tick` are left out: a pass and a new writer
 *  file write those whatever a recovery does. */
function rrJournalKinds(box: RrBox): Record<'file' | 'spool' | 'redact' | 'verdict', number> {
  const out = { file: 0, spool: 0, redact: 0, verdict: 0 };
  for (const r of rrH.journalRecords(box)) {
    const k = r['k'];
    if (k === 'file' || k === 'spool' || k === 'redact' || k === 'verdict') out[k] += 1;
  }
  return out;
}
```

```ts
describe('C58: doctor --rebuild, its store_id and its refusals (W1-B2 Task 28)', () => {
  beforeEach((ctx) => { if (process.platform === 'darwin') ctx.skip(); });

  /** A rebuild through the direct door on a terminal, which must refuse rebuild-refused and write nothing. */
  const refused = async (box: RrBox, args: string[], why: string): Promise<string> => {
    const before = rrSnapshot(box);
    const r = await rrShimPty(box, ['--op', 'rebuild', ...args]);
    expect(rrLast(r.out), `${why}\n${r.out}`).toEqual({ rc: 2, reason: 'rebuild-refused' });
    expect(rrSnapshot(box), `${why}: nothing written`).toEqual(before);
    return r.out;
  };

  it('store.id present and the DB lost: the pass holds store-missing; --rebuild (the CLI, on a terminal) makes a DB with that store_id, bound rebuild, its recovery step registered', async () => {
    const { box, storeId } = rrBuilt('ccrc-hist-c58a-');
    const P = rrRoot(box);
    const oldWriter = rrFs.readFileSync(P.writer, 'utf8').trim();
    rrLose(box, { binding: false, journal: false });
    expect(rrH.runShim(box).stdout).toMatch(/^history-sweep: store-missing$/m);
    const r = await rrCliPty(box, ['doctor', '--rebuild']);
    expect(r.code, r.out).toBe(0);
    rrExpectBound(box, storeId, 'rebuild', oldWriter);
    expect(rrRecover(box)).toMatchObject({ completed_ms: null });
    rrTickUntil(box, () => rrRecovered(box));
  }, 120_000);

  it('no store.id and one journal directory whose heads name S: the pass refuses store-recoverable; --rebuild writes store_id S and store.id', async () => {
    const { box, storeId } = rrBuilt('ccrc-hist-c58b-');
    const P = rrRoot(box);
    rrLose(box, { binding: true, journal: false });
    expect(rrH.runShim(box).stdout).toMatch(/^history-sweep: store-recoverable$/m);
    expect(rrFs.existsSync(P.dbFile), 'the pass created nothing').toBe(false);
    const r = await rrShimPty(box, ['--op', 'rebuild']);
    expect(rrLast(r.out), r.out).toEqual({ rc: 0 });
    rrExpectBound(box, storeId, 'rebuild', null);
    rrTickUntil(box, () => rrRecovered(box));
  }, 120_000);

  it('two journal directories S and T: rebuild-refused naming both, writing nothing; --store-id T rebuilds T', async () => {
    const { box, storeId } = rrBuilt('ccrc-hist-c58c-');
    const T = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000d7';
    rrLose(box, { binding: true, journal: false });
    rrPlantJournalDir(box, T);
    expect(rrH.runShim(box).stdout).toMatch(/^history-sweep: store-recoverable$/m);
    const out = await refused(box, [], 'two journal directories and no --store-id');
    expect(out).toContain(storeId);
    expect(out).toContain(T);
    const r = await rrShimPty(box, ['--op', 'rebuild', '--store-id', T]);
    expect(rrLast(r.out), r.out).toEqual({ rc: 0 });
    rrExpectBound(box, T, 'rebuild', null);
  }, 120_000);

  it('each refusal answers rebuild-refused and writes nothing: a DB present, a leftover history.db-wal, store.id and --store-id disagreeing, a --store-id naming no directory, a directory whose heads name another store, and neither source', async () => {
    const { box, storeId } = rrBuilt('ccrc-hist-c58d-');
    const P = rrRoot(box);
    await refused(box, [], 'a DB present');
    rrLose(box, { binding: false, journal: false });
    rrFs.writeFileSync(P.wal, '');
    await refused(box, [], 'a leftover history.db-wal');
    rrFs.rmSync(P.wal);
    const T = '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000d8';
    rrPlantJournalDir(box, T);
    await refused(box, ['--store-id', T], 'store.id and --store-id disagree');
    rrFs.rmSync(rrPath.join(P.journalDir, T), { recursive: true });
    rrFs.rmSync(P.storeId);
    rrFs.rmSync(P.writer);
    await refused(box, ['--store-id', '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000d9'], 'a --store-id naming no directory');
    // journal/X/ whose month files' heads name S: no directory names itself, so none names a store.
    rrFs.renameSync(rrPath.join(P.journalDir, storeId), rrPath.join(P.journalDir, '0189abcd-1234-4678-9abc-0000000000da'));
    await refused(box, [], 'a directory whose heads name another store');
    // A killed pass's temp is removed first, even by a rebuild that then refuses: under the lock every temp is stale
    // (§9.4). The one write a refusal makes, and only of a dead temp.
    const dead = rrPath.join(P.dbDir, 'history.db.new.888888');
    rrFs.writeFileSync(dead, 'a killed creation\'s temp', { mode: 0o600 });
    expect(rrLast((await rrShimPty(box, ['--op', 'rebuild'])).out)).toEqual({ rc: 2, reason: 'rebuild-refused' });
    expect(rrFs.existsSync(dead), 'the stale temp went before the refusal').toBe(false);
    // Neither source: a box that never had a journal. Its first pass is held by a planted backup, not minted over it.
    const fresh = rrH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-c58e-', { role: 'fleet' });
    const FP = rrRoot(fresh);
    rrFs.mkdirSync(FP.backups, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    rrFs.writeFileSync(rrPath.join(FP.backups, '20200101T000000Z.db'), 'not a store');
    expect(rrH.runShim(fresh).stdout).toMatch(/^history-sweep: store-recoverable$/m);
    await refused(fresh, [], 'neither store.id nor a journal directory');
  }, 240_000);

  it('a kill right after the pending marker becomes store.id: the next pass runs the recovery step (DI3)', async () => {
    const { box, storeId } = rrBuilt('ccrc-hist-c58f-');
    const P = rrRoot(box);
    rrLose(box, { binding: true, journal: false });
    expect(rrH.runShim(box).stdout).toMatch(/^history-sweep: store-recoverable$/m);
    // The first rename naming store.id.pending writes the marker (temp then rename); the second makes it store.id.
    const k = await rrShimPty(box, ['--op', 'rebuild'], rrKill('renameSync:store.id.pending:2:after'));
    // A rebuild that was NOT killed leaves the same three facts, so the kill is measured on what only a kill leaves:
    // no result line, the op marker (removed in rebuildArm's finally), and no bind in the journal (it is still in the
    // new file's outbox; finishBind never ran).
    expect(k.out, 'the pass was killed before its result').not.toMatch(/\{"rc"/);
    expect([rrFs.existsSync(P.dbFile), rrFs.existsSync(P.pending), rrFs.readFileSync(P.storeId, 'utf8').trim()],
      'the kill landed right after the pending rename').toEqual([true, false, storeId]);
    expect(rrFs.existsSync(P.op), 'the killed pass left its op marker').toBe(true);
    expect(rrBinds(box), 'the bind row is still inside the file').toEqual([]);
    expect(rrRecover(box)).toMatchObject({ completed_ms: null });
    rrTickUntil(box, () => rrRecovered(box));
    expect(rrBinds(box).map((b) => b.bind)).toEqual(['rebuild']);
  }, 120_000);
});
```

```ts
    //  - A: a confirmed startup and a /clear in ONE draining file, a recall line, and a compacted transcript (a leaf);

describe('C67: unreadable is not absent (W1-B2 Task 28)', () => {

    // changes nothing here: readContext refuses harness-unreadable right after the identity, before it measures the

    const pane = rrH.withPane(box, RR_ID);

      expect(r.stdout + r.stderr, verb[0]).toContain('harness-unreadable');
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Write `journalStoreDirs` and `rebuildArm`.** In `ccd/history/sweep.mjs`, insert this block directly above the entry guard, below Task 27's block:

```js
// ── W1-B2 Task 28: doctor --rebuild (§8.4 "doctor --rebuild [--store-id <uuid>]"; slugs history-rebuild-verb,
// history-store-recoverable, history-binding-facts-before-link) ─────────────────────────────────────────

/** The journal directories that could name a store to rebuild (§8.4 "Its store_id"): every uuid-named directory
 *  under journal/. Each comes with whether its heads agree: it has at least one month file, and every month file's
 *  head names this directory. A directory carried in by hand under another name therefore names nothing.
 *  Month files and their heads are read exactly as recovery reads them (Task 25's JOURNAL_NAME_RE and journalEnds,
 *  O_NOFOLLOW), so rebuild and replay never disagree about which files a directory holds. A head that is missing or
 *  unreadable names no store (§9.14: link() of a fsynced temp means no month file exists without its head). */
export function journalStoreDirs(home) {
  const dir = historyPaths(home).journalDir;
  const out = [];
  for (const name of listNames(dir).sort()) {
    if (!UUID_RE.test(name)) continue;
    const sub = `${dir}/${name}`;
    try { if (!lstatSync(sub).isDirectory()) continue; } catch { continue; }
    const months = listNames(sub).filter((m) => JOURNAL_NAME_RE.test(m));
    const heads = months.map((m) => journalEnds(`${sub}/${m}`)?.headStore ?? null);
    out.push({ storeId: name, headsAgree: months.length > 0 && heads.every((h) => h === name) });
  }
  return out;
}

/** `doctor --rebuild [--store-id <uuid>]` (§8.4): rebuild a lost DB from what else holds its data.
 *  - First, the writer temps a killed pass left in db/ are removed: the lock is held, so every temp is stale (§9.4),
 *    as Task 26's binding section orders it.
 *  - Precondition and store_id: Task 6's decideBind('rebuild') over the store's facts, `--store-id` and the journal
 *    directories. A refusal writes nothing else and names the candidate directories.
 *  - Creation: Task 24's createStore with that store_id. Its creation transaction holds bound:<ms> = rebuild, a new
 *    writer, the ('recover', <ms>) step and the bind outbox row before link(). store.id, when absent, is written
 *    through the pending marker, which the next pass finishes after a kill.
 *  - Then finishBind (Task 26): open, flush the bind, the release journal half.
 *  The following passes run the recovery step (Task 25) and then re-ingest every transcript on disk from empty
 *  cursors (the backfill path). It runs under history-off too, since it is a binding verb. */
export async function rebuildArm(home, P, args, deps, out) {
  const now = deps.now ?? Date.now;
  const role = readRole(P);
  removeStaleTemps(home);
  const dirs = journalStoreDirs(home);
  const rebuildVerdict = decideBind('rebuild', bindFactsOf(home, role, deps, {
    storeIdArg: typeof args.storeId === 'string' ? args.storeId : null, journalDirs: dirs,
  }));
  if (!rebuildVerdict.ok) {
    out(`history-sweep: ${rebuildVerdict.reason}: ${rebuildVerdict.detail}`);
    if (dirs.length > 0) out(`history-sweep: journal store directories: ${dirs.map((x) => x.storeId).join(', ')}`);
    return { rc: rebuildVerdict.rc, reason: rebuildVerdict.reason };
  }
  writeOpMarker(P, 'rebuild', now());
  try {
    createStore(home, { storeId: rebuildVerdict.storeId, bind: { kind: 'rebuild', nowMs: now() } });
    return finishBind(home, P, role, deps, out, now);
  } finally {
    removeEntry(P.op);   // B1's type-aware removal (history-planted-entries-never-wedge), as adoptArm's
  }
}
```

  - Task 7A (`lib.mjs`, spec rev 3.5): `makePairIndex(pairs, belt = null)`; `redactField(text, idx)`, which is layer 4 (the substring belt) over B1's layers 1-3 whenever `idx.belt` is set, so every node field this task rewrites through it carries the belt with no further edit; `nodeIndexTexts(fields, idx)`, the one `nodes_fts` text rule (each column through B1's `entryIndexText`: the index's escape readings and the belt), which every `nodes_fts` row this task writes goes through and which `beltNodesStep` compares a node's row against; `BELT_NODES_STEP` (`'nodes-belt'`).
  - Task 7B (`sweep.mjs`): the tick's `secrets.pairIdx` is `{ byLen, belt, beltLive }`, and `rederiveFts` restarts `('nodes-belt', 1)` whenever a generation opens.
  - Task 9 (`derive.mjs`): the module-private `parentsBudgetLeft(budget)`.
  - Task 27 and 28's `rr*` test helpers; Task 25's faults-preload knob `HISTORY_TEST_THROW_SQL=<substring>`.
- Produces:
  - `derive.mjs`:
    - `export function redactNodeFields(db, ictx, nodeIds: readonly string[]): number`. It rewrites each node's stored gist, each of its topics (then serialises the list) and its refs through `redactField` with `ictx.pairIdx`, and replaces its `nodes_fts` row when `ictx.fts` with Task 7A's `nodeIndexTexts` of the rewritten fields, as Tasks 8 and 9 index them. This is the fail-closed path for a node whose summary cannot be read again.
    - `export function reparseFailClosed(db, ictx, nodeIds: readonly string[]): number`. `refreshLeaf` per leaf, then one `rerollParents` when any changed (an `'updated'` or a `'failed'` answer: Task 21's refreshLeaf records a parser throw inside `leafFields` itself, writing the leaf `parse-failed`). A throw that escapes `refreshLeaf` (not busy) is counted `parser_crash` and skipped, and the caller's `redactNodeFields` rewrites it; nothing retries either on a later pass. Answers how many leaves changed.
    - `export function rederiveGistsFor(db, ictx, values: readonly string[], budget: object, slice: object): number`: the same-tick fast path over nodes. It moves no mark, and it runs only while `slice` and `budget` last (B1's review 344 F2 rule for a fast path).
    - `export function beltNodesStep(db, ictx, slice): boolean` (§6.2 "The belt"), called by `tick` as `beltNodesStep(db, ictx, slice)`: `slice` is the tick's re-index slice (B1's `rederiveSlice(ctx.budget)`, a `newBudget` object, the one `reindexForValues` and `rederiveFts` share), which `ictx.budgetLeft(slice)` reads. It runs while lib's `BELT_NODES_STEP` `('nodes-belt', 1)` is open; Task 7B's `rederiveFts` restarts it whenever a generation opens. It reads every node in rowid order and rewrites, through `redactNodeFields`, each one whose gist, topics or refs `redactField` would change, or whose `nodes_fts` row differs from `nodeIndexTexts` of its stored fields (a value the index's escape readings now mask, which `redactField` leaves in the stored field). It is the one mechanism that re-derives `nodes_fts` after a pair is learned or a belt falls due. Its cursor is the last `nodes.rowid` read, committed after each batch (D-4730 (`history-reindex-subcursor-idempotent`)). It answers whether the step is complete or was never opened. The tick calls it right after B1's `rederiveFts`, in the same slice.
  - `sweep.mjs`:
    - `export async function recoverReindex(db, ctx, cur, budget): Promise<{ cur; done: boolean; moved: boolean }>` (async: it awaits Task 23's `ftsRebuildJob`). It answers `moved: false` with `done: false` only when the run budget was spent before it did any work;
    - module-private `RECOVER_NODE_BATCH = 64`, `RECOVER_NODES_CURSOR_RE`, `RECOVER_REBUILT_STEP = 'recover-merge'`, `recoverPairIdx(db, belt)`, `openRecoverVersion(db)`, `recoverNodesBatch(db, rctx, version)`;
    - in `tick`, one `beltNodesStep(db, ictx, slice);` call directly below B1's `await rederiveFts(db, ictx, ctx.budget, slice);`, listed as item 7 of `tick`'s doc comment, which then holds 18 items;
    - two derivation rows per recovery: `('recover-nodes', <recover version>)`, with cursor `leaves:<rowid>` or `condensed:<rowid>`, and `('recover-merge', <recover version>)`, completed once the FTS rebuild (its merge steps included) completed for this step. Status never reads either.
    - Before its rebuild starts, any OTHER open `('fts-rebuild', v)` row (a repair the restored file carried) is deleted, so `ftsRebuildJob` starts this step's own rebuild from blob 0 rather than resume a job whose earlier blobs were indexed without the replayed pairs.
  - Test helpers: `rrFtsBytes`, `rrBlobsHold`, `rrMatches`, `rrGists`.

**Spec:**
- §9.14 "Redaction first": a restore whose journal adds a pair the backup lacked re-runs the FTS derivation over the restored blobs.
- §6.2 "A pair learned after its text was indexed": quoted-phrase MATCH, delete and re-insert, re-derive the leaf gists, merge steps.
- §8.3: output redaction needs only the pair.
- §6.2 "The belt" and §8.3 layer 4 (spec rev 3.5): the belt's node step, which Task 7B's generations restart, re-redacts every node's stored fields and re-derives its `nodes_fts` row through `nodeIndexTexts`, so a letter-glued value no phrase finds leaves `nodes` and `nodes_fts`, and a pair-only value glued to a literal escape leaves `nodes_fts`. Two cases of its own (Step 2A); not a departure, rev 3.5 is the rule. The mark `fts_reindex_rid` moves when a generation's blob walk completes, while the node step may still run (§6.2 states that window; output stays masked meanwhile, because `redactForDisplay` carries the belt and the escape readings).
- Pins: **O47** (whole: the rebuild case, the restore case, the late case and both CONTROLs), and **O59**'s recovery-reindex half (spec §9.11 O59 store half, case (7): the recovery reindex, an operator pass whose belt lacks a unit the state records as covered, leaves the belt due; the plan header's pin map gives O59's other halves to Tasks 7A, 7B, 21 and 23). Two cases beyond the spec's: a restored file that carries a repair's open rebuild (the supersede), and a late pair whose leaf re-derivation throws (the coordinator's ruling RB5). And, in the belt describe, the recovery-belt case: the reindex phase re-derives node fields through the pass's belt (review R47: no stretch of a loaded, letter-glued value at the step's completion), and a unit missing from the recovery passes' belt leaves the belt due (the operator passes' belt-state rule, coordinator ruling R-oppass-belt; Global Constraints R2: the recovery reindex's half; its repair half is Task 23's and its reparse half Task 21's). And the reparse case (review R46): the reparse half pinned end to end through the generation's node step, no belt-width stretch of the unit left in a node field or `nodes_fts` once its file is readable again.
- Departures:
  - B1's D-4344 (`history-reindex-mark-by-rederivation`) (consumed): only `rederiveFts` moves the mark; this task's `rederiveGistsFor` is a fast path beside B1's phrase search and moves none.
  - B1's D-4241 (`history-redaction-journaled`)
  - B1's D-4245 (`history-redaction-reindex-merge`)
  - D-4699 (`history-recovery-replay`)
  - B1's D-4243 (`history-fts-indexes-redacted-text`)
  - D-4729 (`history-redaction-fail-closed-node-rewrite`) (NEW). A leaf whose summary is pruned, a raw leaf, and a condensed node cannot be re-derived from text. Their stored fields are rewritten through `redactField` instead, so no stored gist keeps a learned value. A leaf whose re-derivation throws is rewritten the same way and counted `parser_crash`, never retried by the next pass (the coordinator's ruling RB5, applied to re-derivation).
  - D-4730 (`history-reindex-subcursor-idempotent`) (NEW). The reindex phase's own cursors (`recover-nodes`, `recover-merge`, and the rebuild's), and the belt's node step's (`nodes-belt`), commit after each batch's own transactions, not inside them, because `refreshLeaf`, `redactNodeFields` and `ftsRebuildJob` each open their own. §9.14's same-transaction cursor holds for the replay phases; a kill here re-runs at most one batch of idempotent re-derivation.
- Not departures since spec rev 3.5, consumed here:
  - the operator passes' belt-state rule (§6.2 "The belt"; coordinator ruling R-oppass-belt; Tasks 21 and 23 carry the helper): the recovery reindex keeps the tick's belt-state rule through `recoverPass`'s `rederiveFts` and `ftsRebuildJob`'s `recordBeltDueIfUncovered`, with no call of its own (`recoverPairIdx`'s doc says why); the recovery-belt case and M12 pin it;
  - the journal's pairs applied at restore (§8.4 and §9.14; coordinator ruling R-restore-pairs; Task 27): a restored store already holds the journal's pairs, and Task 24's `commitRestore` records them as added, so `cur.pairsAdded` still opens this phase. The restore checks the belt witness before that insert and stamps it after (§6.2 "The belt"; coordinator ruling R-witness-restore; Task 27's `RESTORE_BELT`), so the first recovery pass's `secretsStep` reads the inserted pairs as the restore's own; the recovery-belt case asserts that stamp as a CONTROL, which keeps M12 red-able.

Choices this task makes:
- **The gist fast path searches by unit, as B1's phrase path does** (B1's D-4311 (`history-reindex-by-units-and-complete-loads`)). `rederiveGistsFor` searches each learned value by lib's `secretUnits` (the value itself when it is one `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` run, else each run of 12 or more characters), as B1's `reindexForValues` does, so a leaf whose summary holds only a segment of a value is found; and, like it, it moves no mark (B1's D-4344).

```ts
// ── Task 29's helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
/** The index's own bytes: every blobs_fts data block, as latin1 (B1 Task 23's measure). */
const rrFtsBytes = (box: RrBox): string =>
  rrQ<{ block: Uint8Array }>(box, 'SELECT block FROM blobs_fts_data').map((r) => Buffer.from(r.block).toString('latin1')).join('');
/** Whether any stored blob still holds `needle`: the store stays lossless while the index and the output redact. */
const rrBlobsHold = (box: RrBox, needle: string): boolean =>
  rrQ<{ z: Uint8Array }>(box, 'SELECT z FROM blobs WHERE z IS NOT NULL').some((b) => rrUnbrotli(b.z).toString('utf8').includes(needle));
const rrMatches = (box: RrBox, table: 'blobs_fts' | 'nodes_fts', q: string): number =>
  rrQ<{ n: number }>(box, `SELECT count(*) AS n FROM ${table} WHERE ${table} MATCH ?`, q)[0]!.n;
const rrGists = (box: RrBox): string[] =>
  rrQ<{ gist: string | null }>(box, "SELECT gist FROM nodes WHERE kind <> 'condensed' ORDER BY node_id").map((r) => r.gist ?? '');
```

```ts
    const box = rrH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-beltnodes-', { role: 'fleet' });
    const AN = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789';
    const v = `${Array.from(rrRandomBytes(29), (b) => AN[b % AN.length]!).join('')}7`;
    const work = `Rotating the fixture credential zq${v}x before the release.`;
    rrFs.mkdirSync(rrPath.join(box.home, '.cc-secrets'), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    rrFs.writeFileSync(rrPath.join(box.home, '.cc-secrets', 'belt.env'), `ZQ_BELT=${v}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    rrH.plantSession(box, RR_ID, { uuid: RR_U1, generation: RR_G1, project: 'demo' });
    rrH.plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', RR_SLUG, RR_U1, rrCompacted(RR_U1, 1, work));
    rrH.spoolLine(box, RR_ID, rrStart(RR_ID, RR_U1, 'startup', { reg: RR_U1, gen: RR_G1 }));
    rrTickUntil(box, () => rrLeafIds(box).length === 1);
    expect(rrGists(box)[0], 'CONTROL: the belt masked the glued value when the leaf was derived').not.toContain(v.slice(0, 14));
    // The leaf as a store with no belt state left it: the glued value in its gist and in its nodes_fts row.
    const db = new RrDb(rrRoot(box).dbFile);
    try {
      const n = db.prepare("SELECT rowid AS rid, node_id FROM nodes WHERE kind <> 'condensed'").get() as { rid: number; node_id: string };
      db.prepare('UPDATE nodes SET gist = ? WHERE node_id = ?').run(work, n.node_id);
      db.prepare('DELETE FROM nodes_fts WHERE rowid = ?').run(n.rid);
      db.prepare('INSERT INTO nodes_fts (rowid, gist, topics, refs) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)').run(n.rid, work, '', '');
      db.prepare("DELETE FROM meta WHERE k = 'fts_belt'").run();
    } finally { db.close(); }
    expect(rrMatches(box, 'nodes_fts', `"zq${v}x"`), 'CONTROL: the planted row is a term').toBe(1);
    rrTickUntil(box, () => rrStepDone(box, 'nodes-belt', 1) && !rrGists(box)[0]!.includes(v.slice(0, 14)));
    expect(rrGists(box)[0]).toContain(rrLib.REDACTED_MARK);
    expect(rrMatches(box, 'nodes_fts', `"zq${v}x"`), 'and its nodes_fts row').toBe(0);
  }, 180_000);

  it('a nodes_fts row holding a pair-only value glued to a literal escape is re-derived through nodeIndexTexts by the node step (spec §6.2 nodes_fts)', () => {
    const box = rrH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-beltesc-', { role: 'fleet' });
    const v = rrRandomBytes(16).toString('hex');
    const file = rrPath.join(box.home, '.cc-secrets', 'esc.env');
    rrFs.mkdirSync(rrPath.join(box.home, '.cc-secrets'), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    rrFs.writeFileSync(file, `ZQ_ESC=${v}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    rrH.plantSession(box, RR_ID, { uuid: RR_U1, generation: RR_G1, project: 'demo' });
    rrH.plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', RR_SLUG, RR_U1, rrCompacted(RR_U1, 1, 'Rotating the fixture credential before the release.'));
    rrH.spoolLine(box, RR_ID, rrStart(RR_ID, RR_U1, 'startup', { reg: RR_U1, gen: RR_G1 }));
    rrTickUntil(box, () => rrLeafIds(box).length === 1);
    expect(rrQ<{ n: number }>(box, 'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM redact_hashes WHERE len = ?', v.length)[0]!.n,
      'CONTROL: a tick recorded the value\'s pair').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    // The value leaves its file: its pair stays (redact_hashes only grows), but no belt holds it any longer, so only the
    // index's escape readings separate it from the literal `\n` glued onto it. redactField's one reading sees the run
    // `n<value>`, which no pair matches, so the stored gist below is one redactField leaves as it is.
    rrFs.writeFileSync(file, `ZQ_ESC_OTHER=${rrRandomBytes(16).toString('hex')}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    const gist = `Printed {"t":"a\\n${v}"} before the release.`;
    const db = new RrDb(rrRoot(box).dbFile);
    try {
      const n = db.prepare("SELECT rowid AS rid, node_id FROM nodes WHERE kind <> 'condensed'").get() as { rid: number; node_id: string };
      db.prepare('UPDATE nodes SET gist = ? WHERE node_id = ?').run(gist, n.node_id);
      db.prepare('DELETE FROM nodes_fts WHERE rowid = ?').run(n.rid);
      db.prepare('INSERT INTO nodes_fts (rowid, gist, topics, refs) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)').run(n.rid, gist, '', '');
      db.prepare("DELETE FROM meta WHERE k = 'fts_belt'").run();
    } finally { db.close(); }
    expect(rrMatches(box, 'nodes_fts', `"n${v}"`), 'CONTROL: the planted row holds the glued term').toBe(1);
    rrTickUntil(box, () => rrStepDone(box, 'nodes-belt', 1) && rrMatches(box, 'nodes_fts', `"n${v}"`) === 0);
    expect(rrMatches(box, 'nodes_fts', '"printed"'), 'the row was re-derived, not dropped').toBe(1);
  }, 180_000);

  it('a recovery re-derives node fields through the pass\'s belt, and a unit missing from the recovery passes\' belt leaves the belt due (ruling R-oppass-belt; review R47)', async (ctx) => {
    if (process.getuid?.() === 0) ctx.skip();                       // root reads a 0000 file regardless of its mode
    const box = rrH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-beltrec-', { role: 'fleet' });
    const AN = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789';
    const unit = (): string => `${Array.from(rrRandomBytes(29), (b) => AN[b % AN.length]!).join('')}7`;
    const u = unit();                                          // loaded before the backup; unreadable on every recovery pass
    const v = unit();                                          // learned after the backup; loaded on every recovery pass
    const dir = rrPath.join(box.home, '.cc-secrets');
    rrFs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    const uFile = rrPath.join(dir, 'u.env');
    rrFs.writeFileSync(uFile, `ZQ_U=${u}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    rrH.plantSession(box, RR_ID, { uuid: RR_U1, generation: RR_G1, project: 'demo' });
    rrH.plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', RR_SLUG, RR_U1, rrCompacted(RR_U1, 1, `Rotating zq${u}x and zq${v}x before the release.`));
    rrH.spoolLine(box, RR_ID, rrStart(RR_ID, RR_U1, 'startup', { reg: RR_U1, gen: RR_G1 }));
    const ridOf = (s: string): number => rrQ<{ rid: number }>(box, 'SELECT rowid AS rid FROM redact_hashes WHERE len = ? AND hex(sha256) = ?',
      s.length, rrCreateHash('sha256').update(s).digest('hex').toUpperCase())[0]?.rid ?? 0;
    const belt = (): rrLib.BeltState | null => rrLib.parseBeltState(rrMeta(box, 'fts_belt'));
    rrTickUntil(box, () => rrLeafIds(box).length === 1 && ridOf(u) > 0 && (belt()?.rids.includes(ridOf(u)) ?? false), 12);
    const uRid = ridOf(u);                                     // a restore copies redact_hashes, rowids included
    expect(belt()?.v, 'CONTROL: a completed belt generation recorded u covered').toBe(rrLib.BELT_VERSION);
    expect(rrGists(box)[0]!.includes(u.slice(0, 14)), 'CONTROL: the belt masked u when the leaf was derived').toBe(false);
    expect(rrGists(box)[0]!.includes(`zq${v}x`), 'CONTROL: v is in no file yet, so the gist holds it glued').toBe(true);
    const atBackup = belt()!;                                  // the backup pass writes no belt state (Task 22)
    const name = rrBackup(box);
    rrFs.writeFileSync(rrPath.join(dir, 'v.env'), `ZQ_V=${v}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    expect(rrH.runShim(box).code).toBe(0);                     // v learned and journaled: the backup lacks its pair
    rrLose(box, { binding: false, journal: false });
    expect(rrLast((await rrShimPty(box, ['--op', 'restore', name])).out)).toEqual({ rc: 0 });
    // Ruling R-witness-restore: the restore put v's journal pair into the copy between its witness check and its stamp,
    // so the first recovery pass's secretsStep finds the witness unmoved and records nothing due. What leaves the belt
    // due below is then the recovery's own belt-state rule, which M12 removes (Step 7).
    const restored = belt();
    const vrg = (s: rrLib.BeltState): string => JSON.stringify([s.v, s.rids, s.gen]);
    expect(restored !== null && vrg(restored) === vrg(atBackup) && restored.rids.includes(uRid)
      && restored.w !== undefined && restored.w !== atBackup.w,
    'CONTROL: the restore left the backup\'s covered state and stamped its pair insert').toBe(true);
    rrFs.chmodSync(uFile, 0o000);                              // u's file unreadable on every recovery pass
    const unreadable = (): number => rrH.counters(box)['redact_source_unreadable'] ?? 0;
    const before = unreadable();
    try {
      rrTickUntil(box, () => rrRecovered(box), 12);
      expect(unreadable() > before, 'CONTROL: the recovery passes could not read u\'s file (a root runner reads it anyway)').toBe(true);
      // Review R47: the step re-derived the nodes with the pass's belt (run.ectx.belt), so v, loaded on these passes
      // and glued by letters, leaves no stretch in a gist, nodes_fts or blobs_fts at the step's completion, before any
      // tick runs the node step.
      expect(rrGists(box)[0]!.includes(v.slice(0, 14)), 'no stretch of v in the gist at the step\'s completion').toBe(false);
      expect(rrMatches(box, 'nodes_fts', `"zq${v}x"`), 'nor a nodes_fts term').toBe(0);
      expect(rrFtsBytes(box).includes(v.slice(8, 22)), 'nor a blobs_fts byte').toBe(false);
      // Ruling R-oppass-belt: u was missing from every recovery pass's belt, and the leaf the step re-derived holds it
      // glued, so the step must leave the belt due for u.
      expect(rrGists(box)[0]!.includes(`zq${u}x`), 'CONTROL: the re-derived gist holds u, whose file no recovery pass read').toBe(true);
      const st = belt();
      expect(st === null || st.v !== rrLib.BELT_VERSION || !st.rids.includes(uRid), 'u is not recorded covered: the belt is due').toBe(true);
    } finally { rrFs.chmodSync(uFile, 0o600); }
    rrTickUntil(box, () => rrStepDone(box, 'nodes-belt', 1) && !rrGists(box)[0]!.includes(u.slice(0, 14)));
    expect(rrMatches(box, 'nodes_fts', `"zq${u}x"`), 'and its nodes_fts term is gone').toBe(0);
  }, 240_000);

  it('a reparse whose belt lacked a unit: once its file is readable again, the belt generation and its node step re-redact the reparsed leaf (ruling R-oppass-belt; review R46)', (ctx) => {
    if (process.getuid?.() === 0) ctx.skip();                       // root reads a 0000 file regardless of its mode
    const box = rrH.makeHistoryBox('ccrc-hist-beltrp-', { role: 'fleet' });
    const AN = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789';
    const v = `${Array.from(rrRandomBytes(29), (b) => AN[b % AN.length]!).join('')}7`;
    const dir = rrPath.join(box.home, '.cc-secrets');
    rrFs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    const vFile = rrPath.join(dir, 'rp.env');
    rrFs.writeFileSync(vFile, `ZQ_RP=${v}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
    rrH.plantSession(box, RR_ID, { uuid: RR_U1, generation: RR_G1, project: 'demo' });
    rrH.plantTranscript(box, 'claude-a', RR_SLUG, RR_U1, rrCompacted(RR_U1, 1, `Rotating the fixture credential ab${v}cd before the release.`));
    rrH.spoolLine(box, RR_ID, rrStart(RR_ID, RR_U1, 'startup', { reg: RR_U1, gen: RR_G1 }));
    const belt = (): rrLib.BeltState | null => rrLib.parseBeltState(rrMeta(box, 'fts_belt'));
    rrTickUntil(box, () => rrLeafIds(box).length === 1 && belt()?.v === rrLib.BELT_VERSION && (belt()?.rids.length ?? 0) > 0
      && rrStepDone(box, 'nodes-belt', 1), 12);
    const K = rrLib.beltWidth(v);
    /** Whether `s` holds any K-wide stretch of v (K its belt width): what the belt guarantees no field or term keeps. */
    const stretch = (s: string): boolean => Array.from({ length: v.length - K + 1 }, (_, i) => v.slice(i, i + K)).some((w) => s.includes(w));
    const nodeText = (): string => [
      ...rrQ<{ gist: string | null; topics: string | null }>(box, 'SELECT gist, topics FROM nodes').flatMap((r) => [r.gist ?? '', r.topics ?? '']),
      ...rrQ<{ value: string }>(box, 'SELECT value FROM node_refs').map((r) => r.value),
      ...rrQ<{ gist: string; topics: string; refs: string }>(box, 'SELECT gist, topics, refs FROM nodes_fts').flatMap((r) => [r.gist, r.topics, r.refs]),
    ].join('\n');
    expect(stretch(nodeText()), 'CONTROL: the belt masked v when the leaf was derived').toBe(false);
    rrFs.chmodSync(vFile, 0o000);                              // v's file unreadable during the reparse only
    try {
      const r = rrH.runShim(box, ['--op', 'reparse', '--apply']);
      expect(r.code, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    } finally { rrFs.chmodSync(vFile, 0o600); }
    expect(rrGists(box)[0]!.includes(`ab${v}cd`), 'CONTROL: the reparse ran without v\'s belt, so the gist holds it glued').toBe(true);
    // The reparse recorded the belt due (Task 21); with v readable again, the next generation reopens ('nodes-belt', 1),
    // whose node step re-redacts every stored node field and nodes_fts row.
    rrTickUntil(box, () => belt()?.v === rrLib.BELT_VERSION && rrStepDone(box, 'nodes-belt', 1), 12);
    expect(stretch(nodeText()), 'no belt-width stretch of v in nodes.gist, topics, node_refs or nodes_fts').toBe(false);
    expect(rrMatches(box, 'nodes_fts', `"ab${v}cd"`), 'nor a nodes_fts term').toBe(0);
  }, 240_000);
});
```

  - The fourth case (review R46) is the operator passes' belt-state rule end to end for reparse (Task 21's `recordBeltDueIfUncovered`, ruling R-oppass-belt): it runs `--op reparse --apply` through the placed shim (`rrH.runShim`; `makeHistoryBox` places it by default) with the unit's file unreadable, then ticks with it readable, and reads every node field and `nodes_fts` column for a belt-width stretch (`rrLib.beltWidth`, Task 7A). `node_refs.value` is B1's column.
  - The third case needs Task 27's `rrCreateHash` and Task 28's `rrLeafIds`; `rrLib.BeltState`, `parseBeltState` and `BELT_VERSION` are Task 7A's (`lib.d.mts`). Its blobs_fts read is a middle stretch of `v` (`rrFtsBytes`, as O47's cases read one), because FTS5 stores a term's leading bytes shared with the term before it.

  - `RrDb` and `rrRoot` are Task 27's `rr` helpers; the write handle is closed before the next pass opens the store. `rrQ`, `rrStepDone` and `rrRandomBytes` are Task 27's too, and `rrLeafIds` is Task 28's.

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the node re-derivation.** Append to `ccd/history/derive.mjs`:

```js
// ── W1-B2 Task 29: node fields after a pair is learned late or replayed (§6.2 "A pair learned after its text was
// indexed", §9.14 "Redaction first"; slugs history-redaction-reindex-merge, history-redaction-journaled) ─────

/** Rewrite each node's stored gist, topics and refs through redactField with ictx.pairIdx, and its nodes_fts row when
 *  ictx.fts. This is the fail-closed path for a node whose summary cannot be read again: a pruned span, a raw leaf,
 *  a condensed node, or a leaf whose re-derivation threw. Redaction needs only the pair, never the source text.
 *  Topics are redacted ONE BY ONE and only then serialised (R2: redactField on each raw field before any
 *  serialisation; in the column's JSON text a control character inside a value would be escaped and no longer match
 *  its pair). The column is read through topicsOfColumn (Task 9), so JSON and one-per-line columns both read; the
 *  nodes_fts row is lib's nodeIndexTexts of the rewritten fields (Task 7A: each column through entryIndexText, so the
 *  index's escape readings; topics and refs one per line), as every other writer of it does (Tasks 8 and 9).
 *  redactField is layer 4 over layers 1-3 whenever ictx.pairIdx carries a belt (Task 7A, spec rev 3.5 §8.3), so a
 *  value glued to letters is masked here too; this is also the writer the belt's node step (beltNodesStep) uses.
 *  D-4729 (history-redaction-fail-closed-node-rewrite) */
export function redactNodeFields(db, ictx, nodeIds) {
  if (nodeIds.length === 0) return 0;
  const read = db.prepare('SELECT rowid AS rid, gist, topics FROM nodes WHERE node_id = ?');
  const refsOf = db.prepare('SELECT kind, value, origin FROM node_refs WHERE node_id = ?');
  const setNode = db.prepare('UPDATE nodes SET gist = ?, topics = ? WHERE node_id = ?');
  const dropRefs = db.prepare('DELETE FROM node_refs WHERE node_id = ?');
  const putRef = db.prepare('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO node_refs (node_id, kind, value, origin) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)');
  const fts = ictx.fts === true;
  const ftsDel = fts ? db.prepare('DELETE FROM nodes_fts WHERE rowid = ?') : null;
  const ftsIns = fts ? db.prepare('INSERT INTO nodes_fts (rowid, gist, topics, refs) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)') : null;
  let n = 0;
  withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => {
    for (const id of nodeIds) {
      const row = read.get(id);
      if (row === undefined) continue;
      const gist = row.gist === null ? null : redactField(row.gist, ictx.pairIdx);
      const list = row.topics === null ? null : topicsOfColumn(row.topics).map((t) => redactField(t, ictx.pairIdx));
      const topics = list === null ? null : JSON.stringify(list);
      const refs = refsOf.all(id).map((r) => ({ kind: r.kind, value: redactField(r.value, ictx.pairIdx), origin: r.origin }));
      setNode.run(gist, topics, id);
      dropRefs.run(id);
      for (const r of refs) putRef.run(id, r.kind, r.value, r.origin);
      if (fts) {
        ftsDel.run(row.rid);
        const t = nodeIndexTexts({ gist, topics: list ?? [], refs: refs.map((r) => r.value) }, ictx.pairIdx);
        ftsIns.run(row.rid, t.gist, t.topics, t.refs);
      }
      n += 1;
    }
  });
  return n;
}

/** Task 21's refreshLeaf over each of `nodeIds`, then Task 9's rerollParents once when any leaf changed: what
 *  reparseLeaves does, with each leaf apart. A parser throw inside leafFields is refreshLeaf's own record (it writes
 *  the leaf parse-failed, counts parser_crash once and answers 'failed', which counts as a change here). A throw that
 *  escapes refreshLeaf (its reads before leafFields; busy rethrows) is counted parser_crash, as deriveLeaves counts a
 *  derive throw, and skipped; the caller's redactNodeFields then
 *  rewrites its stored fields fail-closed. Nothing retries it on a later pass (the coordinator's ruling RB5): the
 *  recovery reindex moves its cursor past it, and the late-pair fast path (rederiveGistsFor, from B1's
 *  reindexForValues, which never moves the mark) stops searching the value once B1's rederiveFts has opened a
 *  generation (lib's phraseValues then hands it only the values its tick recorded) or completed one (the mark is then
 *  at the pair). So one bad summary holds neither, and only `reparse` re-derives it again. Re-deriving twice is
 *  idempotent. Answers how many leaves changed. */
export function reparseFailClosed(db, ictx, nodeIds) {
  let changed = 0;
  for (const id of nodeIds) {
    let r;
    try {
      r = refreshLeaf(db, ictx, id);
    } catch (crash) {
      if (ictx.isBusy(crash)) throw crash;
      withTx(db, 'NORMAL', () => { bump(db, 'parser_crash'); });
      continue;
    }
    // 'failed': refreshLeaf caught a parser throw itself and wrote the leaf parse-failed (Task 21, RB5), counted once.
    if (r === 'updated' || r === 'failed') changed += 1;
  }
  if (changed > 0) rerollParents(db, ictx, nodeIds);
  return changed;
}

/** The nodes whose gist, topics or refs hold one of `values`, re-derived with ictx.pairIdx (§6.2).
 *  - They are found by a QUOTED-PHRASE match on nodes_fts (ftsPhrase), which FTS5 tokenises as the index did. A bare
 *    MATCH of a value holding '-' is a syntax error ("no such column", measured on 22.16.0).
 *  - Each value is searched by UNIT (lib's secretUnits: the value when it is one run, else each of its 12+-char
 *    runs), as B1's reindexForValues searches blobs_fts (B1's D-4311): redaction matches by unit, so a node holding
 *    only one segment of a multi-run value is found too.
 *  - A leaf whose summary is still stored is re-derived (reparseFailClosed: same id, parents re-rolled, a throw
 *    counted and skipped). Every node found, re-derived or not, is then rewritten through redactNodeFields.
 *  - It is the same-tick fast path over nodes, as B1's phrase search is over blobs (B1's
 *    D-4344): it moves no mark, and it runs only while `slice` and `budget` last
 *    (B1's review 344 F2 rule: a fast path never runs unbudgeted ahead of the step that ends the generation). It
 *    runs on every tick where a value is owed, until B1's rederiveFts opens a generation (then only the values its
 *    tick recorded are searched) or completes one (the mark then covers the pair). What it misses or leaves (a value
 *    glued to letters inside one term, a hash-only pair, a spent budget) the belt's node step finishes, fail-closed:
 *    every generation that opens restarts it (beltNodesStep, Task 7B). Re-deriving twice is idempotent.
 *  Returns how many nodes it touched. */
export function rederiveGistsFor(db, ictx, values, budget, slice) {
  if (ictx.fts !== true || values.length === 0) return 0;
  // B1's review 344 F2 rule for a fast path: never unbudgeted. What a spent budget leaves, the belt's node step finishes.
  if (!parentsBudgetLeft(slice) || !parentsBudgetLeft(budget)) return 0;
  const match = db.prepare('SELECT rowid AS rid FROM nodes_fts WHERE nodes_fts MATCH ?');
  const nodeAt = db.prepare(`SELECT n.node_id, n.kind, (n.summary_blob_id IS NOT NULL AND b.z IS NOT NULL) AS readable
    FROM nodes n LEFT JOIN blobs b ON b.blob_id = n.summary_blob_id WHERE n.rowid = ?`);
  const reparse = new Set();
  const rewrite = new Set();
  for (const v of values) {
    for (const unit of secretUnits(v)) {
      for (const r of match.all(ftsPhrase(unit))) {
        const n = nodeAt.get(r.rid);
        if (n === undefined) continue;
        if (n.kind !== 'condensed' && n.readable === 1) reparse.add(n.node_id);
        else rewrite.add(n.node_id);
      }
    }
  }
  const leaves = [...reparse].sort();
  if (leaves.length > 0) reparseFailClosed(db, ictx, leaves);
  // A parent the re-derivation re-rolled takes its children's gists as they are now. A node the match found that no
  // re-derivation reaches is rewritten in place, and so is every leaf it tried: a leaf refreshLeaf had to skip (its
  // holding copy unreadable) or that threw is still rewritten fail-closed, and rewriting a redacted field again
  // changes nothing.
  const rest = [...rewrite].sort();
  redactNodeFields(db, ictx, [...leaves, ...rest]);
  return leaves.length + rest.length;
}
```
